When I saw this being played on Twitch, I immediately was reminded of a game I used to play on my TI-83 in my highschool years called "Blockdude".  I'm a huge fan of DOS, Amiga, Apple II, Atari ST, etc. puzzle games, and this is a definite throwback to those. I discovered that Blockman actually predates the game I played, so I checked the shareware version out on a Dosbox page, and I definitely see the 'inspiration'! Kudos on getting permission from Blockman's dev to do this game! Anyways, I've played through most of the levels and absolutely love this game, The first 10 levels are fairly easy but the difficulty ramps up nicely. I was worried after the first couple levels that this was going to be an easy game, but the later levels put those worries to rest.A few suggestions/feedback:- Add more music.  The menu and gameplay songs are great, but would like a few more gameplay songs- The manual is well-written, but many people might not even notice the link for the manual, so an in-game tutorial might be helpful- Level sharing through ModDB / IndieDB works well, but Steam Workshop integration would be even betterOverall, love this game and highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys retro games and very thinky puzzle games. Warning, it is very difficult, especially the later half of the main levels and all of the bonus levels, but it is a welcome challenge.

"The Bridge Curse 2: The Extrication" continues the gripping horror experience introduced by Chinese game developers SOFTSTAR ENTERTAINMENT in its predecessor, "The Bridge Curse: Road to Salvation." Set in a school haunted by dark secrets, the game follows a group of students creating an indie horror film based on true events. Players assume the roles of both students and a curious reporter, delving into the chilling mysteries lurking within the school's walls.The game's strength lies in its captivating storyline, which seamlessly blends Chinese traditions with contemporary horror elements. While the plot can be quirky at times, it adds to the game's charm and unpredictability, keeping players engaged from start to finish. Furthermore, the inclusion of Easter eggs and memes adds a layer of relatable humor for fans of pop culture.Voice acting shines in both Mandarin and English, with expressive performances that enhance the game's immersion. Personally, I opted for the Mandarin voice track for its added silliness, which complements the game's atmosphere perfectly.Visually, "The Bridge Curse 2" is a feast for the eyes, with stunning graphics and terrifying creature designs that will leave players on the edge of their seats. While not an action-packed survival horror, the gameplay offers engaging puzzle-solving mechanics reminiscent of classics like White Day.As a sequel to an already impressive title, "The Bridge Curse 2" exceeds expectations and leaves room for further exploration of its rich universe. I applaud SOFTSTAR ENTERTAINMENT for delivering another unforgettable horror experience and eagerly anticipate future installments in the series.In conclusion, "The Bridge Curse 2: The Extrication" is a must-play for horror enthusiasts and fans of Asian horror cinema alike. Its gripping storyline, stellar voice acting, and breathtaking visuals make it a standout title in the genre.

我非常享受《女鬼橋二》的遊戲過程，可以自信地說，這是一部在氛圍恐怖方面的傑作，將心理驚悚類型提升到了新的層面。作為前作的續集，這款遊戲不僅延續了詭異的設定，還透過精緻的遊戲設計、引人入勝的故事情節和出色的視覺效果超出了我的預期。《女鬼橋二》最強大的部分之一就是其無與倫比的氛圍。從你踏入那間鬧鬼的校園的那一刻起，你便立刻被帶入一個充滿不安緊張感的世界。環境設計美得令人毛骨悚然，陰影交錯的走廊、詭異的燈光，以及讓人不安的音效，讓你時刻感到緊張。每一聲吱嘎、低語和遙遠的腳步聲都增添了越來越重的恐懼感，讓你感覺危險似乎藏在每一個角落。《女鬼橋二》的故事在前作的基礎上進行擴展，並引入了新角色、新的背景故事和意想不到的情節轉折。它巧妙地將民俗元素與心理恐怖結合在一起，讓這種鬧鬼的感覺變得非常個人化，並且情感上深具吸引力。圍繞詛咒的謎團以恰到好處的懸念展開，將你引入遊戲的恐怖世界。敘事緊湊，讓你對角色及其命運充滿關心。在遊戲性方面，《女鬼橋二》也有了顯著的進步。它有效結合了探索、解謎和潛行元素，並保持良好的節奏。這些謎題具有挑戰性，但不會讓人感到沮喪，潛行的環節讓人緊張不已，因為你得小心避開那些悄然逼近的惡勢力。新的遊戲機制，包括環境互動和巧妙的逃脫過程，讓整體玩法保持新鮮和動態。每個決定都有其重要性，並且會對相關角色造成實際後果。在視覺效果上，《女鬼橋二》非常驚人。環境細節、超自然生物的設計以及氛圍效果都增強了沉浸感。光影的運用在提升緊張感方面起了關鍵作用，精心打造的陰影和昏暗的走廊營造出持續的不安感。聲音設計也是一大亮點，陰森的音效與視覺效果完美融合。無論是靈魂的低語還是突如其來的驚嚇聲，音效始終保持緊張感。配音表現非常出色，為角色增添了層次感，使恐怖氛圍更加個人化。《女鬼橋二》是恐怖迷必玩的遊戲。 它將心理恐怖、氛圍敘事和引人入勝的遊戲性完美結合。這款遊戲值得你放進遊戲庫，趕快去購買吧！我也非常建議你去玩一下第一部作品，絕對不會讓你失望！Translation = Imagine you are in a group of college students who somehow think it is a great idea to investigate urban legends and set out to do some serious ghost busting. This game is, so far, wildly better than the first. The first title was held back by poor encounter design and frustrating mechanics alongside some visuals that, while they had impressive animation work, lacked cohesive art design. Bridge Curse 2 not only doesn't suffer from much of this, it looks a lot better and has great scares, puzzles, and set piece moments. It's such a significant jump from the first game that I'm now very interested in what the studio moves on to do, and I hope that they are able to make more of these kinds of games. If I had one lament: I got used to the Chinese voice track from the first game and wish I could listen to the Chinese audio here. Maybe they recorded everything in English and subtitled everywhere else to have more mass appeal? It's a small thing, overall. Fans of the first game should absolutely get this, but even people who haven't played the first can jump right in. In fact, I'd recommend skipping the first altogether and only play it if you want more after playing this one.

Played on Steam Deck.TL;DR - Springblades is an extraction of the battle system from the N64 and Gamecube Paper Mario games and SokPop nails it!The first two Paper Mario games are my favorite, and Springlands is definitely inspired by those blessed games. Badges, 3 stat level ups, even calling it "action command" for the active battle timing mechanic, the crowd sound effects like cheers when hitting and ooohs when getting hit, and much  more. This is really just a bite sized Paper Mario combat game and it's really good!Paper Mario had to pace out the battle system to last the whole RPG length but with only the battles and no need to stretch, Springblades lets you increase your attack and get some good synergies going with just enough time in between upgrades to feel satisfied with creating a setup and ready to mix it up the next time you get the opportunity. The focus on combat is done really well here and the creator is very in tune with what made combat in Paper Mario enjoyable: the badges and synergy options to give multiple build tactics to choose from and swap between.There are a few flaws which could make the experience better, and these are the types of things that I hope SokPop will be able to polish in the future by taking more time with their games. Most crucially experience needs to be scaled to current level instead of fixed. The low level enemies give 1 xp and the high level enemies give 1 xp, so in terms of leveling there is no strategy or reason to grind anything but the weakest enemies. The inventory needs better organization; when selling I could never tell if I had duplicates of items because there is no sorting. Also the catalog of badges and enemies just lists your total; it would be very nice to be able to go in and see which ones you have to get a better idea of what you are missing. Having these small things be the biggest issues I could find shows just how good this game is.

It's a cute game with delightful monster design and flavor text, with a (perhaps surprisingly) deep character building system and fun battle mechanics.For those who know "Paper Mario & the Thousand Year Door", "Springblades" scratches the same itch and the inspiration is evident, with its own twists. Battles are similarly turn-based, and successfully using abilities or defending requires you to perform timed inputs - hitting the button when a moving cursor is in the right spot mostly. Here you can use as many abilities as you want during your turn, but you have to manage your energy - doing to much exhausts you, which forces you to skip a turn. It's a simple and effective system, it's both fun and strategic.You explore the world by traveling step-by-step between nodes on the map. Every step you have to fight through one or two encounters. Every encounter you get to choose between two sets of monsters, so if you find one particularly annoying you can always pick the other. There are a bunch of special locations on the map, where you'll have to fight a boss to unlock it as a fast travel spot and (usually) as a shop, where you'll be able to buy new equipment. Your equipment determines the types of attacks and abilities you can use in battle.The game is 5 to 10 hours long, depending on how thorough your exploration is and how strong you manage to make your character. I didn't find it very difficult, but I kind of min-maxed my build. If I roleplayed more and made a prettier build, it might have been trickier !

If I could give this game a "neutral" rating, I would. However, when forced between positive and negative, I have to go negative.By all rights, Orc Covenant looks like it is targeted at me. Do I like orcs? Yes sir, I do! Do I want a gay romance visual novel where I get my pick of orcs to capture the heart of? Oh boy, do I! After having played it for a while, though, and thoroughly exploring two and a half of the orcs' routes...I mostly came out of it very "meh."First of all, character visuals. Xareth as a main character does not appeal to me. Orc Covenant is billed as a bara VN, but Xareth is a pretty typical pretty-boy elf in terms of visuals. If you're like me and you're interested in this for the orcs, know that the vast majority of the scenes involve either Xareth or the other elf character in the story. Orc on orc scenes are very rare, though I have found at least one brief one.What I really am puzzled by are the designs of the orcs themselves. Now, presumably if you're a gay man interested in orcs, usually that's because you're into rougher and more hyper-masculine men. Orc Covenant makes not just the elves but the orcs themselves a bit too "pretty" and traditionally handsome that kind of disarms the core point. Dagroth looks alright. Karn at least has facial hair. The others look like they belong on a magazine cover, though, and it's just weird. The CGs also didn't really do most of them any favors, and tend to make the characters look even more "pretty boy" despite the fact that we're theoretically dealing with barbaric orcs here. Finally, I probably wouldn't have made all of the main orcs have long hair, as it definitely reduces character diversity there.Now, all of that is very personal opinion. You can probably look at the screenshots and see if the art style appeals to you or not. The story has its own host of problems though.So, Xareth is kind of unlikable as a character even beyond his design. The story very much portrays him as a scheming backstabber who needs to be redeemed by love, which gets a little trite because all three of the orcs I've played the routes of have that as a major story point, which makes it pretty repetitive.More than that, though, the entire story is very repetitive across multiple playthroughs, which is not great when an individual run is actually fairly short. I don't expect a porn game to have amazing writing, but it also shouldn't take me out of the moment. Every route seems to go over the same points about all of the main characters, and you'll sit through all of the same reveals about every character regardless of which route you're on. Sometimes this even happens during sex scenes, which completely pulled me out of the scene I was supposed to find sexy. This becomes pretty tedious. A far smarter way to handle this is have some mystery in each route, and require players to play multiple routes to get the whole story. That would encourage replays and reduce the tedium of learning about Karn's father for the fourth time.So far I've been pretty negative, and the simple fact is that Orc Covenant is a porn game that I didn't find to be particularly hot. Dagroth, and to a lesser extent Karn, are probably the exceptions, and I do have to admit that their routes kept me entertained enough that I went through them completely and saw most of the variations of their routes.I want to finish off by saying I've seen some of the other reviews comparing this game to To Trust an Incubus and Mister Versatile. I have played those games, but they didn't stick with me enough for me to make any comparison. I don't think you need to compare this to those games to find it wanting, though.

Even though Orc Covernat's story is different, I feel like I've played one of Y Press's past games again. The stories' choices and narrative structure seem to have been copied from one game to another. Wasn't it in Hardcore Cruising that you met the characters and then chose the route you wanted? All games I have played until now happen in the same way: the MC arrives at a place, can't leave it based on a (usually) stupid reason that is barely explored, meets hot guys, and then, you, as a player, choose a path (at least this time, you won't be trapped in a loop). One thing here: You can't complete your goal without initially fooling someone and, in some cases, falling in love with them after - of course! This is so stereotyped; it reminds me of all the problems Yaoi stories have, and it's sad to read that again. Can't we have a proper route to kick this stupid narrative trophy away and empower a character? Does a gay man need to be every time “forced” to interact sexually with men every day? In the first 2 minutes of the game, you have already had sex a few times...Anyways, choose a route and make some choices - I believe there are fewer choices than in previous games. It is nothing different from the past games, but it is at a higher price, maybe because it’s an attempt to back on what they were a few years ago. There are plans to post-launch content, but plans are plans. Do you prefer to pay a higher price now or wait for a sale and the post-content launching day? Consider Y Press has been running multiple projects - as you can check on their upcoming games - and has one updated monthly. I know they deliver a few games in a year, but can they deliver everything they promise with an updated monthly game? It's like having two different businesses made by a small indie company, something I never saw from them until now.In short, if you expect some design/narrative innovation, you won't get it. The replayability value is there because superfluous choices can leave you lost on where you need to go to find the most exciting parts of the stories - you can buy the guide if you want. The replayability value is similar to the value Alpha Hole Prison delivered; if you care only about this aspect, get it instead of this game; you'll get more content. You'll pay and get what you always get from Y Press with a higher price: a traditional novel (like their past ones) with a simple story, no design innovation, and very well-made CGs - in less quantity than some of their past games. The Symbiant, Robin Morningwood Adventure, Camp Buddy: Scoutmaster Season and Joke Studio (I'm SO EXCITED to this one), will deliver you a better experience for a better price.I would give it a neutral rating, but since that's impossible, I recommend you wait for a sale. Entertaining story, amazing CGs, all of the routes in the game are a blast to play, I highly recommend.Xareth is a great POV character, because while he has a defined background and motives, the real story is how his time among the Orcs changes him, and most of the decision making in the game involves deciding which is more important; his growing attraction to his Orc partner of choice, or his desire for revenge. My first couple playthroughs in Kurdan and Karn's routes, it seemed a bit simplistic; falling in love with the Orc would give you a good ending, betraying them would give you a bad one.As I explored the different paths you can take, I realized something -- a lot of the most interesting outcomes came not from sticking to one side of the romance/revenge choices, but by going back and forth between them, trying to balance both and failing. (Note I didn't say "good" outcomes -- rather interesting ones). While each route has some events that occur regardless of your choices -- which might feel frustrating at first -- the way certain choices snowball off each other make it clear that your choices do matter.The sprites and CGs are gorgeous, and while I do wish there were more CGs specific to certain choices to make replay more rewarding (some routes it seems you can unlock all CGs with one playthrough) it's definitely feels rewarding figuring out how to get the various endings.All in all, if you like horny bara content with some romance tropes, you'll find something you like in this game.

Having played a number of Y Press Games' games, I definitely think this is one of the better of them! The action starts quickly, and the illustrations are beautiful. There are a mixture of color and gray scale images, and the tone of the game is fairly serious interjected with bits of humor. The narrative itself focuses on a treacherous elven prince committed to revenge against the person who deposed his father, with the orcs initially serving as a means to an ends. The PoV character is the prince's dragon familiar, who offers both insights into the prince's mind and also tempers his regicidal fanaticism with a healthy dose of compassion. The game features four routes with multiple endings each, with the player's decision determining whether and how Xareth's goals are achieved.Additional backer-created content is slated to be added to the game over the next year, with the first of that put in the game just before launch. There are a few fun improvements over their previous games, too, such as an interactive gallery, that I hope they opt to carry into future games.After finishing two of the routes, I place this in a solid second place for Y Press Games' products, behind Mr. Versatile and replacing my previous second: Dear Monster. I personally prefer it much better than their sci-fi games, including Hardcore Cruising, Alpha Hole Prison, and To Trust an Incubus. Obviously some of this will be subjective, and your mileage may vary, but overall I find the game beautiful, the story more compelling, and the characters more enjoyable than most of their other products. If you've enjoyed any of Y Press Games' previous works, I highly recommend trying this one!

I have been a fan of Y Press Games for quite awhile now. I have played most of their games. What I really enjoy is the different routes the story in their games can go based on your choices. So far my favorite game of theirs has been Alpha Hole Prison, but Orc Covenant does not disappoint. From what I can gather there seem to be close to 30 different endings with each love interest getting at least 5 different endings. The endings do feel adequately varied as well. I really do enjoy the distinct differences between the 'good' endings and the 'bad' endings.In regards to the characters I think they mostly hit the mark. Firstly talking about the design of the characters I think that Dagroth, Kurdan, Karn, Thok, and Hork all look fantastic. Nothing I would change with their design. I will say that Xareth's design does not quite do it for me personally. However, objectively speaking, it is very well done regardless of personal preference. I do have to say that I am not a fan of Yundril's design either. I understand that he is a half orc so he needs to look different from the other orcs, but I don't think that the skin color paired with hair color was the right move. In regards to side characters I think they pretty much all look great also. I don't want to go into spoiler territory, but I think the two surprise characters look especially great.I am going to switch to talk about the individual story plots. Xareth's motivations for doing what he is doing do seem solid enough. I do feel like he repeated things regarding his backstory a few to many times. I understand that the trauma he went through had a big impact on him, but with the game only taking a few hours to play through I do not think it is necessary to explain his backstory several different times. That issue aside, I do genuinely think that Xareth is a well developed character. I, again, do want to avoid spoiler territory so I am not going to go into specifics. However, I do think all four of the main love interests have a decently developed story arc. Their motivations for what they do seem solid, and they do not feel one dimensional. Even the himbo Kurdan has a decent amount of depth to his character if you really stop to think about him and his position.I do want to take a moment to talk specifically about Galen. I am not a fan of his design, and I find him to be pretty annoying throughout the game. However, I think this was done intentionally by Y Press Games. Galen makes for a good antagonist for Xareth to deal with. He is one of those characters where it is easy to dislike him. So in that regard I think that they did a good job with Galen.I will say that I was surprised with some of the themes that were included in the game. The inclusion of taboo topics such as incest and rape gives the game a bit more heavy feel. I do personally appreciate that in a game. I feel like they do a serve a purpose in the game, and I would not remove them. Y Press Games do provide a trigger warning on the Steam page, but I think adding some sort of warning in the game itself would not have been a bad idea.The next thing of note is the background music and the background images. I think they are both done very well. The music really sucked me into the game. I do think the music was stronger than the background images, but the they were not something to be dismissed either. They were done well also.Finally, the main reason that most people play a game like this - the spicy scenes. I do think that all of the spicy scenes are narrated very well. They wording goes along perfectly with the images. The images also look incredible. There are a few that are black and white instead of being colored. I do not personally think that is the best decision that could have been made, but it does really bother me to much. I will say that I really like the kink elements that are included in the game. Shout out specifically do Karn and his piercings. The game for sure got my heart beating fast more than a few times. There are a few situations where Xareth does get to top, but for the most part he is usually taking the sub / bottom role. I am sure this appeals to the majority of the audience, but just speaking for myself I would love to get more chances to enjoy some beefy orc butt.  Will say that I thought I was going to lose it (in a good way) when saw the scene of Kurdan sitting on top of Xareth.Overall, would I recommend this game? Absolutely. If you enjoy bara games, then there is no question that you will enjoy this one. The few criticisms I did mention are nothing that would honestly give me a negative opinion about the game. If you feel unsure about the price then just pick up the free demo and give it a try. It games a good vibe of what to expect throughout the game I think.

Orcs! Orcs! Orcs! A barbarian scourge on civilised lands or massive sexy green muscle dads that just need a hug? This question has plagued Elven Power Bottoms ever since Legolas first opened an OrclyFans account. Luckily for us, we need wonder no longer, as Orc Covenant has arrived to let us know the correct response when faced with a charging Orc - go face down, ass up!Orc Covenant is the latest visual novel/orc-bothering sim from Y Press Games, and represents a return to their full-length, multi-route, choice-driven ending format similar to their other games such as Alpha Hole Prison or To Trust an Incubus. The story follows the main character Xareth, a former Elven Prince whose family was executed by an incompetent populist usurper who kept him alive as a political prisoner to legitimise his rule. Xareth longs to overthrow him and take back the throne but lacks an army. If only the Elven kingdom was at war with a race of horse-hung Bara gigachads that he could scheme and manipulate into fighting for him.... Oh wait, they are! The Elves are currently getting their twink asses kicked and hiding behind an impenetrable magical shield, presumably because their warriors are constantly distracted by the Orcs doing pec-bounces mid battle. Luckily Xareth has the one thing the Orcs prize above all else - an implausibly stretchy bussy. Or magical powers. Or maybe both?Into this setting steps the player, adopting the role of Xareth and deciding whether he will stay true to his path of ambition and try and use and betray the Orcs to win back his throne, ally with them fairly and give up his throne in the name of vengeance or give up on the whole politics thing and just get passed around the tribe like a pointy-eared fleshlight. Maybe that last one isn't in there, but it's what I would choose. I always prefer visual novels where there MC isn't a generic, blank slate personality void, so Xareth was a fairly interesting MC for me. He clearly draws inspiration from the fantasy politics of Game of Thrones, kinda like if Cersei Lannister was a Twunk Thot. As the player, you do have agency over his choices however and can choose whether you want him to stay true to his scheming origins, or mellow out after getting some of that Good Orc D. Speaking of which, Orc Covenant has four love interests Xareth can choose from. Each Orc will act as his advocate in the tribe, and he has to try and win them over to get the titular Covenant in question. Let's just get the Best Boy out of the way first - Dagroth, the Orc Chieftain and the living personification of the phrase "Choke Me Daddy!". He's a rough, tough and gruff Alpha Orc who can spread you so wide you'll be covering two postal codes. You might think as Chieftain he is the obvious choice, but before you dive face-first into his hairy booba, know that he hates all Elves due to his Tragic Backstory™! Can Xareth defrost his heart using only the power of his bottomless bottom? Only your choices can decide!Second up is Kurdan, Dagroth's son and next in line for leadership of the Orcs. So if you're insane and not into Daddies, how about.... Sonnies (?) instead. Kurdan is a textbook Wholesome Himbo, with the circumference of his chest outstripping his IQ by several digits. He's utterly adorable and equipped with more inches than a tape measure, but Xareth thinks he can manipulate him into getting what he wants. Can you stand to betray such a pure soul? Or will you fall for his naive charms instead and help him get what he actually wants?Next up we have Tsundere Spice, I mean Yundril. He TOTALLY doesn't like Elves or anything.... baka!! He thinks they're dumb, worthless and he's going to prove it by bending you over, pulling your hair and rearranging your guts until you beg for  mercy. Yundril is Dagroth's first son (Daddy is fertile af bro) but OH NOES - he's a half-elf! As such he has to try twice as hard to be half the Orc and much of his route consists of unpicking the drama around this.... or making it worse for Xareth's benefit. Fiery tempered, volatile and passionate, Yundril is a good choice for those who aren't so into the burly, sweaty, masculine, swole, delicious and god-tier Orc Aesthetic as his half-elf origins mean he's prettier and more lithe than the rest of the cast. A clear choice for the Average Yaoi Enthusiast.Finally we step outside the Dagroth Family Tree and have Karn, or as I call him, Sophistidaddy. If Dagroth would throw you over his shoulder and take you up against a tree in front of the tribe, Karn would light some candles and put some mood music on first, and then order you a cab afterwards. He is the tribe's Shaman and likes the finer things in life, but he's still built like an Orc and has an Orc's needs UwU. Karn is just as much of a schemer as Xareth however, and if you choose his route you'll be deciding whether you want to try and outplay a player, or team up with one and risk getting only half the reward. Karn also has the finest ass I've ever seen in a visual novel (srsly, check the screenshot on the store page).So speaking of the art, Orc Covenant has an absolute ton of CG's and sprites spread across the routes. Most of Xareth with the Orcs, some featuring the Orcs with each other and occasionally some with the side-characters and the main cast. There's enough here to keep CG hunters busy for a while. Take note - some of the CG's are in black & white. Usually this is the foreplay scenes or post-coital cuddles. All of the major scenes are rendered in glorious technicolor. The whole game has an extremely vibrant colour palette that jumps off the screen and the general level of art is consistently very high throughout. The colouring and way the artist does lighting effects are particularly well done. There's a very wide selection of pairings and positions, so the small top/big bottom enjoyers have something to get excited about too. I would say this game and the upcoming Oni Onsen has the best art out of any game in the Y Press catalogue to date.The soundtrack is a fusion of twinkly fantasy and throbbing metal guitar, probably meant to represent the two different civilisations coming together. It sets the tone, is fairly unobtrusive and gets the job done,So far the game has been technically very stable. I've currently played Dagroth and Karn's routes through to one conclusion each and haven't encountered any bugs and I'll be going back to achievement hunt and get all the endings. The endings I've experienced have also been different and interesting enough to make me want to go back and make the choices I didn't explore the first time around. The developers are also going to be releasing extra scenes and CG's with backer content over the course of the following year, so the content in the game is only going to expand and get more diverse. If you're still on the fence, I urge you to PLAY THE FREE DEMO! It has an absolute ton of CG's and art including a multi-scene Orcgy, the first pairing with each love interest and a scene with two of the side characters. It'll really help establish the tone and setting for you and will cost you nothing.In conclusion, Orc Covenant represents a return to the format Y Press established with their earlier successes, now bolstered further by some top-tier art and extensive post-launch content plans. In my currency, Orc Covenant delivered more than enough content and replay value for the price compared to other titles. If you're a fan of Big Boiz, Fantasy Drama or just getting your hole absolutely annihilated, you're going to want to pick this one up.For the Horde! 💚

This game is not a romantic slowburn, but a clear 18+ visual novel. Unfortunately the speed gave the characters the easy going brand, there was no way to get extra attached to them and invest in the individual story lines beyond mouse clicks. The introduction and encounter with the orcs was a massive mistake from my perspective. All of the characters were revealed, they showed their "qualities" and it took quite a lot of drive out of their individual stories, where for example their reveal could have just been something interesting.Another thing that was clear to me from the demo is that the orcs had completely insanely disproportionate manhood to their bodies. If this was a specific trait in any of them, it could be understood, but this was completely off and very much took away my personal drive from the 18+ scenes, which felt completely unnatural. At the same time, their proportions vary from scene to scene, meaning any consistency is an illusion, and it always seemed to be the size that matched the scene rather than the character itself.The last comment is about some 18+ scenes that the creators didn't even bother to color and left them black and white. So were we paying for a finished product, or was it a version that the studio needed to release quickly so they could start cashing in players?

Looking at the trailer for this game is so deceptive. The shallow weapon animations and simpler art style are legitimately the worst part of this game. It's a seriously fun reverse bullet hell.It has almost all the mechanics you probably know from Vampire Survivors, and it does a great job of iterating on them and adding its own touches. For example, there's a loose story you follow that adds a little depth to the game, and rather than doing all your progression via a menu after the round, you have a kind of keep you return to where you interact with NPCs there to help you with your quest; unlocking new levels is done with the help of a magician who can conjure portals, for example. It just feels very lovingly and thoughtfully crafted.The progression feels really good, both overall, and per stage. Weapons evolve and synergize with each other, adding some strategy elements (like making sure you balance long and short range, and fast and slow weapons). There are also different upgrade paths for each weapon that can make a big difference in how they play; plus each weapon has a damage type that you can get modifiers for, like a buff if you have a tool, magic item, and physical weapon.I've only got a little over an hour in the game so far, but it's one of a couple reverse bullet hell's I've tried that I had a hard time putting down.

I'll be honest: that artstyle, that name, that title art, even the font used. Everything made me think this would be a low effort Vampire Survivors clone that does nothing other than adding a +1 to the waves of bullet heaven titles on Steam. As I keep playing this, I realize this pretty far from the truth. While the presentation is nothing special, it has this endearing 8-bit JRPG vibe to it, with the game hub featuring characters you can sort of interact with to gamble money, buy armor and weapons (as opposed to the more classic permanent upgrade of stats), hire new fighters, and most importantly pet a cute doggo. And then there's the combat, which again isn't anything too remakrable on a technical level and somewhat slow with scattered enemies hard to crowd control, but the variety of weapons, the active and passive skills, the varied loot and more give a solid variety. The various levels themselves have traps appear randomly, weather effects and more that can drastically alter a fight's outcome. While hardly the most mechanically satisfying bullet heaven out there, it still offers a take unique enough to worth a try for hardcore fans of the genre like me.Bullet Heaven Fandom review #46. Reviewed Platform: Oculus Rift CV1IntroductionA-Tech Cybernetic VR aims to be an authentic and immersive VR experience built from the ground up for VR. In this review, I will be covering everything that A-Tech Cybernetic VR has to offer and why it’s worth a purchase.Heard of Doom?, of course you have, who hasn’t right?, well A-Tech Cybernetic VR has a LOT going for it to satisfy those who are seeking an amazing First Person Survival experience within a Scfi-Fi zombie/demon genre. The story goes that you awake within a facility with no memories but superpowers, you follow the story of yourself as the main protagonist as he tries to find himself again, whilst surviving a bio-medical outbreak epidemic and also trying to remember where he is. Pro’s and Con’s Pro’s DOOM mixed with Killing FloorGameplay similar to DOOM and killing floorImmersive environment, Gritty atmosphereGreat level designGreat Sounding weapons and ambienceWeapon and item pickup system is unique, comfortable and ties into storyGreat background story with narrationHas a bit more to it then shooting and moving through areas, (Keycards, manual healing through Healing stations and story progression. Various enemies with their own damage and weapons. Separate SWARM mode, Wave Shooting mode with weapons to purchase (Think Call of Duty Zombies mixed with Killing Floor)Con’sWeapons feel great, however, they lack haptic feedback which creates a big part of immersion with gunplay for me personally. Sometimes enemies can be overwhelming, (End of Chapter 2)Pro-Con-ConclusionA-Tech Cybernetic is a great purchase for an FPS or, any VR owner that would love the thrill of a Unique Sci fi set story, a bit of cheeky humour, Great Gunplay, movement and Overall annihilation of biomedical demonic disasters. RIP THROUGH THEM! SAVE YOURSELF!..OFFICIAL REVIEW BELOWPsst. the rest of the review is down here for you enthusiasts. [Spoilers]One of the coolest parts of the story mode in A-Tech Cybernetic VR is the Narrator that follows you on your journey, he makes remarks about your character, and he seems agitated as much as he is crazy. I personally think his involvement with the story ties in amazingly well and he fits the game and gives that sort of twist that you wouldn’t expect in a game like this. It makes this game stand out amongst others. From the first chapter you’re introduced to a great eerie and dark atmosphere which instantly sets the experience before you, It felt strangely calming to me personally. (Difficulty) Ending - Chapter 2Personally I found the end of chapter two to be quite difficult, I had to replay it a couple of good times to finally finish it. The game can get quite difficult at times, but nothing matches to the ending. As a Gamer that's already quite familiar with FPS games and VR, I even found it difficult, so I’m hoping that the ending’s difficulty does not affect anyones overall experience with this awesome modern tribute to the DOOM and Killing floor franchises.  none the less as long as you persist you will be able to complete it, and when it comes down to it, that’s exactly how the original DOOM game was. You had to persist with muscle memory and visualise where the largest threats of enemies were, to put it in perspective with A-Tech Cybernetic VR, the Riflemen enemies need to be taken out first, otherwise your going to have a hard time.  The satisfaction of headshotting enemies at your own pace or just mowing them down with an infestation of bullet hell feels great. I’m very impressed with A-Tech Cybernetic, Mechanically, Visually and cannot wait to see what else lies underneath this games dark and mysterious background. Movement and Mechanics The gunplay in A-Tech Cybernetic is Awesome, the only thing it lacks is haptic feedback for weapons when shot, which would definitely add the cherry on top and make it one of the best experiences on VR to date.The Movement in A-Tech Cybernetic is like other games that feature locomotion controls and teleportation. I use the teleportation when I get stuck in sticky situations with undead hoarding me from every angle, so in that respect it can save you big time. Some people get motion sickness from locomotion but I handle it perfectly, and the reality is that as of now, there isn’t a better way to go other than locomotion for an action game, especially FPS. GameplayOther than the movement and gameplay mechanics I wanted to talk a bit about what makes this game unique when picking up items. The “Superpower” system the game uses is a really great touch , as you can aim your controller at an object, highlight that object and it force pulls it straight to you like a Jedi. I don’t recall The superpowers being tied into the story a hell of a lot, but enough for it to make sense. Since A-Tech Cybernetic VR is Early Access, the more it develops im sure there will be more superpowers and explanation of story to back it up. The enemies in A-Tech Cybernetic VR are great, they are well animated with the 3D Model and textures to back them up, they look as good as anything from the killing floor series, which is one of the series that came to mind once I first played this game.As I said before, A-Tech Cybernetic VR is an Awesome First Person shooter and I definetely reccomend it for any FPS or Zombie Fan and anyone that seeks , Blood , Bullet hell carnage or any of the above points that I mentioned.

Where to begin with this game... so many failures to even be moderately entertaining    The gunplay is mediocre point-and shoot, nothing really to say there. Melee is just waggling your controller when they get close, but the WORST bit of gameplay is that the game has NO indicator for enemies being behind you, and thats unforgivable in a game that LOVES to spawn enemies behind you without telling you, which reminds me...   The level design is...bland, uninspired, primarily your standard Unreal Engine corridors full of easy targets, not the most egregious issue, but combing through near-identical rooms for hours makes it easy to get turned around. Levels can also get VERY dark, which helps one realize the flashlight ACTUALY DOES NOTHING. All of this isnt helped by the fact that the checkpoints are too sparse, making you do whole waves and sections over again because the game spawned enemies behind you without telling you, *again*, and more often than not, checkpoints are before ammo caches so you need to pick everything up AGAIN, and as well, those ammo caches are RANDOMIZED on EVERY POINT RELOAD.   The SFX are primarily stock sounds which I dont try to knock generally but if youve played Terraria for instance, youve heard just about every grunt the enemies will make.    The script is AWFUL. I am beyond done with "Snarky voice in your ears for the whole game" as a concept and this game is one of the worst offenders. The main VA does an okay enough job but the script he's reading is absolute cancer, to the point where I half expected him to drop some outdated l33tspeak. This goes for the tablets you can find too, half of them are all the same "Oh boy I hope I can see my newborn son and I hope NOTHING goes WRONG" message and the rest are detailing a very predictable plot that seems to equate roughly to "Doom '16, but ultra-bland" (could be wrong, but I also couldnt be bothered to see it through)When the game works as intended (and not suddenly crashing) its mediocre, and MAYBE worth a look with a heavy discount, but I unfortunately cannot recommend this game in good faith to ANYONE looking to have some VR funsies.

I'm writing this after my first time playing A-Tech Cybernetic VR and... well, I recommend it.You want more? You want to know why? You want me to stop asking rhetorical questions? Well, read on and at least you can have two of those things.You play [REDACTED] and the guy you're 'posessing' is a sarky scientist of many vices and functional hands. He even invites you to raise them and look at 'his' hands that you're using! The storyline is simple enough and it reminds me of the classic shooters of days gone by. Doom, Quake, Unreal and even Serious Sam. You run in, shoot everything that moves, reload and then shoot s'more!Look around for semi-hidden things, but above all prepare for a fight!Now, it's not perfect... But this feels like what VR ought to be! The movement can be teleport or traversal (my prefered method) and you can chose between snap-turn,  smooth-turn or no turning at all.The controls are simple. Grab/drop, Shoot, move, menu. That's it! It's so simple and so satisfying to have a game like this.There's melee combat if you grab a pipe (Found three varieties. A classic 'straight and narrow', a 'second hand but still good' and my favourite 'BUDGET LIGHT-SABRE THAT MAKES BIG OWIE HIT THINGS VERY MUCH WHEEEEE!'.) and it's surprising how satisfying the melee combat can be. A little short-range but ammo-saving.Of course, you want to know about the guns... oh the guns! Arizona Sunshine can't compare to this.The ease of gameplay, the satisfaction of a perfectly placed shotgun shell, the hard rock that comes on in the most intense moment I've played so far...Let me describe the scene...I fuel up the generator... The music starts and my heartrate goes from 'I'm a gamer, I live for this' to 'I'M PLAYING QUAKE 2 AND ALL THE ENEMIES ARE ON THEIR WAY!'. I grab the 'dark shotgun' from my belt, the 'Dark Rifle' from the other and a whole wall of enemies falls from the top of a cliff!There's got to be about twenty of them... well, that's fine because I've got enough ammo for all of you! Gunning them down, i hear the escillating sounds of incoming death from my right and I see... oh god, it's an arena made of of shipping crates. Shipping crates that arre full of these things!There's a bit of me that's saying "how can I survive this? They can shoot me, they're going to overwhelm me and I don't think I have enough Ammo for this, let alone health". But that's a very small bit of me because the rest of me is running towards them, grinning like a suicidal lunatic with all the bullets in the world and none of the self-preservation instincts known to man!.The fight is gruelling. I have to take cover when my one gun clicks empty and instead of bothering to reload it, I throw it hard over the horde approaching and grab the weapon from my other hip. Now dual wielding machineguns, I mow through the horde with short controlled bursts of hardcore adrenaline-surging precision as the music stands in for my common sense and I reload both fifty-round clips to take out the next wave.My one gun clicks empty and I know I don't have enough to reload both of these, so I throw that one far away, reaching out and grabbing my discarded shotgun, reloading it for good measure as I use the machinegun at arms-length while mowing down legless monstrosities that want me dead.A moment of peace. A moment of calm... Long enough to reload, to grab some ammo from the ground. Enough to keep my machinegun going for... Footsteps of something much bigger than me interrupt my momentary reprieve...These things are big, tough and half of them is bulletproof... Well COME ON THEN!I grab a grenade, hit the detonator and throw it hard (something that I'm far to proud to be able to manage) and it lands close enough. Big boy is surrounded in the explosion as I unload my machinegun at it's gut while it shields it's face.I drop another grenade at my own feet as the beast charges and I backpedal.The explosion sends the horror off it's feet!Just in time for the gates to open and what must be the final horde lurches towards me.Nothing smart. Barely anything more than the standard enemy but lots of them... My machinegun clicks empty. No more ammo!Fine! I throw it and swap out for my pistol (trusty sidearm!) and firing shotgun and pistol at zero range enemies, I finally emerge...Bloodied... bruised... but alive!Of course, later, i would find that I had knocked my lamp over and nearly decapitated my candle-holder... but hot D*MN was it worth it!I highly recommend this game. It's simple and it may not win any awards for most original storyline, but the person you're possessing is quite fun to hear and the voice-actor deserves some kind of award for it!There are few places this could be improved and I seriously hope the company behind this (Yeah, you awesome dudes in the credits) keep up the good work and make more of this vein.

Remember that time we all hoped for Doom to have a cool VR version, and how much fun it could be to play? Then VFR came out and explosively deflated that bubble? Well, A Tech might be the game that will make up for the letdown we got from Doom VFR. For one, even in its EA state, this game actually already does "do Doom in VR" the way it should have been.Setting up for room scale was painless. All the basic mechanics are done right. You're not stuck with one or another locomotion method, you've got options (free rotation, free loco, teleport, snap rotation, etc) and you've got helpful features (force pull, snap to holster, augmented throwing force) that will make any player able to get going even in the most limited of spaces and arrangements, all without the worry of wrecking a controller or anything in your real environment.The game itself delivers a good pace of storytelling and combat, with an interesting variety of the kinds of guns you'll be familiar with from other action-horror first person shooters, and all of it will function well without any weirdness at the basics (for example the gun angle is correct in this game, unlike VFR who required an update 3 months in that made the game normal... and yet still managed to not quite pull off that simple basic)I've enjoyed a good hour and a half in A-Tech Cybernetic and while 95% of it was highly enjoyable, I do have a few pieces of criticisms to bring up. First let's mention the more pressing issues that can hinder gameplay:-This game has an issue with personal space. Enemies can end up tangling into your player collider, causing you to be unable to move. This doesn't happen too often, but when it does, it can take you out of it completely, and will most likely cause a player death, since when the enemy gets stuck "in you", you can't even see them to shoot back. There needs to be a delimitation where enemies simply can't enter into when it comes to the player rig to avoid this, with a sort of push-back.-Melee in VR is inherently clumsy 100% of the time, and this game isn't doing itself any favors with it. Prehaps the "whack the enemies with another dead enemy's limb" can stay as a fun gimmick, but melee is something I'd ditch altogether given its complicated nature, and the fact this game's shooting and archery is so utterly satisfying.A couple of less pressing issues I noticed:-Some elements like the effigies of intertwined dead specimens can really, really cause the framerate to chug. These need to be optimized because they do look good and give a nice "Doom" twist to the environment, along with a little spook when you first see them.-Enemies want to funnel far too much. There needs to be a bit more RNG to the packs in order to get some more varied behavior, hopefully a pattern that allows them to use more space within the game's spacious levels. This would likely force the player to move a lot more within the areas while fighting, which when I was given a chance to, felt utterly satisfying.-The voice acting is OK, in fact by moments kind of charming... but the tone is a bit too excited. I would suggest preserving the people performing the voices, but taking on a bit less of a radiophonic tone for the main narrator. Think blazé like the Arizona Sunshine VO, or maybe along the lines of Cave Johnson from Portal 2. The staff you've got is competent, it's just about adjusting that tone.That's my two cents for now. I really enjoyed my run through the game despite the stated issues. I'd recommend this to anyone, provided they're ready to forgive said issues. It really is, to me, something that makes up a lot for the lack of a proper VR version of Doom. For a more fair comparison, I'd slot this next to Dead Effect 2 VR, and I'd go as far as saying it already clobbers games like the VR edition Killing Floor.

My first impression of A-Tech Cybernetic. (Early Access)A narrative-driven full locomotion/teleportation shooter available on Steam VR for the Oculus Rift and HTC Vive.Great voice acting.Great asset/character design.Awesome graphics.Love the concept – trapped in the Antagonist’s head.The mild tongue-in-cheek humor brings balance to the scarier, more intense moments of the game.The “voice” assists with the current mission, directing the player in a humorous/aggressive manner.Navigate through a map, directed by a voice in my mind (or vice-versa, lol).Encounter a barrier of some sort, get directed by the “voice”, fight monsters on the path, encounter a terminal and enter a puzzle mini-game, then proceed down the route to the next barrier.Looting is a vaguely strong dynamic in the game, as ammo and life can be an issue.You must actively holster your weapons, and will lose your weapon if you drop it and walk away.You can directly pick up, or “force-grab” ammo, health, armor, and weapons.You drop these items into your waist and leg holsters.Combat involves melee and ranged – no scopes, sticking to iron-sights on the weapons.I encountered an iron pipe, crowbar, shotgun, pistol, machine-gun, grenade, and “dark” variants of a few weapons. Time slowed down twice during my gameplay, but both times were narrative driven, activated by the voice in my head. There is no way to directly slow down time. It would be nice to do this as a power, perhaps.You find yourself moving around a level, picking up ammo, finding and holstering appropriate weapons, and looking for keycards. The design on the key-cards is pretty cool.There are scary and intense moments as enemy numbers can get overwhelming, or the area can get pitch black. The sound of a door closing is the spookiest thing in the world.The game feels like a futuristic house-of-the-dead mixed with Doom.Features a Mission mode and “Swarm” (wave) mode.-------------------------------------------------Overall, I recommend this game - it has a great creepy vibe highlighted by the narration to balance things out. I love the graphics and the theme of the entire environment. A very visceral journey into the bowels of some un-godly facility. I look forward to updates as they come, as the game is still in Early Access. Can't wait to master this game!

A solid, and creepy, story based FPS that felt more Doom like than Doom in some parts. A-Tech Cybernetic starts you off with a Solid tutorial that runs down the basics of the game. Not much to say here. It did its job.Reloading mechanics were not as in depth as I was expecting however the combat was fairly arcadey. More Raw Data than Onward or H3vr. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, just some of the wording had my expectations set differently.A-Tech Cybernetic uses both Teleport and Trackpad locomotion. Teleport feels a bit more like a way to climb over obstacles than a standard locomotion option however I didn't try to play pure teleporter. I do like both options available at all times though as there are situations where a good teleport can be extremely convenient or life saving.Unfortunately waggling seems to be at least partially effective with melee weapons however the number of enemies and the number of ammo drops you get make this somewhat of a moot point. Also, while I can technically waggle and do damage, a full bodied swing carries a lot more force with it. Enoug to lift enemies off their feet and send them flying. So while you CAN do it, you're not really rewarded for it. This seems acceptable to me.The light play in spots was really well done and I would have liked to see more of this used. Dark tunnels and glowing eyes make for some creepy firefights.Overall the atmosphere of the game was very creepy and had me jumping at every closing door sound. Even managing to legitimately scare me when the teleporters showed up. I don't jump easily so props to the designer who placed that surprise there.I loved the voice acting and by that I mean I hated the guy stuck in my head. Which as far as I'm concerned is how you're supposed to feel about the guy so great job there.My biggest complaint/request is that: Holsters need haptic feedback to inform you that you've placed your weapon in the appropriate slot for holstering your weapon. Too many times did I drop my weapon to the floor when i thought I should have holstered it. A simple, on enter volume, vibrate for a half second line of code would go a huge way towards QoL improvement.I would have also liked to see a two handed grip for the rifle. Even if it didn't provide a benefit. It just feels better.While very well done, the chapters feel fairly short. The current story content is on the light side at the moment. You're buying into the promise of future free content updates. This has it's pros and cons and depends on your past experiences... You're going to get about an hour and a half to 2 hours give or take depending on how much you rush vs explore. I tend to explore more and want to see all the things. Someone who just wants to rush the game is going to probably be able to clock in around an hour or so. Thus is the risk and drama of EA.The swarm mode seems like it could be fun if they added a multiplayer component to it but I don't see myself spending a lot of time in there. I strongly prefer the story content.Ultimately I had a hell of a lot of fun with this game. I can't wait to explore the rest of this story. XReal Games. More please. Now.

A-Tech Cybernetic is a really nice VR FPS. The weapon handling is good, except for the missing recoil which makes the guns feel less "big". Melee is an option you always have (either using melee weapons or just your fists), but for the most part I just used guns. The locomotion system combines direct locomotion with teleporting allowing you to use both at the same time and it feels great. The only issue is that direct locomotion currently is always relative to your head, not to the controller. There are a few different enemies in A-Tech Cybernetic (I think I've encountered 5 different types of enemies) which is enough for the current 2 chapters, but for further chapters I'd hope for for diverse enemies.The story mode is nothing special, but still enjoyable, even though the voice acting is a bit too loud and quickly gets annoying. The levels are built mostly linearly with a few detours for finding the next keycard, but you're never wondering where to go next (also because the direction of your next goal is always visible).The biggest issue A-Tech Cybernetic currently has in my opinion is its inventory system. Each ammo pickup needs to be picked up and placed in your inventory manually and you have only two holsters available for the 4 different guns I've seen until now. Taking a shotgun, a rifle and a backup pistol with you just about works with two holsters and a hand, because you always need a free hand for picking up ammo and interacting with things. Dual-wielding the same gun is nearly impossible because there's not enough ammo to use only one weapon type and thus you need the inventory space for backup weapons. Melee weapons and grenades can't be holstered/stored in any way, so you're not going to be able to effectively take them very far when finding them.A-Tech Cybernetic is still in Early Access and it shows, but the developer is pretty active and the issues I've pointed out here are all currently being worked on. More chapters of the story are to come, but even right now for the current 2 chapters I feel like the 15€ pricetag is definitely reasonable.

Pros:+ Great looking environments and lighting. Dark corridors are actually nice and dark.Cons:-  You can be looking around and everything looks nice, but man enemies, wires, etc have extremely low framerates compared to your hands which makes it jarring.- The HUD just doesn't feel necessary. The environment/atmosphere is the strongest aspect of this game, please let me see it with less UI elements in the way.- Headshots are purely visual in this game, even if you blow an enemy's head clean off... you still have to shoot him ~5 more times in the chest to actually kill him. Its extremely unsatisfying, and with how many enemies in each room, its annoying having to follow up with a bunch of body shots.- The enemies don't make many sounds, so you can't really tell if there are some behind you etc. - Audio is pretty weak across the board, gun shots should just be louder in general.- Weapon holsters should be closer to your actual body, not floating in front of you. It causes you to grab your weapons or flashlight when you mean to open a drawer at your side, etc.- You should only be able to grab items with 1 button (grip buttons for vive wands). Currently triggers can inconsistently do things the grips can also do, and it makes you make a lot of mistakes.- There are too many items scattered around. It kinda hurts the atmosphere and immersion when there are just magazines, health canisters, etc ALL over the ground. I feel like I had infinite ammo (which unfortunately is needed since exploding headshots don't kill.)- Melee is floaty and light, needs a little meatier audio and haptic response.- If there is a dedicated flashlight holster on my chest... why can it take up my weapon holster slot? If I let go of the flashlight, just return it to its dedicated holster, otherwise I could potentially lose whatever weapon I was using. Thoughts:This is a really strange situation. From this review, it might look like I'm being super negative and that I hate this game. But oddly enough, I feel like there is a TON of potential here. Most of the issues I have mentioned are just adjustments to what already exists. The only bigger complaint I have is the choppy enemy animations, which might require a bit more work. I am not going to immediately uninstall this game, because I feel like maybe I can get past these things if the content gets better further into the story. Theres a lot thats done well here, but all of the small issues add up and just makes the game feel like it just needed an extra month of polish and tweaking. If this game was early access, I would recommend it, because these small quirks seem like things that would absolutely get addressed in "the next patch", etc. However, given that this game was $1 in the newest humble bundle, I assume that means this game will not be receiving any more support. Therefore unless my mind changes further into the story, I won't be recommending this game ESPECIALLY if it isn't in a $1 tier of a bundle.

Full release? Give me a break.Yes, first couple of chapters were pretty impressive for an early access game, and some issues were expected. But since it's a full release now, I won't close my eyes on those things:- Enemies popping up from air and having an ability to teleport into you- Enemies with guns sprinting into invisible walls and shooting you with perfect accuracy from great distances- Items falling through the floor- Visual glitches- Physical glitches, especially with bodies- Dark (scoped) rifle drops fps to single digits when you take it in your hand (issues with a scope, I guess)- Overall unpolished and poorly made late game levelsI decided that I've had enough of this on the level, where you need to go through a series of portals to reach your goal, but there are always more than one portal on your way, and if you choose the wrong one you're sent back to the beginning and every single enemy will respawn.  Earlier on the same level there was a door that played Willheim scream when you approach it. Every. Single. Time. And giant boulders which instakilled you if you're not psychic and can predict them appearing behind you.Even if all the issues were fixed (and I really doubt they will be), it would still be a pretty average game with cringy dialogues, uninteresting story and very questionable game design. Take note that developers now work on another VR shooter Zero Caliber, which is also in early access and pretty fun, but unpolished, especially in terms of physical glitches and AI. I wanna be optimistic, but A-Tech Cybernetic is a great example of early access game that wasn't actually finished, and it's hard for me to trust XREAL Games now.

Giving a red thumb is harsh. This   has its nice sequences, its nice gunfights, and I'd like to generally encourage developers to provide games for virtual reality players. The problem is, even for the standards of VR shooters,  is fairly average in many aspects.First of all, for the standards of 2020,  is graphically poor. Some textures, especially from nearby, look like a messy pixel soup. Assets are not very detailed and the animations are very basic. You'd then think that it should run flawlessly on a strong PC build ? Forget about it, the optimisation is just as bad. RTX 3080/HP Reverb G2 here (yeah that's a lot of pixels to compute, I know), and despite the overall poorness of the graphics, I had to downgrade the Steam supersampling to 50% to have the thing running at a constant 90 fps.Gameplay-wise, I must say I had some good things shooting down zombies. Nothing fancy or original there but having one gun in each hand feels good and the game gives good shooting sensations. Close combat is however buggy: there is no hand motion smoothing algorithm in the programming of the game I'd guess, because a little (but sudden and fast) rotation of your wrist can result in sending a zombie flying over several tens of metres. If you wanna have a good laugh, place yourself in a corner of the hub room of chapter one, and see if you can homerun zombies to the opposite corner (on the ceiling !).Yeah, bugs, let's talk about them. They are everywhere, all the time, and yet another hint that the game was developed by a modest team (and I don't mean this in a bad way at all). Enemies stuck in walls, enemies not realising your presence, invisible walls for the players, music suddenly disappearing (although this might also be related to the G2...), the completely inaccurate throwing of grenades, dialogues triggering too early... I even had a bug in chapter 6 that prevented me from going down the whole to the cave, I had to reload my progression from the checkpoint. Because yes, you read me well, this game's progression relies on fixed checkpoints placed every now and then in each chapter. No possibility to save your progression manually whatsoever.Being quite motion-sick, I appreciated the possibility to teleport all the time. That being said, one thing with the teleportation annoyed me very much: the direction you're looking towards at the end of the teleportation is determined by how you tilt the wrist of the hand you use to teleport. I found this extremely incommodious, as teleporting is usually something you want to do fast, and you don't spend time tilting your wrist precisely before doing so. I would have found much more intuitive and comfortable to just face the same direction after the teleport than before it.The second half of the game was certainly better than the first half: the first three chapters look like they are all the same, with the same corridors, the same rooms and the same enemies all the time. The endgame was disappointing though. Finally, I also tried the swarm mode, which could have been a good idea if the games had been shorter. Standing so long ends up being a little painful; the initial few waves are too weak and the build-up towards more intensive fights is too long.In summary: not a very bad game, but still an average game probably from a modest team.  is really too lackluster to get your attention in the middle of all the VR shooters available on the market.

I am just beginning with the game so this is something like a first impression, not a knowledgeable evaluation. There are definitely some in game mechanics that I haven discovered yet and I have experienced only the very beginning of the game (or at least I hope so :))Imagine Doom 3 in VR and you get this title. This is exactly the kind of game I have alvays expected from VR. And what I especially like about it is how well is everything though out.Motion: You can choose between teleportation and locomotion and both you can set up to your liking. Even if I am very prone to motion sickness I can use locomotion without any problem in this game. I just set the turning to 45 deg steps, because smooth turning nauseates me instantly. Forward and backward movement and strafing is ok for meGunplay and controls: Again this is well executed, handling both guns and other objects feels natural and I instantly fell in love with the posibility to pick objects from a distance. You are equipped with two weapon holsters and a harness for flashlight and grenades. Reloading or arming a grenade doesn't try to be realistic like in some other VR titles, but I thing that the simplicity fits this game. Thu gun handling is well executed, only sometimes I put the gun into a ground instead of holstering itGraphics: It reminds me strongly the first levels of Doom 3 - corridors, sliding doors, vent shafts, airlocks, all filled with dead and undead. I think that it does it job well without burning your graphic card. You have three levels of graphic quality and three levels of antialiasibng tochoose from. All settings are applied instantly, so you can easily choose what fits your setup.  It sems to me that even the best quality is something that avarage VR PC can handle without any lags or issues.My only gripe with graphic is, that each type of enemy seems to have only one model, which does not feel right especually in bigger groups. Adding at least more skins would improve hordes a lot Sound: Sliding doors, pressurized air, gunshots explosions etc. - some gunshot sounds might be imptoved but overal a very good job againIssues: So far I came only across one big issue and that is too small joystick deadzone for trigerring the footstep sound. I can stand still and still I hear my footsteps. I have to carefully position the joystick to the very center to silence them. It made the first few rooms really scary for me, before I realized that the footsteps I hear are my own. So at first it was scary, but later it is just extremely annoyingOveral this title is - at least for me - something like a benchmark game. Motion and object handling are well executed and I expect at least this level of quality from any future VR title. And if you are a fan of Doom series or titles like Dead Effect or Killing Floor, this is a must have.

I do not get why more people are not talking about this - for an early access game, this is a really polished title and a hell of a lot of fun to play. It takes me right back to the excitement I had first playing Doom - only now - here I am *actually* in there. The flow of the game is spot on (at least for me) - bouts of intense fighting and moments where a group of the dead just jump out at you, interspersed with slower paced exploration (but exploration where you are constantly anticipating the next attack). The game is full motion exploration and the sense of immersion is fantastic, what a change from the countless stream of copycat wave-shooters.I simply do not get the negative comments here - I think when a group of devs put so much effort and work to bring us a quality experience, as a community we should support them both financially, and in *constructive* criticism. The result of not doing so in a very fragile and unprofitable part of the industry should be clear to everyone. If we want quality titles to be developed, we should support them. This is one of the many titles that I found entirely by chance that have rewarded me with many hours of immersive game play and  given my a truly fantastic experience. So good luck to the devs and thanks for providing the community with a solid game with high quality graphics. I cannot wait to see what they bring up next, as the game is totally playable as it stands.

A-Tech is one of those games that always had a few things missing but the dev team has been so attentive to the community enjoying it that I can now unequivocally say that this is the VR game I'll be playing in lieu of DOOM VFR. It's polished for an Early Access game, let alone a VR Early Access game, and the one level of shine that was missing for me was the audio - I'm happy to say that with the latest update as of 2/16/18, the audio is MUCH, MUCH better and on-par with what you'd normally consider a finished product (though I'm sure the dev team will continue to make changes and continue to refine the game).I have to point out that the physics in this game with regard to melee is the best I've seen it done in VR. For some reason it doesn't carrying the very flimsy sort of physical interaction you'd find in most VR games with melee and it makes melee extremely satisfying. The graphical quality of the game should also be mentioned - It's brilliant. Really, you wouldn't expect an Early Access title to so consistently uphold the visual quality on display herebut it does. Even the new Intro level/Menu level is brilliantly stylized and pretty awe-inspiring at the right SS level.I implore anyone looking for a good full-locomotion FPS with melee (or anyone burnt by DOOM VFR) to consider investing in this budding piece of tech - if it's this quality now, I can't wait to see how it turns out when it's done. I'd also implore anyone who wants to support intuitive and community-focussed devs to consider a purchase too - A-Tech is a gem and it's only gonna get shinier.

Might *look* good, but not a very good game.The story is pretty generic; mad scientist, space station, Not!Zombies cyborg things, a lot of dated references scattered throughout the random documents and dialogues in the game. Environments are creepy sci-fi base generic as well, though the textures are pretty nice and the enemies look interesting. The gameplay has... issues. You've got a few different kinds of firearms and some assorted melee weapons. The game only gives you 2 weapon holsters, but a good feature is that at any time you can hold out your empty hand and activate a weapon wheel to spawn that item to your holster. I greatly appreciate that, as it always allowed me to have a weapon with ammo on hand and not worry so much about trying to tote around specific weapons to maximize efficiency. The melee weapons are random pipes, crowbars, glowing pipes, wrenches, stuff like that. You hit the bad man and they usually go flying like Super Smash Brothers, then get back up and you have to hit them again. First issue is that when they're knocked to the ground, they are invincible until they perform their getting up animation, which is tedious as hell. Let me just club the damn things while they're down so I don't have to wait, because I've got other enemies coming along and would like to take care of this one quickly instead of politely letting it dust itself off so I can brain it. Another thing; all the melee weapons operate exactly the same, and I think even have similar hitboxes despite being quite different in size. So it's like, why bother with different ones? Plus, they're hardly satisfying to use. Barely any rumble to let you feel like the swing had impact and they're light as a feather, no weight at all. You can only hit one enemy per swing, so no wide sweeps to stop a mob surrounding you. A glaring problem in the item wheel is that while each gun has its own slot, melee weapons only have 1 slot. The game will let you spawn the last melee weapon you picked up, which for SOME reason includes Flashlights as a melee weapon. Flashlights are pretty essential for certain game sections, and melee weapons never stop being effective unless you face the big burly enemies that are immune to being clubbed around. But Flashlights themselves do practically nothing for melee damage. So if I dropped my melee weapon to go down a dark tunnel and shoot some guys with my light, then I'm SOL afterwards unless the game decides to leave a pipe in the next room. Why wasn't the flashlight just made its own slot in the wheel? You can pick them up in the world, but you have a specific holster on your chest exclusively for the flashlight. Why not just have it return there?That leads me to the next problem; weapon holsters. One on each side at the waist, one for the flashlight, and three grenade slots above it. These holsters are crap. I can't tell you how many times I tried to holster a weapon while on the move from an encroaching horde only to reach for it a moment later and find an empty holster. Having the weapon wheel spawn stuff somewhat mitigates this, but you don't need that kind of sudden twist in the middle of a mob of enemies. Always be checking to make sure you put the weapon away properly. This goes double for the melee weapons for the above mentioned reasons. Along with that is constantly grabbing a grenade or flashlight when I'm trying to pick up random things off the ground. I don't even know why it constantly makes me grab those, but it leaves me ditching the grenades just so I don't keep grabbing them by accident. Seriously, the holster detection is crap. I saw in the forums somebody mentioned that the sniper rifle caused their frames to drop to single digits and basically freeze the game for as long as they held it, and yeah same thing happened to me. My best guess is that whoever coded the scope on the gun didn't know what they were doing and it causes massive performance issues.The terrain also has this constant issue of tunneling molerats. That's the best explanation I could come up with to explain the fact that you'll be walking along and the terrain will visibly shift right in front of you. Dirt will rise a foot or two, settle down, crawl up a wall, you name it. If there was some kind of tunneling enemy in the game, this would be an excellent way to keep the player paranoid for an attack of some kind. Alas, it's just crappy level programming.Aside from molerats, the movement in this game also has a politely hostile relationship with the terrain. The movement just feels wrong and janky, not helped by the fact that you have to hit buttons to rotate instead of flicking the analog stick to the side. Some later areas like in this lava cave and the surface have an annoying tendency to light you on fire and kill you for wandering too close to a puddle of lava without even touching it. In fact, your entire hitbox feels much too wide for your body. Enemies will swipe at you from annoyingly long distances and still manage to do damage.The thing that made me stop and write this review was where I was on the Surface, which is basically its own chapter. I made my way through, la dee da, die a few times and respawn at checkpoints, nothing major. Then, I get to this massive enemy rush where I need to push through to get to a huge gate, and deliver a fuel can... somewhere? I couldn't find the generator I needed to drop this fuel can in to progress. No idea if the enemies were respawning because they popped in all around me and I was just trying to survive. Unfortunately, I got surrounded and died because if you get surrounded you're pretty much done. So I hit the reload at checkpoint which was right before this mob section... and found myself at the beginning of the level. There's no "restart level" on the death screen, only checkpoint and main menu. I decided ♥♥♥♥ that, quit, and uninstalled the game.This game was in early access for a while, and comes out with this many issues? Save your money. There's plenty of good VR games with gunplay and melee, find something better.
