your experience with this game will depend ENTIRELY on how much you educate yourself before getting into itof my 113 hours, i probably could have saved 20-30 hours, maybe more, if i had known what i know now. the most *painful* parts of the game's early-mid game grind can be skipped almost entirely because so many main quests and side quests reward gear. and not just "meh" gear. like REALLY good gear. and once you get that gear, it puts you into a higher matchmaking bracket with people of similar gear. meaning when you go *back* to those older areas, it's *easier* to grind because there's so many less players there. because most of them are grinding farther north. it really is a shame that stalcraft's grind goes from tedious, to easy from early game to mid game into early late game. upon completing the main quest the player is awarded with a piece of "Veteran-ranked" armor. when you receive this armor, it instantly awards you the "reliable gear" achievement. an achievement for owning a "veteran-ranked" armor piece. only 2.6% of people who have played stalcraft, have this achievement. that's how few players actually finish the main quest. this game is pretty fun IMO. PVP is great with the homies. gear progression is rewarding and meaningful. if you educate yourself to avoid the painful early grind areas, you will have a much more enjoyable experience.i made two videos to help new players. both of these videos are basically "things i wish i knew before playing stalcraft" videos. i'm not trying to become a youtuber. i'm just trying to help people enjoy a good game. - watch first - watch secondedit: also, apparently the russian version of the game, which is ahead of the steam version in terms of updates, has some "pay 2 win" components. the current iteration of the game on steam is NOT pay 2 win. you can buy premium which has some slight benefits, with real money. but you can also buy premium with in game currency and it is quite cheap to buy premium with in game currency (as of writing this review). regardless, playing now or soon(ish) would be in your best interest just in case they turn the game into a pay 2 win hellscape in 6 months or something. hopefully that doesn't happen.2nd edit: devs responded to a post regarding monetization here:  some pretty hopeful stuff said, no promises though. at least they approached the topic. guess we'll see what the future holds.

I usually dislike PvP games and this one is no different regardless of how much i want to like the game.however the real reasons why i dislike this game are due to frustrating bugs and issues that could and should have been solved before its initial release let alone the international one. I will state a list of issues i have experienced with the game ranging from bugs to balance problems before later on explaining why they are problems and not simply "gameplay design choices".Problems:Getting killed in a safe zone by both players and NPCs alikePoor visibility of anomalies leading to constant death or injury beyond your controlConstant loss of materials in stupid ways causing waste of time and loss of progressLost Backpacks are a stupid idea and should be done away with or heavily modifiedPoor balance and overtuned NPCs making combat feel unfair and unfunLack of respawn locations making reclaiming lost items annoying at best and frustrating at worst-Elaboration-Safe zone Deaths:normally in games like this safe zones disable damage to the player and disable their ability to attack so that griefing them while they shop is impossible however this is not the case in this game, if you find yourself outside the safe zone you can just fire into it and kill people, i know this is possible as it happened to me by both a player and an NPC at different instances with one such location being in the starting area of the Swamps where one meets Shaman because for some reason there is a spawn point for NPC enemies just outside of it. this needs to be fixed immediately as this type of griefing will only become more popular.Poor Visibility of Hazards:While i understand they want you to feel as though you "have to watch your every step carefully" this ends up just being frustrating if not impossible due to the NPCs that can spot you like a hawk from miles away and take your head off before you even see them. add to this is the looming threat of other players who can steal your loot and you quickly understand why running quickly is often the only option and running quickly makes the already hard-to-spot anomalies next to impossible to see. to my understanding there was another way of detecting anomalies in the STALKER games which is not present here, perhaps that should change.Loss of Materials:In order to get better gear or upgrade the things you already have you have to gather materials, in doing so you will likely encounter the anomalies or other players which can claim said materials. i understand the desire to add a "Risk/Reward" system but dropping all of your materials when you die to something stupid like getting caught in a barely visible anomaly, stepping on a landmine during a gun battle or get shot in the back by a player you had no way of knowing was there is not fun its frustrating. this is not helped by the fact that most if not all of said materials are locked into a "lost backpack" for other players making PvP feel unrewarding. as of 6 hours of playtime in this game i have had the luxury of buying exactly ONE new weapon which was an uzi and a red dot sight, an incredibly minor upgrade from my starting SMG.Lost Backpacks:This idea would be a good one if you had a choice between opening the backpack for the goods inside or ransoming/auctioning it off to other players, as of now i have yet to see anything else to do with them other than ransoming them back to the player you got them off of and most people will not engage with this, as well as the most you could get is some money which is already really easy to come by without fighting other players. it seems as though the only point of them is to rob PvPers of their reason to fight other players.Poor balance and Overtuned NPCs:during the earliest phase of the game me and a friend were on a quest to find a killer who had fled camp and when we went to his location we came under fire, not by enemy players but by a random set of NPCs which downed us both before we knew they existed. after running back to get our stuff they once again opened fire leaving my friend who had purchased a rifle to take them out as i could not even see them with clear line of sight let alone be able to engage due to only having the starter SMG and them being beyond my range, after dying a second time i was told i died to a standard M16 and at that moment i knew the enemies were just aimbots with better gear than we would be able to afford for some time, 6 hours later and this has only proven more true.Respawn and shop locations:you can only buy certain gear at certain locations and you have to upgrade most of your gear into better variants so if you move to a new camp and decide you want a certain item you may find yourself needing to go back to a previous area to get an item to exchange it. this happened to me and as i tried to run back to the starting area i ran into multiple frustrating deaths causing me to run down the same road 5 times each time with only one magazine in each gun. once i had reached the starter area i was in a safe zone where you meet Shaman as an Emission(dangerous storm) started i took shelter there and upon exiting i was gunned down, not by a player who was camping but by an NPC group who had spawned during the emission, when i respawned it put me back where i had started at the second camp with no ammo forcing me to run all the way back to the starting area again. the solution in my eyes is to allow us to choose from some respawn locations when we die and make it take longer to respawn depending on distance and restrict respawning to only the local area.

At the time of writing, I have played this game for 416 hours, and am quite passionate about it. Why then, might my review be a negative one? It is and will stay a "do not recommend" until the glaring problems are addressed, since the game could be so much better than it currently is with a couple small fixes. The developers of the game boast this game to be a loot-based PVP game - and to a great extent, it is. Their intention is for the game to invoke emotions from the player, ie. when you are trying to get to safety with some very valuable loot and do not want to lose it to enemy players during PVP. Or the opposite, when you are excited to have claimed some valuable loot by means of killing an enemy player and looting their items. These are scenarios which definitely exist in the game, boast player-interaction via "emotional responses", and are generally what this game (in my opinion) should be all about. If you lose items by getting killed in pvp, then gear up, improve your aim, and kill the enemy player back to get his items instead. What is not fun is when you as the player, are inhibited from having any option to do the previously mentioned. When you lose your loot to something unpreventable or unexpected, such as game performance issues or simply making a mistake when fighting PVE monsters in the zone, and then instead of an enemy player taking your things, your own faction members do. The difference here being that you simply cannot interact with your faction members. They are free to steal your items with no repercussions whatsoever. This is something that I see actively complained about in game and on the communities, and it is so easy to fix as well. Just remove this interaction as it is not something that makes people want to play more, but rather less. Imagine having real life responsibilities, then setting aside some time to play this game, but then the play session is completely wasted as you feel essentially "helpless" in this scenario. You've lost all your progress, and there was nothing you could do about it. That is not a "emotion" that would make the game more enjoyable rather than less. There are easy fixes to this problem:1. add a grace period of friendly (allied) looting, or disable it completely2. remove factions so that the entire game is just a free-for-all pvp scenario. In this case, there is no distinguishing between friend/foe and so anyone SHOULD be able to loot your items on death.3. improve the performance of the game so that unfair scenarios do not lead to deathsThis list could go on and on. It is not difficult to come up with a solution to this problem.

The challenge comes solely from the probability of you getting killed without a chance to fight back going to or from the objective.Oh yeah, and you drop everything but your weapons and armor when you die. Finally got that rare material you spent an hour to get? Well  just domed you with a sniper rifle, so you're dead without bleedout which prevents teammates (if you even have any) from reviving you. This type of gameplay does not in any way encourage going out and exploring the world, it encourages a sedentary playstyle of camping on an angle, waiting for players to pass by, shooting them dead and looting their corpses, and rinse and repeat, or to put it simply; playing like a rat.I'd've been fine if I could  footsteps if they were flanking me but the developers thought it fine to make footstep sounds as subtle as humanly possible, there's also no flash or any indication whatsoever for when an enemy's scoped in with a sniper rifle, so if you're in their crosshair - chances are you're dead or very dead.TL;DR - Absolutely amazing realization of the stalker world in a voxel-based game, both visually and atmospherically, but is however marred by just a downright horrendous, forced PvP setting coupled with a small maps that almost guarantee you'll face players a minute of leaving safezones.

As you can see, I easily dumped 8 hours into Stalcraft, and I plan to dump more. Stalcraft is an independent take on the S.T.A.L.K.E.R series which turns it into a segmented MMO-RPG-FPS and a more limited player loot system.Graphics - Stalcraft, as per its namesake, easily reminds you of both Minecraft and STALKER and is, as a result, surprisingly light on resources despite the details available. However, if you're running older hardware, prepare for some hiccups if you don't have this game on an SSD.Gameplay - Starting with the gunplay, the gunplay in question is more realistic than most FPS titles like you'd expect, but don't expect jamming, ammo blowups, etc. as it's more simplified take to keep the game flowing. However, weapon durability can be a problem if you're out there shooting for extensive periods of time. HP and stamina (anything but walking and climbing) regen follows an exponential pattern, so don't expect to heal quickly if you're wounded bad or to get your breath back in time for the umpteenth bandit unless you use a medkit or eat food, which assists in that endeavor.Armor is simple enough: it's a plate of armor that you slip into your current clothing to prevent damage from body shots. However, a good gunfighter aims for the head and that's where the armor doesn't protect you. Once it expires, the armor is just plain gone and now your torso's exposed.I mentioned a limited player loot system. I'll explain. Items that are locked to you or are explicitly protected from looting will not be shown to others who are looking to take your stuff. As far as I can tell, non-default clothing, medium arms, medium ammo and anything outside of their packs otherwise are fair game, with the exception of weapons and munitions you get from quests.Presentation - The story presented mostly follows the story beats of the STALKER series, but introduces the Blessed, those who have had wild dreams of a blue sphere and feel a calling to enter the Zone and receive the wisdom of the original explorers. Not all is well however as some go crazy and attack their own and others think the whole thing's stupid and join the Orderlies who hunt down the Blessed. You can play as a Stalker or Bandit, the two sides having side factions and different outposts available to them, as well as different unique weapons belonging to their respective side factions. You can also team up with other players to tackle harder content as a group.Pros - A good STALKER spinoff that will introduce you to the lethal shenanigans of the Zone.Cons - Dying with non-locked ammo on you would leave you SOL after respawn unless you're in a story-specific location. Keep most of your ammo in the packs you can get and you're set.

Stalcraft takes inspiration from "S.T.A.L.K.E.R" series, anyone who played or watched it already knows what to expect here.Game offers both PvP & PvE activities but gameplay wise it revolves around PvE while forcing you into PvP, which really is a shame. Map of Stalcraft is huge and while both Stalkers & Bandits have their own dedicated zones to farm resources and do quest there are shared zones such as Scrapyard & The Bar where both factions clash. Once you're done with the main story line you have an option to join one of the 4 subfactions (2 for both Stalkers and Bandits) after which you gain access to brand new maps and more PvP activities (Faction wars).Like I said earlier game revolves around PvE, you get better gear, crafting materials, sellable loot and do quests (They are really well voiced and even side quests provide you with lots of lore) through PvE, other than walk into the enemy zone to talk to NPC game doesn't have any quests that require you to interact/kill with opposite faction players. Now into the PvP, whenever you kill a player his consumables, ammo and sellable loot is up for grabs but the items used to craft gear can either be thrown away or sold at auction, materials used to craft gear  by you which puts PvP in weird place where To cut a long story short, Stalcraft can provide you with great single player experience only to put you off with it's mandatory PvP.

It's a F2P game with an actually pretty decent core gameplay. The gunplay is decent (surprising considering it was once a minecraft mod) but there are unfortunately many big negative points, which mostly die down to two mechanics (forced PvP centered around stopping other players' progress, few spawns)- you drop things on death. Not your guns or armour, but every bit of resource you've collected. Nobody else can loot it, it's just... there. You might get lucky and whoever killed you sends it through the mail, or auctions it so you can buy it with in-game currency. But 99% of the time, that "dropped loot" is just deleted instead because the mechanism to send it is undocumented and unrewarding.- There's PVP, and it... exists. Due to the above, there's no looting anything of value. There isn't a leaderboard of "competive PvP". There's no territory to conquer for recognition or mechanical benefit. there's no leaderboard, there's no territory to conquer. Basically it only really exists for the players that enjoy the idea of griefing others and removing their progress.- there is a lot of kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things that kill you. One of the most common anomalies can just kill you with nothing to do about it (vortex) - you'd think you can run out of it but it will sometimes just randomly set your movement speed to 0 as soon as you touch it, then kill you slowly. There's radiation, which kills you, and the only warning mechanic is a geiger counter that stays silent until pretty much after you've already got a lethal dosage. Some of the areas with radiation are big and "obvious", but there's also areas where the map just randomly has radiation by a ton once you pass an invisible wall, no warning. And then there's "more dangerous" anomalies like the black hole that also basically just suck you in with nothing to do about it and kill you, but then they also delete your "dropped loot" so it gets destroyed even without another player interacting with it.- there are a whole 3 spawnpoints in the game, as far as i can tell, the first being the starter zone and useful ONLY for the starter zone. The second is right after the starting zone. Then... well a big effin' map. If you die, you will always be spending the next 3-5+ minutes just... running to get back to where you were. Couple with the above two that make sure you die all the time, the vast majority of the game is just running through the same terrain. - NPC enemy variety is very shallow. The original stalker games had a lot of enemy variation. In the 18 hours i've played, i've encountered rats (which run at you and bit you), dogs (which run at you and bite you), malformed pigs and boards (which run up and... stomp you) and people, who mostly stand still and shoot you, in a few variations (most of which are fair, but one of which is basically going to aimbot one shot you as soon as there's line of sight). Basically, there's only really two enemy types, and the more interesting one is fairly rare all things considered.- resources are grindy and -far- too rare. It's not too bad (though sort of repetitive) until you get to the point of needing aluminum (so shortly after going "past" the immediate surrounding of the second spawn). Then you need to use a ... metal detector. Problem is where it works is very specific areas and spawns are horribly low and shared in the world, so you'll go spend 1-3 hours trying to get the required material and you might get 10 out of the 25-30 you need for a single item (hundreds for full progression to the next stage). Coupled with the first point about dropping inventory... yeah, you're just not able to progress. I'm sure there's going to be some "loot boosters" in the cash shop, if there aren't already.- in part due to the resource point above, progression is basically nonexistant. I've played 18 hours, the past 10 or so i've been right at and around the second spawnpoint, because i can't go anywhere else. The main questline "should" help you gear but is impossible because it shoves you into PvP central, hard to even get to and when you're there you'll probably die long before achieving part of the quest.So many things in the game act as a stick to thwack the player, so little actually rewards anything. The only thing you can get reliably in the game is the currency, rubles, which is about as useful as IRL russian rubles at day of writing. You can buy some bullets and med packs if you run out, but not any gear. I gave it a fair shot all things considered, hoping i was just unlucky. But it's not luck, the progression and PvP mechanics just absolutely suck the fun out of what could be a great game.EDIT to reply to developer response: I'm well aware of where the NPC is for getting more gear, it's just that the resources required are essentially unobtainable. The loot of another player seems entirely meaningless to me, since the resources you can't use and currency is basically worthless. Artifacts, there might be good ones later in the game but at the point where i got to, every single artifact had massive downsides that rendered it a way to make yourself weaker rather than stronger.I did also try the discord, and... well it required entering an actual phone number. First and only time i've had that prompt. Supposedly "not shared with the community" but i have no intention of giving private IRL info online for vague reasons.
In general, it’s good for a free game, monetization does not bite, there were sets with equipment for donat currency, but they were removed
For the free price tag its an experience worth giving a little bit of time too.

Stalcraft is a pleasure for your eyes if you like the Minecraft-style, and a nightmare for the gameplay like Tarkov. That being said let's dive deep in the game.It starts quite good with a tutorial that allows you to try a lot of powerful weapon, just for the pleasure to do so, because with not enough NPC to try them on, you would be tempted to create countless characters just to repeat the tutorial and try all the weapons. Because choosing what weapon researching from the tree would be like picking chocolates out of a box. Like Forrest Gump teaches us.When you start your journey keep in mind that you are playing a PvEvP game, (for who doesn't know it means that you have to gather resouces out in the wild and compete with enemies and cooperate with allies).This is very important because at very beginning players will be on the same (or slightly over) level, gear and weapon, meaning that is possible to pull out a fair fight in every corner. Starting to Cordon things are going sideways.The more you get close to the center and north of the map, the more fights can be unbalanced, unfair, with possibilities (some days very high, especially during weekends in EU servers) of CHEATERs. ---------> SO BEWARE!!But that is the the top of the iceberg. The game is very nice, the story keeps you glued to the screen, and you want to discover how things will continue. But to move in different regions of the map is strongly raccommended to complete  the majority of the side quest that you can find in the region you are about to leave. This side quests can give you some sweet gear and some sweet modded weapons that would require a lot of time to farm. Not to mention that they may do the difference is some occasions. ---------->SO KEEP EYES OPEN FOR QUEST GIVERS.Now the "fun" part. THE GRINDING. It is a very important part of the game and will take a lot of time to gather what you need for crafting. It is fun to discover little by little all the grinding/farming mechanics, but not so much when "ENDGAME" players takes advantages on low tier players. This can be way more than frustrating and demoralise a lot of new players. You need to keep this in mind when playing.Some days you will be so lucky to find humongous loots and mountains of artifacts, the day after you will die straight to the entrance of your base, with your backpack full of resources, because an opposing players, doesn't want you to level up, or because it is easier for him/her to farm in that way. Not to mention players camping in farming areas just for the fun of killing, not even caring about your loot. This said cheaters will be always present, after some experience you will be able to spot them after the first kill. Usually this kill can be made when you are in covered areas and the chaeter is seeing you even if not supposed to. They will have weapons crafted only at the very end of the game, but on their play time you will see that things are sus. Low hours, high tier guns, huge amount of kills.AIMOBOTTING is the classic one. And of course the one tha gives you all the advantages you need. People are also doing giveaways fot them.---------- > So despite what EXBO says, there is no "real" enforced policy on cheater, they will always pop-up like pimples on a teenager face, new name, new account, same cheats.Some cheaters are smart and kill only in open field, but always check they're gear.There is no gaming manual, so I suggest to watch a lot of videos on internet about how to start and what mechanics you need to know to play properly. On this side the manual on player's PDA is just fresh water on an erupting volcano of game mechanics.Must be mentioned the EXBO devs attitude. Fixing problems is always an issues, meaning that if you don't make it properly you will inflated the problems and it will cause more problems.Weapons in this game is one of them. Unbalanced and never fixed. Ever after some nerfs some weapons are still OP just because of their classification, and yes I'm speaking about the AS Val and VSS Vintorez. But more are on the list.Last problem, like cherry on the cake, are the bosses you encounter during the story. Some of them are very well done, mechanics scripted properly and ways for beating them very acceptable. Some others are still crap, and the fixes are adding more crap to them. Minstrel is one of them. One month ago, by the time of this review, beating the monster would mean to glitch it in a corner and dump lead, or running like and headless chicken, turn and shoot for long time. Watching videos of tecniques for beating it one month old, and playing it now, will make you shiver on the fixes made by the devs. Increase speed, bigger hit ares for the monsters. So ,practically, the monster got a buff and the player a salty pickle in the bottom jar.Do not care about people that say "If you cannot beat a monster stop play the game, don't complain if you are not good enogh. If you are trash do not come here and complain". Some players are experienced and can spot when a script has been made just by passing the keybord on the ass.As of today EXBO announces three month of constant updates so, MAYBE, something will change. Or maybe it will be just fog, but it is a fact that the player base is reduced to a half of what was before. In the end, I would recommend this game only if you have  lot of patiance and self control. AND IF YOU HAVE A BS TOLLERANCELEVEL SET ON VERY HIGH. So after cooling off I decided to edit my review to be more constructive and less angry rambling after dying to a vortex an hour into farming.  This game has amazing bones, the ideas and art style are fantastic and I hope to see them improved on in the future.  This being a free game the premium options given do make quite a difference and do not give premium players too much of an edge, personally I got the month subscription of premium and enjoy it very much.  This game does need however more safe zones deep into the end game territories.  I understand it is meant to be difficult and that is fine, mission accomplished but dying to vortexes or bio zones after farming for an hour and killing countless players feels so bad.  There have to be more safe zones where you can respawn, there is no question about it.  The crafting aspect is very fun in terms of armor, weapons, attachments, etc...  The only advice I would give on it would be to increase the amount of resources obtained from end game proto events, gamma fragments and such.  The game being free is fantastic and truly something special, this is not another run of the mill free game thrown together to cash in on skins and P2W features, its an amazing game with developers who really care.  The newest aspect of the PVP battles is a really nice touch, however, capping the type of armor and or plates people bring in could help the fight be more fair for everyone.  Fast travel is also something that needs to be explored ASAP at the very least allow it between the major settlements.  Seeing as how vehicles aren't very likely on being added there needs to be a feature that allows faster travel.  At times it feels like a running simulator.  Overall, the community in the game is very funny and supportive at times.  I would recommend this game to anyone who wants a breath of fresh air in their gaming experiences.

Too grindy in a boring way.Most of the time you will be roaming location and completing same mini-activities multiple times - there are randomly generated spots with ~5 monster/human NPCs that you need to kill, for this you get monster/human crafting resources and a bit of reputation. To upgrade a weapon you need to max out reputation within location which takes a lot of time and by that time you will have more than enough resources to craft several weapon types and armors so that you won't need to return to the location.Almost cleared 2nd location, so far killed almost a dozen of actual players, died to them only a few times so there is no much problems with pvp until mid-game locations (bar which is 4th?). When you die you lose resources that you did not put to stash - so upon death you lose ~30 min worth resources although you have excess of them and don't lose reputation that you farmed so dying is pretty much nothing. In case of dying not to player there is a high chance of retrieving your backpack with resources. Along with resources you may lose ammo and healthkits but you will have so many of them in your stash and they are so cheap that you won't even bother.Story is rather interesting and you make meaningful choices, there are some fetch quests with interesting plot but they all feel same gameplay-wise, there are not much of them and they don't give much reputation so still most of the time you will be roaming locations boringly cleaning small spots of NPCs.There is no sense in hunting players as you don't get their weapons, you get ammo and consumables that you have in abundance, you may get some artifacts or other sellable loot but you will have excess money, at least until mid-game, and crafting resources are not really lootable and you get excess of them while farming  reputation.As for pvp gear curve, next tier/location weapon/armor don't add really much. By the time you reach pvp intensive areas you will be wearing mid-grade gear so for what I have seen from crafting trees your weapons should give like 20% lower damage comparing to end-game weapons, while endgame armor does have significant stat difference.Advise for begginers - ignore first location. Second location is the only one where you can craft gear without gear from previous location and maxed reputation from 1st location really only adds some stash space that you have a lot. Weapons rewarded for quests can not be upgraded although they come with attachments that can not be used on other weapons but it lets you not to craft attachments until you get better gear.So be prepared that your first ~20 hours will be rather boring and then you will reach locations where, as people say, you will be killed a lot by campers just for fun because players loot is pretty much useless but there is nothing else fun to do.UPD: later you get another mandatory activity - choose sub-location and roam in circles until you hear a beep from your metal detector, equip it as a weapon and search for a container. First you will be doing this is friendly area with other players and loot spawn rate barely acceptable for one player so get ready to run to another sub-location. Mandatory means that specific resources can not be found anywhere else. Then you will be doing same thing in pvp intense are for another type of resource which both fractions get only in specific location.And then head a really long way to base like running for 5+ mins hoping not to get killed by monsters/humanoids/anomalies/players and losing all you have collected.The last drop for me was main quest mission being platformer with enemies pushing you to fall to death, with this terrible engine and controls.Don't play this game, really, you may only try if your friends love to suffer but still a terrible idea

It really does pain me to write this negative review, because Stalcraft does have huge potential to be a great game and I really do enjoy most aspects of it. However, after playing it for a few days after release, the cracks in the game are beginning to show just like the cracks in my patience and that of others.Stalcraft came to my attention by accident from an acquaintance of mine, whom I know through a Discord gaming group I frequent in order to socialize with old friends and enjoy like-minded passions together. We are all avid gamers, who are more than familiar with and accustomed to competitive first-person shooters and MMORPG's, amongst other genres as well. We are always looking for games to play together and even boot-up the old Minecraft server occasionally. This is the reason why, after perusing through Steams "Featured & Recommended" section one Saturday morning, my acquaintance came into group chat and informed us of this exciting new game and we were more than willing to give it a go.From the get-go we were blown away. This was a game that had a beautifully crafted complex post-apocalyptic world, filled with action, diverse enemies and characters, crafting etc. I myself, having played S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Call of Pripyat before, found the aesthetics of the game very charming, because it took the grim and dark world of Stalker and softened it into something much more light-hearted, but without loosing or changing the core premise of the game itself. The game-play was similar but refreshingly different to that of most MMORPG's and we all had a chuckle at the ridiculous stretched faces of our Stalkers, but most importantly it had a huge plus of being a free-to-play game, which meant that we could all play together without worrying about the cost.Sadly, this joyful bliss only lasted a short while and after having spent the better part of the day, finding myself in a constant frustrating loop of dying in-game, respawning, purchasing/sorting out ammo + other provisions and adventuring out to simply die a short time later and repeat the whole process again, I feel compelled to share my criticism.First of all let me start by saying that this is not Minecraft. No-matter what other people claim or the fact that it looks like Minecraft. The most important difference being, is that in Minecraft, every block can be interacted with and with the help of your imagination can be used to craft/build almost anything. The only things you can and must craft in Stalcraft are your armour, your weapons and some few weapon modifications and devices. Modifications that play seldom, if at all, any understandable role or purpose. I say "must craft" because if you want better equipment you cannot buy it, you must craft it with materials.These materials have to be gathered, either through random drops by an NPC, searching for them with a metal detector or as a reward for completing daily quests and/or events. The "Events" in question are essentially mini-quests that are spread across the map. They are generally "human" or "animal" based and vary from attacking enemy encampments to destroying animal dens. The rewards they give vary depending on the region they are in and are in conjunction with the resource requirements for  the weapons/equipment that are made there. Even though, they look equally divided on the map, in reality the animal events are much more frequent and more accessible than the human ones. Another way of obtaining some of these resources is by purchasing them from a special vendor that takes premium currency only and even though the developers have taken out the "starter packs" and claim it's not P2W, this clearly shows otherwise. Because without spending your hard earned money it is a horrible tedious grind. A grind that is made worse by several factors:1) Not enough resources to go around. When trying to find them using the metal detector you will spend hours going back and forth around a designated area that has already been picked clean by other players.2) Inability to get gear or loot from the bodies of other players. 3) Having to run to other areas due to lack of fast travel, which in itself is not a bad concept and follows the STALKER aesthetic but ultimately fails because of bad map design and the materials which are assigned to certain areas only and without the ability to purchase them.4) Large amount of invisible anomalies that you can bump into at anytime and which can kill you instantly. Anomalies which are also sometimes placed in such a way that it makes it impossible for you to retrieve your dropped loot.5) Other players camping out spots, valleys and passes making them impassable.And don't get me wrong I am all for a bit of grinding when it comes to an MMORPG but the risk-reward ratio has to be good enough to make it worthwhile.Now to the last point some might say "it's PvP, what did you expect?" and "stop moaning and git gud" which is all fair if it wasn't for the way the map was designed and how it ultimately makes the factions unbalanced. In the beginning both factions start together on the opposite sides of a swamp in the south. It is a fairly balanced area and is divided from the rest of the map by a train track that acts like a natural barrier and can only be passed through via a few choke-points. Now after the starting area the Stalker faction move to a base on the south side of the tracks and the Bandits move to a base on the northern side. Their base is located next to the junkyard, which is where vital resources and main quests are located that are necessary for crafting and the progression of the Stalker faction. There are 4 roads that lead to the junkyard and beyond. One road leads directly from the Bandit base and the other 3 run through valley passes with steep cliffs to either side that cannot be circumvented unless you go through the Bandit base. The roads and valley passes are also surrounded by higher ground and hills. On one of these hills and adjacent to 2 roads sits the Bandit base. The Bandit players sit on top of the hills and shoot the Stalkers who are trying to get through the pass. And who can blame them really, they have a natural advantage and any military tactician will tell you that those on higher ground will always have the upper hand. With no way to go around the Stalkers are forced to go through the pass and are easily picked off. Even if they manage to kill some of the Bandits, the Bandits simply re-spawn at the nearby base and take up the same positions. The Stalkers on the other hand, re-spawn further away and have a much longer trek, through the choke-points in the barrier and along open roads on lower ground, where they are also vulnerable. If the Stalkers manage to somehow sneak through to the junkyard and close to the main quests they are yet again met with waiting Bandits (I've tried this by slowly crawling for a total of 40 mins, taking the longest route possible only to be shot in the head a few meters away from the quest)All of these points create a very frustrating and unrewarding experience, which is sad, because the game shows huge promise and is generally fun.The problem with resources could be fixed fairly easily by making them more abundant or being sold in a shop. Likewise, the anomalies could be made more visible and their amount reduced, but the problem with the map is something that ultimately breaks the game. The only way I think it can be resolved is with a total overhaul of the map and something that I don't think can be achieved considering how long this game has been in production already. TLDR: A fun game with an interesting concept, but one that ultimately fails due to poor map design, unbalanced factions, a large amount of invisible hazards, the grind for resources and a poor risk-reward ratio. All of which leading to a very frustrating and unrewarding experience.

I rarely write reviews, but Stalcraft X has completely grabbed my attention for the past few weeks. Having completed the main quest and pretty much learned everything about the game, here's what I think: This might surprise some people, but you really don't have to spend money to enjoy Stalcraft. Sure, you can buy stuff like the battle pass that gives you extras, but these don't dramatically change how you progress through the game. It’s nice to play a game where spending money is truly optional. The combat is awesome. It feels like a real FPS game, so if you've played games like CoD or CS, you'll have a good time and probably do better than other people. I don’t get why some people complain about enemies camping or stealing loot. Just fight back, team up, or get better gear. That’s a big part of what makes the game fun and challenging. If you liked the original Stalker games, you’ll love this. Hunting for artifacts is even more fun here, especially once you get better gear like the advanced detector (Buryat). It will be a lot easier if you start grinding for it early on as well. The maps are huge and well-designed. Each faction has its own base, and some places will remind you of the original Stalker games, which is a cool throwback. Despite what others have said, the bosses in this game are tough and rewarding. Beating the final boss in the North without any tips or tricks was one of the best parts of the game for me. The initial experience in Stalcraft X can be overwhelmingly confusing for newcomers. The tutorial is rudimentary at best, offering little beyond basic shooting mechanics. Once released into the game's vast world, players find themselves without clear directions on critical aspects such as crafting, choosing suitable gear, and understanding the role of different NPCs. The learning curve is steep, with crucial game elements like crafting systems, weapon choices, and tactical approaches not being adequately explained. This lack of guidance is further complicated by the PDA's insufficient reference guide, which fails to provide the detailed information required to navigate the early and middle stages effectively. The game could benefit immensely from a comprehensive, accessible guide that gradually introduces applicable information as players progress. That would offer contextual help at each new stage. Interactive map and Wikipedia do not provide sufficient information as of today. The game’s community can be pretty toxic. Even within factions, it feels like you can’t trust most people, and there aren’t enough activities that bring players together. Some type of a reputation system among players could help foster a more cooperative environment. Also, when you ask for advice, some experienced players just push their own opinions on you which isn’t always helpful and could lead to some poor choices. Since crafting and upgrading gear involves a considerable investment of time, it would be beneficial to have a test lobby where players can experiment with guns separately from the main game. I play on NA servers, and the amount of lag and bugs can be really annoying. I feel like I've died more times to glitches than to actual enemies. Sometimes the environment causes problems too, like artifacts and signals getting stuck in walls or mobs glitching out and running into the textures. After finishing the main quest, there doesn’t seem to be much point in continuing. The daily and weekly quests get boring, and the side quests don’t offer much that’s worthwhile. There’s a big gap between finishing the story and getting the best gear, which makes it feel like there’s no reason to keep playing.While Stalcraft X offers an immersive and enjoyable experience, it would benefit greatly from a more comprehensive beginner's guide and a smoother introduction to its world. The current resources do not fully prepare new players for the challenges they will face. Despite its potential, I find myself reluctant to continue playing, at least not in the foreseeable future.

For a strange simulacra of STALKER's Zone as done through the eyes of a block/Minecraft themed lens...It's honestly not bad. There's some charm here, and the progression system is a novel idea if a bit grindy due to the sheer amount of resources needed and amount of maps needed to collect them from. Here's the big rub: The PvP system is stupid, as it stands. It serves no practical purpose in gameplay beyond stroking your ego as you can't get anything from other players beyond loose sell-fodder; which is good. Items like armor and weapons should be bound or else progression would be killed dead if you got unlucky.At the same time it's just there as a gate to keep people from progressing quickly since all that'll happen is as a loner, you'll go to get the resources to get upgraded gear, get murdered by either a bandit, or bad luck from the AI. Then your bound loot drops, someone runs across it and yeets your bag into the trash and you're screwed.Bandits aren't really much better as you'll be doing the same sort of exploration and grinding, but because as a whole the bandit faction picks on loners way more. Even if you specifically aren't looking for a fight, it's too late. You're the wrong faction, and so you'll get domed and looted...or just get bad luck by the same anomalies and have someone loot your junk and throw away your bag.At this point, they either need to confine PvP faction interactions to specific chunks of the world, or retool the drop system so that ALL bound items remain in your inventory and all that drops is unbound fodder, ammo, medical, etc.Ontop of this, while overall I'd rank the map design as good as the source, or even better than STALKER in some ways. Rostok is a awful design and shouldn't have ever been added. It's a central hub for BOTH sides of the coin, so what happens is bandits get domed by loners, and loners get camped by bandits. With either side getting screwed over and not having any fun trying to leave the central base of the game to actually play. Should just admit it sucks, and break it into a loner base at Dark Valley, and a bandit base over in Agroprom. There's even already places where it could easily be done and make logical sense.As it stands, while I'll probably poke around this game with a friend because as it stands the options for a multiplayer STALKER like experience are basically just THIS. The moment options become better for a genuine Zone coop experience without xXx3dGyB4d1Tl0RdxXx shooting me in the back, or being screwed by my own faction because of bad luck with an anomaly; this Zone wanderer is turning around and not looking back fondly.

I strongly recommend this game if you enjoy mmofps and want an incredibly punishing full loot (everything you carry except for weapons and gear) pvp open world game. This review is for people who are okay with a bumpy start and want to know if its worth the time investment to get to endgame raiding and pvp.I played to endgame prior to the massive X update. I was lukewarm on the game then since there wasn't much to grind for and the only endgame zones were boring and campy. However, stalcraft: X is SO DIFFERENT. Everything they added to the endgame is amazing and has easily put hundreds of more hours of content and G R I N D to the game. There is enough to do to keep me interested and addicted every time I log in. Some key points if you're still on the fence. - Great visuals and aesthetic. Feels like a lived-in STALKER world and you can get really immersed, blocky heads and all. - Combat is responsive and snappy. Better fps netcode than any mmofps I've played before. - PVP is (mostly) fair, with server and region balancing. Lots of weapons and playstyles to experiment with thanks to artifacts having a significant effect on combat. - On NA, I've met far more kind and friendly people than the opposite. If you put yourself out there its easy to make friends. - PvE is NOT A JOKE even at endgame. A handful of mobs can quickly end your life if you're not careful. Between pve mobs and open world pvp, you can never feel 100% safe, and I love it- Multiple different endgame zones, each with different focuses (group pvp, faction wars, tarkov-styled extract) as well as some brainless pvp playlists if you just wanna frag without consequences.-If you're experienced with high-stress shooters, you will clap cheeks. Theres enough mediocre players even at endgame to feed your pvp addiction.  - The endgame grind is real. This is a proper MMO, so go into it expecting to invest a lot of time before you get top-tier weapons and armor. - There is pay-to-win. Its not too bad though, theres a hard limit on player progression/upgrades so you won't get dunked on by a whale. Plus theres a lot of freebees and you can even buy premium time/battle pass with ingame currency. - Don't expect frequent and constant fights in the overworld. Its much more like tarkov (unless you're hunting for fights) where you can go an hour+ without seeing an enemy. - Expect different quality on different regional servers. I love NA, but I know that EU has hackers (never met one on NA) and SEA is pretty dead. Overall I give the game a hearty recommendation. There really isn't anything like it on the market.
As for me, a game for those who like to shoot with other players, if you are an ordinary pve player, then I think it will be difficult for you, and so I liked the game.

This game channels big Stalker Energy. From the cruel and often random deaths you can suffer to the heightened stress and paranoia that you feel as you trek through the Zone. So for me on that point alone, I will recommend this game to any Stalker fans plus it's free so you can give a quick try and see if you like it or not.Quick Breakdown of Pros and Cons:This game definitely feels like playing a Stalker game. You have familiar factions like Free Stalkers, Bandit, Duty and Freedom and the map layout can be familiar to veterans of the series. Famous Stalker mutants like Bloodsuckers and Snorks are also in the game.The atmosphere is surprisingly good despite the Minecraft looking graphics. The game sports really good lighting and it definitely helps with the overall feel of the world. The game also have very decent sound designs that kept me on my toes early on.The gun modifications is more in depth than you would think. While this game doesn't quite reach Tarkov level of gun modding madness, it does have a similar system where you can add rails and handguards to allow attaching of all sorts of attachments like grips, laser sights and gunsights.I know some of the reviews are complaining about this aspect but in my opinion, this is one of the defining features of Stalcraft. In regular single player Stalker, all you have to contend with are NPC humans with godlike accuracy (which is present in this game) but even then their AI is not advanced enough to form complex tactics or create and take advantage of a battlefield situation. With the simple addition of other hostile players, Stalcraft allows fights to be far more intense and fun. I am gonna be real honest with ya'll right here, I personally hate grind in video games. Like any form of grinding is usually enough to make me stop playing a game outright. And yes, Stalcraft can be pretty grindy. The best way to explain why there is grind is to explain the bartering system in game. To barter your way to a better equipment, you would need to farm and gather resources from specific regions in the game world. Then once you gathered it, you have to make your way back to base and then turn it in to acquire whatever gear you wish to get. Problem is if you die for whatever reason, your stuff would drop into a pouch on the ground and you either have to get it back or hope some kind soul retrieve your gear and mail it back to you.Now this will be a big turn off for a lot of people but to get it out of the way --- THERE IS NO FAST TRAVEL.In this game, in order to get anywhere and do anything, you must walk the whole distance on foot. So get ready to walk and pack some energy drinks if you want to speed up the process by sprinting more often. And remember when I said dying causes you to drop all your stuff? Yes that's right, in order to get it back, you have to walk all the way back and pick it back up. So I can honestly understand people who are miffed by this point and want to drop the game. For me this isn't as big of a deal seeing how in Vanilla Stalker, you walk a lot anyways.I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of Stalker and/or "hardcore" shooters. This game is free anyways so there is no harm in giving it at least a few hours try. Grind is bad but hey when you're playing with friends, you kinda forget about the grind.

Gear that will allow you to take down anyone you can get the drop on.While speaking on gear, this game has a lot of gear options and playstyles.  And gear is how they separate people.   You wont see any Veterans dunking on newbs in this game, its literally impossible.  There are 5 tiers of gearscore and once you pass a threshold, there's no going back. I'll never see people who are below "Semi-Master" in the open world, nor they me, i can still see them in the hubs, but unless we group up, they wont see me.   Grouping pulls people UP, not DOWN. Is it a friend or foe?    Do you hide or hunt?  Well that will be up to you.All of this is to say, for a free title this game has a lot to offer in both PvE and PvP. Many of the armor designs make it almost impossible to see anyway.Hope to see you all in the Zone!

Starcraft is a unique mix of Stalker, MMO, and Minecraft.The game is funny and pleasurable if you have some friends and you understand how to play by the rules which the game provides. The game and its rules aren't perfect, but developers usually try to make the experience better, they actively fix game problems and think about different groups of players, also they time to time provide additional content for high-tier gameplay. From the last update, we got a nice weapon to rebalance ( not without small mistakes ) but after the update in-game combat become much more understandable and reasonable.Also, they take care of starters and low-tier players and provide them with a great way to make characters better via artifacts. Artifacts become more usable on low levels, become more reasonable on high levels. Also, they give you a great amount of valuable in-game items if your artifact after the update doesn't fit your needs now. So you will be able to replace it.As additional content, we got great, unique PVP activity with PVE elements, which provides a good amount of in-game resources and feels interesting and refreshing. It's shocking how some small game developer studios can create such a unique experience for players and make it interesting and helpful for all player levels.There are still some problems in this game on my mind:A too-large count of users on the server:It gives us braindead war on a high level in prime-time when players fighting for a single farm point ( North locations from and including Army Warehouses). And low chance to successfully farm resources because you can die at any second, even 8 hours in a row without any helpful impact on your hero.Weapon balance feels good now, but I feel as if they focus on PVP balance, but mutants feel the same strong as earlier, but your damage is lower. This game is a personal exercise in a sunk cost fallacy that i cannot in good conscience recommend to anyone. Allow me to elaborate.I'll admit, i'm a huge fan of whatever is STALKER. I've always been a huge fan of the franchise and its modding scene. You've likely heard of it by now, as it's become hugely popular. So imagine how the concept of a STALKER MMO would resonate with fans of the franchise, it's a no-brainer to at the very least give a shot.Upon starting Stalcraft, you get the option to pick either the bandit or the stalker side. There's actually a pretty big difference between the two (or rather, four, but we'll get to that later), but early on, it doesnt change much aside from two factors. There's more players on the stalker side, and the faction 'home base' is in two different locations. Even from the get-go, it's a turf war over resources you need to acquire and your quest locations will overlap, meaning that you will run into opponents and there's no avoiding it. At the very least i find that the devs deserve credit where credit is due, the first thing you see on the store page is an image clearly stating that the game is ruthless. Unfortunately, it's worse than that.As soon as you leave the starting region and enter the next one, Roadside, you will be met with your first experience on 'gear disparity'. This game does truly function like an MMO in the sense that gear progression is linear and is a step up above on what you can get. However, when you have to contend for the same resources as your opponents, this also means that this disparity in gear will mean you're rarely truly fighting on equal terms. The difference is small at first, but becomess stronger the further you get. And simultaneously, progression slows down in equal measure, meaning that the gaps become increasingly larger.It doesn't help that progression is tied to personal progress. To elaborate, you can purchase certain items from the market (which is in most cases not recommended) and everything else is set in a tech tree. So, that rusty AK you start out with can be exchanged for a slightly less rusty AK, and that can be exchanged for a non-rusty AK, and that non-rusty AK can be exchanged for a rusty modern AK, etc. You cannot do so with money, instead, you must farm these barter resources in the open world. As i mentioned before, progression slows down immensely the further you get, meaning that you MUST farm. There is no way around it. Simultaneously, the game is full-loot, ss such, it becomes quite easy to simply fight other players and take their loot for yourself. I have no issue with this, as i've long played - and enjoyed - these kinds of games, with EVE online and Escape from Tarkov particularly hitting well over 1k hours. What does not, however, make any sense is that there's everything to gain and nothing to lose from hunting players that are farming. You do not lose your gear, as these are bound to your character, you merely lose your ammunition and meds, which are dirt cheap and widely available, but you stand to gain a lot from hunting players farming, as they do carry items of value. The end result is that people kick the people down that are below them on the progression ladder, that kick those down below them, etc. It develops a toxic community and an overall very unpleasant experience. What doesn't really help matters is that a huge chunk of the endgame, and lets be real, that's always where the good stuff is in an MMO, is locked behind finishing the main storyline. It is obvious that the developers have came a long way from the original vision of the game as the game gets a lot better in the newer content. Unfortunately, not only must you contend with the aformentioned issues, the storyline is set up in instances that you are alone in. This means that it's entirely PvE, which unfortunately provides no respite, as it's straight up NOT fun to play. The story is weak, the missions aren't fun (although with a few cool moments) that were cluelessly designed. So, instead, this game turns into a convoluted 'detective' style game with no narrative to keep you interested in, then sets you off to do parkour style maps when all you want to be doing is shoot stuff, it just goes on and on and it requires endurance and perseverance. The pay-off, however, is that once that is finally over and done with, you can go 'north'. Essentially, bandits and stalkers split off into two ideologically opposing factions for each side and you are now hostile with all other three factions. This part of the game is separate from the area that you went through before, and honestly, it's fun. You get to fight with others over territory and finding a clan becomes an interesting prospect. It starts off good, but it still retains all the issues i mentioned before. It gets better, but it also gets worse. Money is finally interesting by this point in the game. Artifacts, a key feature of the STALKER games, make a return here too. They can be equipped and provide bonuses as well as maluses. At this point it becomes worthwhile to start working out a build and playing to your strengths. This would be cool if it wasn't already solved by those having minmaxed their builds. Though variation is possible, there are key strengths you should play to with your gear and playstyle and deviating from it isn't advised. Good artifacts are, however, ludicrously expensive, and carrying a good amount of them requires you to have a special - hard to acquire - container to carry them, lest these radioactive items instantly kill you by turning you into a literal human torch emitting gamma rays and become a walking Elephant's Foot. At the same time, you can get access to high tier gear to finally get that gear disparity rate solved. All that time you've been trashed, stomped upon and tossed around, you finally can get to the big leagues where you have an actual fighting chance. Sure, not everyone carries the same gear, but yours isn't necessarily worse than theirs. So, how did the developers implement this final stage of progression? Gambling. Lootboxes. Because every bloody game needs a battlepass these days, so does Stalcraft. And there you have the infamous lootbox. It drops pretty often, and oftentimes, it's just consumables, skins and trash, with a very slim chance of getting 'blueprints' you must collect a bunch of to acquire some serious armaments. And, man, you won't believe how awful your chances are here. Lady fortuna better be on your side. That in-game economy they boasted about on the store page with? It's all ludicrously expensive! But you too can become one of the lucky ones, if you just. Draw. The. Right. Item. Exchange your season pass points for a container with a random drop, maybe you'll get lucky! The actual good end-game weapons? Armor, attachments? Yes, you can trade them. And the cost is so damn high, that you cannot reasonably purchase this from other players without drawing a high value item yourself to sell in return. If you don't get a lucky draw, you're out. Don't get me started on having to level your items on top of it. And artifacts.The TDM PvP mode, standoffs, is also tied to gear and isn't balanced as a result as there's no matchmaking. Because screw you, that's why. You don't get to partake in it.I think it can. There are examples where the devs have proven that the game can be great, particularly the Dead Time gamemode is excellent. Until then i will be playing still, because i refuse to give up and embrace the sunk cost fallacy. Don't become like me. Avoid this game.It's a Russian Gacha game set in the STALKER universe. Avoid it.

Mainly in the form of the enemy AI, it is abysmal to say the least.  Solo players will find that, upon entering the dark valley it is detrimental to avoid NATO enemies at all cost. Sure you could say that I am just a bad player, and you would be correct; while, it is possible to just sit far away with a sniper and pick them off, this is also difficult because the AI will just "hold w" until they over run your position. At which point, you could have the best armor you can possible have at that point in the game and you will get melted by consecutive head shot's with no time to react as soon as you peek. This just makes an experience that feels unfair. The main issue is the difficulty of the AI is based on the aim bot instead of just better overall gear. Also, the AI always know where you are as soon as they see you. You can run behind a hill to get a better position and the AI will know exactly where you are even if you can barely see them, resulting in you're immediate evisceration from an enemy you cant even see. EDIT: Tried coming back with a new mindset, and new strategies, but there's no strategy to dealing with black holes. Instant death traps were manageable with quicksaves. As it stands they just invalidate whatever you'd been doing for the past hour.I am torn on whether to recommend or not. I love this game, but it wastes your time with pointless setbacks. It's a beautiful and well designed piece stuck within the horrific structure of free-to-play. I think, in the end, I'd rather recommend with caveats than give a negative review to an independent developer.If you go into this game with full knowledge of its downfalls, and are able to pull yourself away from addicting games when they become a problem, you will probably have a very good, limited time as I did. I don't regret any of my hours played, but I will not be putting in any more.the good:The devs' love of STALKER is palpable, they did an amazing job rebuilding the Zone to be familiar but different. The mechanics all fit in with the tone of the original series, and once you get used to the aesthetic, the game can be strikingly beautiful. Gunplay is responsive and enjoyable, and the combination of npcs and players keeps you on your toes and the world feels alive.The writing also blew me away, just rough and crude enough to really fit the Zone as a place and community. You only lose loot, ammo, and medicine.The music choices for the safe zones actually slap, and I am now listening to a lot of those outside of the game itself.the bad:The setbacks from death, be it from pve or pvp, will eventually overtake the amount of time you spend making forward progress.Black holes, the anomaly which makes it near impossible to get your items back even if you beeline straight for where you died, since they throw your loot out and leave it vulnerable to despawn.Players who KOS and then you've lost however many  hours of materials, and they get next to nothing out of it. I had no trouble with money and ammo and meds, all come quick and cheap, but the amount of hours I've lost to random death is beyond what I'm willing to put into a game. I've played a few hours of this game over the last few days, and I think from that I've managed to figure out what this game is meant to be, and how it compares to the aforementioned games of which this is very clearly inspired by. These are however still considered my first impressions, and I will probably update this review if I play more and notice something is incorrect, or learn about something new that adds to the overall experience.The art style is certainly... . It's world is designed with voxels in mind, with square trees, leaves, walls and grass, but does not limit itself to that. It has some models that stand out, being of a much higher definition than the blocky style you'd expect. It does feel strange having a computer and desk rendered with a high (ish) poly count when a short walk away there is a BTR made entirely out of cubes and slopes. The same can be said for the first person animations which contradict the goofy movement of the minecraft style character models. But ultimately it's up to you if such an art style is appealing.Besides that though, the atmospheric effects from fog, to the ambient sound effects and music are superb. The fog impedes your vision while also adding to the fear of what might lie around the corner, the music although very much in the background creates an eerie atmosphere as you trek through the zone. You also must not forget anomalies, I'm going to leave new players in the dark regarding those because your first encounter with one is something special. But if you are new to stalker, This is a game with guns (duh), therefore the gunplay is one of the most important factors in determining if you enjoy the game. Guns in stalcraft have very little recoil, both visual and physical. Guns are accurate but do have drop off over range and some degree of spread to categorise weapons into their respective ranges. The TTK feels nice from my experience, some tracking is involved when dealing with fast moving targets and such a ttk provides a timeframe to move and reposition in npc or player fights (did I not mention this game has pvp? More on that later), but is extended dependant on the amour used by both parties.The animations for the guns in first person are excellent, you can tell that the animators had a good time making these, and the blocky hands might have helped since less time was spent ensuring the animation curve for the Z axis of your left hand's pinky finger is set juuuust right., and more was spent on ensuring the overall animation feels good.It's worth noting that dying in this game does NOT cause you to lose your weapons or armour. Some items are tied to your player and are not lost on death, and the main reason why is because of how this game deals with progression. Guns, attachments, backpacks and whatnot are not meant to be found in loot containers or npcs, regardless of what the tutorial leads you to believe.You have merchants in the main settlements who offer you gear in return for items. Each region has a set of items that are used to purchase new gear, the first region (the swamps) providing you with swamp stone and mold, both of which are obtained by completing timed missions that appear in the world, ranging from clearing out a den of wild dogs to taking out a camp of bandits. These resources however, ARE lost on death. So the fear of losing your progress towards your next gear unlock or upgrade is what provides that sense of dread that both Stalker and Tarkov pride themselves on.This means that your exploration of the world is fairly linear. Stalker fans will recognise many locations on the map, but due to how progression works, you will often stick to one region to unlock the gear you want, then move on to a higher level region to start gathering the next level of materials while being able to use your new toy.You can expect to unlock new guns in many categories, attachments for said guns ranging from grips to laser sights. Armour that are specialised in exploration or combat. The guns themselves have an in depth customisation system that tarkov fans will appreciate, providing you with all sorts of information for those minmaxers or cursed gun creators to drool over.Like stalker, there is a main quest to follow, something along the lines of being 'blessed', which I believe means you have received a vision of some mysterious blue artifact alongside an unexplained desire to venture into the zone to find it (wish granter much?). Frankly you can skip the dialogue and still enjoy it, which is what I'm doing, but there is a story you can follow as well as side tasks for those wanting that.As I hinted at earlier, multiplayer plays a heavy role in this game. You will see players all over the map, doing these timed missions, fighting npcs, fighting each other. There is no way to avoid the pvp which is a very important thing to consider. Tasks you gain will often have you wondering into territory close to the opposing faction, where you choose one of two upon starting the game, who are of course not likely to want to join each other for a leisurely picnic. The fact that you keep your weapons does alleviate the annoyance of being killed off by someone of the other faction, but it will happen and it will slow down your progress. Which is why you will sometimes need to consider taking it slow, scouting out for enemies before moving and taking the less beaten path in order to get where you need to go.Interactions don't just have to be hostile though. You can chat to people nearby using text or voice, and witnessing the chat devolve into utter chaos during an emission is a sight to behold.This game is a forced pvpve, multiplayer mmo rpg style game, inspired by games like tarkov, stalker and minecraft all the while changing up the formula to make it it's own thing. The art style is a mix of voxel and high poly, with high quality weapon animations and sound effects that add to the overall feel of the zone as you explore it. The gunplay feels tight with a lot of options when it comes to customisability. Fights can be tense, where ai pose just as much of a threat as real players who wonder the zone alongside you at all times. You will die often if you are new to this, and that is fine. Learning how to deal with challenges like that is what makes it fun, and makes getting that next upgrade feel even better.The game loop though will boil down to farming the resources required to get new guns and gear, tasks provide other motives but ultimately you will go from region to region, powering up and dealing with the threats that the zone presents you. If you like that sort of thing then you will love this. This game feels like it has a clear goal in mind as to what it intends to be, and as a strange concoction of minecraft and stalker alongside many other games it works surprisingly well. This is a pretty interesting and somewhat fun take on the "Stalker" franchise. You'll want to be able to convince your existing friends to get into the game, or be willing to make new ones within the game. A lot of the game's annoyance sort of happens due to the fact that you're alone, so it helps a lot to even have one buddy who will revive you. As in, "oh man, I died again, now it's time to run for 2 minutes back to the place I died" sort of annoyance. You can revive your friends, and if you're lucky, a random stranger could be around to revive you.There is PvP, but no friendly fire. As of now, you can't really turn the PvP off, but you don't really lose your guns and armor, but moreso just lose your easier-to-replace stuff, like sellable items, medkits and ammo. (The game is very clear on what you'll lose; anything with a "lock" icon you keep). I really like how the game handles sprinting. You can sprint even while prone, or you can sprint-climb. The game feels fun as a game in this way. Linux Proton works well. I notice 0 issues. Monetization is a monthly premium that just doesn't seem worth it to me, it's just some slight bonuses to earnings and access to more dailies. But that means the monetization highly unaffects the game.It will take you a little while until you can get access to the "courier" and interact with the game's economy.If you're planning to be 100% solo and not interact with others online, you might be more interested in downloading "STALKER Anomaly" instead. It's free made by fans of the series. But since both are free, you really don't lose anything by downloading the game and giving a try, unless if you are data-capped; the game is about 12GB big. If you're a newbie to the STALKER series, please keep an open mind and understand some things might be a little different than you might initially expect. The metal bolt you throw is NOT a magical anomaly killer, it just triggers some of the anomalies, or just shows that they're there, but that's it.

I wish there was a "maybe" option between Yes and No in Steam Reviews, because I like this game, but it comes with a lot of baggage. For longtime fans of STALKER looking for new content, I recommend this. For people just getting into STALKER, go download STALKER Anomaly and play that instead. This is basically a STALKER fan game. It outright copies the names and appearances of most mutants and some artifacts. It has a few really interesting original quests (like one with a psy-dog that is pretty mesmerizing) and a good sense of exploration. But sometimes the quest design is outright perplexing and difficult to follow. There's one quest that requires you to climb a radio tower, and it hints at this in a riddle, but the climbing function normally doesn't work on shear surfaces, so it's unlikely someone would guess that without a hint from another player.It captures the atmosphere of STALKER better than any game I've played outside of mods, but it's also an incredibly lengthy grind. The story missions give you everything you need, but the weapons and armor you get from the story can't be upgraded to their next stage in the upgrade tree. If you want to engage with anything other than the story, or go for a variety of weapons, you need to grind by collecting crafting materials for incremental upgrades. With a punishing PVP and anomaly system, you can wipe an hour of progress easily just by stepping on the wrong tile. With a little patience it can be thrilling, but one wrong step can send you back to base three maps over, with 15 minutes of walking to retrieve a bag of items that might not even be there when you get back.
