To begin with, Stalcraft is one of the best games I've played recently. It is a combination of games such as S.T.A.L.K.E.R, Minecraft, and Escape From Tarkov. It is highly addictive and the "last hour of the game" turns into a sleepless night. I love it and I hate it at the same time.First of all, let's talk about the things that make me hate this game. In my opinion, the tutorial is not fully finished, it doesn't explain some game mechanics, so the player has to figure out how some things work on their own. Stalcraft does not treat the player kindly and immediately throws him in at the deep end. You will die here dozens if not hundreds of times. Enemy NPCs are deadly, they can spawn on you and spray you out with one magazine or use their "wallhack" to kill you through walls or dense forests. Animals will swarm you and bite you to death. Anomalies like Vortexes, Trampolines, or Black Holes will make you lose your sanity. Global anomaly will wipe you off the board if you won't get to the bunker on time. Sometimes you will die falling outside the textures of the map. Enemies will hunt you down, campers will laugh at your face killing you for the 7th time with one headshot. You will suffer many times trying to recover things from your corpse. More than once I wanted to use alt+f4 and uninstall the game, but as the story progressed, it happened to me less and less. Furthermore, some quests are really "basic", like "go and kill 5 boars", "bring me 3 cans of beans" or "go around a map and scan some areas". Spawn Points of different factions are not equally fair. In my opinion, the Bandits have better spawn locations than the Stalkers. Even though I hate the things mentioned above, they give the game a raw atmosphere, charm, and character that makes me want to play it all the time.The advantages include the fact that the game works great even on weaker computers (and it's free!) The game world is huge. The music and graphic style of the game introduce an unearthly atmosphere. More than once I stood for several minutes in the base just to listen to the singing NPC or admire the wonderful views of the post-apocalyptic world. Cities (bases) have their own atmosphere - music is played everywhere, conversations or sounds of generators are heard, and NPCs walk around the city. After death, all equipment is not lost, and the player does not lose weapons, armor, or some items marked with a padlock. Only items collected in the Zone or "lockless" items are lost. There is a huge amount of weapons and accessories available in the game. The shooting feeling is phenomenal, gun sounds are realistic. The PVP in the game is wonderful. The ability to play with friends or other players to create squads or guilds makes the game even better. This allows you to organize joint expeditions into the Zone, joint animal hunting, joint cleaning of enemy camps, or jointly organized attacks on enemy players. The game gives you the feeling that you always have something to do, which makes it hard to tear yourself away from it. It's worth mentioning that on the release date there was "pay to win" but players of the game convinced devs that it was not good and the devs got rid of it. Now if you want to spend real money on the game it's only used to buy premium that allows you to progress faster in-game (more daily quests or more loot from events) but it's not giving you an upper hand above others.In my opinion, the game is definitely worth recommending. In my rating of 8.5/10, I feel that I will spend hundreds if not thousands of hours on it.

After 100 hours and two playthroughs, All I can say is this:Pros: 1. Storyline is interesting and fun to progress through UNTIL you reach the Bar.2. Cooperative STALKER experience with friends3. Interesting take on the Zone which is fun to explore.4. Great weapon (soon to be character) animations5. Texture work is actually really good for it being block style.6. Weapons and Armor are bound so you cannot lose a gun you like BUT this is also a curse, I will explain why in Cons #4Cons:1. FORCED PvP RUINS THIS GAME! The Storyline after reaching the Bar becomes quite difficult to do as some parts require you to go to hotspots where both starter factions (Loners and Bandits) must talk to an NPC sometimes unprotected in dialogue. 1a. Fast Travel points between levels are rolls of a dice because there are different server clusters. ie. Cordon #1 Cordon #2 etc. You can be told in chat that Dump#2 is safe but when you travel you get Dump#4 and enemy players are camping it. Its such bad design. On top of that matchmaking is kind of confusing and I can only assume the moment you get a different colored gear level you then get matched higher.2.  Lack of VOIP means this is essentially a shoot on sight no matter what game. EVEN THOUGH everyone is trying to reach a lot of the same goals.3. Subfactions are used as ways to create an endgame and not a dynamic Zone. Starting as any of the known factions and working your way up would make for a more interesting experience seeing how this game scales matchmaking. It would be a great opportunity since this is an MMO and not a singleplayer STALKER4. Weapons, Attachments, Armors, etc are locked behind a "Bartering Tree" which is what makes them bound to you. However this is used as a way to gate your matchmaking level because of different gear ratings (colors): Basic, Newbie, Stalker, Veteran etc. 4a. They require materials to use in the bartering/crafting which CANNOT be taken by other players that kill you. Instead if leaves all your materials in a "Lost Backpack" which other players can mail back to you or extort you for the resources with Rubles on the Auction Market.4b. This leads to a lot of painful running around for hours collecting resources and then rolling the dice on whether or not you get BS'd by a player spawn, Mutant spawn, anomaly that doesnt make much noise or is hard to see.4c. Gravitational Anomalies in this versus real stalker are literally just there to be instant deaths. Vortexs will kill you if you get stuck on a lip of terrain or a bush which slows you down. Blackholes have a very hard to see boundary with the current effect it gives off. Every other anomaly is piss easy to avoid. Blackholes are used to wall off certain pathways... some of them permanently.5. The PvP is just too static since character movement is essentially a flat hitbox, hopefully when they add new animations, crouching would actually do something as you get caught out of cover A LOT.6. Lack of a dynamic AI like STALKERS A-Life means the game will spawn what are called "events" of Mutants or AI Stalkers sometimes (a lot) on top of you which *WILL* screw you over when an enemy player wanders into your area. In my brutally honest opinion STALCRAFT is really set up to be more of a Cooperative PvE game than it is a true PvPvE MMO. The way factions are set up to be like a TDM race to the objective match more than actual factions with separate motives, camp heavy quests or level changes make the game feel cheap and basic. Not even a basic form of A-Life exists because of the way events are used to get you crafting materials. PvP being forced upon you even though it does NOT yield any benefits for your own crafting/bartering needs essentially makes PvP a griefing tool over giving any ACTUAL meaningful reason to PvP. There are no faction wars, consumables are easy enough to obtain by buying or as rewards through quest and looting to create incentive for you to kill other players for their consumables.This game has two different roads it can go down imo. I do understand this is no easy task.For the PvPvE environment as it stands currently:I think the developers should look into redoing the entire faction dynamic of the game to where you can start as a newbie just like in STALKER Anomaly/EFP/GAMMA. Overhaul some of the map locations to make room for better/more faction bases. Duty has Rostok, Freedom has Yanov. Mercs own Dead City. Bandits have parts of Dark Valley and the swamps. Loners have starts in swamps or Cordon. The Covenant should be the only faction you can actually join through a special questline. Orderlies should be scrapped and swapped with the covenant. Ecologist should return as a more neutral playthrough with a bunker location in the Pit. The Main questline can stay but would need some tweaking for sure. It would be a good way to introduce the Covenant for later. The Bar should be remade to exist as it does in actual stalker and the Arena could be used as a great way for people to fight for some kind of PvP currency. I do like the idea of the far north being complete PvP though. That makes sense as you would be consenting to PvP. Most of the southern end of the zone is just farming. Like I said, PvP only exists to grief people in 70% of this games play area.For PvE.The Loner playthrough could be the start of a great cooperative experience with your friends. I think you could keep most of the main questline and game world. Keeping the multitude of sidequest. Relegating PvP to the Arena at the Bar which is in the real STALKER setting. Stalkers face off against others or even mutants for money and fame.There really isn't much else for me to say on the game. I would say if you haven't played the real STALKER series of games or the Anomaly mod and its derivatives or cannot run them... then this game is pretty damn fun for you. However, if you have played them I would just stick with the standard experience. I think that STALKER GAMMA is the most refined experience of The Zone one can have. Hours can be poured into playing different factions and having a very dynamic playthrough. STALCRAFT is a game that while has colossal potential, is held back by some of the same problems many games of its genre contain.While I do enjoy this game a lot for the starter experience, it just does not do a good endgame well. I don't see a reason for it to exist in the manner it is currently. I wish there was a neutral option for recommending the game. BUT I will give it a thumbs up for what the developers have pulled off with this title after nearly a decade of work. Your support team is very good as well EXBO great job! I wish you well.

So, here we are again boys, and girls. god I hope I'm not the only girl playing this. My take has changed. and I'm here to say this is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. "roblox stalker mmo" is pretty fun with a lot to do that will easily keep you entertained for hours. with it taking good inspiration from stalker in making the guns feel meaty with good sounds and recoil. great movement. with a lot of depth in making builds and choices on what you bring out to the radioactive zone.if you saw some of my old review you know I didn't like it. and I wanna address somethings here from that and then talk about the bad.1.it being p2w. in a way no it's not. So lets brake down what's in the shop: there's a battle pass, cosmetic sets, and cosmetic loot boxes. the latter two aren't pay to win clearly. the battle pass however does give you 4 things that might be seen as it. as it's not PURE cosmetics sadly. It will drop 3 different currency two that carries over between seasons and one that doesn't. as well as a loot box and guns/armor. and those two are the 'trouble' elements.the loot box mostly just drop repair parts, with the odd upgrade and food item and rarely 1 part of a gun/armor in which you need 4 to make said bit of gear. these are actually pretty good bits of tech but it's pure luck if you'll get them. just shy of the best stuff. more over you can ONLY get it from the battle pass. and the currency you lose at the end of the season idealy being used to get more crates to roll more.and sadly this sorta stuff is common in the mmo space even for paid games like eso. tho unlike eso you can't actually out right buy crates. however however: you can BUY level skips. now I can't tell you if you can do it once or if it's repeatable. as the price to skip levels is wildly high. and I don't feel like dropping the price of a new full AAA game on 20-50 levels for a battle pass where I can get 15-21 levels in a day. I'd rather it not be there since it's one of a few pointless things.all that being said, it doesn't matter cause it won't help you with pvp as you are only ever matched with people who have equal gear score and stats to you. meaning at most it might help you with pve. but if you are struggling that much in pve: I'd recommend doing some grinding and upgrading your gear. in pvp if you are bad you still lose even with 'better' gear. so after all that talk we end up with a nothing burger and everything I said about the battle pass hardly mattering. would I still like to see the paid level skips gone? 100% but I think the idea is if you couldn't play for the first half of the season you could "jump in later with a head start!" or whatever.Well we are here lets talk about pvp: this is not tarkov. people do not drop all their gear when they die, and you can't gain crafting parts from killing people, nor their weapons, armor, and bound items (like ammo bags, medical bags, relics they've brought to base or other oddies). what's dropped is some healing items, ammo, barter loot, unbound items (relics, upgrade parts are both unbound till you bring them to a faction base) and home crafting items. Meaning it's not- super worth it imo to hunt others or camping base spawn points other then the lols. killing out in the zone tho? sure. they might have relics on them. or hauling a lot of crafting parts. "but wait you said you can't gain crafting parts from people" correct! they drop in a sealed bag that no one but the og owner can open them. however they can be picked up by anyone and can be auctioned. so if they want their hard work back you can sell it back to them... for a price.you can also- sell the bag itself to an npc but you'll get far less. just be sure to get their bag safely to your own base and don't get caught by the person you just killed.So I've yapped a lot. in the end this is a pretty good game that's held back by a bit of annoyances and sorta iffy monetization

If you've played STALKER SoC, Clear Sky, and Call of Pipyat and you wish you can enjoy it in an mmo format, this is definitely the game for you. For the few who remember Survarium, a game that lied about the Free roam mode which allow you to roam a PvEvP world, well its this game.Pro:- Its STALKER but online with Minecraft artstyle- Plenty of unlock so leveling and progression feels great- Not paywall or massive grind with predatory freemium (So far)-Since STALKER is such an old game, the minecrafty landscape and texture isn't that much different than STALKER was. If it wasn't for the minecraft looking people walking around, I might be fool it is STALKER.- Death Penalty isn't that bad as Escape from Tarkov.- Attachment unlock is rather expansive - Plenty of Armors and style to unlock- Branching choices that can lead the quest in complete different direction and alternative route.- Replayability should you ever want to restart in the other faction since their starting location and maps are totally different.- Plenty of hidden secret to unlock- Loot recovery system that allow other player to help you get your stuff back- The Developer keep it updated and more stuff to come so far- Micro transaction isn't predatory so far, there the Premium membership which give you minor stuff when you log in and more daily quest slot but you get your hand full with the amount they give you already. There only skin cosmetic is chest so far.Con- Forced to PvP whether you like it or not. There two faction and if you run into other person in the open world then be prepare to be shot at. Luckily the death penalty is more forgiving than Escape From Tarkov. You end up losing the resource you harvest and loot but you keep your gears. It still piss me off when I spend 30 minute gathering resource only to get killed by rival faction on the way back to the base.- The Art style is inspire by minecraft so if you can't look past that then you are going to have a problem.- Certain design is rather tedious and stupid such as finding metals resource using the metal detector.- The gun sound alright, although I wish it sound better.- Customization on gun and outfit paint lock behind microtransaction.

STALCRAFT is a MTX/Lootbox gambling game with some questionably poor graphics and even worse asymmetric PvP, where you control post-apocalyptic Lego men with extra chromasomes and you shoot other Lego men.  While the game mostly works, there's some questionable design decisions that make the game generally unpleasant to play, and some reasons to avoid playing the game due to unethical marketing practices. The focus of the game is pure PvP, there's no single player content and very little in the way of PvE content (although there is some).  The developer gambled that other players would be an acceptable substitute for adding storytelling, level design etc to the game.   The vast majority of PvP-only games fail because they don't "go viral", and without players, or single player content to add a lasting value to the game, the game dies.  Developers must learn that other players are not an acceptable substitute for adding content to a game.The game features strong PvP elements, fine, but the problem is that it's asymmetric, open world PvP.  The upshot of this is that new players simply cannot play this game, they will immediately be hunted and kerbstomped by experienced players and griefers who enjoy sealclubbing.  It's simply impossible to get into the game as a new player due to the dominance of established players and a lack of consideration towards game balance from the developers... this will ultimately kill the game as experienced players will get bored without seals to club. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.Despite there being a welcome array of graphics tweaks, there's bewilderingly no way to set the resolution for the game.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The game features lazy low-polygon voxel "Minecraft"-like "art", making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the 1990s.  A lot of amateur developers see Minecraft's success and assume it's because it looks bad, not because it had unique and appealing game mechanics, and they try to emulate the success without understanding it.  It also happens to be easy, and doesn't need any proper talent in terms of game development/graphic artists etc.  That's why reviewers are faced with so many of these terrible games with confrontingly bad graphics.  Developers must learn that Minecraft succeeded despite the bad graphics, not because of them.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.STALCRAFT didn't appeal much to the people who own a copy of the game, either.  It has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the game didn't really capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for surviving an 'Emission' event in the game, trivial to get, but less than 34 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the game.  Hardly a success story, gamers just weren't all that interested in the game, even though it's "free" (but not really free). The game isn't really free as the developers have infested the game with a cash shop, and you're expected to fork over huge amounts of money for access to both basic game systems that are needed to play, and of course spending money gives you access to stuff that gives you an edge against other players... the game is heavily pay 2 win and must be avoided for that reason alone.This game is infested with loot box gambling.  While the contents of the loot boxes are mostly cosmetic, this gamer gouging practice is unethical and insulting to gamers, preying on those vulnerable to gambling addiction.  Gamers should be cautious and consider avoiding this game for that reason alone.

Playing as STALKER:Everything is extremely fun throughout the first two zones. Then the game becomes a slog from Dark Valley and the Dump onward, and there's not much you can do about it because in this game which restricts you based on your progress NORTHWARD, your opponents' spawn is literally in the northernmost part of each map. You will be camped by enemy players with more gear than you, and there is absolutely nothing you can do to address that.Additionally, there is a REQUIRED STORY MISSION about halfway through the Dark Valley chapter of the game which feels like it was INTENTIONALLY designed by the developers to lose you your gear and cause you to be as frustrated and miserable as possible. The mission involves doing parkour (yes, parkour in a bloody STALKER game based on Minecraft- very cliche) through an obstacle field to find an enemy you're meant to kill.The obstacle course is not only littered with anomalies and infinite enemy spawns in unfair locations, but while you are balancing on a knife point and trying not to fall off of the ladders you are climbing, there are floating wisps that heat seek you and cause KNOCKBACK DAMAGE. Without looking for a guide online you will be stuck at this location for longer than you would like, and it is quite possible that you will become so frustrated that you will be unable to progress simply because you are too frustrated to do RIGGED PARKOUR correctly. Oh, and there are no checkpoints. You restart at the beginning when you die. When you finally make it through the parkour, the final boss fight is... shooting a dog a couple of times with a pistol. After completing this mission I was legitimately angry that I had wasted my time on such an anticlimactic ending. I haven't been angry at a game in over 14 years. I played through the high-population days of every single Dark Souls entry when you couldn't go three steps away from a bonfire without being raided. I was *immune* to being angry at games until this mission cured that immunity. Thanks, guys.From a game design perspective this mission is utterly dreadful. You should NEVER treat your player unfairly in a required mission, especially one using new mechanics (you literally run into zero wisps or parkour segments before this mission), and especially not one that bars you from progressing through the game several hours in unless you slog through it. The original STALKER games had missions that were difficult and could kill you if you messed up. They were hard if you made mistakes, but I have played through all three of them, Call of Chernobyl, *and* Anomaly. I have NEVER felt as if any official OR unofficial STALKER game has given me a mission that is completely unfair until STALCRAFT. As you progress northward, you will be forced to put more and more time into collecting resources which you can still lose in the event of a freak accident or getting ganked/camped by someone with vastly superior gear whose base is five feet away from the exit to the location which you need to reach in order to progress. This requires you to use a metal detector (which takes your primary slot up if you equip it, by the way, leaving you vulnerable while collecting resources) to pick up the third tier of loot. That would be fantastic if the area surrounding the third tier weren't always completely saturated in bandits (opponent faction's players), forcing you and any other players you're with to huddle in the bottom right part of the Garbage. By the way, material spawns are not client-side, so if multiple people are looking for caches in one spot, no one will get any resources. That means that in order to actually find resources, your options are to spend a long time in a spot where there are a lot of friendlies but you will get nothing done, or go find resources in an area where there are definitely enemy players looking for you. If you do the first, you might find resources every now and again, and you'll have to squirrel them away a few at a time. That means grinding for hours. If you do the second, there is a coin flip chance that an enemy squad will shoot you while you're collecting and steal any resources you did collect, making you feel like torturing yourself with option #1.I think I enjoyed getting beaten with a switch when I was a child more than I enjoy collecting resources after tier 2. Oh, and tier 4 is actually even worse. From what I understand, it keeps on getting progressively more difficult to get resources without dying to players who out-gear you as you move up the chain.The game is otherwise extremely fun. The devs being the spiritual embodiment of the teacher asking "Well why didn't you go to the bathroom during break?" several hours into the game, however, is not. I am very disappointed to write this review, as the game has a ton of potential and frankly I could see myself turning it into a regular piece of my video game hobby. As of right now, however, the devs have made the game feel intentionally designed to be hostile for the STALKER faction, and this one mission is so dreadfully designed that I cannot bring myself to give the game a good review.Update:After tripling my playtime since the initial writing of this review, I still cannot entirely recommend the game to a new player as much as I do enjoy playing the game after already becoming an established STALKER. The grinding portion of the game is entirely doable and the gameplay cycle is reasonable and enjoyable if you have the patience to farm resources for a couple dozen hours to buy new gear. Because I'm used to that and the gunplay is more than passable, I enjoy playing.However, the previous issues I noted with the game still intensify later on in the gameplay loop, and there is not much more indicative of this than the persistence of camping the STALKER spawn in the Bar, and around the faction (Duty or Freedom) bases. It is entirely possible (and even likely) that you will leave the Bar or your faction base only to be shot in the back while you are leaving by someone who is wearing armor and a weapon which vastly outperforms yours, but because they have put on a lower end backpack and taken off their pistol or primary, their gear level is equivalent to yours and they are allowed to join your server to camp your spawn.Several times, I have left the Bar on the STALKER side only to come face to face with gunshots as the players at the entrance are repeatedly dying to bandits using gear one or even two tiers higher than them, thanks to the ease with which the balancing system is exploited. In fact, yesterday I exited the Bar and was immediately executed by a man with armor and a weapon which were each two tiers higher than mine- this means that my chances of killing this man alone were virtually null even if I fired first and by surprise attack. Fortunately I was not alone, and so (after dying a couple of times) a friend and I were able to kill him by combining shots from both of our weapons at once. Despite the fact that we knew where this man was, attacked him first, and took him by surprise, one of us still almost died and the other was heavily injured.The developers replied to my prior review, but did not address most of what was said, instead preferring to point out that they would be updating the game with a new movement system and that people are distributed based on skill and gear level. Well, that is all well and good, but it does not stop people from simply taking unnecessary gear off (like backpacks and sidearms) to lower their gear levels artificially.I am patient enough to handle this over and over again because I am used to this sort of gameplay loop. Will the average new player be able to say the same? No, and therefore I cannot yet change my negative review.

If you're a fan of the STALKER franchise and have been waiting to try it out in an online multiplayer setting, this game is definitely worth a shot. You're hunting with a metal detector with no range items that only spawn on probably 1/3 of the map but aren't instanced so every other [allied] player is also competing for you with them. At the time of writing this review I have 1 Stalker character at the Bar and 2 Bandit characters at Photon-2 both on the NA server. I don't believe I have every single ounce of information in the game to make a concrete review, but generally this is my perception so far.-TL;DR I like game but game have problem that annoy me and othersHands down one of the best Stalker multiplayer games to date, with a shockingly friendly community, with a decent progression system.-First thing's first, this IS NOT a straight rip of the Stalker games. It follows a linear progression system with weapons, armor and other equipment, where you need to gather materials and turn them in to the gun merchant at each respective base in order to get your new swag, with each part of the map having it's own separate and unique materials to gather.-Pve is"okay", the AI isn't terrific but that isn't too much of a bother for me. The mutants basically run straight at you and the Human AI enemies have laser accurate aim, which is a bit of a challenge but not impossible. I don't want to excuse lazy coding or game play elements, but to me the pve is alright, despite what some reviews will say.-Pvp so far for me has been fun up until I got to the Bar (Will discuss the oh so ever controversial bar), then It's not so fun. Generally, If you get the drop on some one first then you will kill them most of the time, and vice versa. A little annoying that recovery is almost impossible, but at the same time, It teaches you that you have to be methodical about your movements and keep a keen vision on the landscape and not to make stupid moves.Pvp up until the Bar is pretty balanced (Granted that you don't run into any smurfs, though this hasn't happened to me yet). The Swamps and Cordon, everyone basically has the same level of gear and normally have the same level of play time, so it's pretty balanced, not much else to say about that.-"Forced into pvp" I see a lot of people complain about this, but let's be real... IT'S A PVP GAME AT HEART! Yes, I know it's a big pill to swallow and I'm sorry that we can't all be Billy Bad ass over here and win every engagement, but if you play your cards right then you will get out alive in most situations.But to shed some light on the "Forced into pvp" complaint I see a fair amount of is this: Some quests require you to go into Bandit country or Stalker territory. While Stalkers tend to get the short end of the stick with this one where they have to go into Bandit controlled territory more often, It's not the end of the world. Ask around Attaman's or Garages (Stalkers Bases) for help and you'll usually find 1 or 2 kind souls to help you through it.-There is a bit of a balancing issue between Stalkers and Bandits where Bandits normally get an easier time with shorter travel time between all 3 bases and the fact they control the better half of the Cordon. This is a bit balanced out with Dark Valley being 10x better than Agroprom. But yeah, this is a valid complaint and does feel like you are being a bit stifled as a Stalker.-The Infamous Bar... So, I've seen a lot of people complain about the Bar and pretty much brushed it off because it never seemed well thought out and always just felt like people would get killed there and come here to complain and downvote the game with a very informative review of "THE BAR SUCKS!!!", so hopefully I can paint the picture to hopefully help you decide if the game is worth it or not.-The Bar is a base (The last one you'll be at in the game) where both Bandits, Stalkers and their respective sub-factions all play nice with each other and do all their shopping and hanging out. The Bar has 2 entrances (Not counting the sub-faction doors), Bandit door on one side and the Stalker door on the other. Now, you might start to see the issue with this...Too many times when I'm trying to do some farming around Rostok (On the Stalker side) I always end up coming across a Bandit with late game equipment (Guns and Armor that do more damage and protects better) and a 4 man squad that ends up tearing me to pieces; and I'm not alone with this issue. I see in the kill feed and on the map so many other lower level Stalkers in Rostok also falling victim to these Bandit goon squads that run around with impunity on the Stalker side, just taking out every single Stalker they find.This issue tends to be worse at night on the NA server, but during morning or daytime It's easier to avoid Bandits, which I am not excusing this massive problem in the game. The Bar is probably single most infuriating part about the game, and a massive oversight that needs to be fixed.I get it, It's S.T.A.L.K.E.R., It's supposed to be a bit unforgiving and the horrors of the Zone are supposed to come to the forefront; but is it too much to ask for possibly a couple of more Stalker camps in Rostok to atleast dissuade these Bandit death squads from running around freely with no challenge to them? I'm not recommending a wall between the two parts of Rostok because that would massively hinder pvp and being that pvp is a core part of the game would not work.That's pretty much all I gotta say about the Bar. Hopefully I painted enough of a picture on why so many people complain about it and offered a helpful suggestion to the Devs (Don't laugh, I know they won't read this)I hope this review was helpful, If you feel like I was missing something in it or I'm just flat out wrong about some of it then feel free to comment.

You'll notice a going trend of people with ungodly hours into this game giving the majority negative reviews. I guess this is my turn to join them.Listen, coming from a developer myself I appreciate the work that was put into the project. Despite the world being a 1:1 ripoff of the STALKER series, its done relatively nicely with the Minecraft/Roblox aesthetic the developers bottlenecked themselves to, and the gun selection/customization is great especially for fans coming from games like MW2 2022 and Tarkov. I like the story and the characters introduced relatively enough as well. The game certainly promises a lot to the player within the advertising and first ~10 hours of gameplay.Thats about everything I liked, and 50% of the reason is because of everything STALKER did, not these devs. Which isn't inherently a bad thing, but STALKER belongs to GSC not EXBO.The most disappointing part of this game is the debilitating feeling of lack of play testing and built against fun mechanics. I feel like 90% of the obstacles presented to the players weren't play tested enough, if at all. A developer should always be asking themself "is what I am making fun?", and as long as the answer is "no", your game is not ready for play testing. Your game is not ready for release. And thats okay. We should normalize developers taking more time with their product in order to not waste a consumers time.EXBO, your game is not fun. You did not ask yourselves if your game was fun enough.When you're not running into anomalies every 5 or so meters, its mutants, or mutants that knock you back into the anomalies. I wouldnt mind the anomalies if they were more spread out, as they feel randomly dotted rather than carefully placed in order to keep the player on their toes or even hell, making them loss frequent but also dynamic. Then theres the problem with PvP, and I have a lot to say about this.EXBO, your "gear score" system is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Plain and simple. I am okay with being presented with an unfair challenge in PvP, what I am not okay with is the unbalance between choosing STALKER and Bandit, and said Bandits two, even three armor or gun levels above where I am in packs of 5+ and being placed into their lobbies, over and over again disallowing me from even exiting the Bar.I do not find it fun to fight every AimLab caffeine infused autistic Russian on the planet, all day every day, just to access the grind.And the grind, what the ♥♥♥♥. I counted 40 or so hours of farming Pickle, Alpha Data Fragments, Radio Parts and Chernobyl Chamomile for the upgrade from the SVT to the SVD, and its the worn variant. Not even just a regular SVD. Theres still another variant I need to grind for. With 1600+ barter items in total I need to collect. The fact that anyone on the dev team thought that was a good use of someones time, is delusional.I am okay with a grind in games, what I am not okay with is now I need to cut class/work time and socializing in order to unlock a gun I have free access to in any other game in what, a few hours or less? It took me 40 hours after reaching the Bar to get the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SVD? That's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane.I am done with your game. I am not playing it again. I'm sorry, EXBO. I cannot support your project anymore as much as I want to. It is not worth the time required to do anything substantial.God help you if you have any future projects. I hope you improve from now until then. And please, if you need help, ask the players for it. Please listen to us as players in order to improve, because if you create another experience like Stalcraft, I guarantee you will fail, your company will fail, and I really don't want to see that happen. You have a very talented team, that is unbelievably misguided.

this game had so much potential to be good but ultimately it falls flat in too many fundamental aspects that make it unenjoyable:-wind anomalies are near invisible, and the more you progress in the game, the more numerous they are. anomalies are a cool and characteristic part of the Stalker universe, but these cannot exist in a FPSMMO game like this for them to retain their charm or their purpose.- no fast travel in a setting like this makes about 70% of your game experience running to and from base and collecting your body when you die. throw in possibly running into semi-invisible wind anomalies that guarantee kill you makes this a completely miserable feature for a 'fast-paced' open-world FPSMMO.- the level of power/gear creep also makes this game unplayable for anyone semi-casual or, frankly, unable to devote hours upon hours a day into this game. this is usually the case in any given game, but the lack of any meaningful post-death information makes it all the more frustrating.the real reason for this negative review comes from the fact that the devs themselves market this as a fast-paced and 'skill-driven' shooter, but not only does the game lack the situational HUD alerts that better FPS games include to show where you're getting hit from, the existence of near-invisible, guaranteed-death anomalies automatically hamper any sort of meaningful combat experience. again, throw in no way to fast travel or save checkpoints outside of major bases, the game quickly devolves into Wasteland Running Simulator.both the story and writing are very bland and chud-like.as a fan of the Stalker franchise and both FPS and MMO, I really wanted to like this game. on paper, it should be great, but there are too many foundational flaws of both the FPS and MMO element that make this completely unenjoyable for any sort of meaningful gameplay experience.

I would like to recommend this game but I can't. tl;dr it's grindy, overly punishing, and the playerbase is apathetic and willing to push new players away if it means they can be on top of the leaderboards (or just their personal k/d I suppose.)The game starts with an excellent proposition: STALKER, but multiplayer, with factional PVP. Sounds really great to me; but what's not shown to you for maybe the first 30 hours and while you're blasting through the main story quests is how bad the underlying mechanics are. Early on you're lured in with low bars to entry, new guns aren't that hard to get you just need to scrape the money and materials together with a couple runs out into the respective area you want the gun from - meaning that if you want to start an upgrade barter tree from the beginning it means going back to noobtown (note: this is not necessary as you can just pay in barter materials but it'll be more without bringing a tier lower weapon in the tree to trade in). While you're out in the wilds of The Zone gathering materials you have the opportunity to kill or be killed by other players of the opposite faction, your choices are Bandit or Stalker with subfactions coming in later for the endgame PVP areas. But it's just that simple: are you Bandit or Stalker? Kill em - there's no other interaction available. Early on your material hauls will be inconsequential, but as time goes on that material cost skyrockets to HUNDREDS for a single upgrade in weapon (not including the actual upgrade system which you need to do to squeeze more damage out of your gear.) Herein lies the problem: the map is split conveniently into halves that are intended to be your farming zones, with a slightly better one in the middle where you will likely encounter more resistance. In practice this means, during primetime, people farming in their respective zones will be rudely killed by the people who already farmed up long ago and got their top tier PVP gear. You will not get your materials back as they will either price gouge you on them when they sell them back or they will just sell them for pennies to a vendor.Gear level, it's a mystery in some aspects. If you jump into the season pass or get a lucky crate from it that gives you cool gear, and you decided to try it on then oops! You just put yourself permanently into a higher gear level. This is the culmination of your artifacts, armor, and weapon and as far as I can tell upgrades do not contribute to this level, only the base stats. Want to help a new friend join the game and catch up? You can't downgrade, you can only bring them up to your level (thankfully temporarily) when partying up together. This is a double edged sword, on one hand I am hamstringed into fighting insanely powerful, endgame weapon wielding, +10 (or higher) gear upgraded, game VETERANS. For your notes I only have maybe 15-20 kills and more than twice that in deaths. Your K/D also plays a part, but as it's a proprietary formula people can only guess to what extent it affects your matchmaking into instances. Now, on the other hand this prevents smurfing, but I would say that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ primarily because if the game was designed in a smarter way to calculate gear score it would be a non issue.PVP is exhilarating. PVP gets my blood going dude, it's so much fun. When you die to a guy who outplayed you I just laugh and reup my ammo and meds to come back. But I can't do that anymore, I've hit a wall. Let me lay it out for people who have never played this game:Each tier of weapon requires different tiers of materialsOne of these materials is called Dopestone, the only ways to get it are from daily or weekly quests with a rate of 20-40 per quest, respectively, or from killing human NPC enemies in 'events'. Events being locations in the world that have a set of enemies such as "Zombie Group" or "Stalker Camp," things of that nature. The AK-103 which is my next weapon in line costs ***899*** to get. If we work this out at the BEST possible rate running events dropping 11-15 dopestone per completion (which require you to get all the kills or otherwise it's shared and you get lower amounts) I would need to complete roughly 75-80 human NPC enemy events, of which there are maybe 2-4 at a time on an instanced area. This is doable, but drags on and is severely boring. Now add in other players competing for these resources, add in PVP spontaneously occurring in these farming zones where you will now be losing all of your farm (go to start, do not collect $500), and the likelihood of campers on the path out of the safezone hubs to where you're trying to reach.All of these makes it a supremely frustrating experience when all I want to do is have fun fighting with these people. If you want to have good PVP experiences why are you coming into farming zones to knock peoples' heads off? It doesn't make any sense, you're not fostering a playerbase, you're not fighting the people who are equipped to fight you, you're running into what I'd class as a noob area or just a PVE area to gank people who actually want to gear up to have good fights with you. It makes no sense to me other than basic bullying, basic ego stroking, and it will be the death of this game if things don't change.Right now the grind keeps the hardline core players hooked, on upgrades, armors, and the season pass crap that is being injected into many games. This game is free so some cosmetics are purchase only, some are lootboxed out, but I would say the FOMO mechanics are fair enough that I can't complain about them in a free game I spent 0 dollars on.All that said, if my barrier for entry is to spend the better part of 64 hours grinding, I'm done here. The drip is unreal later on but the cost of my time to acquire it is beyond reasonable. Things need to change, but they won't, as I imagine like any free game this is entirely geared towards the whales who will continue to keep it alive and trick many new players into sinking far too many hours into it before coming to terms with the sunk cost fallacy. I want this game to be fun.As an addendum to my review, as of 9/4/24 I bought an M4 off the market and dumped resources into it. I actually have fun in PVP now, it feels like I actually have a chance to kill someone. I have a massive problem with gear score however. If I want to play with my friends or some other players, I get jumped ahead into their gear score bracket and I'm facing end game weapons and armor. The solution? Just don't play with them? Sure - so then what's the point of playing this game solo. It's a multiplayer game, multiplayer STALKER right? So they can't downgrade and join me they're ALWAYS their higher gear level and we are ALWAYS matched up with higher gear score people, which isn't fun. The easiest solution? Just let us know how matchmaking works, let people downgrade, and if veterans want to go stomp noobs they need to use their garbage gear. Make the checks more stringent in the mystery algorithm. Some of these noobs are getting dropped wicked ridiculous gear from the season pass or from crates, which they're completely ignorant of. I've lost two friends potentially playing this game due to this, they just get absolutely wrecked when they're less than 3 hours in.As of 9/5/24Serum is the hard to acquire material for barter and upgrades at the end of the game. You need anywhere from 50-90 serum with the only ways to get it being weekly quests (that drag on way too long) and from the shop where you can use the free season pass currency to get it. It used to be 250 season pass units of currency and now that the new one is here it costs ONE THOUSAND units of currency to get A SINGLE SERUM. And these were the same devs who said they were 'committed' to making the grind less frustrating.

Basically budget Tarkov but with stalker anomalies and monsters. PvP can completely halt any quest progress with griefers/seal clubbers intentionally camping quest locations specifically to farm new and helpless questers. They even get to hide behind the bots that constantly respawn at these points, allowing them to mow down newbies without ever taking any damage.There are some protective measures for newbies to prevent from losing basic gear, but the tiny amount of ammo that's covered by those measures is exhausted immediately and every bullet afterwards is free to loot once you die. So you're left with the option to take enough ammo and lose it all to a griefer or take just enough to fill your magazines and be left helpless when they're empty.There are all sorts of bugs from mobility interactions with the terrain to randomly getting a partially loaded magazine despite having tons of ammo (you do not have multiple magazines like Tarkov).To no real surprise the community is extremely toxic and the fanboys are in a constant state of frothing at the mouth.If you want Tarkov, go buy Tarkov. If you want Stalker, you can get the whole bundle for like $10 if you watch the sales. There's really no good reason to choose this game.[Update]The further you progress the worse everything gets. Camping and cheats are rampant, wall hacks have sky-rocketed very recently, and there's nothing you can do about it other than living in the safe zone bases, never progressing. There's no sort of balancing so regardless of what gear you bring you'll very likely run into someone who's gear can shrug off whatever you have and pop your armor and health in a split second from hip-fire. Good example from earlier today, I had a complete low-end loadout, weapons and all, and I get ROFL-stomped by a single camping bandit with all gear that's literally the tier below max (think tier 3 vs like tier 11).Your allies are just as detrimental as the enemy in terms of your resource progression, part of which is due to terrible designs within the game. When you die you drop a bag with all your non-bound gear (ammo, heals, un-equipped armor plates, etc.) as well as a "lost bag" that is basically a bundle of specific resources that you had. Even if you die from monsters or bots, most allies will steal all the items they can and MAYBE give your "lost bag" back. - Then there are resources that only drop from roaming enemies, mini-events, and hidden caches. Because these events and caches are very limited, allies will hover around you letting you do all the work then swoop in and hoover up all the important loot. There are client side reward boxes that are granted to guarantee some reward to those who participate in the mini-events (mostly just junk that can be sold for worthless money), but that doesn't apply to roaming bandits and caches or the enemies killed in the process of the event. Caches and enemy corpses are server side, so the second a cache or corpse is exposed anyone can take the contents. Then of course, apply these same things but to maps full of both factions, and you need an absolutely insane amount of these resources (less-so if you only focus on a single weapon and armor tree and never experiment).I've been putting off progressing into the point where you join a sub-faction (splits the faction into 2 that are hostile towards each other, in other words more players are going to kill you) but everything I've heard about that aspect of the game is terrible. There's also no real info to base a decision on, you only get a 1-2 sentence summary of their ideologies. Unless you want to play in the bandit faction, camping and screwing over stalkers over the entire time, you're better off playing anything else. You might only have a limited window though, who knows how long people are going to put up with it.I hear that this has existed for awhile as a mod but I think the standalone release is just trying to bank on the excitement for Stalker 2.[Update 1.5]After even more progression, things are several times worse than before. Not only are there massive squads of campers at every transition but there are dozens of people at any given time abusing the transition system itself to grief people. Not sure if it's a hack or another exploit but they've also figured out how to kill players even though the target/victim has player invulnerability from transitions. I haven't even finished the story and the game is borderline unplayable at this point in the game.[Final Update]Finally finished the story, some decent ideas but overall much more pain than it's worth. It also basically requires specific gear to be used in order to complete, and even then it's a big headache. I also get that they want to showcase their "parkour" mechanics, but it's the weakest mechanic in the game and so much of the main story revolves around it.Everything is still very terrible in general gameplay. The servers are garbage, cheaters galore, camping squads at every corner, and the long overdue updates that were supposed to release month/s ago are now pushed for several more months (not that they'd accomplish anything). Stack on the insane grind and it's even more of a nightmare. You also have no allies, just vultures waiting to clean up whatever is left of your corpse. Those vultures will also dispose of your "lost backpack" rather than mailing it back (which is free to do).I was going to join a sub-faction and explore the rest of the North zones to get the achievements before uninstalling but I got completely fed up. I've still heard nothing good about joining them, but I know they spend more time arguing and hunting down each other than the actual enemy faction. I also hear that the North is basically "who has the best cheats" territory, so I doubt I would've even made it to the two zones I needed to visitI know it's free and all, but save yourself the skull splitting headache and just pass on without a second thought.

But that fails in lower areas, such as Swamp, and sometimes even Cordon. There are  not enough players with high gear to have a high gear Swamp or Cordon, so it forces them to get put in low level servers where they grief. I played this game back when it first came out for US servers, finished it, and played it about half a year after release, finished it. The second time I played through was much more difficult due to other high gear players, in the starting areas. Once you get to bar, that's where 40% of the players are. So you get a good balance, once you're there.The second issue I have, the grind. Now I know Im going to hear something saying Im not trying hard enough. Well, its still crazy how much you have to grind. I get its an MMO and I get its supposed to take time to grind late game, but it gets insane. For example, going from the "Worn RPD" to the "RPD". To get to the RPD, you need Thousands of materials. I had PREMIUM (which increases the amount of loot you get from encampments) and I spent over a week, about 5 hours a day, if not more, trying to get it. Mind you, you can spawn right in the area if you join a faction (I was mercenaries), and walk right outside to get these. Now I wouldn't mind it as much, if it weren't for the fact that it is literally just walk from one encampment to another, over and over. Now I will mention that I never got a chance to to do clan wars, so I can't say nothing on that.Third, the events, they are kind of mid after a while. If it's not a frisky boar looking to scoop you up, a man-bear-piglet who wants to face-smash or some NATO soldiers who just wants to wipe your stains from the remnants of civilisation, then some sort of bizarre sparkle, windpoof or suckbomb is out to fondle your entrails. My time with this game has been pretty rocky since I first booted it up. Got told by friends to hop on and try it out, and that it'll be a good time. I will say to start I am biased on one thing and that's the factions. Bandits and Freestalkers first and foremost as I haven't reached the grind needed to be any of the other sub-factions. Anyway, right out the gate I will say that the maps seem pretty lenient towards Freestalkers in the South. Bandits after reaching Cordon only really get control of a small section and have most of their quests focused in the Southern parts near the Loner spawn, giving one side an edge with PVP. Both sides camp that center bridge since it's the only effective way to get anything done. Once you move on to Dark Valley and Agroprom that's when I noticed a slight problem in map balancing. Loners get a straight away road that leads where they want into Garbage and The Bar (Rostok), while Bandits have this inferno to lead into The Pit which then connects into Rostok, or their choice of 2 separate entrances into Garbage. It's strange but whatever. Rostok is also a hellhole if you try to go anywhere, even outside your spawns. Some of the quests also have the same issue - I won't mention which outside one that leads into an Instance where both factions can still PVP against one another, even when they still need to progress through a teleporter. That level is flawed as well with a bunch of constant enemy spawns that harass the player trying to go through and can actively kill you at the right points in time. Even with those issues aside my main problem comes from the pseudo looter-shooter mechanics. You resupply at safe zones for your faction; get meds, ammo, and other supplies needed for quests and run out there to finish them. Anything you gather outside your armor, weapons, and a select few bound items will then drop upon death. The issue lies in the fact that bartering materials will get put in this bag only /you/ can open. Another problem? Yes. If whoever kills you or finds your body doesn't auction or send your bag back, those items are lost forever. They can't even get gains out of killing aside from ammunition and meds mostly. What PVP mainly boils down to in the grand scheme is just screwing over someone else's progress because you have the ability to. Some can find that as a problem, I don't mind it. What bothers me is the anomalies and how they are seemingly placed everywhere without a second thought whatsoever. Black holes come to mind specifically as a horrifically designed anomaly with zero counter play outside just avoiding it outright if you can ever tell the difference between it or a Vortex. What does it do? Raises you up into the air, negating any chance of escape and then killing - throwing all of your items around until they de-spawn or some brave bastard runs over and grabs it. If it wasn't for Black holes specifically, I'd have a higher opinion of the game - they are such a massive point of frustration for me, and many players I've seen in the chats. The other anomalies usually have obvious tells so you can avoid them, or don't instantly kill you so you can at least move out of the way to survive. Electros let you activate them for a short period so you can run through, for example. For a free-to-play game I'd honestly say it's above average in polish out the gate - I've personally not encountered bugs but the ones my friends have are usually graphical and nothing that breaks game play. The customization system for your weapons is reminiscent to Tarkov's for weaponry. Changing a lot of individual components for stat gains. The progression over all is grindy, but not to the point of tedium unless you die a ton (it will happen). Currently at 20 hours I sit with 200k in the bank, fully modded AKM and a Trapper suit on my Bandit and am at the Bar. If nothing else, and for the sake of a tl;dr. If you like semi-hardcore shooters with punishing deaths that hinder your progression exclusively, this isn't terrible. There will be minor annoyances that add up into frustrating balls sometimes but it's bound to happen. It's especially enjoyable in groups when starting out - which I do recommend. The solo experience is surprisingly difficult yet rewarding if you survive your expeditions. I am pleasantly surprised nonetheless and do recommend the game for those people who want a semi-hardcore shooter that can emphasize squad-play and is free. Just be mindful of a potentially long grind, frustrating enemy/anomaly placement, and the inevitable PVP encounters that leave you scratching your head. Such is par for the course. To note: I did leave plenty out of the review as I am writing this late. If anyone wants to add on with missing points, feel free. I do enjoy the game myself but find it irritating beyond belief in some points. Over all, solid product for a Stalker MMO.

Stalcraft is fun. It's centered around grinding and PVP, which means it's not for everyone. In my opinion, the satisfaction of progression outweighs the negatives of the game. You can tune your play-style to decide how much PVP effects you, which is why I don't believe it has ever been an issue apart from early game.Onto the point of early game, it is where I believe Stalcraft struggles. Better guidance and training wheels could be implemented to help players who have minimal experience with the "S.T.A.L.K.E.R" element of the game. I've seen new players who don't know any better get themselves caught up in unnecessary PVP, which frustrates them.By the time you reach the north, you'll have invested enough time to know what you're doing. The game excels in atmosphere, creative quests, narrative, and mechanics. However, its greatest strength—emphasizing PvP—is also its biggest flaw. If PvP is central, there needs to be better player balance for fairness. While I acknowledge my skill level isn't the best, that makes the disparity in stats even more frustrating.There are some questionable design choices. The game limits gear differences for zoned quests but not for open-world PvP, leading to experienced players preying on those with lower gear levels. This creates a frustrating environment, especially when "Credit Card warriors" camp quest areas to steal valuable drops. If you can balance gear gaps for zoned quests, it shouldn't be too difficult to apply the same logic to open-world PvP.This imbalance causes unnecessary frustration, particularly for players who don't spend money on gear upgrades. While I understand the challenges of creating enough zones to match players by gear level, there are other ways to mitigate the issue. For example, you could prevent players with vastly different gear levels from looting each other's items or offer a low-cost item to protect drops during quests.This situation reflects a disconnect between the developers' vision and actual player behavior. There's no incentive for higher-level players to protect lower-level ones from griefers. Implementing a system where players can hire others as bodyguards, with payment in a new currency, could encourage cooperation. Making the game less enjoyable for those who don't spend money isn't a game mechanic; it's manipulation.

Its Not-Stalker in an MMO as a semi-hardcore shooter. While you are not losing significant progression, the entire world is open to PVP from the opposite faction/s. On death, you lose most of your items, including ressources you need to upgrade your current equipment which are currently on your person. Luckily, there are several steps you can take to prevent that, such as a player-number indicator next to your minimap, as well as teaming up with other players or putting down stashes to hide away your items. Luckily, exit camping is not much of a thing due to several circumstances, one of which being that the ressource items are bound to your character so that they can not be used by another player. They CAN be sold for marginal profits or on the auction house back to you however, so there IS incentive to actively kill other players aside from your own survival. You will NEVER lose your weapons or armor though.Stalcraft's Endgame has recently received a massive overhaul which included quite a few quality of life changes and vast changes to the map. There will be a rework in for the early and midgame sometime in the future as well as of the writing of this review (August, 2024)As of right now, we have a lot more East-Bloc weapons than NATO-weaponry, although the arsenal is being continously expanded upon. Currently, gear progression is being time-gated by "Serum", a Daily/Weekly ressource you receive from quests, up to 16 a week, where one end-game weapon or armor will cost you 65 Serum. It IS possible to receive more Serum through Non-Time-Gated PVP activities, although rarely and chance-based, as well as needing gear to compete in the first place. There is currently a rework of this system in the planning stages, but there is not a lot more information surrounding this.Outside of time gate, Progression starts out fast and turns very slow towards the endgame, which makes planning for what gear you want and targetted farming a necessity. Matchmaking is gear-based much more than it is skill-based. There are a few breaking points which will pit you with much better-geared players, which can make gameplay feel frustrating to rage-inducing at times. Luckily, for most of the game, each faction receives their own "farm"-maps which give around half the rewards of the mixed-PVP maps, which makes deciding on where to farm a risk-reward calculation.Your best bet is to bring a friend or two and help each other out. This will split the rewards, but even out the odds in firefights and make most of your lost items upon death recoverable by them. Thankfully, supplies are cheap and easy to come by.As for what factions exist:There are the Stalkers, which are the "good guys" of the story (they sound like nerds from a chess club)And there are Bandits, the "bad guys" (they sound like they ate gravel mixed with broken glass for breakfast)At a later point in the game, the player can choose which subfaction to join.Stalkers become Not-Duty and Not-Freedom, a.k.a. Frontier or Rise. The former are a neofascist paramilitary group that wants to murder every mutant the zone has produced and generally views the zone as a threat to humanity while the latter are a bunch of furries who would turn the Not-Bloodsuckers into their anime-waifu-furry-girlfriend if given the chance. (Not joking, there is a furry Rise-member in the game...)Bandits on the other hand can join either the Mercenaries, soldiers of luck and fortune, booze and money, drugs and hookers, who will sooner shoot you in the back than give you a helping hand. Also, they are wusses who have to team up 5v1 to land a kill or the Covenant, religious zealots that view the zone as a punishment from god upon humanity for its sins and which needs to be cleansed of all infidels inshallah.As for current populations: It seems a lot more Stalkers join Frontier than Rise, whereas Mercenaries and Covenant seem fairly balanced.There are further systems such as clan/guild wars, instanced PVP and so forth, but you are better off experiencing it for yourself.As for monetization: This game features a Premium model (which is necessary to receive the full 16 serum/week) AND a 3-month-battlepass while allowing for MTX to increase the rewards from the BP, albeit at highly expensive prices. Both the Premium Membership and Battlepass are obtainable with ingame currency at reasonable prices (around 3-6 million Rubel each where you can earn 50-100k Rubel within 20-30 Minutes of efficient grinding or while farming for ressources passively) Pay to Win seems to very rarely be an issue as you can still easily drop someone with a non-Battlepass weapon/armor by simply being slightly better than them. Weapons are all fairly balanced from an objective standpoint, which of course will not feel that way when you die towards the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemy for the third time because you didnt pay attention while clearing the proto-anomaly you needed for your daily quest and that motherf**** snuck up on you AGAIN f***- as I said, the game can be frustrating at times.If you are not afraid of receiving death threats in Russian or Polish, feel free to try out the game. As is common with Stalker-themed games: It has a large Russian/Eastern European playerbase and a Russian developer. Luckily, the Discord has a dedicated English-speaking community too. Chances of meeting someone who speaks English at least somewhat fluently seems to be around 65% - just remember that this game is meant to be an MMO and therefore progression WILL be slower towards the end to keep you from achieving everything within a few days. Think of it more in terms of Classic WoW - progression is a journey and that journey takes time.

Stalcraft is the world of S.T.A.L.K.E.R with Minecraft graphics, Largely faithful to the S.T.A.L.K.E.R world and lore but with a few changes and alterations. Out of all the online Stalkergames so far the closest to that "Zone" experience" people loved from the original single player games.The game itself is pretty decent, but it also has some major problems. weapon balance is all over the place, the player base is literally divided and extremely hostile and the early game can easily be deadlocked by a player of the other faction being in the same zone as your story quest. The game is also very "Modern" and uses a crafting system for your equipment which can greatly imbalance the late game.Pros: *The most like S.T.A.L.K,E,R SoC and Clearsky out of the other choices.*A great Stalker game to play with your friends.*A Beautifully crafted and realized world.*True to the S.T.A.L.K.E.R experience.Cons:*Early game can easily become annoying and push you to quit due to forced PvP*Certain Anomalies have bad detection and can cause annoying and unneeded deaths.*Crafting system that forces and deadlocks players towards certain weapons/armor and highly incentives a Pay2Win store.*A unbalanced combat system that quickly kills the player, often before they can detect or react.*The game has Boss fights, and the Bosses have large health pools and sometimes even Mob spawn Assistance. Mixed with a crafting system, these bosses can be impossible to fight with lower ranked equipment,  and can only be fought alone.*Limited animation which can make certain npcs or players actions highly unpredictable. *Enemy identification is difficult, its very hard to tell a enemy from an friendly and npcs can be mistaken for players.*The game has the Stalker radar on the top right, however it does not show enemies or friendlies and is disabled for quests.Overall the game has potential, but it also has alot of problems. Despite these problems I highly enjoy it and hope to see improvements in the future. Game Rating: 7/10.

This game is a lot of fun. There are a few bugs here and there but it runs great most of the time. Graphics take a little bit of getting used to, but they're not bad, just looks minecraft-y. There are a few inconsistencies, however. Like, some props on the map will have rounded edges like barrels, generators, tanks and so on, but wheels that are on cars, tractors or on the ground will be square?? It's a bit weird. Could look better if those inconsistencies were fixed. Maybe an increase in polygon counts across the board would make the game look a lot better and less like minecraft. Characters modeled like the game "Polygon" would be really cool. Speaking of characters, there is absolutely no character customization, which sucks in a major way. The least they could've done would've been a few faces to choose from. Or better, 10 different sets of eyes, 10 noses, 10 mouths and 10 hair styles and it would've been A LOT better. And I guess that would make the current face skins given out a bit pointless, but they could just split those skins into eyes, noses, mouths and hairstyles and allow the players that have them receive the same skin's parts instead. An outfit/transmog system would allow for a lot more customization too. 'Cause right now, pretty much everyone looks almost exactly same and that's just not great. Armor could be split into pieces like helmet, top, gloves, pants and boots, and that would allow for a lot more customization both in stats variety and looks. And an outfit system where you pick shoes, pants, shirt and headwear would be really cool too. Obviously all outfits fitting the theme and immersion. These would allow players to immerse themselves in the game a lot more and feel more of a connection to their character.Player housing would be really cool, too. Or clan housing.Anomalies are a bit too hard to see but I suppose that's kind of the point of them.Another thing, I think it would be better if barrel extensions allowed muzzle attachments attached onto their ends.---------------------------------------------More to the point of a review though, game is really fun, to the point of being almost addictive. PvP is tough, and unforgiving, but also makes it fun. PvE is tough as you progress, too, especially with anomalies around every corner.PvP could use some balance, especially spawns, as in most starter areas Bandits have the better spawns that are closer to most quest areas, which allows them to have an unfair advantage. That changes later on in the game, though.Overall, I highly recommend this game and as it is free, you have nothing to lose by just trying it out. Absolutely no P2W even though it's a F2P MMO. Even with the bugs and a few areas in which it is a bit lacking, it is a gem. With a few balancing adjustments, QoL and aesthetic additions this game could be a true masterpiece.

this game has great potential, but as of right now i cant really recommend it. there are moments in this game where im having fun, but sadly those moments arent as frequent as the frustration i get whilst playing this game, in a way that makes me question why anyone would think it would be a good idea to make the game the way it is.The First and Main problem i'd like to bring up is the travelling. its horrible, your character in the beginning is rather squishy and remains this way for pretty much the entirety of my current playtime. im not horrendously far in but ive upgraded my armour a good few times by this point and im still quite squishy, which is fine and what i expect. the problem however is that bases are immensely sparse, the first 2 bases are seperated by about 1.5km of space, and the 2nd and the 3rd base are probably about twice as far away from eachother, this means that while being squishy, needing materials and trying to traverse the anomalies death couldp otentially bring a near 2 kilometer journey back if lets say you're in the dump, which is about equidistant from the stalker base "the garages" and "the bar" i shouldnt need to explain why this makes the game incredibly frustrating when death can bring a roughly 10-15 minute sprint, and on this sprint there are a number of anomalies, potential players, guard outposts etc that could block your way forcing you to once again rearm your weapon and medicine. at the point of writing ive died 3 consecutive times to various sources in the zone whilst trying to just do some quests in the dump and that alone has caused me about 30-40 minutes of traversal times with 0 progress and i realise at this moment that im just frustrated with this game. it could be great but too many things are wrong with the travelling system. the movement is somewhat janky and doesnt feel fun and so to have to spend so much of the game engaging with it at threat of heavy penalisation for mis-stepping really just sucks. not to mention such a long journey makes armour plates unlikely to survive meaning you have to piss away roubles on spare plates and extra meds and ammo.lets talk about another reason why this system sucks. Bartering. lest you make the mistake of moving on from your first base to your second without first buying every single pre-requisite gun, lets hope you realise that mistake early because for some crackpot reason most later guns require pre-requisites that can only be acquired from the previous zones and thus only directly purchased from there. meaning, lets imagine for a moment that you are enjoying SMG's and so you pick up the stuff required for an UZI down in the first zone, keep using the UZI find its quite fun and take it to the next base. upon entering that base you see a cool AKS-74 you'd like to try out... well imagine your dismay at realising that the only way to get that AKS-74 is by first grabbing a worn out aks74u from the first base. so now you have to travel all the way back to the first zone and then back to the 2nd base, a 3KM round trip JUST to try out a new weapon... baffling why anyone thought this was a good idea, i mean i can only imagine the horror of finding this out when in the 3rd base area. having to travel around 10KM there and back at this point JUST to try out a new gun.a complete lack of any sort of fast travel system (sort of) baffles me in ways i cant even imagine, its like this developer thinks people LOVE to run around for an hour before they can actually do anything worthwhile, i'd say so far ive spent more time running around pointlessly than i have actually doing things i want to. need aluminium? well best get hiking over a kilometer to the area with aluminum! hope you dont die on the way! want to get some rusty metal? well even further! the tedium around the travelling system is bottomless, and it sucks because this game has amazing potential. but i dont even know how they'd fix it? my main thought was having primary and secondary base types. there are already sort of these anyway, for example in the first area you have the main base which allows you to use your storage use traders etc, then near the end of the first area and the start of the 2nd, at a rough half way point there is a mini base where there is a trader selling basic ammo and a safe zone, my idea would be to also allow these zones to double as spawnpoints, as the travelling initially isnt the big problem, its having to backtrack upon dying. having these little outposts that you can respawn at would alleviate almost all of my problems with this game, ensuring that i never have to run THAT far after a death.This has been a somewhat rambly review so far and i apologise for that. I want to move on to a seondary more minor gripe, and that is the anomalies. the anomalies in this game are.... oversaturated to say the least. in the second area the forest is absolutely teeming with vortex anomalies and blackhole anomalies, to the point where it feels like there's one every 50 feet. this consolidates the issues with travel. such a rediculous saturation of anomalies coupled with huge travel distances almost guarantees the occasional slip up causing you to be just sent straight back to your last base camp because you didnt stay completely eagle-eyed whilst running 2killomters and finally got caught in one of those near transparrent black holes that just instantly grab you and kill you. I understand this game is inspired by stalker, a game i hold in MUCH regard. the difference being that thats a save/reload game. not a fluid MMO where death leads to you being thrown back such lengthy distances, and even then THIS game the one with MORE stakes for dying still has a much HIGHER amount of anomaly saturation. it makes little to no sense from a balance perspective and i suspect its to drum up business to the store maybe? perhaps the dev thought "if i put anomalies every 50 feet and resource zones kilometers away from the nearest base perhaps people will be disillusioned with even trying to farm and just buy resources outright?" which i guess is solid thinking but i think its more likely to just drive people away.ultimately this game has GREAT potential but squanders almost all of it in my opinion, i keep finding myself playing the game because im bored and its potential is great and ive wanted something like this for so long, but find myself quickly closing out of it when i realise what i need to do and how far i need to go and how unlikely it is that its going to be even partially pleasant.
