ridiculously fun game, BUT, it has a lot of problems. These problems need serious thought and consideration by the dev team.#1 black holes - an anomaly that randomly spawns in the zone and will instantly kill players if caught in one, spawns far too often in many areas, and the tick rate for the visual effect that allows players to see it, is far too low. it is very easy for players to not see one and instantly lose their lives and loot. Additionally, black holes often spawn atop geography and can be 15 feet high, invisible to the player, and still kill them#2 Lack of spawns/ spawn saves - Players do not have the option of fast travel or to save their spawn in stalcraft. When attempting to do quests between zones of the map, players may have to travel several kilometers by foot, leading to long travel times that not even the gameplay loop of animal dens and enemy posts can help with. Players should have the option of either fast travelling between safehouses they have reached, or to save spawns to bunkers within map zones in order to reduce travel times.#3 The gameplay loop - stalcraft boasts an excellent gameplay loop that keeps players engaged in quests, destroying animal dens, or fighting enemy camps and bases. Unfortunately, these random enemy encounters often spawn extremely frequently and close to one another, with very great range of aggravation and attack. It is not uncommon for players to be swarmed by large swaths of enemy soldiers, animals, and creatures all at once, due to several spawn locations being in close proximity. There should be implimentation of limits to how close these spawns can be placed in proximity to another.#4 Interior dungeons and quests - many quests in stalcraft have indoor dungeons that require the player to fight enemies in enclosed spaces or to simply speak to NPCs or complete quests. One problem i have noticed while playing is that the escalation of fighting in these spaces is often not disclosed to the player. Often, the player will find themselves speaking with an NPC only to be fighting swaths of enemies. These enemies may often be much better equipped than the player. Stalcraft human enemies are also extremely accurate and will quickly pursue players behind cover. This leads to very one sided engagements indoors that often kill the player on their first attempt at a quest. The game will also delete player non-bound items upon death in an indoor dungeon. This often feels very punishing for the player. The development team should implement a way either for items to reappear outside of the dungeon, now despawn, or simply inform the player in a dungeon that they may be entering combat.All in all, these were the major problems that i saw while playing Stalcraft. Beside these points, i have found myself truly enjoying the game. It has a very fun gameplay loop that keeps me engaged when traversing large areas of the map, and a very friendly and helpful playerbase. The PvP aspect of the game also seems incredibly well balanced. I would reccomend this game to many MMO fans and players, with the caveat that it does have some very large problems and PvE balancing issues

Stalcraft is a MMO RPG set in an alternate STALKER reality (probably way after the events of CoP as some hints show that the original Stalker main chars existed in the world). Now, i'm going to be honest with y'all. This game is hella grindy (in the northern part of the map, the southern part [Below Rostok / Bar] is easy and fast to progress)Some of you may have read some negative reviews that just talk crap about the game, about people camping or complaining about anomalies and other aspects. So, lets talk about these in detail.Anomalies:These anomalous formations which defy the laws of physics are an essential part of the game as well as the STALKER universe in general. Most of these entities are stationary and only rotate or move when an emission occurs (Some anomalies can move in a predetermined path though). In Stalcraft, anomalies can be seen almost everywhere, with some areas having less and some having way more. You can SEE these anomalies and none of them are invisible. Some may be difficult to spot until it's too late but usually these do not kill instantly and can be escaped or easily avoided. The most common of these is the vortex, it's an anomaly that looks like a tornado forming but isn't bigger than your character. In order to avoid them you can use your infinite supply of bolts so you may see their range / hitbox. Other clues such as the visual particles and sounds it produce can help you avoid it. In case you get caught it is recommended to not stand still and try to "run" / "fly" out of it, act which can easily be accomplished unless you take too long.Players:Stalcraft consists of two main factions (and their respective sub-factions): Bandits and Stalkers. If you've read other reviews, you may have noticed that most players can be found in the Bandit faction which is technically true. Bandits have safer farming maps and their areas have little to no Stalker activity, but this does not mean that they're 100% safe, as some experienced Stalkers may choose to enter their areas in order to PVP and / or just annoy them (this does not apply to the bar most of the time, as they're probably farming pickles, a resource you get from enemy NPC camps).It is highly recommended to join the bandit faction if you're looking for a relaxed experience. But this does not mean that you cannot play Stalker. Those with the skill, patience and will are most likely to succeed in their playthrough as membes of that faction, even dominate and rise above bandit players.Do remmenber that this game revolves around PVP and making it PVE would simply become a walk on the park as the NPCs both "human" and mutants aren't the smartest nor hard to beat. The main story is great but can easily be beaten in less than 3 hours. This being said, Stalcraft is not an easy game, but it is quite entertaining, specially with friends. Do not give up but do take some rests from time to time in order to avoid getting burnt out or feeling bad if you've had a bad day of grinding.You will enjoy the game, trust me. Hope to see y'all soon in the Bar!

Writing this review at a time where I've seen most of the southern area except for the most northern zones so you know where I'm coming from in terms of experience (~40 hours in).If you have played any similar games like Stalker Online (Stay Out), Will To Live or the likes prior to this you won't have any issues getting into Stalcraft. Honestly though, the gameplay loop here is much faster here than in SO or WTL. Stock up on supplies, go farm and/or PvP, bring your gains back, improve your gear - rinse and repeat. Also, in Stalcraft you'll be picking your starting faction at the very beginning unlike SO or WTL where you can remain totally neutral. Absolutely stay away from this game if forced faction PvP is a red flag to you.PvP itself is very fast paced and TTK is quite low which is a plus because I just hate shooting at tanky players. Now some endgame PvP gods might become quite tanky, but once you get a mid tier gun with some attachments you'll be able to take down 80% of the playerbase and that is maybe 30-40 hours in if you're solo, not rushing and not spending any money on the game. I'm quite impressed with this as becoming competitive in SO sets your wallet back by hundreds of $/€ and in both SO and WTL you'll likely grind your character for 300+ hours before you can participate in PvP. Community is also great as people are generally helpful and often funny. I am a bandit of course and I love fellow bandits greeting me with stuff like "Hiya, good bandits!" to which I like to respond with "What's kickin', lil' chicken?". Stalcraft devs apparently know the STALKER meme culture pretty well and despite its darker tone in quests etc. the game isn't taking itself all too serious which is another plus. The only thing I really dislike about Stalcraft is the fact that battle pass + premium gives you a pretty huge boost on progress. That's 15 bucks every 90 days for the battle pass plus 8 bucks for every 30 days of premium... which imo you can better invest in buying other games. Take note: If you really want to be among the best in Stalcraft, you're somewhat required to swipe. Overall verdict: solid free to play game (probably the best f2p game I've played in years) and a decent option for you and your STALKER buddies to get some fast paced PvP action. There's really no need to pour any money into this game unless you want to become a top tier player. If you're looking for a massive persistent MMORPG experience this probably won't be it but Stalcraft can definitely scratch that STALKER itch. 7.5/10

This is a good game, and for the low price of free, its worth a shot. What started as a Stalker mod for Minecraft is now a complete game, with the developers still making new additions and updating content semi-regularly.On the outset, this is a survival MMO-FPS hybrid, with elements like player hubs, Stalker related missions and a narrative story, and Tarkov-style player on player violence for loot.There is a break up gameplay into roaming the map doing quests, farming mobs, doing quests for rewards and, in my experience, the rare player encounter. The farther north you travel on the map, the more difficult the enemies and environment become, necessitating player progression in the tech-tree of items that build your resistance to the various environmental hazards like radiation and thermal zone. This ties in to the regions that you will explore, each with unique resources and an expanding roster of enemies and anomalies to encounter.The zones and regions are divided between the player factions, being Stalkers and Bandits, with Stalkers mainly taking up the right side of the map and Bandits on the left, with some larger zones in the middle that contain valuable resources needed to progress.That's the basic gameplay loop, quest, explore, loot, upgrade, and move up to the next region. Repeat. My problem with this progression is twofold. The distance between safe hub zones where you can buy new gear to progress the tech tree, becomes larger and more hazardous the farther north you go, and at this time there is no fast-travel between them. This makes beginning a new tech-tree later on a real hassle, requiring you to go back through zones and risk encountering hostile players or just dying to the elements for a simple item. The second issue is that later progression gets EXTREMELY grind-y very quickly. Early on, items require two or three types of resources from a zone, and maybe a dozen or two dozen will be enough. Then suddenly as you hit the mid-way location, you need a hundred or more of a resource, and you need four or five unique types, and the means of getting them are more complicated and tedious. This might be a barrier that some won't want to invest the time in, as now you will be soft-locked into a handful of zones, running back and forth farming and doing daily quests, just to progress one item in your kit.If you're worried about losing equipment if you die, there are items that are Bound to you, including your weapons and body armour, so you won't lose those if a fight doesn't go your way. What you will lose are items like ammunition, medkits that aren't bound, any loot you've picked up and special resources for progression. The special resources will be dropped as a 'backpack', and cannot be looted by players, and likely players will put these into the games Market for auction. This incentives players to loot one another, and ransom back special resources for extra Roubles, because selling to NPC vendors will get you a pittance by comparison.I also want to say that there is a monetary side to the game, in the form of cosmetic loot boxes and a subscription package. The loot boxes are 5USD each, and each one will give you a random body armour or weapon cosmetic. If you upgrade your armour, you keep the skin, HOWEVER, if you overwrite the skin with a new paintjob, you destroy the old skin. So that 5USD is just gone. Roll again.The subscription is a weekly, monthly or annual payment plan for access to premium content, being extra daily/weekly quests where you can CHOOSE the rewards, so that cuts down on grind. You also get special bonus login rewards, which you get daily and reset each week. Overall, not a bad system, think like World of Tanks premium, and with prices ranging from 10USD to 100USD depending on the length of your subscription.Overall, I like this game. The Russian language is fun to hear coming out of Minecraft-looking Stalker characters, and the translation has some really cheesy dialogue and writing that i just find so appealing. This is a game set in the Stalker universe, handling some very horrifying and dramatic concepts, but its all packaged in a game that looks like Minecraft with guns, and that's the charm.It's worth a try for the price, and I think with more work and some love from the community and developers, it can become a worthwhile addition to the Stalker family.

Currently sitting at 201 hours, I actually enjoy this game a ton for the most part. Because I'm on the NA server there isn't a huge problem with cheating unlike EU, but, there's still the glaring problem of late game progression. I don't mind grinding for hours to be honest, but grinding for hours only to get shot by a camper in the back of the head really hurts my soul and makes me force myself out because if it happens twice in a row I'm going to completely quit this game. People who already maxed out everything refuse to go too far into the farming areas because they just want to pvp at that point while waiting for more content to explore. This unfortunately ends in it being less hardcore and being more of a, you lose simulator. Being required to have friends with you should not be a thing in an mmo for farming. Anomalies are also far too prevalent, they serve no actual purpose, they're hard to see and can also be visually bugged to not show at all. Throwing bolts 24/7 while having to sprint for 15 minutes isn't exactly riveting game play. Horrible base designs as well, I can deal with the no stalker base in cordon but the bar is completely garbage especially once you enter into subfactions. The fact that subfactions are hostile literally everywhere and yet have the same exits and entrances at major bases and the exact same farming spots is insanity. Oh you want to farm for some beta data frags? ♥♥♥♥ NO! You want to get camped right outside the entrance of your base? HELL YEAH! Admittedly the subfactions are the endgame of endgame right now so that's not too concerning. But then lets get into the pvp, there isn't much fair pvp unfortunately despite what this game will tell you. Sure it's mostly still down to who sees who first but overall you could just be ♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you use an asval against a +5 damage centurion it literally won't work; you're going to get turned on and die immediately to a vss. After 300 gear score matchmaking is so completely messed up. Seekers mockingbirds vs damaged centurions is an impossible to win matchup. However the absolute biggest problem at least to me is travel times. Even if I start spamming energy drinks, steroids, and hercules there's still going to be a 5-10 minute run to most places. Couple this with losing literally everything if you die(besides bound items like ammo bags) and you have a problem on your hands. Remember when I said getting shot in the back to lose your loot? That becomes a rampaging problem once you enter the North and guess what, you need to keep spending money to go back again and again. It's become so bad with subfactions that I take to farming at the absolute worst times ever, 2am-5am. A simple fix would be ANYTHING to allow players to farm in peace somewhat. Most people either quit or are stuck at the bar because of how screwed the pvp is there. Once again I do actually enjoy this game that's why I have spent 200 hours on it as of this point. But sooner or later they're going to need to release at least the RU content to NA and EU which will cause a cluster♥♥♥♥ with the endgame players. Because of how few players are completely done with everything it will create an even bigger rift driving even more players away from the game. If you're on the EU servers I recommend maybe playing up to Cordon guns and seeing how you like the game and if you're having good luck with cheaters. On the NA servers I can recommend playing to the max of photon guns and deciding if you're ready to put 10x the amount of time as that into the game or roping friends into this game who can consistently play with you and go everywhere with you. 2am being the best time to farm makes sense because hardly anyone is on, however when players like myself who are near to completely maxing out resort to playing that late because it's the only time we can realistically farm without campers it's a problem. I said this in a couple discussions but I really hope this game survives and betters itself to keep a solid player base. All in all, the problems I've outlined are massive and I don't see any signs of them being fixed. I can't recommend this game currently unless you have a lot of friends willing to play with you consistently. I'm definitely not a good fps player and I have no problem admitting that but when even really good players share these sentiments it's safe to say they're real issues. If you choose to play this be ready for a huge grind, really frustrating moments, and some real bs moments.Edit: Also a lot of the positive reviews seem to be shady accounts with like 2 hours saying it's a really good game. Nothing concrete but before reviewing an mmo most people usually play it for more than the tutorial, no?Back in 2024: At least on NA there do seem to be way less cheaters than before and they've fixed the problems I had with the Bar and the North. Camping is no longer incentivized nor is it possible for the most part, they have definitely added to the pay to win aspect since last time the gear being able to go up to +15 and the strongest guns can only be gotten through paying basically, unless you save for years. The grinding is still insane but I am personally fine with that. Anomalies have gotten way better and are not just everywhere for no reason as well now. I can't with the goodness in my heart recommend this game to anyone in the state it is in at the moment. Forced matchmaking, forcing to engage in high PvP areas through the main quest, constantly nerfing the battle pass and charging the same amount of money for it, time gated resources, weapon and armor upgrades that could take weeks - months, zero player to developer feedback, AI that has the same attack pattern as a minecraft skeleton and absolute zero respect of your time. This game has a lot of phenomenal aspects about it, if you're a fan of STALKER and any media associated or related to it you will love the atmosphere and art design of this game, the main story is good and only suffers heavily when you have to fight a boss. You can tell the art, animation and sound team put a lot of love and care into this game. The first 10 - 20 hours of this game can make or break your experience as it did for me a year ago until I came back for the X update. Players that have hundreds or thousands of hours on this game will make new characters and transfer over 'beginner' gear they can buy via the player ran market and camp quest and popular farming routes. The only way I was able to complete the beginner quests was from the sin I just listed, I had my friends who played the game for hundreds - thousands of hours make new accounts so they could help me push through the camping of main quest areas. Without their help I would have never made it to the Bar. Let it be known there are ZERO PvE servers and the devs have come out and said they will never include PvE only servers. This will be a problem that persists until they fix the matchmaking system or they add PvE only servers, which isn't happening. The starting area can even be more hell if you manage to get one of those really cool weapons from the crates. If you manage to get a Master or Veteran gear item from a friend or more commonly through the crates you can buy with tokens you earn in the battle pass, you equip it and have only starting gear up to Stalker, you're now put in instances with people who have full red or pink gear or a mix of the both. Unless you're lucky or get the advantage you will be doing no damage to these people and they will melt you. When factions from the end game come to bar and start spawn camping this can make progression come to a hold and make grinding feel impossible. They said they're fixing matchmaking but for a lot of people this has been a deal breaker for them. For NA servers I see a very common trend of people stopping before they make it to the mid - end game. Be it because of the horrid matchmaking or the massive increase in grinding. Okay, so you've managed to struggle through all the pain in the starting area. Now you've made it to the North. This is where the game starts to consume literal years of time. Before I break down why it can take months - years to complete this game I would like to give a quick run down of how the North is. Each side has their main spawn area, two areas where you'll be fighting the same faction and a shared middle part of the map where every faction can fight. Every side is identical in rewards and dangers the only difference is the aesthetic of the maps but mostly identical layouts. This is where you'll be grinding to enter the endgame. Each side has their own unique faction armor, story and dynamic with the faction they're fighting. Mutant areas are different and PvP is more focused into certain areas. As of right now there is a huge issue of clans coming over and spawn camping the other faction, personally, I think this issue could be watered down with a few roaming boss AI and snipers but I'm not sure. If you can manage to get through the awful design of the South then the North feels a whole lot nicer and more open. Problems start to really arise once you get settled in the North and realize how this game is designed.Doing weeklies and a single daily grants you access to resource called Anomalous Substance. This is how you'll be crafting your red item gear and some pink. As of right now it will take 1,543 Serum to obtain every single armor, weapon and container in the game. If you play this game everyday right at reset through the week you can obtain 16 Serum. I know if you're part of a clan and PvP through session battles you can obtain more but I will not be adding that statistic one is chance based and the other doesn't apply to more than half of the player base. If you play everyday through the month, doing the serum weeklies and daily's you can get 64 serum. A month of work can get you 64 serum. That is enough for a weapon or armor at the end of the tree, then you have the wait for the 8th day's daily. This invokes following a meta and not wanting to try out new weapons and armors if they're added, unless you've been playing this game for years and have been saving your serum.Playing this game non-stop, it will take you a little more than over 2 years of play time, 17520 hours roughly, to obtain every single piece from the barter trees for one faction. Serum needed to obtain:Weapons: 1,038Assault Rifles: 270SubmachineGun: 215Machine Guns: 75Sniper Rifles: 335Pistols: 48Melee: 95Armor: 465Science: 65 (an additional 65 for Cov's special suit)Combat: 260Combo: 140Containers: 40Serum you can obtain a month without a clan playing every day: 64I didn't bother trying to estimate the time to get the resources and the money you need to obtain as well. For people who want to collect weapons, modify them and make them unique it is very hard when it can take weeks - months to get one of your favorite weapons only for it to have short comings because it's not the current meta and you don't have the resources to make it +10 or +15 so you can compete with others. After you hit a certain point in the North the game no longer feels as if you're playing for fun but playing on a schedule so you can start having fun once you get the weapons you really desire. STALCRAFT:X has some serious deep rooted issues that I pray are fixed and re-balanced but as of right now with how the developers are communicating with us (yes, I understand there is a language barrier but that's why bilingual community managers exists) there seems to zero indication of change for the greater good of the game. It does seem at times they wish to line their pockets and not focus on a project that has endless possibilities with endless ways of retaining players. I'd also like to mention that there is a weapon and armor in this game that can take 2 - 3 years to obtain, 8 parts to complete each piece and you can only purchase one part for one or the other once per season. If you manage to get these then you'll never need to grind another weapon or armor piece again. TLDR; This game has a beautiful atmosphere and art direction but horribly developed. No matter what skills you have from other FPS titles it will not be held up here, meta and cheese is king. Obtaining Serum can take months even years out of your time if you'd like to 100% complete the game. With the time gated resource it also makes playing how you want to play very difficult, being a waste of possibly hundreds of hours to go for a single weapon in a tree that you like if it's not the current meta. If you don't want to play STALKER: RuneScape then I do recommend doing another STALKER play through to scratch your itch.

I want to rate this positively, i really do, but in its current state, the game isn't worth putting the hours i have into it.the top 5 negative points on this game are.- Weapon/Item Balance = There is a clear meta build in this game, it consists of 3 endgame weapons that for an average player who isn't paying for premium and is maybe getting a less then double digit hours in a week, is a near impossible thing to reach, as deaths in this game cause setbacks in the form of losing items which you need to craft/barter with to advance. If you are running anything other then this defined meta, not only are you at an extreme disadvantage, but you are also practically softlocked out of progressing by people who use nothing but the meta.- Player placement and matchmaking = Now the issue above wouldn't be so bad if the player matchmaking was good, sadly it isn't, matchmaking in this game is based on a very simple concept of item rarity, despite having a gear score, it means very little, you will be placed in lobbies with players who have unlocked the same rarity of weapons/armour as you, this sadly means that by the time you complete the main campaign (which you can do with minimum issue from the moment you enter the bar, no matter how under levelled you are) you will be given your first pink item, now, regardless if you use the item or not, you will now be put in the highest bracket of players, meaning even if your still using green/blue armour, (2-3 levels below pink) you will now be matched against players who use only pink weapons and armour. - lack of content = now up until you beat the main campaign, side quests and quests in general are abundant, but once again, the moment you reach the bar, you and every player are hit by a wall of content block, there is so little to do at the end of the campaign that players either quit, or farm until they are the most powerful they can be, and then camp the low level players this happens on both stalker and bandit side and ruins the experience for players who have just entered this content block- Cheaters = the game is currently full of cheaters, especially in the end game, as the game studio doesn't have an in game report system, has no way of perma banning players, and currently has no solid anti-cheat in place, they roam almost unchallenged, so much so that the official discord server has dedicated threads of people to name and shame cheaters, not like it ever does anything.- Camping = Gameplay is very unforgiving, but unlike titles like dark souls death is not a learning experience, Death in stalcraft is a setback, and depending on how many items you've lost or how much time is wasted, it can be a very very large one. Because the game is PvP there is no feeling of a fair death, especially when camping is so prevalent in the end game, you could spend 1-2 hours farming for resources, then return home on the safest path, but because RNGesus decided to put you into server(x) you are now unlucky enough to walk right into a spawncamper and loose those items with little to no hope in getting them back, as there is no way to decide what servers you end up in. as it stands, the game is a love letter to a franchise that hits all the wrong notes, the game isnt S.T.A.L.K.E.R and shouldnt try to be, the game is an MMO-FPS with stalker elements, and for the casual player, i cant recommend it,

Summary : A game with a ton of potential, sadly ruined by toxic PvP and player base.I've played many "hardcore" PvP and Extraction shooters over the years. Admittedly, I'm rather average at them but I've always enjoyed them. So when Stalcraft popped up in my recommended list I was excited to give it a try. Unfortunately, any good experience I had was ruined by multiple toxic players and community members making the game horrible to play. There is nothing fun about doing one of the first side missions and getting ambushed by a group of enemy players camping the objective. There's nothing fun about moving on to the main story mission and getting sniped by yet another enemy player camping near your spawn location. When asking the players if there is any way to avoid it, I was told to "get good", "skill issue", and that I should "quit and play something else". There's no skill involved in sniping a new player in one shot as he's trying to get used to the game. There's no skill involved in three geared players camping an early game objective, easily destroying a player with their starting equipment. When I asked if this is how the game normally is or if I was just having bad luck, I was told it gets worse in the later zones and that we were relatively lucky. I was told that I should "stop being a b*tch" and that I wasn't good enough for the game.I watched chat for a bit and saw others complaining about similar experiences. They were also met with disdain and hostility. Told to, essentially, piss off and go play something else. The game, in these players' eyes, is perfectly hardcore and anyone that doesn't love it just isn't good enough to play it. This game is not hardcore. You don't lose anything by dying other than a few bullets and trade items. It's not like Tarkov, where a death means you've lost your kit, potentially hours of work. It's just pure frustration for new players who are just trying to get used to the game. This isn't healthy and it will lead to fewer and fewer players sticking around past a few hours.I had high hopes for Stalcraft, and I still do. Perhaps I just have terrible luck. Perhaps the steam release has just lead to an influx of toxic players that won't stick around once they get their rocks off to "pwning the noobs". Once things settle down maybe the game will be as fun to play as I had hoped. Or maybe the community will just stick to it's toxic ways and kill the game it's based around slowly. Only time will tell.

This game is not for everyone, but the people that it is for will likely enjoy it quite a bit. If you are a fan of the STALKER series than this game is a no-brainer. The games progression and sense of community is one of the best I've seen, even if half the players don't speak much english. The games developers seem like they actually care as far as I can tell, they are fairly transparent with their plans and at the moment there is practically 0 P2W features on the NA server. The only thing that can give you an advantage is if you do a monthly sub you get like 10% more mats and I think 2 extra quests a week. Other than that you gotta earn every weapon or armor.I do have some complaints, mostly about how much running to get from one point to the other there is. In this game when you die you only lose the loot you gathered on that run and any ammo you might have. But much more valuable than that is the time lost. There are times when you have to run for almost 10 minutes, dodging players and anomalies the whole way. Sometimes when its your 5th journey to an area you need to loot, and you keep dying at some point on the journey, it can be very discouraging. Even more so than a game like tarkov I would say, because you dont get any XP outside of rep in this game, so if you die you have truly just wasted your time and gained nothing.Dont let this discourage you from trying, the game is very fun and the progression is satisfying when your not getting blocked by bad luck. Gunplay is weirdly really good for a minecraft/roblox based game. Landing headshots with a Mosin feels pretty damn good, and the games balance is actually pretty good overall. Every weapon and armor type has a place that it excels. I play solo mostly, but if you had a group of STALKER fans to play this with I imagine it would be an amazing time.

STALCRAFT: X is the largest online game set in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone.Explore an open world filled with mutants and anomalies alone or with friends — unforgettable experiences are guaranteed!GAMEPLAYMost of the time the player spends in the open world of the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone. Locations are filled with all kinds of PvP and PvE-activities, beloved by fans of Stalker: search for artifacts, mutant hunting, exploration of uncharted locations, doing quests and laboratories, participation in faction wars. For those who have little time to play, there are various session modes.A LIVING OPEN WORLDWhile exploring the locations, other factions players may shoot you, but you won't lose all your gear and progress; instead, you'll only leave part of the resources you've collected during that trip. This ensures you retain the thrill of each raid, while setbacks are not overly fatal. The open world of STALCRAFT: X is truly alive, and players create unique situations for each other, forging loyal friendships and relentless enemies along the way.A UNIQUE COMBINATION OF FPS AND RPGThe balance of weapons is not typical for open-world MMOs, and rather resembles session shooters like Counter Strike and Call of Duty. We define the shooter component as fast-paced, tied primarily to reaction and shooting skills. At the same time, you will remain motivated to progress further on as, over the years, developers have managed to achieve a unique combination of FPS and RPG mechanics.PROGRESSION AND AN OPEN ECONOMYDon't let the MMO genre scare you away — there is no levelling mechanic, and you progress through the game by obtaining new equipment. You can get it in many ways, including buying it from other players — because STALCRAFT: X has an open economy. You can become a legendary merchant without leaving the base! And by the way, there are no game wipes.THE DISTRIBUTION MODELThe game is distributed for free, and there is no catch here — monetization is organized according to the P4T (Pay for time) as well as cosmetics model.Any items can be obtained through playing the game, however, the soft monetization method allows you to speed up some areas of character leveling.so i think its a valid game

I'll just list the negatives of this game and you can decide if you want to play it as long as I have. -Pay to Win Players can buy their way to the end game and best gear. If they got a credit card, they will beat you. Period. Don't think you can get around this by "gittin gud". You can't. Even if you have all your gear maxed out like them, they can recruit more people to help them because they get WAY more money than you from the auction house. 10 dollars in this game can get you 500k roubles. So $200 can get you 10mil. 10 mil is enough to buy your way to the end of the game, essentially. 10mil is also enough to help out a lot of your friends along the way, if you want them to have an easier time. -That brings me to my next con, the game is designed around a HUGE time sink. Hence why so many people play for so long. It's kind of addicting too. When you get a big haul back, like in Tarkov, it feels good. That's fun. But when you die you lose ALL of your progress towards your gear. So if you spent 2 hours farming loot and want to go home, but someone with a WAY higher gear score pops out and kills you, you just lost 2 hours of your life my man. Thems the breaks. This part actually WOULDN'T be so bad if players with max level gear could LOSE their gear by fighting, because then the economy would actually be balanced more around skill. As it stands, once a guy buys his way to end game, he basically has no incentive not to just go raid other players trying to farm up and kill the ♥♥♥♥ out of them for fun or money or attention. He doesn't lose anything. Nothing is on the table for him. But for the other players, the stakes are incredibly high. This is a massive flaw imo. Finally, add in all the instant kill traps the creators have meticulously placed all over the maps, with little counter play and the game itself is killing you about as much as other players are. And a lot of your deaths are like Tarkov. Getting hit from beyond visual range by someone you can't see. In tarkov that's fine because I could kill that guy and get his ♥♥♥♥ if I was given the opportunity. In this game, killing that guy provides me nothing but I lose everything when he kills me. See the problem there?-There's no trade chat. Another reason I've clocked so many hours into this game is because the auction house economy is actually pretty fun to interact with. There's markets, you have to predict market demands and you can make deals with other players (like 3 premiums for 1mil) and make profit off of those deals. However there's no designated chat for this. It's all cold calling. I tried using the main Stalker chat for trades but got warned for spamming. So this is another dumb oversight (on a game that's 5 years old btw)-Moneygrab, this game is a money grab in North American markets. It's been out in Russia for about 5 years now. Probably because when they add the real endgame (which is massive PVP on a huge open map between clans) players who don't pay for power (pay to get past the 200+ hours required to get endgame gear) will start leaving very quickly. I think they're hoping they can tweak some things to keep people around but I don't see how they're gunna do it.-RPG The game is kind of like an RPG mixed with an FPS. We're talking about the difference between 2-3 headshots scoring a kill and 5-8 headshots. Yes, some characters have like 4x as much hp as others, which again would be fine if they LOST that ability when they died, but they don't. They're like an RPG character, that's just part of their character now. They naturally have 400 more HP than you because they have the end game gear that can't be lost. So when you run into a guy who has 400 more hp than you and a gun that kills you in 1/4th of the time which also has perfect accuracy and no recoil, ontop of that an extended clip mag. UPDATE: 17/07/2024TLDR: I got better at the game, it's -okay-, in terms of bad Online Stalker knock-offs, Stalcraft is probably the best one you can find, unfortunately, it does suffer the exact same problems as the others, that problem usually being needlessly difficult, forced PvP, item loss on death, and running simulator, complete with refusal for PvE servers. (I really don't know why Stalker-Like Devs are so against PvE).So, After giving this game a real go after some updates, I've come to somewhat enjoy the game, but it's a love/hate relationship, I returned less than a month prior to the X Update. I Re-joined the game with a handful of high-level friends who helped me understand the game much better than before.Previously, my friends were burnt out and no one was particularly interested in helping me out, which was understandable given the time.After taking some advice, and some tips, I very quickly picked the game up. For the most part, it was addicting, and learning that most loot is easily replaced after about 20 minutes and that items lost aren't that big of a deal, it became more bearable to live with.The only items lost on death is essentially Meds, Ammo, Trash, and Farm, the biggest kicker being the farm.The game is relatively smooth leading up to bar, but once you reach Veteran Rank gear, the grind *really* starts, however, since the X Update, items have gotten easier to obtain.Unfortunately, the game is still a running simulator, and if you die mid-travel, you'll respawn at the last base you visited, which sucks, and I wish there was a fleshed out fast-travel system.Prior to X, the only fast travel was the tunnels between Bar, and the Bases, but you had to run through them, since X, it's instant.Would be nice if reaching max rep with a base unlocked a Guide to Fast Travel to it.Quest and Boss design is.. really lacking, I haven't experienced the MSQ in full yet, but, from everything I've seen, and after experiencing the Beast Quest - Yeah it really needs some work, to simplify it, they've intentionally made the fights/instances difficult with little regard to the average player, and I believe the fights weren't tested properly - Rather, tested by people with end-game gear to begin with, or by the person who made them. (Normally the creator isn't suppose to be the tester outside Debugging, nor are the Testers suppose to be in End-game equipment). But I have no evidence for this.The Master of the Zone fight is a shining example of how not to do a boss fight - The mechanics are there, it looks fun, but it's not, the Boss moves far too quickly and kills you far too easily. It's a min-maxing fight that needs to be optimized at every turn in order to beat it.Personally, I'd have the boss a very slow moving target, he does enough damage and soaks enough as is, and should only move faster at the 25% Enraged state, instead, he moves as fast as the player, but at 25% he moves twice as fast.The game is -okay- but, as they say, once you reach Bar, you'll find out whether you like the game or not. This game is actually really good. However there are a few things that make it not worth the effort. I'm not gonna review the good, cause that's not the point of a review. I'd recommend it, but just know you'll lose loot to stuff you cannot control. Number 1 is anomalies, losing loot to NPC's and Players is stressful enough as is, but it's understandable, and it's something you can get better at, get new gear to counteract. Anomalies especially the dreaded black hole is just a death trap, and it's near impossible to get your loot back without risking dying again. I don't even understand why they added them into the game. It is 100% a game killer, it's fine early on, but later game losing all your stuff to something you have no control over(albiet walking slowly and I still don't think that helps. There have been times i've stood in the same spot looking at my inventory for a few minutes and next thing I know i'm dead. So I assume they can spawn ontop of you.) Plus you can barely see it, can't hear it cause the sound is janky and it sounds like you are surrounded by stuff 24/7(Which will be another thing I touch on later.) And for the last gripe, most of the enemies you need to be constantly running from to not die, so you can be running away and almost be safe, and run into an anomaly and die.Number 2: This is almost just as bad as the anomalies. Your own faction can take your dropped loot. You are supposed to be a team, and they'll watch you die, and take your stuff and that is that. You run back it's gone, and you know there were 4 of your own team nearby. You may be lucky and get your lost backpack which is practically nothing of what you had, plus any rare stuff you collected. This shouldn't even be a thing. The game might as well just have no factions and everyone versus everyone at this point. It's also not needed, once you get a sub faction you pretty much split the community in quarters, which is another thing I don't really understand. I personally feel like your own team should not be able to take your loot, no matter the "But we are bandits, it's what we do" yeah, and plenty of bandits have been murdered by their own for much less in real life(But guess what you can't kill your own team mates in this game).While these are the two things that are the main problem i've encountered so far, and I feel like should be removed. Bandits can't steal from bandits(if you have a sub faction you can't steal from your own subfaction). And Anomalies need to be removed, got a giant map, but it's stupid to try and run off the road to lose all your stuff to something that can't be countered, except by throwing bolts and it doesn't even do anything for some of the anomalies. Maybe when a bolt is tossed into an anomalie it disappears for 5 minutes it wouldn't be bad, but it pops right back after two seconds, if it can be destroyed at all. If there was an item you can eventually get, that can just make you immune to anomalies giving yourself better map control, i'd even be fine with that, but there isn't so you know you are just gonna die to black holes the entire time you play the game.Other then those two major issues.Sound is also an issue: I personally am unable to select what sound device I want the games sound to come from, so I am unable to play with my headphones. I've heard it doesn't matter anyway cause the directional sound in this game isn't great. And that needs to be fixed ASAP if it is true. A survival horror game, but you can't hear where bullets are coming from, if someone is walking near you and what direction, if there is an Anomalie actually near you, or half a mile to the left.That's pretty much it, those are three issues that you have no control over, and can very much ruin your play experience. Other than those, the game isn't bad. But those issues easily drop it from like 7-8/10 to closer to a 5-6/10. I do love the fact it's one of the very few survival games where you actually keep alot of your loot. But those other games you either lose them to an NPC/Player and some of the more extreme games food/water deprivation. Ontop of it, if they just removed factions from looting their own factions stuff, it probably wouldn't be as bad, alot of times it usually has to be your own teammate, or possibly a hacker, cause finding peoples loot bags isn't easy. But a team mate can see where you just died, and come right over and grab your stuff then choose wether they want to keep it or mail it back to you, and I've only gotten my stuff back a few times and those were usually from the enemy faction.

The terrain has to be one of the poorly made terrains I've seen in my time. Between having to jump over 2 foot blocks instead of simply walking over them and having to absolutely slowly scale 3 foot blocks slowly is painful.-The area between facilities and the facility themselves are filled with almost invisible "anomalies" which are ABSOLUTELY pointless and provide NOTHING to the game. I wouldn't say it provides variety to the game, because all it does is damage you. It simply acts as a barrier or something to watch out for when walking about, but what is the purpose of this? Why do they feel the need to add this to the game? It simply withdraws you from the immersion of the game by being careful with invisible objects which almost kill you or bring you to near death.-The AI is ridiculous to the point of question. If I am sneaking around an enemy camp and I can't even see the AI yet, then why are they automatically locking onto my location and shooting at me when I can't even see them yet?-The biggest enemy in this game is yourself, because 15 minutes in there and you'll already want to kill yourself.Things needing fixing asap:-You cannot find weapons out looting (at least in my time playing), which means you can only buy these weapons. If you can buy the weapons, then just allow ammo to be purchased at the same time.-The reason why not finding weapons out in the field needs to be fixed is because when you die, you do not drop your weapon. Do you know what this means? People with much better gear can simply sit in the woods just outside of spawn and pick you off, which is what happened to me. There is 0 risk to them losing their gear when you can just respawn with it on death, giving 0 risk to the idea of dying, which leads to people who are much stronger than yourself killing new players constantly.-It feels like the game is trying to tie a mix of looter, shooter, extractor (kinda?), and mmorpg. It's hard to find a balance between it all, but it feels like this game just falls flat.-Dialogue with NPC's is far too long and shouldn't be a story for each possible interaction that you have a difficult time skipping.Overall the experience playing this mediocre game was on par with an internet browser game some college student made for a school project, gonna be an incredibly hard pass for me.

See the update at the bottom of this post.While not perfect (a hacker problem, prominently) this is the first game in a decade to deliver on the premise of "co-op STALKER." It's a fairly standard MMO, but the FPS elements are well implemented, and I find it compelling and fun.It is nearly impossible to pay-to-win. There are cosmetics, and one can buy SOME of the weapon materials that you usually have to adventure for, and Premium lets you take more missions to get more materials, but you won't have someone spawn in for the first time, having spent $100, and immediately ruin the day of everyone else on the server.Matchmaking is determined by gear-whatever the best gear you've equipped is, determines who you get matched with. This won't save you from tryhards who've been playing FPSes for the last twenty years, but it levels the playing field. The squad system works well-even if the noise suppression on the chat kind of sucks-and the community on the US servers is friendly and often helpful.Do be aware that there is a major issue with Russian hackers on the EU servers, as of March 19th 2023. No idea when it'll be settled, but the last hacking issue was dealt with in about a week, so we'll see.April 4th 2023 update:It is worth noting that several story missions force you to do Minecraft/Roblox-style parkour sequences...except you get nowhere to put your gathered items, so when you die from falling off something-because you will, a lot, thanks to murky level design or unclear progression paths-your ♥♥♥♥, to quote MC Ride, is gone.The latter also applies to a few instanced side missions. Essentially, if you're going into a non-plot mission, bring nothing about which you give a ♥♥♥♥ unless it's Bound.Those, however, are small nitpicks that can be planned for and avoided. I've changed by recommendation to a disrecommendation for a different reason.Namely:The entire third portion of this game is PVP. This wouldn't be so bad if the PVP weren't so heavily based in meta loadouts-on top of the hacker problem, which has only gotten better insofar as hackers stay north of the Bar now.Unless you are willing to search out what the current recommended loadout is, and capable of spending literal millions of Rubles, you will not be able to complete this game.PVP is a joke at any point past the Cordon-even with oneshot sniper rifles removed, TTK is still 2-3sec only if you're lucky, and sub-1 with endgame gear, even if wearing ideal armor and using ideal artifacts. On top of this, roamers will attack faction farming areas at random, giving you less than 5sec of time to react after n+1 hours of farming, and that 5sec assumes that someone else was killed before you and you register the "person entered minimap range" noise as a potential hostile. Sound cues are borderline nonexistent, and overrun by ambiance or gunfire when they do happen.Escape from Tarkov has only survived as an all-PVP MMO for as long as it has because of stellar design across the board, and Escape from Tarkov this is not. At this point, only hardcore FPS veterans and people who use Aim Lab and KovaaK's need apply.

I cannot in good faith recommend this game right now.  The game wasn't so bad starting off, grinding materials in the beginner areas and occasionally running into some PvP, it was fun and rewarding.  But as I progressed further into the game, the community or lack thereof got worse.   After finally making it to The Bar and I realized how much players like to camp and any sort of "honor" system is out the window.  When I say honor system, I don't expect players of different factions to be holding hands and skipping through the meadows together, but in the beginner areas, when you got killed by another player or you killed them, sending their material bag back was almost a given.  It was a way of saying "Hey, good game, here's some of your stuff back" and I never had any problem sending back player bags or getting my own back.  That is until I made it to The Bar.  The biggest problem is that as you progress in the tech trees, the materials required it make the next weapon/armor/etc would jump up, requiring hundreds of each different resource depending on what you were working on.  Now I'm not mad at how grindy the game gets, I actually love very grindy games because it gives me something to focus on, the problem is that after getting some resources and running them back, majority of the time you're gonna run into players that are sitting in a corner outside of your factions entrance just waiting for a player to be running back with stuff.  And it's not like they can even take the materials for themselves.  No one else can open your material bag besides you, which I think is a great feature, but certain players have decided that mailing the bags back isn't worth it.  They could either put your material bag on the auction house for a price, which I'm not totally against, or they can just throw your bag somewhere and leave it there to never be found again.  And this is where a lot of the issues come in.You're forced to farm a lot of materials for the next tier of weapons/armor to even compete against players who are already way more geared than you are to then run into some of these players sitting in corners outside of your factions entrance just to take all your stuff and throw your material bag somewhere, because players did the same thing to them when they were working on their stuff and so they are doing it to other players.  All they are accomplishing is just slowing other players progression down because it's not like they can use the materials you gathered, it's simply just to troll and ruin other players experience with the game.And you'd think that coming from a game like Tarkov would prepare you for this game but that's not the case.  Tarkov, which is very much "Lose everything on death" has a more supportive community than this game.  After playing Tarkov for years, I never saw as many extract campers than I saw in this game.  That's not to say that Tarkov doesn't have players like that because it does.  But those players are few and far between back when I played it.  This game almost encourages this type of behavior without rewarding the campers with much.  It's honestly a shame because not every player in this game plays like this, you will meet some very nice players and even have fun running in groups, which is unfortunately the only way to play this game because playing solo is just not fun with how this game is set up.Until the devs do something about the useless camping outside of The Bar or make it more worthwhile to send material bags back to players, I would avoid this game at all costs.  And if you're one of the players that enjoy this type of gameplay? That's awesome and I'm glad you're having fun.  But I see a lot of people talk about these issues in game to then get bombarded with the basic "Skill issue" responses from other players.

TL;DR: Do you enjoy Tarkov sort of games and/or fighting a constant uphill battle and getting seal clubbed? Then you might enjoy the game. The game is incredibly frustrating with an occasional moment of victory or relief, but it does have a certain appeal I can't quite put a finger on. As frustated as I am, I'll probably continue playing. That said, enjoy the rant up ahead.The game is enjoyable enough, even fun at times. It's fairly simplistic in how it looks, plays and functions. You have your suit, your primary and secondary weapons and a few tools. You have a lot of choice when it comes to weapons and armor, at least superficially so. The game has amazing music and in general it's quite fun to play as far as an online STALKER-esque experience goes. However, once you get past the early game of Swamps and Cordon, the gameplay quickly devolves into the Stalker side repeatedly getting shafted by either the map layout or the bandit playerbase who seem to have nothing better to do than camp every single entrance and exit in every single gearscore bracket. On the server I play, the opposite seems to happen excessively rarely, if at all.Once you are past the early game and graduate into the midgame with +300 gearscore, you will be thrown into the same pool with all the big boys with the best gear in the game. While you're struggling with an AKM or an M4A1 and a Hawk armored suit, or some other combination of blue-rarity gear, you will constantly find yourself fighting against the veterans who are all decked out in Exoskeletons, Centurions and other top tier armor who will delete you faster than you can blink with their SIG 550, AS Val or one of the many bolt-action rifles that will oneshot you. Enjoy your 5-15 minute corpse run.You might have a chance against them if you get the drop on the guy. But typically bandits are so numerous and so omnipresent in most areas of the game that even if you somehow manage to kill one, there are two or three more waiting to stomp you and steal whatever loot you might have managed to gather. On weekends this is even worse. While your gear itself -- guns, armor and other bound items -- aren't dropped on death, all the vendor loot, artifacts, loose ammo, etc. will be. Your crafting resources are dropped in the form of a Lost Backpack which only you can open. This backpack can be ransomed back to you for tens or hundreds of thousands of rubles, or if the bandit is feeling particularly generous he'll throw it away into a black hole or some bush somewhere where it can never be found. Or maybe he'll just sell the bag that took you an hour or more to farm to the fence for 500 rubles.This is the biggest glaring issue in the game. You will repeatedly, constantly and in every single tier of the game, be set back by people who are by design objectively more powerful than you are. And given the absolutely insane amount of grind that is required to break into the higher tiers of weaponry and armor -- literally up to two thousand or more crafting resources required for a SINGLE upgrade in the later game -- you will be spending days, possibly weeks trying to grind events that pop around in the maps. All of this while a minimum of half of the playerbase will shoot you on sight and most likely have some meta combination of items that will put you into the dirt with you having very slim chance of successfully defending yourself.And if those were all the complaints, the game might not even be all that stressful. Challenging and unbalanced to be sure, but playable and fun if you're into it. Another problem is your own team. When you go down to any one of the million random anomalies, mutants, sharpshooter AI, random bandit or stuff spawning directly on top of you, your own faction will more than likely steal everything that is of value from your corpse if you died somewhere that sees a reasonable amount of traffic. So not only are you fighting against the enemy team with significant advantages, you are also struggling against your own team who will happily ransack your corpse of everything that isn't bound to you. Your remains are afforded a two minute protection, but when it takes anywhere between 5 and 15 minutes to run back to your corpse without anything getting in your way, it's unlikely you can salvage your items if you are in a populated area.And lastly there's how many missions in the game are designed. If a mission -- be it the main quest or a side job -- requires that you enter an instanced area, make sure you never bring anything of value there. If you die in an instanced area, you will lose EVERYTHING that was not bound to your person. And you will die in those areas repeatedly from things you cannot reasonably prepare for without consulting a walkthrough beforehand. From hostile NPCs spawning behind you, to the game's horrible jumping and climbing system being stretched to its breaking point by jumping puzzles under constant pressure from enemies, to areas that are designed in such a baffling way you wonder how you were supposed to figure it out in the first place. Such as the solution to a problem being to deliberately jump into anomalies to "surf" them, for example. And of course in places you have your infinitely spawning enemies or bosses with insanely inflated health bars that you will not be able to take down for the first half a dozen attempts. Enjoy running back to those instances from wherever you happened to respawn at, by the way. You're going to be doing a lot of running. And there's no fast travel either, and only a few missions in the game have check points that allow respawning within those instances.Naturally any and all criticism or cries of the game being hideously and obviously unfair and unbalanced will be met with the the lines "git gud", "get a squad" and/or "such is life in the zone". While there may be some merit to these stock responses, at some point the repeated failure will grind on your nerves and your patience. There is only so much gudder you can git when the enemy has anywhere between 30-50% more effective health than you do and dishes out as much more damage per second compared to you. Squads do help somewhat but it does not remove the fact that if you get whacked, you will regardless be looking at yet another corpse run. And about it being life in the Zone... I guess so. But it makes this game an incredibly frustrating experience that will leave you questioning why you play it in the first place.In summary: the game's unbalanced PvP is on at all times, the player tier system is broken, the maps are filled with more anomalies that you would see in a single singleplayer STALKER game combined, the design of many missions is at best questionable and you will grind for days, weeks, possibly months to hopefully one day get into the end game while you you get knocked down over and over and over again. And every time you die, you get to run for an average of 10 minutes before you're back where you died.

Stalcraft is a love letter to the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series in taking a lot of the game series' established universe and game design, then adapting it into it's own MMO RPG style interpretation, which I find to be rather enjoyable as a S.T.A.L.K.E.R. fan. I do warn it has a competitive survival aspect to it that might turn off some people who expect to move around freely with out threats player based or environmental.Basic Game Explanation: I get to scratch that Stalker itch of exploring the dangerously wonderful Zone, area to area, making my way farther North looking for new gear to craft and treasures to find with plenty of danger along the way. This game does have survival elements, you lose unbound goods you collect out exploring on death and some consumables you bring out, but guns and armor stay on though deteriorate over time with use. As well, enemies like AI mutants/wildlife, AI humans, and players of opposite faction you choose will be active threats. Fighting AI humans and mutants in world events provide materials needed to craft gear like armor, guns, attachments, and devices, but said events other players will be actively trying to get the rewards of too. Materials only are available in certain regions and specific gear requires them to be made at an HQ with a required reputation level. The crafting trees will require prerequisite gear to be made at times to progress to better gear which is too keep in mind. As well, doing world events, dailies, and quests will help you progress your reputation with certain HQs you have available. The map is large over all, but has defined areas you must pass through at a time that don't take too long to traverse across, but anomalies, enemy players, mutants, and emissions can deter you at a given time. Radiation, Bioinfection, and Heat can also affect your character harmfully if exposed for too long to them, though radiation actively increased intensity farther North you go requiring armor that can resist it. Friendly players are always active doing their own tasks and are typically friendly so far, some bad actors here and there to be expected, but for a small community for a niche game people will try suppressing enemy player camping, making squads to go farm or for protection or even mailing back lost materials, which is pleasant. Clans are in the game, but seem like a lot to start and possibly maintain since they are more focused on doing activities in the far North regions of the map. It has it's issues, but nothing game breaking or forcing more to wanna stop playing so far.Visually the game looks rather nice, has good lighting, keeps that washed out and dry looking pallet like the orignal Stalker games that made them so creepy. Character models, structures, and some terrain does look rather inspired by Minecraft and & Days to Die, but I think it kind of lends to the charm of it. It still has well modeled gear, enemies, and some other minor structures that I think fit over all. The draw distance is short I think to limit being able to see enemy players from far away and take advantage of long engagements with snipes since the areas can be somewhat small.

This game is basically Stalker if it was made by Roblox. The game starts off great with the first area and it's a great tutorial zone for all newcomers. I loved the conflict between players and map control but I felt like more could be added to it. There isn't really any objectives to actually control so it's more camps to conquer for loot with no purpose other then that and quest locations. On a different note roaming through the map I felt always on high alert and loved the feeling of adrenaline when you tried not to get killed by other players or deadly anomalies finishing up a quest or gathering resources. The enemies are what you'd expect from a free to play game, mostly low budget animations and still figures for the humanoid types but they can pose a challenge at times. I can't help to love the atmosphere of the Stalker where you'll see grotesque creatures and bloodthirsty bandits out for you and your belongings. I liked the progression system towards guns, armor, etc. It's a free game and an mmorpg so I was fully accepting the fact going into this game that some things would be a grind. The artefacts are interesting in this game as they are valuable and more rare then in the Stalker series. Loot isn't shared unless a camp was completely cleared and you shot or killed some things, also if you're in a squad (highly recommended) loot is shared but other then that it's a free for all. Keep in mind my whole experience was solo and no guides were looked at during my playtime apart for the usage of the metal detector for aluminium cables. I did end up finishing junkmens quest but I wanted it earlier. Also tip just use the Bolt action rifle, it's broken in early pvp and most people use it. Also carry more then 1 primary because you don't loose your guns and ammo is cheap but you might be encumbered quicker.I recommend to try Stalker (Call of Pripryat) before even jumping into this game. It's the same premise. I believe Stalker and the books did it first.Now for the negatives and why I stopped playing. The major things I found wrong about this game was the trading system. I couldn't figure out how to sell my surplus items (like ammo, grenades and med-kits) and worthless foods (Vodka and Bread I had like 3 stacks of 64 Bread) I accumulated while scavenging and yes I know about the auction it's just not what I was expecting. A merchant that you could sell your surplus items to would be a great addition or just the ability to do so overall would increase my liking for this game. The ability to fast travel with the use of currency would be a great addition to the game. Certainly when the majority of the time you'll be spending just running from large areas to another which can be a grind at times and you risk the chance of dying soooo running some more. I would say the great part about this game is that you don't really loose much on death. But I'd argue that it makes pvp more of being annoying against one another then actually getting rewarded with useful weapons or loot. When a player is killed you loose all the useful grindy material he scavenged for that's turned into basically a worthless trash bag. I mean it's really not worth much to kill others unless you just want to kill someone. You get a chance of them carrying an artefact or rare item but it's a very very low chance. After at least 10-15 kills I was better off going through the map and doing objectives then killing others. I got one artefact from the kills but it was in the first area and the poor guy probably didn't bank it (It was the electric artefact).Overall if the rating was out of 10 I'd give this game a 6. It's above average and I think my issue is I wasn't looking for a game with the negative points which I wrote about. Stalker was my point of reference so I might of been comparing too often the differences and resemblances. But this game has something to offer and for people whiling to be patient through the grind I'd recommend it. It offers something which I wish Stalker had, and that is multiplayer.

TL:DR -Most people are toxic/unfriendly. By destroying the work of other players (simply for fun), some people wonder why there is no player base. I may have played over 150 hours in the first two weeks of starting the game, but in no way shape or form does this make the game good. This game has a whole truckload of problems that I will briefly give insight upon.       The grind is crazy bad, many hours of farming goes into each and every item you craft. This is an open world PVP game where everything on your body can be robbed, left, or thrown away in a ditch. Many hours can be lost at the ill will of other players, erased for no reason.      The farming is not too exciting between killing boars, pigs, dudes with guns, dogs, and metal detecting. The enemies i mentioned before are basically the only enemies in the entire game. (Starter pig, bigger brown pig, mid game dark pig, end game jet black pig) There are a few big tough spooky enemies that are added later, a really big feral dog and the tank from left for dead.      Weapon balance is a nightmare. Use a specific couple Assault Rifles (AK, AS VAL, F2000) and like one of three shotguns, or die. Pistols, lmg, smg, and melee are completely gutted and useless. Later areas are only filled with a couple small children who want to farm or the polar opposite, players who will chase you down only to grief your items into the abyss.     This game is NOT SOLO FRIENDLY. The bigger your friend group the better time you will have, the later into the game you keep the group the more protected you are from others. Late game everyone needs air drops for weapon/armor parts and a literal material to make end game weapons. Defending these alone is almost impossible.     People warned that the game becomes toxic at the end and i would have to agree. T bagging with people used to work before mid game, but now only pain. There is no room for friendship in this game unless you are in the same team. If you do not shoot enemy players on sight, 90%+ of the time you will be shot with a meta gun to death in under a few seconds.     I forgot to mention the good part of the game so i will leave it at the bottom. The gun-play is cool, the head hit-box of enemies is huge because it is Minecraft. The guns look pretty good, feel good, and it is nice to put attachments on them. Finding artifacts and getting them back home is always a feel good moment, especially if they are rare or in the Meta. The game is not really P2W, the premium membership is only a slight buff to gathered materials. It really does have that Stalker aesthetic and feel to it, so that is pleasant. It makes you realize how fun a multiplayer CO-OP Stalker game could be.

TL;DR - It's free. Try it out, you might enjoy it. Some mechanics are meh, but the core gameplay loop of STALKER is present. If you wanted STALKER with friends, this is about as close as you can get right now.If you are scared of losing your stuff when you die,  This isn't an extraction shooter, it's an MMO at heart. You DO however lose some things on death - Ammo, medicine, trade items that you sell for rubles, and the "barter" items which are used to progress through the weapon and armor trees. PVP is more of a minor setback than it is the core focus of the game. Figure out the player hotspots and stop sprinting everywhere if you want a better chance at surviving. Ceramic Armor is arguably the best at PVP to avoid getting instantly destroyed. Snipers are only good at the start of the game for one-tapping people, and very quickly lose that ability to.The game itself is absolutely solid. This is as close as you can get to a vanilla STALKER MMO (hell, even some of the assets are the same!) Combat is fast and dangerous. Exploring the map and questing is very fun. Gunplay is good, gun modification is absolutely fantastic. There is quite a bit of granularity here, and I love it.The art style is likely to turn some people away, which is sad but understandable. I don't think the art style suites the game, especially considering that the story takes itself seriously and is actually decent if your are a STALKER fan. Despite that, it has some charm to it.  The much lauded STALKER atmosphere is here, albeit in a diminished capacity due to stylistic decisions. Everyone in the game gets nightvision immediately, rather than having to suffer with a flashlight. Makes me sad, but I get it.Some things I think are pretty mediocre about the game is anomaly diving for artifacts. We needs detectors for things, IMO. An optional item one can purchase to give them a heads up that they're running head first into an anomaly would be very nice. Let it have four tiers - each one giving you a longer detection range for anomalies, with the last one giving you their exact location. There is already a mechanic in the game for charging your detectors - just let us do that to balance it out or something, I don't know.The metal searching mechanic is pretty boring in my opinion. Felt like a bit of chore for me near the end of my time in the Cordon. I never had a problem with the detector energy, as you aren't supposed to equip it until you hear the detector go off in the first place as it scans passively from your inventory. The problem I have with it is that the "metal" goods that you are supposed to get gatekeeps about 90% of the content of the game. This isn't a problem for people who like to do exploring - but if you are in this game just to quest and shoot stuff, you will be sorely disappointed by the time you reach the Cordon. You can earn minuscule amount of metals from dailies, but it's faster to just go and find the stuff yourself. Emissions suck, plain and simple. You need to go underground to survive an emission, but the underground locations are not marked on your map when a emission starts. Shouldn't be too hard, right? Well, emissions happen with exactly zero warning. Suddenly, the whole map turns red and you got to book it to the nearest underground zone - which, unless you have prior knowledge of, is not marked out for you. There is a community made map detailing all the spots in the game that are underground - go find it and keep it open in the background for when you get caught out.There used to be a cash shop, but they took it out. There is now a Premium mode that you are able to purchase that lets you pay-to-not-grind-as-hard (which, at 11 dollars for 30 days, I figured wasn't an awful deal considering how much I adore the game.) It's not a monthly subscription - you buy the premium currency and then buy the Premium. You don't have to buy packs of premium currency - you can set to purchase EXACTLY how much you want. Neat, non-predatory feature by the devs!Lastly, some requests to the dev. Please let the SKS get a 20 round magazine after you purchase the tactical stock for it. Please add an anomaly detector, as well as a 2 minute heads up for Emissions. Otherwise, your product is phenomenal!

A fern (Polypodiopsida or Polypodiophyta /ˌpɒliˌpɒdiˈɒfɪtə, -əˈfaɪtə/)[citation needed] is a member of a group of vascular plants (plants with xylem and phloem) that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers. The polypodiophytes include all living pteridophytes except the lycopods, and differ from mosses and other bryophytes by being vascular, i.e., having specialized tissues that conduct water and nutrients and in having life cycles in which the branched sporophyte is the dominant phase.Ferns have complex leaves called megaphylls, that are more complex than the microphylls of clubmosses. Most ferns are leptosporangiate ferns. They produce coiled fiddleheads that uncoil and expand into fronds. The group includes about 10,560 known extant species. Ferns are defined here in the broad sense, being all of the Polypodiopsida, comprising both the leptosporangiate (Polypodiidae) and eusporangiate ferns, the latter group including horsetails, whisk ferns, marattioid ferns, and ophioglossoid ferns.Ferns first appear in the fossil record about 360 million years ago in the late Devonian period, but Polypodiales, the group that makes up 80% of living fern diversity, didn't appear and diversify until the Cretaceous, contemporaneous with the rise of flowering plants that came to dominate the worlds flora.Ferns are not of major economic importance, but some are used for food, medicine, as biofertilizer, as ornamental plants, and for remediating contaminated soil. They have been the subject of research for their ability to remove some chemical pollutants from the atmosphere. Some fern species, such as bracken (Pteridium aquilinum) and water fern (Azolla filiculoides) are significant weeds worldwide. Some fern genera, such as Azolla, can fix nitrogen and make a significant input to the nitrogen nutrition of rice paddies. They also play certain roles in folklore.
