One word will be used to sum up your overall experience: *Frustration*Pros:- Exceptional atmosphere- Superb gun animations and sounds- Well written dialogue and intriguing story and side quests- The devs took S.T.A.L.K.E.R. lore and ran with it, the overarching story being similar enough to the game this is inspired by, but fresh enough to give S.T.A.L.K.E.R. fans a new experienceCons- Forced PvP with quests often put in high traffic enemy territory, forcing you to fight an uphill battle and ruin people's days for measly rewards- Progress feels okay, until you repeatedly lose hours worth of grinding to a random enemy or an anomaly you did not see- An epidemic of level transition campers with no way to counter it- Fetch quests that overextend and with pointless side-objectives are more common than you thinkOverall, early game is intriguing enough to get you hooked on exploration and experimenting with various weapons and armors, but by the time you reach the Rostok area, the game will have already put you through the ringer. The rose tinted glasses come off once you will have lost countless hours of farming for resources, being set back over and over by the listed cons above. From there on out, it will be pure frustration as you try to accomplish your quests while losing as little time as possible to cheap deaths. You will often find yourself set back to zero after losing heaps of barter items which are required to advance your equipment.PvP often feels like it is forced by devs with questionable mission placements in high density enemy areas, obligating players to traverse deep into enemy territory and fight people who do not want to participate in PvP. Not to mention there is little to gain from PvP, besides items that you can sell for pocket change, since barter items, which are more valuable for progression, are unable to be used by anyone besides the player who initially collected them. More often than not, you gain very little in the long run from killing players besides a +1 to your K/D ratio, while the people you kill lose an hour's worth of grinding. It is a lose-lose situation. Needless to say, this half-baked version of PvP is the reason why I cannot recommend this game. It is unfulfilling, it feels cheap, it is unrewarding and it is forced. The time to kill is very short, regardless of what armor you are wearing. There is no noticeable difference between wearing a combat oriented armor, or a paper bag anomalous suit.Simply put, it feels like the devs have consciously made the decision to pad out the progression by making sure players have a high chance of dying, even in relatively safe areas, constantly forcing them to start back over with grinding. Unfortunately, the only effect this has is making the player realize that their effort is often rewarded with a cheap death, frustration and the prospect of having to spend thrice the time to recover resource wise.The games feels half-baked, more of a mid-term beta with questionably thought out design decisions. Many will argue that since this is based off of the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. franchise, it has a pass to be punishing and cheap. However, S.T.A.L.K.E.R. has the excuse of quick load/save buttons. Here, if you die, you have to accept the fact that you were put back to the starting point and that you lost time of your life in exchange for zero progress.

Now, before I explain the main reasons why I like this game, I want to briefly mention that this game is definitely not for everyone. If you have a high tolerance for bs situations, you'll probably be fine. Just be prepared to constantly die, because this game is very cruel. You have to look out for enemy players, dangerous anomalies that are hard to see (especially in foliage), AI enemy gunmen, AI enemy monsters, all while sometimes completing quests where you need to search an area. On top of it, the enemy spam in this game is enormous, so prepare to get mauled if you don't have a shotgun. Essentially, if you're okay with escape from tarkov but with extra dangers to look out for, then I think you'll be fine. Now there are 2 main reasons why I like this game. The first being the core gameplay loop. I am a huge fan of game's setting. The idea of scavenging for supplies in a wasteland filled with monsters and anomalies is really appealing. The pvp element of this game only makes it more fun, as the game feels more like a battle for resources, adding to the hardcore survival aspects of the game. The main gameplay loop is essentially the following: Equip a limited amount of supplies you're willing to lose (ammo, med-kits, etc.), leave the safehouse area and scavenge for supplies, complete quest objectives, or hunt players and/or ai enemies, then return to the safehouse area, enjoy new loot obtained. I guess it's really similar to a game like tarkov but it also has a pretty cool story with multiple endings and perspectives to play from, adding to the enjoyment. I'm not going to lie, the story and atmosphere of this game actually hit me so hard that I bought the S.T.A.L.K.E.R games (I know the story is different, but the atmosphere and interactions between characters was very appealing) and I can't wait to play them. As for the second reason, it is the playerbase. I'm not exaggerating when I say that the playerbase in this game is one of the best communities I have ever interacted with (maybe i'm just really lucky with the people I run into?). Let me give you just a small pinch of the interactions I have had in this game:1. Was scavenging for supplies in the first area (when I was new to the game), finally collected enough materials and headed back to safehouse, got mauled by a pack of dogs and died, went back to get my stuff, died again, gave up and decided to do a side quest, returned to second area safehouse after completing quest, noticed that I had mail, another player found my stuff and gave me the resources I worked hard to get,  he included the simple message "Don't give up. Happy hunting".2. Scavenging in the third area (near centre of map), insta-killed by a shotgun out of nowhere, felt like that was a pretty cowardly thing to do for a player but shrugged it off and continued playing, later when I returned to a safehouse I noticed that the guy who killed me mailed me some of the resources I lost, he said that it wasnt a fair fight.3. When I was still pretty new to the game I kept getting killed by a couple of camping bandit players with higher tier gear. After dying multiple times, I got upset and mentioned in chat that there is nothing I can do about that, so I would just have to close the game and wait for the campers to leave, a guy responded by telling me to "stop ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" which I figured he was just being a jerk, but he then said "grab your gun, let's go kill that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥", both me and him along with two other people joined forces and fought the campers and won which allowed me to complete a quest I had in the area. 4. I grinded for materials for an hour but once I returned to a safehouse area I realised that I was missing just 5 more of a specific material, meaning that I would have to travel all the way back to a far away place to get more. I don't know if I'd recommend or not recommend this game. There's no middle thumb, but whatever.As far as the gameplay, world, exploration, PVE encounters, and quests go, this game is very well put together, with a clear amount of love and care put in by the development team over the years. It's very much STALKER underneath the minecraft look, and a lot of the game mechanics are readily apparent. It is so close to being a perfect STALKER MMO, but it falls short for one big reason.You can play this game and have an amazing time, or have a terrible time, the deciding factor is mostly your patience and how often you run into PVP. The group of people who play solely to fight other players can and will ruin your experience with the game, and if you're lucky enough to only meet them rarely, you'll have a far better time than if you meet them more commonly. PVP in this game is heavily disincentivized; you can't get crafting materials from it, only ammo, medicine, artefacts, and vendor trash. Money is rarely a problem in the game as well, provided you do quests and grind the events, which you should be doing anyway. This leaves the main driving force behind PVP as griefing, or just fighting for the hell of it. It's not rewarding, nor is it very fun, the winner mostly being decided by who fires first or who ambushes who. Spawn/Entrance camping is rampant at some times in the day, and playing during peak hours will have you constantly impeded by groups of players sending you back to your respawn as you try to finish quests, grind reputation, or just travel between base camps. Despite the lack of reward, most people still adopt a "Shoot on sight" mentality simply because they don't want their time to be wasted. The developers have stated that PVP is a cornerstone of their game design, but in the game itself it seems that every PVP mechanic is stuck on the fence, and it just feels like a total waste of potential. If the devs removed it, very little would change overall in terms of progression, and if they made it more impactful, it would make PVP deaths feel like they happened for a reason, rather than just being a mild annoyance that teleports you back to your base. It just feels tacked on.Unfortunately, any reference to this in the reviews seems to be met with a copy/pasted boilerplate from the developers, stating that the game is designed with PVP in mind without any further discussion. I understand, of course, it's their game, and they're clearly designing it as a game they themselves would like to play, but without any wiggle room, both passive and aggressive players suffer from the lack of affirmative direction in the design of PVP gameplay, and that's a real shame.I hear the RU servers have more of a point to PVP as well, though I haven't personally played on them. It just makes me wonder why the international version seems to have been released in such an unfinished state while the CIS server is running the "real game", so to speak. For all I know, my issues with PVP were solved months or years ago, and just haven't been ported outside of the post soviet countries.Edit: As a developer has responded, I figure it would be good to edit the review to take into account what they had to say. It's not exactly a good sign.The language the developer uses, especially when it comes right after speaking about the re-implementation of a "Cash Shop", worries me a lot, specifically as to the actual behind-the-scenes purpose of the PVP mechanics. I had originally thought they were a half-baked implementation, designed to remove the incentive for PVP in order to keep players from falling too deeply into it. I realize now that I might have been wrong.The developer says that PvP is an activity that "doesn't have to be rewarding", and that your only reward for it is your loot (which, in my original review, I said doesn't really matter) and your life (which, in my review, I said doesn't really matter, it's just an annoyance). This makes me think, now, that the idea behind PvP isn't to be a "fun" mechanic. I now worry that it's actually designed to be an "annoyance mechanic" to push the soon-to-come freemium shop that, from what other reviews have said, is incredibly unbalanced on the RU servers, letting paid players more or less walk all over free players. If I'm right, it would seem that getting killed by a spawn camper, being sent back to base, and being forced to retrace your steps time and time again may actually be designed expressly to grate on you, which in turn would encourage you to pay up yourself in order to level the playing field. If you've played War Thunder, you should be getting flashbacks by now. Yes, technically you lose nothing from death. No progression, only a portion of your materials. Yes, technically playing free will be completely possible, but as other reviews have noted, playing with paid items will tip the scales in your favour immensely. That's my major fear now, supplanting my earlier fear that the development team was simply content to leave the PvP mechanics in an unfinished state. Perhaps they're not unfinished at all, more simply designed to be as unfulfilling as possible in order to drive the playerbase to cough up enough dough to either ignore it, or stomp everyone else to pieces.Amazing.

If you get killed by a player with slightly better gear, then pay2win is your excuse. PvP in the game is easy, especially in the early stages, so if you let the player kill themselves so early, you don't have enough skill. Donat does not solve as much as it might seem. For 300 hours of playing, I did not feel that I was losing to donat. In addition, on Russian servers you can buy donated items from other players. And despite their high price tags, with the right allocation of your time and resources, you will farm any amount very quickly. I wrote this comment under the post that the starter kits were cut. It pissed me off even though I haven't put a dime into the game in 300 hours, so I'll paste my comment here so you know what I'm talking about:  You saw the kits and it seemed to you that they somehow help. The game has a very low TTK, so you think that such players have an advantage, but they die just as fast as you. These kits helped only in the beginning. In addition, many things from the sets can be obtained for free. According to the plot, they give out weapons and equipment that are many times superior to this one. What was in the sets was relevant for the first couple of hours of the game. Developers need to make money, they have been selling these kits on Russian servers for a very long time and no one complained. In addition, there are a lot of donations on Russian servers that were cut out for you, but you can buy it for in-game currency from the players, and you cry because the developers have added a couple of sets for an easier start, mainly against NPCs and mutants. I'm not making excuses for pay2win, but STALCRAFT did it right. We in Russia could donate to make the gameplay easier for ourselves, but we could also buy any donated weapon or armor with in-game currency. It was even more interesting that way, because we knew that we didn't have to invest a single penny into the game, but we could buy top armor in the game if we farmed for a week. Very vile players who have no idea how much work the developers have put into this game. The distribution in the game works in such a way that you will very rarely be thrown onto an empty server, so if there are not enough players, unfortunately, you can really stumble upon an enemy with very good equipment and it will be difficult to kill him. While there are a small number of players, this can really become a problem, but after a while, most likely the chance of this will be minimized. Yes, indeed, there are idiots in the game who can deliberately choke you until you burn out and exit the game. They will kill you at spawn, on quests or just on the way to the base. But it is rare if we say that this happens on purpose. If he talks about random meetings, then this is quite normal. If you have a risk of losing everything, then it is more interesting to play. In addition, when playing with friends, most likely you will not feel this factor. Perhaps now, in connection with the release of the game on Steam, many toxic players from the CIS are doing this, but these are few. In addition, you can easily get rid of them simply by changing the server by re-entering the game or re-entering the location. I myself have played 300 hours, so I am sure of my words. The point of the game is to grind equipment, upgrade your character, search for artifacts, build your own special loadouts, exchange and trade with players. Ridiculously repetitive. Hope you enjoy doing the same grind for hundreds of hours, consisting of:Walk to location. Kill things at location Walk back to base. Repeat for a couple hundred hours. Your health regenerates, your radiation regenerates, there's no survival mechanics, you can't loot weapons or armour. Most of the gameplay consists of "walk here, talk here" to NPCs standing around -- Most of the "PvP" gameplay ends up being pleading to the guy you just killed to buy his stuff back. When you die to another player, your premium currencies that you got from grinding goes into a bag. Only the person who died can access this bag. The player who killed you cannot do anything with this bag except sell it back to you. Meaning to get returns from PvP, you have to hope the player buys their bag back. Except most of the time, they just don't... Would you pay your killer? No. And if you had extremely expensive currencies, chances are is that you can't afford to buy it back anyway. So PvP is effectively useless and serves to only delay another players grind, which is why it's largely frowned upon by the community and why it's a waste of time to hunt players.When dying, you don't actually lose any of your equipment, you lose your ammo and consumables. The ammo is ridiculously cheap, where you can buy 100 rounds for 52 rubles (you get thousands of rubles easily), you also can't sell ammo. Health-packs are pointless because you regenerate health. You're then left with misc items which are just for selling and your special barter currencies.  The special barter currencies are used to get the next tier of weapons and the only effective way to get them is through events. Events are very stingy, so expect to do looots of grinding to get the next tier of what you're after. It doesn't help that the events are amazingly boring. Hope you enjoy mutants who run around in a circle and then make a B-Line towards you when you shoot them. It involves a lot of shooting them from a distance, running as you reload, turn around to shoot again, and repeat until the event is over.You'd think, to speed things up, to engage in some PvP to get another players grinding, but as mentioned above, that will only get you rubles (if anyone buys their items back, but no one ever will.) But to make use of those rubles you need the event currencies anyway, making PvP even more pointless.Okay, so maybe instead you can use those theoretical rubles to buy the event currencies that another player is selling? Wise idea... But it's not cost-time-effective to do this and is primarily for endgame content, which means sinking a couple hundred of hours to make the auction shop useful. In other words, hope you're content with grinding the same boring event for a couple hundred hours. That's the whole game.

Note: This review has been further expanded on in the comments due to some people not understanding what this review really means, and who this review is really for.I really, really, want to recommend this game. But I can't for one major reason: The way emissions work needs to be changed to be more in line with the traditional STALKER experience. 1) Scientists sending out warnings over the PDA network to inform of a coming emission.2) Above-ground structures providing cover from emissions provided that they are fully built and secure.Without these two things, frustration and eventual burnout are inevitable. It is not fun to be caught out in the Zone with no hope of escaping an emission. Part of the fun of such a mechanic was the ability to run for the hills and get to safety in some building, only for a bandit to be hiding inside.EDIT: A smaller but also important issue pertains to anomalies. Some of them are too hard to see or hear. Vortex in particular is a frequent cause of death. I have an Artifact detector of sorts. It mentions something about a 'passive' radius for detection at about 60m. I was hoping it would alert me to anomalies as well, but it does not seem to alert me to the presence of an anomaly that is about to kill me in the way that one from STALKER would: Panic inducing beeps. Those beeps from a detector are crucial for survival in the Zone. Why do we not have such a tool?Edit 2: The detector isn't even for anomalies. It's JUST a metal detector to find crafting materials. Come on now. Where are the iconic STALKER tools?

This adds an extra layer of realism to the game's world.Combat in STALCRAFT can be challenging and unforgiving. The player must manage their weapons and ammunition carefully, as resources are limited. The game's AI is also intelligent, and enemies will work together to try and outflank the player.Overall, STALCRAFT is an excellent game that has aged surprisingly well. Despite being over three months old, the game's unique blend of horror, exploration, and open-world gameplay still holds up. If you're a fan of horror games, first-person shooters, or open-world games, STALCRAFT is a must-play.

I like the idea of the gameplay and aesthetic but there's a few things that make it very difficult to like the game, instead I'm just left thinking about how the game could be better.The most major issue with the game is the crafting system. If you did not buy every weapon/armor or whatever piece of equipment from the first area, you will have to walk back there to buy it. You also need to do a rep grind in this tutorial area that is extremely boring or else you will not be able to continue the upgrade paths in the next areas if those items require it. The gun crafting system also makes very little sense, it is very outlandish that you have to trade in guns all the way down the line with a couple materials each time to get the next gun.This issue with the crafting system is compounded by how long it takes to travel between bases. There is no fast travel, so between the first and 2nd base is just 20 minute round trip of holding shift W. The most simple solution is obviously just remove the requirement to go to a specific base to craft items, but in that case you'd still be stuck with rep grinds for certain items in previous zones if you didn't do them. The best solution would be to remove the trade in requirement and not require you to go down a line of items to upgrade.The AI in this game is also very bad. Human NPCs feature the same AI as the mutants, they just walk at you while shooting, they make no effort to use cover or anything like that. Every interaction with enemies will involve you being run down by a train of 4-10 enemies, just kiting them backwards. This feels especially bland since the first 2 areas will have you doing this to dogs and rats.Because of how much walking there is, when you die you also drop all consumable items aside from those in pouches that you have to open. This means that when you die, you either need to buy/retrieve from storage, ammo for each gun you are carrying, medkits, a plate for your platecarrier if it broke, and a piece of bread if you remember to for increased stamina regen. It is far too often that I had left base to run back to where I died while forgetting to buy 12g shells, to then have to return to camp or suffer being incapable of killing mutants since non shotgun weapons do negligible damage to them.In the same issue of running being extra tedious, there's 2 more issues. Because this game was a minecraft mod originally, the terrain is very sharp on slopes, and these slopes cause a really bad slowdown if you do not jump them, and jumping consumes a large amount of stamina. There's also a large amount of anomalies, a lot of them have dust clouds that make them visible, but others only have air distortion like heat and are extremely difficult to spot while running. So it is not uncommon that you would run into one thinking there's nothing there, especially when actively avoiding the ones with dust clouds that you can see. This is made worse that some of these invisible anomalies will just instantly kill you requiring you to run back. And if you want your backpack that was left there, if another player did not take it, you have to risk dying to the anomaly again.

TL;DR Game is fun, community is incredibly toxic, EXBO aren't prioritising help for newer players.Let me start off by saying this game is fun.That being said as the game currently stands I cannot recommend anyone to play this game.There are a few systems that are fundamentally flawed that gets more and more noticeable the further you get into the game.The biggest issue for newer players is 'Matchmaking'.The matchmaking system is a hidden system in the game that you cannot view, your gear score is irrelevant.Whenever you leave the safe zone the game takes a 'screenshot' of your gear. You will be match made to what the game believes is your highest level gear you have ever worn.If you get a Purple or a Red quality item from a loot box or the Season pass and go to take it for a spin, you will suddenly be fighting people with Purple/Red gear. Even if you go back to your earlier gear you will still be facing people that heavily out gear you.Sealclubbing/GatekeepingEventually you will reach the Bar. Regardless of which side you are on, Stalker or Bandit. There will be other factions camping your locations just for the sake of PvPing or ruining your day. They usually have zero reason for being there, sometimes they will steal your resource bag and sell it back to you via the Auction House OR drop it somewhere. Sometimes they will drop it somewhere easy to find, sometimes they will drop it in a impossible location. If they die, they can be back within minutes while you can lose all of your farm. They also usually will outclass you in equipment and artifacts.This both gets better and worse in the North.The North:You've finally made it to the end game. Both Bandits and Stalkers both get split into 2 Subfactions each. The game is now a four faction game instead of two.Each subfaction has their own 'Safe Zone' (Note other factions can walk to the safe zone) with access to the very basics. The resources you can gain from these safe zones are much lower than the conflict zones, but generally speaking it's a much more pleasant time farming in your Safe or the Conflict zone next to you compared to the Bar areas. It's a lot faster to run back if you die as well.That being said, the camping and gate keeping gets a lot worse, expect to see the same names pop up over and over again at the entrances and exists to zones in the North. At this point they don't even try to hide it. Some people even have alts in other factions so they can scout the areas safely and worse, trade your dropped loot over to a alt that is friendly to you so you can't get it back. (Which according to EXBO is a perfectly legitimate strategy)Clans:So you have either saved up 10,000,000 and decided to create a clan or you are applying to join one.It's worth noting that established top clans typically control most of the market for high quality artifacts and equipment and have high KD and gear requirements. But my recommendation is to try to get into a top clan rather than creating one.First off congratulations, you have made it to the very endgame content.If you decided to make your own clan, in order to promote anyone to any sort of administrative position you will need to level up your clan. Else your clan has three ranks, Recruit, Trooper and Leader.How do you level up your clan?You need to recruit 30 members.You need to perform 10 (very easy) special deliveries (Capped at 3 a day)You need to win 5 subdivision battle stages.The problem is with the subdivision battles. They are a mess.Clan Subdivision Battles:Every day at the same time, a Clan Subdivision battle can occur. Either a Brawl, a Tournament or a fight over one of four locations on the Map at Forge-11. If for whatever reason you cannot make that specific time of day, tough luck, you can't participate.Clan Subdivision battles are the only way to obtain Crimson Casings.If you are a new clan, you will struggle to win any of these unless you can get all your members online and geared up in +15 Master gear and have a decent artifact build.As a Brawl is a 4 way fight, where alliances is allowed. Typically speaking the top clans will try to 'buy' the lower clans out so they can get a free or easy win. You will either need to get lucky and hope you get matched against three other even clans or just try again another day.A Tournament is a 1v1 fight between two clans, that only happen on specific days of the week. The easiesst way to level up your clan to level 2 is to win at Tournaments as it's less chaotic. But then again you have to get lucky one of the 10 clans that signed up is at your level and you get paired with them. (Not many people actually sign up to Tournaments)Basically subdivision battles come down to how active your clan is and how much money you can invest in your clan mates.RMT: (Real money trading)Did I mention this game can be considered completely pay to win?On the surface, there isn't too much to see. You can buy a Season Pass and Premium, both offer slight advantages but both can be easily obtained using in game currency if you wanted. This is the first time that a MMO game has taken my interest.For a long time after discovering stalker anomaly and subsequently the original trilogy, i have always wondered what it would've like to play a stalker game in multiplayer. While this is very different from the original Stalker game it is a good enough adaptation of a MMO version that EXBO has made.There are quest from NPC's, daily quest and courier quest from Cordon's garage base (i'm a stalker), dynamic quest from hunting mutants and clearing enemy camps. I have a tendency to clear hunting missions a lot more rather than clearing camps because the enemy can literally snipe you with any weapon that they are holding forcing you to snipe back or just rush towards the nearest cover and play the game as a cover shooter.The trading system where you can progress your gear is great but i would've preferred to grind just money to buy more rather than getting insignificant items on specific quest on specific locations. Makes the grind much more bearable considering the clearing camps quest are in the enemy territories which can lead you to lose all of your hard work just like that.Also the anomalies man they're not as visible or recognizable as the original. The anomalies effects cant be seen on a naked eye unless you see the distortion that it makes. There are no anomaly detection noise (like in stalker anomaly) and the sounds of the anomalies are too quite or just non existent (trampoline).While this game is certainly unique from the original it does have its problems that i hope can be solved by the devs by introducing alternative solutions rather than changing how you deal with them now for the people that are fine with them.I hope this game flourishes so that new stalkers can enjoy the stalker universe.edit: new update brought limansk (new high tier area) and a new emission alert system, where a guy will radio you on the stages of the emission (alert, start with small damage, peak and end) and show you on where are the shelter or safe spaces from the emission. very good QoL update i hope there will be more update further onSteam Awards 2023 edit: the game certainly has gotten some good updates over the months, the dead man marathon event for the haloween is one of my favorite events with how much replayable it is, although the lootbox system is stilll ♥♥♥♥. over 200+ boxes never have i gotten the gold blueprint for me to finish the collection to trade it in, really a waster of time and money that part. the clan war update certainly added some good competition where the rewards are tradeable currency that you can trade with for like serums, anomalous battery for energy and more. also the anti-cheat and cheater situation is still up in the air. the devs tried to add an intrusive anti-cheat but that only results in steam services being unavailable for the game making some players cant login to the game making them unable to play. i would still recommend this game just for the stalker multiplayer experience where you can grind together with friends and fight againts other players while others might not like that aspect of the game. i hope with future updates for the game it can resolve the current problems and make the game more accessible for new players.

The STALKER-inspired MMO/PVP-PVE we always wished for is finally here and its free. I reccomend it solely for how much of love letter it is towards one of my favorite franchises, STALKER. However, the game is a mixed bag of genuinely great ideas but also horrible decisions from developers, that just makes you question on what were they thinking on adding this or that.Here's what to expect:-Plays similar to Escape from Tarkov by being somewhat like an extraction type, but you don't lose everything when you die. Your gear and "protected" items remain with you, so its not a complete loss, but at same time it can be very daunting if you happen to carry great amount of loot.-The progression mechanics are well made at beggining, but after a while it just degrades into "either you pick meta or you never win a single fight", giving you little options of gear. Lately the game is getting lot of rebalance changes so I assume they're working on reducing the "meta-overshadowing-everything" issue.-The grinding can be challenging at start, but at much later it becomes very tedious as you're required to do exact same boring acitivties for over 100 times (no exagguration) for just ONE armor or weapon. If you don't mind the mindless grind, then great, otherwise, you might find yourself putting the game away after the main questline.-Quests have multiple outcomes and rewards, and can be failed, which is cool feature. But at same time many quests are exceptionally badly designed, especially the main questline. Its not uncommon for players to quit because of questline being extremely difficult and unfair for no good reason.-PvP is fun and is to be expected almost anywhere, there are arena-like gamemodes to partake and the matchmaking system tries its best to group similarly-geared players together. However it can sometimes have a hiccup and have you face players with weapons far stronger than yours.-Part of PvE comes from hostile NPCs that appear around maps to attack players. Now this is all well and good, but they can sometimes create an unfair scenario of screwing you over in heated PvP battle, such as revealing your position. They also tend to be exceptionally annoying at following you across the map.-Artifacts are special items that improve your character's stats, such as giving you movement speed or extra resistance to damage. These artifacts are found in "anomalies" that appear about anywhere. And these "anomalies" are deadly forces that can kill you if you aren't careful, as well as contaminated zones that require proper hazard protection. So on top of NPCs, you got all these death-zones to avoid, greatly punishing lack of perception and uncontrolled greed for those lustrious artifacts.Lot of people can find the difficulty of this game off-putting and that's understandable, it clearly caters to specific demographic of gamers who enjoy the upmost unforgiveable hardcore gameplay. Should you and your friends ever want to seek fortune within radioactive war-scarred wasteland, filled with hostile wildlife and unexplainable hazards... The Stalcraft is worth a shot. If it gets too much for you, don't be ashamed to stop playing, I'm sure you had a valid reason. But those who stay... I don't know what drags you towards the danger, but best of luck Stalker.

A nightmare of game design.Everything is clearly cobbled together from old ideas from the game's development. The game started off as a minecraft mod, turned into a standalone hardcore shooter, and then developed into a typical MMO but with rather tight shooting mechanics. The end product seems fine on its surface, but the game will make you frustrated more than once and often it's in a very bad way.When I got to a story quest well over twenty hours into the game and it gave me a new mechanic for moving around that environment that I have not seen since in the open world, I was able to put a finger on the feelings of wrongness that I had over the game. If you put 20 hours into this game, you'll play a good amount of nice content with a rather fun little bit of progression, grind, and PVP. If you put 25 hours into this game, you'll get to one of your first instanced dungeons that are a meat grinder of time, effort, and RNG. If you put 35 hours into this game, you'll get to one of your hopefully last instanced dungeons that introduce yet another new mechanic: Stealth.This game's stealth is not good.The enemies move around erratically, randomly, at odd intervals, and their detection cones are as far as their eyes can see and nearly 180 degrees from where their head is facing. Exclamation marks above their head show when they are close to looking at you. The problem is that the moment they see even a small bit of you for more than a quarter of a second, they'll come to where they saw you at and look around. This means you can't duck behind cover or try to get out of the way. Considering the map this takes place in is open and filled with enemies, you can't even run reliably back to get out of the way. ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5)After a solid 16 hours in Stalcraft X, I’m intrigued. It’s an ambitious blend of STALKER-style atmosphere with MMO elements, wrapped in a voxel aesthetic that feels fresh yet hauntingly familiar. While it has a few rough edges, Stalcraft X manages to deliver a compelling survival experience that keeps you coming back for more. Here’s why it’s worth diving into:Stalcraft X combines gritty survival mechanics with the exploration-driven atmosphere of post-apocalyptic Chernobyl. You’ll spend a lot of time scavenging, fighting off mutated creatures, and constantly managing your resources. The challenge of staying alive makes each encounter meaningful, and every piece of loot feels like a small victory. The mix of PvE and PvP elements adds a unique tension; you never know if that distant shadow is a friend, foe, or mutated beast lurking in the fog.Progression in Stalcraft X is satisfying, with a focus on skill-based growth and gear upgrades. While you start out feeling vulnerable, every upgrade makes a noticeable difference in how you handle the game’s many threats. There’s a good balance between grinding and reward, and as you explore, you naturally grow stronger, finding better weapons, armor, and supplies to aid in your survival.The voxel visuals might seem like a strange choice for a survival shooter, but Stalcraft X manages to make it work. The environments are moody and eerie, capturing the desolation of a radioactive wasteland while adding an uncanny charm. The foggy landscapes, abandoned buildings, and radioactive hotspots feel alive, each filled with secrets and dangers that beckon you to explore. And the sound design enhances this atmosphere, with distant cries and eerie wind sounds keeping you on edge.The player community is an interesting blend of helpful and competitive. People are often willing to offer advice to new players, but in the field, it's every stalker for themselves. It’s a nice mix that adds both camaraderie and tension. Teaming up with other players can be beneficial, especially in more challenging zones, but there’s always that thrill of not knowing who you can trust.After 16 hours, Stalcraft X has left a strong impression. It’s gritty, intense, and surprisingly immersive for a voxel-based game. While it’s not perfect and has a bit of a learning curve, it offers a fresh take on the survival genre, with plenty to keep players invested. If you’re looking for a unique survival game that blends exploration, PvP, and PvE in a haunting, radioactive world, Stalcraft X is worth checking out. for survival game fans who crave something different in a gritty, voxel-stylized Chernobyl setting!

This game is goodHere's a review for the game:The Good:-The story for the game is actually original and non-linear, and makes a good amount of sense-the environment and immersion is also pretty good, from time to time when you wander the zone you will hear sounds like a scream in the distance, really builds the atmosphere of you not being the center of everything-the progression is also rather good, whenever you have to go to a new location you tend to stay in your current one for a bit and prepare, get some good gear from your area. My advice to new ppl playing this game is to take your time-Locations, this game has a lot of locations and though they are mostly inspired by STALKER they are still nice to wander around in-you don't have to talk to people to do a quest or find info/lore about the game, when you wander the zone you tend to find things that just tell a story about what happened. there are also hidden quests-good youtubers, i would like to HIGHLY rate MaximumAggro on YouTube because when i played the game 1st try he carried my ass so hard, he has guides for every quest in the game for both factions-when you talk to someone or find someone, while you do tend to go your separate ways the people in the game are really friendly-has quests to do even after you complete the main story (which gives you a good level suit for you to explore new areas) -loads of quest weapons, giving you an incentive other than cash to actually do them-The quests are actually interesting and give a good amount of lore-gives you an incentive to explore because higher level gear needs new materials that you probably cant find in your current area, a general rule of thumb is that the higher in the map you go, the more dangerous it gets-there's voice chat-if you die while hauling a ♥♥♥♥ ton of loot, all isn't lost! you drop a backpack that has all the materials in it that no-one but you can open. if someone finds it and mails it back, you still get those materials (not for junk though)-when you die you dont lose your gun or suit, just any junk or materials, or bullets that you brought with you so once you buy something from a vendor, if its a gun or suit you prob wont have to buy it againThe Bad:-Grinding is really really repetitive, you have to earn hundreds of materials when you get to the bar and sometimes even thousands just to get one suit, and sometimes you cant even skip a generation of them, for example lets say i wanted to get a suit called X. Now, to get that suit i have to trade in a suit called Z plus loads of bartering items, and to get the Z suit i have to go a few locations back to get the suit Y.  Its really repetitive, and even when you have the correct suit you have to grind the materials for it not to mention the cash needed.-Re spawning, this isn't really a problem with the game itself but when you are in a place where it took you 10 mins to RUN to WHILE UNDER THE EFFECTS OF SPEED BOOSTING ITEMS, and then either DIE THERE or BECAUSE YOU HAD TO RUN BACK TO A PREVIOUS ZONE TO GET A SUIT NEEDED FOR EVOLUTION (but its not a problem with the actual game)-when you first start out, anomalies are really hard to see and once you get sucked into a black hole, you cant really do anything. its rather annoying to die all of a sudden because you didn't see anything (but its not totally a bad thing, it teaches you to watch out and be more observant)-this isn't the games fault either, but on the SEA servers like there's very little people playing-once you complete the main story, you kind of lose interest in the game after a whileOverall, i would describe this game as a gem of Steam, and i'd give it a 8/10 or a 9/10, glad i found this game and i suggest you play it

The open world PvP is what makes this game. In some way it scratches a similar itch to your average extraction shooter (or Tarkov like) but with much lower stakes as you never drop gear on death, only ammo, meds and sellable/tradeable items.The PvE based missions are fun enough, and actually have some pretty good instanced single player missions that give me high hopes for coop dungeons, a feature that is not in yet but promised for later. Most open world PvE missions are kind of just fetch quests or "Go there and kill 10 rats" kind of deal, but the tension is always high as the risk of bumping into an enemy player is always there. I thought the open world PvP would bother me but I've really fallen in love with it. You are given a lot of tools that make it difficult to be completely surprised. Whenever a friendly player is killed by an enemy player their death location is marked on the map, so you know there's someone around that area. And there's a counter that goes up whenever you are near another player, but it doesn't specify what faction they are, so you'll want to find and identify if there's a friendly near you, because otherwise it might mean you are in danger. It helps that the game also shows you where the main towns for both factions are so you can make an educated guess based on which town is closest if that nearby unseen player might be friendly, but its never 100% guaranteed as quests often push players into enemy territory, so that player could very well be an enemy sneaking around to complete a quest, or just looking for easy kills.Overall I highly recommend the game, but you have to treat it as a PvP focused game as the PvE aspects would be repetitive without that added player tension, and its not like you can just chose not to participate in PvP, you WILL be killed by opponent players, so better accept that, arm up and defend yourself :)

I really want to like this game, it has a nice (albeit frequently used) concept and game-play. I do find the idea of player factions unique as well. However, my main problem that is keeping me from recommending this game is how you are introduced into the zone (after the tutorial). The swamp area you find yourself in definitely helps you learn the basics of the zone that the tutorial did not contain (like certain people to talk to to buy weapons or to sell artifacts). The problem with this area is that every time I tried to do a simple quest or minding my own business outside of a safe zone I was constantly attacked by players of the opposing faction. I've lost more ammo from dying to enemy players than shooting the enemy faction. It was really frustrating to have to make my way back to where I died only to find nothing there after I died multiple time trying to get back to where I first died. It would be better if the first area was a place where you would only encounter bots so that you can get used to the AI before you encounter other players in the next area.It also should be mentioned that the AI for the enemy NPCs that you encounter are very OP and can generally pick you off from about 100 meters away with their sub-machine guns. Fighting the AI is difficult enough but when you add enemy player who most likely has better equipment than you, It's VERY hard to progress. Having the first area a place where you only encounter bots would definitely help with teaching players how the over powered AI and the zone function and not feel like being punched in the face by other players. Another way the devs could mitigate this problem would be to lower how far they can shoot you, lower their accuracy, and just some general nerfing. I personally like the AI difficulty, though, it makes me think and strategize like no other FPS I've played before. Otherwise, it was a fun experience (ignoring the above problems of course) with great animations and graphics. I really wish I could like this game but with how it flows in the first area I can't really recommend this game especially for people who want to play casually.

This is a really, really, really solid bedrock for something special.  There's a lot of familiar mechanics here, but arranged in ways that make the game more unique than the individual components.  As it's also free to play, it's a very easy recomend and you'll get probably 50+ hours before you feel fatigue set in if you're a fan of this kind of game, but that also comes with a few concerning areas and negatives.The gameplay loop is basic, but enjoyable.  The game is broken up into zones, which are then filled with NPC humans, NPC monsters and mini-events.  These drop variable types and amounts of materials you require to upgrade yourself, from your weapons to armor to misc. gear items.  You travel the area killing and gathering, doing main and side/optional quests to gain these resources and money, upgrade your items to the next tier, then move on to the next area where you do it again.  All the while, you are supported by friendly-faction players and under threat from enemy faction players.This is the first good change from a standard loot-shoot PVP, taken from a more RPG style game.  There are many guns in the game, but most require you to first purchase them as a basic grey item, then upgrade them from area to area to the next form.  What starts as a bolt action rifle turns into a winchester rifle turns into a heavy duty sniper.  What starts as a 3-round burst assault rifle turns into a fully automatic M16, etc.  This is what gives your progression purpose in each area, as you require the upgrade materials.    While dying causes you to drop your ammo, health, most consumables and all your currently held upgrade materials, you  drop any of your weapons or armor.  This means the threat of dying is the threat of losing the last 10, 20, 50, etc, minutes of farming items to upgrade your gear, but  the gear itself you spent the last 15 hours upgrading.  While I highly enjoyed this system and having the game act like a mix of Rust PVP and slower/calmer MMO questing, issues begin to appear in the latter stages of the game, where the cost to upgrade guns begins to skyrocket for marginal benefits. The world is broken into two groups, Bandits and Stalkers (who are later also broken into sub-factions but just imagine it as two sides for expedience.)  While there are some areas of the game that are essentially faction-specific, having basically no reason for the other faction to be present, the entire world save for safe-zones is more or less accessible to both sides at all times.  This means, as you are questing, farming or just traveling, you are constantly under threat from being killed not just by NPCs or hazards, but other players as well.  This will send you back to the last-visited base/safezone, and drop all your non-bound (typically everything but your weapons/armor) gear where you died.  However, this comes with some caveats for both victim and killer; though you can freely loot dead enemy and even friendly players of their consumables, ammo, etc, you cannot steal their weapons.  Additionally, you cannot steal the upgrade materials needed to advance your own gear's progression.  These items drop in a player-specific backpack item, meaning you cannot simply gank enemy players to steal their upgrade materials rather than farm for it yourself.  This means PVP is in a somewhat weird space as there is, usually, no significant reward for fighting other players save for preventing them from killing you.  While you can quickly amass consumables this way, the only benefit is for money from selling any loot they are carrying (you cannot sell ammo/consumables, only specific loot items from enemy NPCs) or to ransom the player's backpack of upgrade materials on the auction house.  Where the player you just killed can decide if they want to spend 5, 10, 20k rubles to buy back their loot from their killer, or simply write it off as a loss and go farming again.  Additionally, because of the difference in loot, the game is broken up into brackets to prevent stomping of early players.  Reaching certain thresholds (going from grey > green gear, green > blue, blue > blue+5, etc) prevents you from encountering newer players and keeps you in instances with more experienced and better equipped players.There is a lot of enjoyment, but problems that also begin to appear as the late game approaches.  While early on, you have great highs and lows of going out, gathering a lot of resources, losing it, getting lucky and killing an enemy with thousands of dollars worth of loot on him, etc, this wears thin as the amounts you're required to farm grow larger and larger.  A human NPC with loot will always drop around 3-5 'currency' of that area's human-specific loot, but whereas in the beginning you may only need 30-40 of this currency to buy a gun, you'll then need 90 of the next area to upgrade it.  Then 140 human and 200 mutant resource to upgrade it again.  Then 350 human, 400 mutant and 80 special event.  And you're carrying 2-4 guns, at least 2 armor sets, bags, melee weapons, attachments which all have their own upgrade tree, etc.  This not only slows the pace down extremely, it makes the game incredibly and deliberately grindy in order to encourage the player to pay for premium membership, which more than doubles the rate of dropped/gathered upgrade materials.This is compounded by the current issue of PVP irrelevance.  Money is not hard to acquire with a bit of effort, and you can far more reliably make 50k in 15-30 minutes doing events than trying to steal it off players who may or may not even have loot, or trying to ransom back bags for 15-20k if they are especially loaded.  On top of there not being really any good reason to PVP once you reach the midgame grind, being progressively matched against better and better players means a constant feeling of spinning your wheels in the mud.  None of your upgrades feel especially significant past a point because everyone upgrades around you to counter it, and you one-tap headshotting a new player with a sniper in hour 3 is about the same feeling as you 2-3 shotting a player with a blue+5 assault rifle in hour 50, or visa versa.  The very nefariously paced experience to practically force going premium or suffering ten+ hours of grinding for a single tier upgrade is also a bad thing, and that's completely ignoring the 'elite super rare' guns/armors that require farming events with a 1% droprate needing 10+ drops, or a guaranteed drop from an event you can find once every 10-20 minutes needing 150 drops for a single cosmetic.This is still a recommend, even after all you've read, if you love open-world shooters with PVP aspects, or if you love the idea of a multiplayer STALKER game with all the nuttiness that inherently entails.  However this is absolutely not a finished game even if the main quest is 'finished' and there's no early-access tag.  The late game is a mess, there are many good design decisions that are undermined by a lack of purpose, and though gunplay and PVP is fun, it is currently pointless for anything more than laughing as you frag someone and get a brief endorphin rush before realizing you didn't actually gain anything and may not have even earned enough to cover the cost of the ammo you just spent.  You can get some solid hours of enjoyment here, but only until fatigue sets in and you, seeing the grind ahead of you that serves no purpose but to deliver you more pointless PVP, put it down to do something else.

Stalcraft is the only MMO I have ever found interesting enough to play. Based on the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. game series, which was based on the novel "Roadside Picknick" by Arkadiy and Boris Strugatsky, and it´s movie adaptation "Stalker" by Andrei Tarkovsky, the game puts you in the boots of adventurer who wants make a living in the Zone - region, where after strange catastrophe physical laws were bent, many hazardous areas called "anomalies" emerged and local flora and fauna mutated beyond recognition. Valuable "artefacts" with supernatural abilities can be found in these anomalies, and sold for a fortune. Some say the Zone is a punishment for humanity, some see it as a gift, which is also reflected in philosophies of different in-game factions you can join.The basic gameplay is FPS with survival elements in semi-open world. What I see as most important aspect of the game is freedom of choice, how to approach the gameplay and progression. There are no character classes in the game, neither there is leveling (you do "level" your reputation in bases that allow gear progression though). Your stats are based on gear you equip (weapons, armor, containers which allow you to benefit from artefact abilities etc.). Most of the gear is bartered at bases for materials that you find in the Zone, mostly by killing mutants and other factions NPCs. There is definitels a grinding aspect to this that gets steeper the more you progress. Following the storyline gives you decent starting gear for free, but to be viable in PvP, you need to grind for better ones.Now here comes the problem that may turn many people away from this game. The PvP is always enabled in the whole world except the bases. When you get killed, you drop everything except your gear - that means consumables like ammo and medkits, but also valuables like artefacts not bound in containers, and most importantly, also all the crafting materials you were grinding for. Enemy can loot them, but not use them - it´s up to the enemy player of they are nice enough to send the materials back to you via mail, or sell them back to you in auction. Mostly people just throw them away, so may feel your time spent grinding has been wasted.And that´s true, but it´s also part of the unique atmosphere of constant danger, true to the source material and older games. Without this atmosphere, you could not feel the immense joy when fellow Stalker shows up and saves you in the right moment, or when the enemy is nice enough to send you your lost backpack back and wish you a nice day. There is emphasis on player interaction, and maybe if you will be nice to other players and return their materials regularly, others will also act this way towards you.As I´m not a regular MMO player, I enjoy the storyline and atmosphere more than farming for materials. But there are ways to bypass the grind. Basically everything except gear can be sold and bought at the auction with player-driven economy. You can do things like market speculation - buy items when they are at low, and later sell them for higher price, making a profit. This way, I was able to sell rewards from recent events for big money. This is important, because there are exceptions with gear - some special weapons and armor which are very good even at later game, can be purchased in auction for high prices with basic currency. You can´t buy all your gear this way, but you can purchase a decent later game weapon and armor this way, without ever sticking your head out of the base, if you wish. Also there was very decent gear obtainable by just playing recent special events that take place like 3 times per year. Gameplay of these events can be also grindy, but they ensure your progression towards this gear without chance to lose it.Make no mistake, this game is hard and punishing. But if you enjoy more old style gameplay with not hand-holding, this game may be for you. It is the best MMO with Stalker theme I have found. Obviously it can be a lot easier, if you play with group of friends, but even as solo player I must say it is totally enjoyable.If you decide to try Stalcraft, I have a tip for you: look at player count and if your timezone allows it, grind only at low server population times of the day. This way you will see a lot less people, which will make your grinding much less dangerous and also makes each encounter with other players more memorable.I said come in, don´t just read reviews.Get out there, Stalker, and make some friends!

This is a review of this game with 166.2 hours played (as of writing this) and has completed both South Zone & North Zone main-quest lines (on 9/18/24).  And again, this isn't a hard "dig" at the game; it still has promise and can be fun, so please give it a try at least!The good parts:- F2P Stalker game that combines aspects of PvP and PvE in a large exploratory world with other players- As I currently understand, there are a few playable areas in the base game (South Zone, North Zone, Lyubech-3, Stillwaters, Labyrinth?)- Main & Sub Quest lines can give you gear upgrades (rather than spending rubles & resources in-game), but you must know which dialogue options to select to get that said item- Matchmaking for servers take in multiple factors (gear score, K/D, amount of players online at given time, etc.)- Freely able to join-in & play with other people in your faction (Bandits/Stalkers) within the world or bases respectively- Generally plenty of stash space (as long as you max out your base rep)- You can buy the battle-pass from just playing the game with gaining "Act Tickets" (if you don't spend any before you reach the required amount)- Ability to gain better gear from in-game buy-able crates without paying money (from points you earn in the battle-pass)- Daily & Weekly tasks and Backpack delivery tasks to help with material collection processThe rough parts:- If you want to proceed past a certain point AND feel like you are progressing gear-acquisition wise, you MUST buy Premium (in order to get more materials faster).  This is $10 for a month, $20 for 3 months, and $30 for 6 months respectively.  This is non-negotiable, as this will take you 5x longer without doing this (even start to feel this as early as getting introduced to the Black Willows/Kolos Agrocomplex zones due to cache looting/searching)- Most players quit about half-way through the South Zone due to how harsh the grind is for gear from collecting materials (for reference, it took me a little over two weeks to get my veteran gear in the third hideout called "The Bar" playing 6-7 hours a day straight every day; this is considered the end of the South Zone grind and is supposed to be nothing compared to the North Zone grind) before moving on to the North Zone (second map zone).- Game loop can be considered okay within first two areas of the South Zone (The Swamps & Roadside), but get old extremely, EXTREMELY quickly (and the game play loop changes to a certain slight degree once you reach the North Zone, which is essentially better QoL for the events you did in the South Zone)- Fighting over loot between teammates/squadmates in your faction happens extremely frequently, leaving you with nothing if you don't play extremely selfishly and rush to get loot BEFORE you even decide to fight AI humanoids/animals/mutants (when others are around you).- Game does an extreme skim over how to do certain things in the game (only recently learned how to upgrade artifacts ONLY AFTER COMPLETING THE NORTH ZONE MAIN QUEST LINE from other people). Most things you will have to learn will be through outside resources (player wiki/youtube guide/asking other players in-game).- Only starts to introduce revive stims at max-level Bar (third base).  This is a problem where the majority of players tend to play solo in the first two base zones and players typically don't group up until they start grinding from Bar hideout areas (would be a nice QoL to have this earlier)- Main difference in PvE when progressing is that AI humanoids/animals/mutants simply just become "tankier" as you move on, not giving the player any new experiences in how to approach/deal with fights (gets old quickly, especially for early game quest bosses in South Zone; excluding final South Zone quest boss).- Lack of "reward" from killing other players essentially.  Yes, you can loot certain items off players, but materials they have collected are off-limits for you (can only either sell it back to them via Auction which most people don't buy back, gift it back to them which is extremely rare, or sell it to the trader in the base for pennies).  This is understandable from a cheater prevention level, but doesn't feel rewarding and essentially help you progress gear-wise as a player (and hence could make PvP more enticing to do).- Noticeably smaller player base after attaining lowest-level veteran gear (primarily now fighting against high upgraded Veteran gear players or master level gear players at all times)- Matchmaking fails to work properly due to smaller player base (that at least I feel; especially noticeable if you have base Veteran gear with no upgrades in South Zone).  Low level veteran gear players with no upgrades can now infrequently (about 20%-30% of the time) be seen in servers that have Master level gear players with +10 upgrades- Players generally only group-up to do PvP activities (and avoid grouping unless you are playing with friends due to the massive decrease of resources you gain during material runs).  Hence, the grind of the game pushes people away from grinding mats together/grouping in the South Zone (especially since loot from events feels like it is EXTREMELY performance based; unknown if it is damage driven or kill count driven).- You only unlock Daily & Weekly tasks, as well as, backpack deliveries once you get to the second base (Located in Roadside). Not terrible but could help out with some grinds if introduced earlier (especially if it's just Daily & Weekly tasks being introduced at The Swamp).- This game is a MASSIVE walking sim.  If you need to get a specific weapon/armour from the barter tree because you didn't pick something up at that base earlier (before you moved on), you MUST go back to that base to barter for that item before moving through that tree (this only changes once you get to the Bar hideout, where you can buy some weapons/armour immediately for a LOT of mats; hence adding to the sheer insanity of the grind).Overall, this game has a lot of promise and potential to be extremely fun and enjoyable, but is overshadowed by a completely insane material grind which starts when the game introduces you to cache hunting (hence where the fun-levels start to decrease and it feels like another 9-5 job to collect mats just to progress). Even though the player base (going off of Steam Charts & not including their own launcher) has increased from 8.9k players (peak players July 1, 2024) to 23.3k (peak players September 16, 2024), only 7.7% of players have completed the first story line in the South Zone, 7.4% of players have joined a faction for the North Zone, 4.3% of players have played one of their "Session Battle" modes seen when you press escape for the menu to find, 2.9% of players have completed a Weekly Task, and roughly 10% of players have achieved Veteran level gear (all of these being global achievements).  This just amplifies the effects of the lows on the game which are highlighted above (i.e. players aren't enticed to hang around).People have stated that they would be adding some form of "Raids" into the game in their next major update, alongside adjustments to the first zone (South Zone).  As raids in MMO's are considered end-game events for players, I am expecting this will only be shown for people that have progressed through the entirely of the South Zone quest-line (hence only the upper parts of the South Zone potentially; or maybe just for people who moved on through to the North Zone).  Regarding the South Zone adjustments, I do hope that QoL features that are present within the North Zone are utilized within the South Zone to make for a better grinding experience (material wise).Lastly, I hope there are changes/adjustments to looting that do not extremely hamper the player experience & allow people to play in groups more while doing PvE events; while not feeling like their mats collection is being negatively impacted.

What do you do? You run around completing quests, gathering resources, and upgrading your gear. As you progress the resource grinding for gear becomes more and more grindy. First level you needed 10 of an item, then later on you need 1,000 of an item. You get the idea. There's also artifact hunting which is very fun to do, just like in STALKER. Occasionally there's PVP, but we will get into that later. Also, despite CRAFT being in the name, the game has very little similarity to Minecraft. There is however the new hideout system added in the X update.Is there a Main Quest? Yes, its a very long one, it involves boss fights, problem solving, and parkour. Its at times very frustrating, very ambitious, and very tedious. During the quest you get rewarded with items such as armors, and weapons. These are very overpowered, almost to the point of making you wonder why you are grinding in the first place. It took me around 5-8 hours to upgrade my armor to Veteran quality, and its still not as good as the Veteran quality Exoskeleton given to me by the main quest. Later on theres faction quests which again, give you some really good stuff - an SVU, a shotgun sidearm, and even a ticket that lets you get a free Veteran quality armor of your choice.Graphics and Sound? Graphically the game looks like 7 Days to Die, not everything is blocky like in Minecraft, instead they opt for a voxel style, and decent textures. The armors are done very well, the guns are done very well, even changing in appearance to other players depending on which scopes and attachments you have equipped. The sound is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Some surfaces have no sound whatsoever when running over them, some surfaces make the wrong sound when running over them, the guns sound like ass, the mutants barely make any noises, player footsteps only play when they are like 5 meters from you, you get the idea. Fast forward to the X update and the sound is still ass, but the graphics do look a bit better - no more blocky trees, some nice water and godrays.How's the PVP? Well its kinda OK. The TTK (Time To Kill) is extremely fast, so upgrading your gear is very important. You have a nearby player meter that goes up and down depending on players who are 50 meters from you, it doesn't differentiate between friendlies or enemies. If you're in a hostile area then its a 99% probability of being a enemy player. But if you're in a friendly area grinding, it could be anyone, and because of the hustle-bustle of players, that number is going up and down constantly *beep beep beep beep*The devs try to encourage PVP in several ways: by having you do things in the opposing factions area, this is great at creating tension, but it ends up in you running thru a friendly-area with loot, and getting ratted by some corner camper who has nothing to lose. The other way they encourage PVP is by giving you the option to join a sub-faction. For example you're a Bandit, you can join Mercs or Covenant. These sub-factions are at war with one another, so now when you're grinding for those 3,000 items you need, you can get shot in the back and lose it all.Why do I still recommend it? I have almost 200 hours and I'm hooked. It's very thrilling to return to base with an inventory full of loot, and say, "only 200 more diggy-doos left to get." and then gearing up to head back out there and see what kind of fortune or misfortune you incur.

An ACTUAL MMORPG-style shooter. Progression, your typical fetch quests, all within the vein of "open world" PvP. Zones can get pretty big, and dying can feel bad sometimes, but what open PvP game doesn't? You don't lose your guns, you don't lose your armor... You lose pretty much everything else, but I think that's great. Your risk for being out in the world is losing the mats to help you purchase and progress your next gun or armor upgrade and I think that's fine. You don't have to go out and REGRIND the armor and weapons you already own. I've heard lots of gripes about the end-game grind, and that can understandably become a problem. Enough of the community has said something to the point where they have buffed and nerfed some things. If you care enough to continue, you'll find more woes than positive feedback, but the game really isn't THAT bad. The grind gets pretty heavy, but it just creates more opportunities for PvP engagement and I've SELDOM run into anyone higher level going down into lower level zones just to mess around, so it's not like you'll be dying to something/someone you can't contend with. It's in your best interest to find some people to group up with and ask around in the game for someone to help out as the community is pretty nice overall.I think if Stalcraft received more attention and finances, they could really polish up and fix community gripes within much more reasonable timeframes. We could easily see more content as well, and seasonal content might be more frequent. It just needs attention and they need more of a Western audience to continue to cater to the Western audience. They apparently pander to Russian players, but idk if that's even remotely true. I've enjoyed my 66 hours in the game, and once I've got some more free time on my hands, I'll gladly return.7.5/10 game - could easily be 8.5 or higher with some content, balancing, and polishing.

Check out my Livestream review of STALCRAFT at Lunaril's Channel on TwitchFor those who want the short version, I'll give you the highlights, Pro's and Con's as I saw them.STALCRAFT is a PVPVE Shooter that combines aspects of Minecraft with the Stalker series storyline. The tutorial is pretty self explanatory, but some of the controls are a little wonky in places. The voice acting is in Russian, as the game takes place in the Chernobyl Exclusionary Zone, and I was not able to locate a way to change the settings for English, but the text and subtitles are in English, making it easy to understand what is happening and being said. I was unable to change the aspect ratio or graphical settings to resize the window of the game, it appears to only be in full screen mode. The controls are your basic survival settings, W,A,S,D for movement, inventory is E, and looting is F. There are other basic keyboard controls such as accessing your PDF, which contains quest and task information, maps, messages et cetera. Pretty standard stuff.Much like STALKER, there are bases and checkpoint settlements with merchants, researchers, mechanics and more to upgrade and repair gear, purchase gear, weapons and items, or complete quests for. You can explore and collect anomalies for study, take on Bandits if you are a member of the Stalker faction, or ambush Stalkers as a member of the Bandit faction. It seems that just about everywhere outside of faction areas is fair game for PVP, but the game does allow for a temporary invulnerability when entering or exiting new area's, to help reduce the damage that campers can do.There seems to be virtually no character customization, other than in game weaponry, gear and tactics of how you want to play, which I found disappointing and there also appears to possibly be a pay to win system when you visit the developers website, as you have the ability to purchase currency with real world money. Aside from these limitations and possible problems, the game looks neat, it's kinda fun, and made me a little nostalgic for the Stalker series as well as minecraft. Unlike Minecraft, you do not appear to be able to build in this game as it is primarily a shooter, but all in all for a free game it doesn't seem that bad. Check out my Livestream review for actual gameplay through the tutorial and first few quests to get a better understanding of the game. It probably wouldn't be a game I would play again, just because of the Con's I listed, but for anyone who enjoyed Minecraft and is also a fan of the Stalker series, you will probably get a kick out of this game.**Warning** After posting this review, I was sent a link to the discussion page where fans post about this game. My spouse Daeminos had asked a question in the general discussion about whether PvP was forced in the game, or whether it was optional. They had not seen my review and had only caught wind I was going to be playing it and obviously were interested in finding out more. Since I was busy with the review, editing the video and uploading everything, they went to the forums. The responses they received were completely toxic, with personal attacks, others joining in the pile on, my spouse was accused of trolling the forum, of  baiting and so forth. The sheer level of toxic behavior by active fans of the game, made it necessary to write this warning, as it is indicative of the types of players one is likely to encounter when they play STALCRAFT. I stand by my assessment of the game on it's merits and faults, but I urge everyone to evaluate whether this type of toxicity is something they want to put up with before deciding to play this game.
