Let me preface this review by saying that I enjoy this game. Terribly so. I'm a huge fan of the STALKER universe and genre as a whole, and this game is a welcome addition to the many stalker games/fan creations that I have come to experience over the years, but unfortunately I cannot recommend this game to anyone who does not have as much patience as I do.Now lets get to the review. Like many fan creations of games in the STALKER genre, STALCRAFT boasts an atmosphere full of life, mystery, and full on anxiety inducing panic attack moments that I oh so adore from these types of games. Your life can be so easily snuffed out, whether it be by an anomaly, bloodsuckers, or running from bloodsuckers into an anomaly, this game simply fills that empty space that STALKER: GAMMA left behind after I found myself longing for a multiplayer STALKER experience once again. Even if the characters in it are blocky minecraft characters that sort of throw you off balance every so often when you see their faces, this game makes you realize that its not just a bunch of funny looking block characters in a video game... It's a bunch of funny looking block characters fighting for their f*cking lives in The Zone.The gunplay feels solid in STALCRAFT. Gunning down creatures in The Zone feels just as good as it did the first time I ever played a STALKER game, and it keeps me coming back for more. Guns feel weighty and chunky, leaving you with that satisfying feeling that you just absolutely obliterated whatever you were shooting at. Not to mention the fact that the animations for the guns are absolutely gorgeous. I'm looking forward to unlocking more weapons and armor as I grind through this game.Speaking of grinding, the PvE loop in this game is honestly pretty damn good. It feels extremely rewarding when you make it back to a safe zone after an hour long grind session, not to mention the weight lifting from your shoulders knowing you made it back with the bag. Dying in this game means losing all of that loot you accumulated (unless you're able to run back and get it, granted nobody has looted your body.) The reputation grind system is also pretty straightforward and rewarding as well. Granting you bonuses to crafting/buying items in that specific safe zone.There is also a PvP gearscore matchmaking system in place, which makes sure you aren't matched with somebody that's going to absolutely rock your sh*t with a railgun as soon as you spawn in. This feature does help tolerate the PvP just a bit more at times, since areas seem to be a bit less congested than the early game once you're around 300 gearscore.  PvP is an absolute nightmare in this game as of this review, not to mention it plays no active role in making the world FEEL like STALKER. When you start the game and leave the first safe zone after picking one of two factions (STALKER or bandit,) you are immediately at risk of being PKed in the open world. This would be fine if it didn't mean you are sent back to safe zone, having dropped all of your ammo, meds, looted items etc. It's honestly not that bad in the early game, but once you reach the mid-game area called The Bar, you are immediately subject to camping and griefing from the enemy faction. It doesn't help that some of the materials needed to craft the mid-game armor and weapons up to this point require you to kill other players so you can sneak into their side of the map and try and grind out these items without being spotted and killed. There are essentially two types of looted items that you look out for when you're on the grind in STALCRAFT. These items are trash loot items which you sell to a vendor, and trade-in items which you use to craft guns and armor. When you die, players can loot these trash items and sell them to the vendor themselves, but the trade-in items drop in a little bag. This bag CANNOT be opened by the people who loot you. They can, however, choose to mail it to you (if they're feeling generous,) drop it on the ground so its lost forever, or list it on the auction house. Other people can buy the bag from the auction house, but only YOU can open it, which pretty much eliminates any reason to hunt players who are actively grinding. Sure you can kill people for their trash loot, but at the same time you can go out and grind it yourself for 90% less hassle than you would if you just wanted to kill people. This has made the PvP experience as a whole in this game feel like a waste of time, resources, and not to mention your f*cking sanity. You can be out in the open world, having spent hours of your time grinding it out, only for some guy to come along, kill you, and gain nothing from it. The mid-early game is horrible with this, being constantly camped/griefed while you try to do dailies/weeklies/MSQ/grind. To combat this I think it'd would be novel to introduce PvP specific zones, where fighting other players garners faction PvP repuation and PvP specific loot. Climbing through the PvP ranks in the open world, or in these zones and having actual positives/negatives to this open world PvP would spark my interest for it. Other than that, the PvP feels solid gunplay and balance wise. I never ran into a situation where I was like "wow that was busted" because I can just turn around and cap the guy who shredded me in a second. If everything is OP, nothing is.The main story quest is another gripe I have about this game. The story itself is not so bad, and progressing through it in the open world doesn't feel like much of a chore at all. However, once you get to the instanced zones in the story, it takes a nosedive in quality. This game introduces a climbing mechanic in the story which is honestly pretty neat, however you hardly ever use it in the open world besides during story specific missions. Sure I find myself climbing over things every now and then, but the things you can climb are extremely limited. The fact that I can't hop a fence in the middle of these areas I'm grinding out just doesn't make any sense to me at all (Specifically talking about regular ass fences that you simply cannot hurdle vs. the border fences in the game.) The instanced main story missions will occasionally use these climbing mechanics again, but it implements them horribly. One mission that stands out to me is the "Hunting Minstrel" mission. This mission has you climbing all throughout this cave that is a nightmare to navigate, and once you finally get to the "boss," it's just a bloodsucker that is faster than you, kills you in 3-4 hits, and is nigh impossible to kite around the pillars in the boss room. After 20 deaths in this mission I just said ♥♥♥♥ it and left. I honestly don't think I'll ever go back unless it's made less tedious to not only get back to the fight, but actually fight this "boss."The anomaly placement in this game is abysmal. Sure you get used to seeing 100 vortex anomalies on the road, and sure you'll get used to avoid the blackhole anomalies strewn about the open world, but the fact that they are just placed haphazardly throughout the entire world adds nothing to the overall STALKER experience. It also doesn't help that both of these anomalies are night invisible most of the time and running into them might mean you lose everything you just spent loads of time grinding for.I truly understand that the devs want to make this feel like a hardcore STALKER experience, but the way they went about it feels way too "tryhard" if you will. They have a lot to work on if they truly want this to be the experience that they want this game to provide its players. Like I said, I truly enjoy this game. I mean ♥♥♥♥ me it's a free STALKER-lite mmorpg that has been really getting me going lately, but I feel like it could be so much better.

I am mostly a casual gamer and enjoy a bit of side mission hustles and the grind is tolerable. My only issue is the PvP. Now Im not against PvP entirely but I'd say a PvE option would be a good addition for those who enjoy just trying to survive the brutal landscape (darn you blackholes and sending my items everywhere). Traversing back and forth huge ranges only to be one tapped by a bush baby and forced to do it again really sucks. A big issue presents itself as the hacker issue. The Devs are dedicated to stamping these undesireables out but the time that takes varies which is understandable. I've been one tapped from a player who flew up from the ground like he just resurrected from the grave below and zoom right back again. Getting shot from 150m+ away with a pistol that has a 45m range cap is no fun either. The game is extremely challenging with just the various anomalies and hostiles that dot the regions keeping you constantly on a swivel. Many would cite that a PvE server option wouldn't be any fun and my only answer is just don't play on it then. I was honestly stoked to hear that game in spirit of Stalker would be released and i honestly tried giving this game a fair shake in spite of lot of bad reviews that were circulating.My hype soon after quickly drop down after encountering problems that i think many will have issues with... admittedly for those who visited Zone in the past, know that it is unforgivable place any Stalker explored BUT in this iteration Zone is brutal to no end and keeps punishing players at every corner possible... from blood hungry mutants, to enemy players (who will more than happily camp quest areas and grief living heck out of you) to heavily armed NPCs that have some unreal aiming that will hit you from long distances with such accuracy that even Vasily Zaitsev would be put to shame. To make things far worse is that while you are struggling to deal with these God tier snipers, enemy players will abuse this lull in your attention to put one in your back and enjoy possibly some good loot galore that you gone through lot of effort to haul to that point. Crafting system is really unintuitive as for a single piece of rifle you want to buy, you have to find some radiated moss or anomalous bits and pieces in order to get it... why would one seek trash for sake of obtaining firearms is beyond me. Finding artifacts seems very random and nothing you learned from Zone applies here, as they randomly appear and there is no devices that can help you locate them easier... anomalies are also at times hard to spot as majority of them melds into environment. One saving grace in this whole mess is that players get some supplies that you can't lose and weapons and armor stay locked, but anything else that you bring with you is bound to be lost if you are careless. Another major gripe i have with this game is that basic functions are locked behind "reputation system" that will not allow you to even redeem items from mail that game sends you by default or buy different weapons because you lack same reputation.Global chat is lacking moderation and is also full of N word bombs and some edgelords that do it due to lack of ramifications involved in the process. Psy emissions and blowout last too long and dynamic of game is slowed down.General verdict of this game is: Even though it is F2P, don't bother playing it if you have issues with poor dev/player communication, lack of moderation, quest areas ganking justified, NPC aimbots and plethora of other issues. You should play this game ONLY if you wish to punish yourself constantly and train your nerves.

I'm extremely conflicted on this game, and even though I've played 120 hours at the time of the review, I feel like I was always addicted to the promise of the game and very rarely the game itself. The structure of the game has all the right components to bring the MMO FPS to life in a real way. It's in many ways what Tarkov claimed it would be but never was, and much the same it takes a lot of the themes of simulating the daily life of a Stalker just trying to make a living that a lot of Stalker fans crave. However it's the little things that add up over time that have very little to do with the format itself that start to take it's toll. That's why it's difficult to review this game, but I'll try my best to describe what ultimately adds up to why I've stopped playing this game.The most obvious problem is something that, like most F2P games, only becomes more obvious as you play for longer. This game has a Korean style enhancement system for armor and weapons. Granted this system is unobtrusive right now as it's fairly easy to get your equipment to the current +5 maximum, and in that sense it seems unobtrusive and people largely don't think about it, but the Russian server has a much higher maximum enhancement for gear, and with that comes an RNG KMMO style luck grind for higher enhancement gear. The system in it's current state now is simply like the frog in the boiling pot, where they slowly increase the F2P heat until you don't even realize you're in boiling water. I've seen this too many times and I don't want to be here when the water starts to boil. This is also the case for artifacts to a certain extent but I think you get the idea already. This leads into another point: weapon balance and power. The primary goal of the game is to obtain higher tiers of gear. Enhancement will in the future become the primary gatekeeper for gear, but for now it's simply getting to the highest "tree" of gear. Even then it becomes very apparent how critical this can be in deciding the outcome of a firefight. The current standout weapon is the VSS Vintorez, which is just about what everyone in the current endgame is either trying to farm and is currently using the VAL waiting to turn it into the VSS, or already has the VSS. The VSS is functionally an assault rifle but with a 1.5x headshot multiplier. Functionally it melts people at all ranges faster than anything else. Gear being such an important component of PVP is just not a good system in my opinion, but that brings us to our next point.Hostile player encounters aren't always strict 1v1 in the sense that you both know you're there and you're waiting to make your move, so in that sense having the strongest gear doesn't always guarantee victory. Much of the game is getting the drop on the other person, and sometimes that system flourishes well. I would say one of the if not the best areas for that is an area called the dump. This area is primarily comprised of stalkers and bandits in equal measure. Every blip that indicates a person is near could just as easily be a friend or a foe. It's a careful ballet of completing objectives, scoping out the area and being on guard. There are safe exits for both factions and dangerous exits that're faster for reaching your base. I would say the dump really emphasizes the game at it's strongest points and when I truly felt like the games strengths truly shined.Unfortunately that brief glimmer ends very quickly, and you're once again consigned to mostly safe herbivore environments where only griefers who have no real reason to be there will kill you rarely, and you're largely clearing boring POI's with bad AI, running around anomaly clusters, scanning the ground with metal detectors, the truest essence of the "kill boar camp" style of automatically generated questing. Still, with that said, it's a necessary component of the game that, with the right amount of enemy stalker tension, can still make the experience of farming enjoyable, but that subtle mixture between making it too boring or too frustrating rarely meets in the middle to make it a well designed experience (like I said, basically only the dump). Other areas tend to not capture that appeal because they're simply designed different, or designed poorly. Once you get far enough into the game you join a subfaction which will pit you against people who might have formerly been your allies. This system however is horrifically implemented because the herbivore areas that otherwise were mindless farming instead become a system of exit camping and prairie dogging out of underground zones. Picture yourself farming up a bunch of stuff and some guy pops out of a level changer to kill you and runs back to his base underground to auction your stuff, but it happens just rarely enough that you don't really want to scout EVERY single time you get a blip that someone is nearby. Regardless of how bad this sounds to you, understand that it's simply objectively worse than two sides converging on opposite ends of the map. Level changers should NOT be a large component of the fight. The next part is the northern section of the map, where both subfactions must exit through the same level changers to enter and leave. Again, this creates the same problem where people can simply prairie dog through the exits, either deliberately or accidentally because opposition factions enter and leave through the same area. This is simply put, a bad system. where hours a farming can be undone by a person simply apparating in front of you at the wrong time. For a game that already had the system handled so perfectly it's bizarre and unnerving that the endgame undoes it so badly. The developers just slap an ungodly amount of vortex anomalies everywhere all over the entire map. Once you're used to them they rarely kill you, and when you're careful and cautious you can easily avoid them, but what they do successfully is just annoy you constantly. They slow you down when you have to literally run kilometers from place to place constantly, they trap you in place when you're busy with something else like trying to kite a mutant or run from another person, and above all else they seem to misunderstand what anomalies are supposed to accomplish. Anomaly fields where you carefully navigate the area to collect artifacts is a system that made sense and worked. They deformed the environment and created an interesting puzzle for the player to navigate. Those still exist in Stalcraft, but that's primarily the bulk of how they should be used. Anomalies should not be literally everywhere. The only thing adding tons of vortex anomalies everywhere accomplishes is making you constantly, at all times when running, throw bolts in front of you or simply slow down and bleed for one second when you get caught in them, or get unlikely and get attacked by a massive aggro radius boar and get ping ponged back into the vortex until you die. I would go on but I'm certain the archaic character limit has already been reached, so I'll end with this. The game has promise, but it's built upon the seed of a predatory F2P model that will bloom into a monster that's already present on the RU server, and the design decisions over time have become too burdensome for me to bear.

IE Wonderful concept, poor execution. (No like really, REALLY poor execution) They are abundant in places that would otherwise be amazing to have pvp fights in. The blackhole literally turns invisible for about a second and it WILL kill you. Certain times of day make them near impossible to see but for a split second, with or without NVGs. This causes everyone to travel along the outer edges and along trial-by-error paths throughout most maps and totally ruins the whole exploration aspect because everywhere you go is littered with these stupid death traps that kill the whole atmospheric vibe this game pulls off so damn well.- (TO ME THIS IS THE MOST EGREGIOUS OF THEM ALL) Gotta walk everywhere (I'm aware of the kind of game this is, but with the latter two issues, having to repeat a long-winded journey to do something as simple as switching your spawn location because a trap you didn't see or a pack of dogs you got too close to is irritating beyond measure; now imagine PVP campers like me on top of that, just waiting to pick you off just for some semblance of fun. Make it so we have to pay to reset our spawn location and only at places we've already visited. Give us an escort mission that allows players to queue up and ride passenger in an exposed vehicle going from one base to another. I don't really care what it is... but give us SOMETHING other than Shift + W.-Despite having "Craft" in it's name, you don't craft anything. At most, you trade materials you don't want for items you do. Would be so cool to offset these often fruitless back and forth trips and constant deaths with CRAFTABLE crates (I know limited time purchaseable crates exist) or even cute little customizable/upgradeable campsites that let you rest up and stow your crap in a midway point. Raidable and destructable ofc.-AI Aiming is unreasonably accurate at long distances and they can spot you through vegetation even though you can't see them at all. The Tab targeting thing somewhat offsets this but it's also a cheap way to find enemy players. All this makes stealth a relatively useless tactic in this game that tries heavily to focus on stealth (Having all suppressors hard locked behind hours of progress) because all a player has to do is mash the tab key in the direction they got shot from to almost instantly locate you.-There is a public ban list for what I assume is cheaters, meaning cheaters must exist within the game, so I guess at least you can blame your very very many deaths on what are essentially invisible traps, mini raid bosses, aimbots, and chernobyl squaters (get it? like Tarkov Shufflers).-Groups of Zombies sounds sooooooo cool. Until you finally get to see one.-Mob spawns/Anomaly Spawns/Dig Spots all spawn in the same general locations, making every aspect of this game grindy, farmy and robotic.The most fun I have is when I'm camping in the Cordon picking off enemy players from the bushes or when I'm out in a new area discovering little camps and shelters full of mostly junk loot; neither of which do I load up on consumables and ammo for because I'm already expecting to die. This causes me to farm just outside of bases and shelters and make many trips back and forth, because I know going out further or staying out longer puts me at risk of one of these really annoying deaths that not only throw me all the way back at the spawn base but also cause me to most likely lose any loot (progress) I just made for any quest or upgrade. Of course this is a survival game, restocking is fairly cheap and this is how you're supposed to play the game but is it enjoyable? NOT REALLY GUYS, not unless you manage to get a team of players who know what they're doing together and all play for hours to get ya'lls random assortment of quests done.Separately; They offer premium, which in short is just a P2W feature that consumers have convinced themselves isn't. The aesthetic bonuses you get from it (which is usually the only feature you can add that isn't P2W for a lot of games) are minimal as are aesthetics for the game as a whole. The weapon skins suck, there's only a few options to pick from, really it's just for the trade coins which can be used to skip gathering loot to trade for better gear (ie P2W). So if that's you're thing, they got something for you.I don't recommend this game because I don't get enjoyment out of it. I get far more frustrations than I do any enjoyment and the grind/travel/mobs/loot just ain't worth it anyway to keep trying to find some enjoyment. I just got my ghillie suit and the game already feels overplayed and repetitive, and like I'm just gonna have to go through endless frustrations for minimal rewards. Lots of squandered potential here. Also, the tutorial completely lies to you, giving you this sense that you'll be picking up the weapons of fallen enemies. Not at all. I think that's a completely abhorrent dev decision considering the tutorial is a required part of gameplay no matter which faction you choose or which playthrough you're on. Ixnay on the tutorial or change some gameplay features so we can pickup guns. That'll force ya'll to lower the quality of weapons enemies use and give players a fighting chance when it comes to progressing throughout most of the core game.I'm not sure why some players are convinced survival games need to require this endurement of losing your loot and endless back and forth travelling to be good or challenging; or for the player to be good at it, but it's a really toxic mindset to have for an otherwise very fun genre with loads of potential as most games that give players some sort of health bar could technically be categorized as survival games. But this game often requires a player whether they're solo or not to kill entire camps of these AI aimbots who will pick you off from afar even if they shouldn't be able to see you and will relentless track and charge your location if you decide to get close enough to pull off a full on assault. It's already challenging enough without the annoying nuances they're trolling you with like anomalies. Admittedly vice versa when the AI can't see you, they'll just stand in that same spot getting shot to death. It completely ruins the immersion of all the great voice acting occurring in the background.Also a Quest Reward Mosin Nagant+4 takes 2+ headshots on NATO soldiers and players. Come on man, that's just stupid.Remember kids, if you aren't holding Shift+W, you probably aren't playing.I told myself get to the Bar, get the next Scientist outfit, fully deck out your MP5 and your AKM, stack up some Bar reputation, check out this PVP deathmatch type event, and then you can be done! I highly doubt I have the mental fortitude to put myself through the torture of going any further than that despite how intriguing it all seems. But alas, redemption is always achievable in the second half; there may be one final revision to this review if I can hold out. Wish us luck!Other than ALL that..... TL:DR :Lots of Grind, Meta Guns make a whole two weapon categories irrelevant, Clientside Advantage means PvP feels like you barely saw someone but they managed to HS you 6 times. etc.The game has a good chunk of content in it to do, the mainline story quests are pretty decent, there's a good bit of equipment to work towards unlocking, there's enough to satisfy people who simply need a reason to work towards a goal, though, in my opinion it is not satisfying/gratifying in the least, it is simply  Stringing you along for a long period of time to unlock anything mid-late game is the bread and butter of this.The real problem comes when you realize that ever since a major gun/damage re-balance from many months prior there are almost no ACTUAL variety for weapon choice. The current meta equipment is so severely good that it is insane to use anything else. Nearly the entire tree of Submachine Guns and Sniper Rifles(Bolt Actions) are pointless to use both in PvP and PvE, because there are two Assault Rifles that not only have better damage, recoil just as low, rate of fires just as fast, and way more range (damage drop-off).There are even weapons that you cannot unlock except through Seasonal Event crates that rival those or are better.If you want to visit the Atmospheric world of S.T.A.L.K.E.R. but in a voxel-based Minecraft style, then sure give this a try. Maybe even stay on until you reach the Mid-Game, but beyond that I can guarantee the markers where you feel accomplishment for having gotten something get so far out in the distance you'll cross them as a dusty skeleton with no satisfaction.

I left a review after playing for 10 hours. I have played 50 hours now and think I'd be best to change my review.Stalcraft is a game that brings the Stalker series to the next generation. Here are some pros:1. The gunplay is solid. I enjoyed using the guns. Many felt different, and there aren't too many different ammos as to bug things down. Using improved ammo can really feel impact when used in the correct times.2.The amount of weapons is pretty nice, a good verity without being overwhelming.3.It works! Most people who say to play the older Stalker games seem to forget how buggy and badly optimized they are, Even with the player made patches, the don't always work smoothly.4. The setting is still pretty faithful to the original while including new elements.Here are the cons:1. Quest design! Some of these quests are so badly designed you will likely need a walkthrough. And that's if you don't get one of the many bugs that gives you wrong information or refuses to allow to to complete the quest. The rewards for these quests are improved weapons or armor, some of which can be useful, but most of the time takes more effort than it's worth. Some quests give you instanced areas that if you die in them, you'll respawn in the instanced area with enemies respawned. Other times, you respawn at base and can never recovered dropped items. They may also teleport you into an enemy area. There is even at least one mission that requires you to jump through an anomaly that normally kills you to continue the mission. The reward for this mission is a weapon you can get for less effort by playing normally.2. PC/NPC health. Players have so little health in comparison to NPCs. You'll find that a few headshots, as in maybe 3, on an unarmored player will kill them with an assault rifle. A sniper rifle will likely kill in one headshot or 2 body shots. This is pretty much in line with the single player game. NPC's on the other hand can take 10-20 headshots from a rifle or 5 sniper headshots to kill. It can get out of hand with the NPC's with Exoskeletons, and the become common pretty quickly.3. PVP in everything but safe areas. While this isn't the worst idea, in practice it encourages people to be toxic. After leaving the starting swamp, the toxic behavior increases the more you go north. Thankfully, toxic players aren't the majority outside of the furthest north areas.4. Bad explanations. There are a lot of systems in this game, things like artifact freshness and closing portals are things you'll have to look up. If you don't know why you stopped gaining reputation at a base even if you aren't at max level? Better look it up yourself. This is something that isn't the end of the world, but would make the game much easier to get into and maintain playerbase.5. Monetization. It's a free game, so the need to make money somehow. They sell a premium that makes progression a little easier and now have a battlepass. The battlepass introduces new high tier items to people willing to pay massive amounts of money. They also have lootboxes that have more endgame items, like one of the best armors and great guns. If you have a lot of money, you can have them now. If not, it will take months to catch up. I don't mind premium, it just negates some grind. The battle pass encourages massive money expenditures, and that's never good.TLDR: It's a fine game to kill days of your life, but you may hit a wall and never want to play it again. I'd give it a neutral score if that was an option, but since I can't I'd lean toward not recommending if you don't have friends to play with and a lot of free time.

This review will be coming from a Veteran Stalker played who has played every offical stalker game and several of their mods and fan made ones such as Anomaly. This game is not Stalker. It's a MMO Shooter with "Hardcore" mechanics such as loss of loot on the player upon death, and very questionable design choices that has a theme similar to Stalker.A lot of other Stalker "Veterans" say Stalker is a hardcore game. It is in no way a hardcore game. The only case that can truly be made is for Shadow of Chernobyl when you decide to keep progressing with the story after disabling the brain scorcher and not restocking. (The game does give the player the feeling to keep going instead of restocking to be fair). The Stalker games are honestly quite easy with it's grind that's only money and maybe flashdrives for upgrades, its saves, its many indicators for anomalies and emissions and npcs, and the npc behaviors themselves (They don't just swarm you). Here a several things the game does different, for better or worse.-Story: It is interesting and pretty good from what I've seen but there are very glaring issues such as parkour missions. The parkour missions have 0 warning, are frustrating, and cause people to loose loot permanently. These missions could be less frustrating if the loss of loot is reversed for these missions.-Maps: Obviously alot has changed for it to be an MMO. Some of the designs are true to the game and others are not. Bases for factions have also changed. Although some maps such as Rostok Factory is horrendous for combining pvp and pve.-Grind: It is ok, not perfect. Long grinds that can be made longer through pvp. With poor placements and maps such as Rostok Factory, it's frustrating. It's why Pickles make people quit the game.-Upgrading armor and weapons: Reduced from the systems of Clearsky and Call of Pripyat to just a tool to upgrade preset stats. Worse variety in my opinion.-Attachments: A lot more customization. Very good.-Backpacks and containers: This idea is honestly better than having all 5 slots always open or limited to type of armor. Gives incentive to what the player wants.-Enemies: Stalcraft was made from Minecraft orginally so it does have limitations but enemies can be down right horrendous. Dogs, Pseudodogs, and Boars dont have their original AI and attacks so they just swarm like baby zombies from Minecraft. Snorks just leap with 0 downtime and dont fumble if they miss their leap like the Stalker games. Chimeras are just death if you dont get them stuck since theyre just beefier Snorks. Pseudogiants are just bulletsponges. Bloodsuckers are fine. All the enemies will basically chase you across the map though which is very annoying. Humans are just like skeletons from Minecraft honestly.-PVP: It's alright but the Minecraft base mechanics hold it back. The time to kill is also insanely quick. Like .3 seconds quick. -Atmosphere: This is awesome, very close to Stalker games.-Emissions: All of a sudden, people don't broadcast when emissions will happen like in Clearsky and Call of Pripyat. They occur any time from 2-4 hours after the last one. Also the shaking, the emission is a release of energy with a huge shockwave, not a earthquake. Devs seem to have forgot this. -Artifacts: Artifact detectors don't exist anymore since it uses Shadow Of Chernobyls dumb artifact system. Now it's just like a glowing star you sometimes see randomly instead of being an adventure into an anomaly.-Anomalies: Similar to original but feels at times they're only there to ♥♥♥♥ people over instead of being an obstacle like the original.I'll add more to this list when I think of it.

My rating: 4/10* Despite being in development since 2015, this game has only ever reached a peak player base of 9,088, and its core issues overshadow what could have been a standout title within the gaming community. The game suffers from design choices that limit its appeal and prevent it from gaining significant traction.Map Design and GameplayThe map design borrows heavily from titles like S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Anomaly, with few original changes beyond a Minecraft-esque aesthetic and some repositioned locations. The starting area in the swamp to the southwest is well-balanced for PvP, with the factions (Freedom STALKER & Bandit) having a balanced distribution of quests. However, Bandits benefit from a shorter and easier route to the central map area, The Cordon, which is a recurring issue in the gameplay loop.The Cordon emphasizes choke points contested by each faction, which must be crossed during certain quests to progress. North of the Bandit Safezone is the Dump area, featuring a shared Safezone and intense PvP. This area is flanked by faction-specific zones, Agroprom (Bandits) and Dark Valley (Freedom STALKERS), each requiring unique resources (copper and aluminum cable) essential for progression. This setup significantly slows down quest and equipment progression, with factions guarding their resources fiercely and selling them at a markup at an auction house.Progressing through the Dump leads to Rostok, another shared safe zone where resources can only be obtained by defeating opposing faction's AI. This area is plagued by safe zone camping and constant PvP, which frustrates many players. The northern areas require special items for access and entail over 500+ hours of grinding to obtain end-game armor and weapons.Story and DialogueThe game's tutorial is well-written and narrated in English, setting up what seems like a promising story-driven experience. However, this potential is not realized beyond the tutorial, as with all STALKER titles, it mostly involves reading (or skipping) dialogue that lacks consequential choices, coupled with random Russian dialogue from agitated AI.Community and Server IssuesHaving been playable for over a year in Russia, many Russian players are already at the late-game stage, which, combined with limited server options, results in overcrowding on NA servers by Spanish and Russian-speaking players.Monetization and CheatingA Russia-exclusive "donation" shop allows for easier progression, embodying a mobile game-like "pay to grind less" design. This game also suffers from rampant cheating, including players modifying local unencrypted files to change player model colors for an unfair advantage in PvP.Minor IssuesMany key bindings, such as weapon inspection, are non-rebindable.There is no dedicated crouch button, typical for the STALKER series.Core functions are not explained in the tutorial, and there’s a lack of helpful YouTube content.Item management and achievement systems are poorly implemented, with some items decaying in inventory and some achievements failing to unlock.ConclusionIn its current state, I cannot recommend this game. However, with continued support and updates from the developers, there is hope that these issues may be addressed and the game could improve significantly over time.---{Graphics}---☐ Realistic☐ Beautiful☐ Good☐ Decent☐ Bad☑ Simple☐ Don't look too long at it---{Gameplay}---☐ Amazing☐ Good☑ Average☐ Below average☐ Bad☐ Read a book instead---{Audio}---☐ Amazing☐ Very good☑ Good☐ Below average☐ Bad☐ Buy earplugs---{Audience}---☐ Kids☑ Teens☑ Adults☐ Anyone---{PC Requirements}---☐ Check if you can run paint☑ Potato☐ Average☐ High☐ Nvidia tesla p40☐ Runs poorly on anything---{Difficulity}---☐ Could play with guitar hero controller☐ Easy☑ Average☐ Difficult☐ Cuphead and Dark Souls combined---{Grind}---☐ Nothing to grind☐ A little grind☑ Average grind☐ Too much grind---{Story}---☐ N/A☐ Bad☐ Below average☑ Average☐ Good☐ Amazing☐ It'll replace your life---{Game Time [Hours]}---☑ Depends on how much you like grinding☐ 1-3☐ 5-8☐ 9-12☐ 13-20☐ 21-50☐ 51-100☐ 100+---{Price}---☑ Only if you're absolutely bored☐ Worth the price☐ Only if on sale☐ Not recommended☐ You could just invest in VHS tapes---{Bugs}---☐ None☑ Minor bugs☐ Quite a bit☐ Fallout 76 on launch

this game is great! i really have enjoyed getting into it and its quickly eaten up my time as an easy way to brain off and progress, its a very bread-and-butter grindy mmo.but, there are some seriously massive blunders that the developers have made that completely crush the game for me to the point where me and some of my friends are very close to quitting the game over.one of the biggest blunders that is the most unfortunate part of this game is the weapon specialization feature later in the game, and the lack of a softening of grind if you wish to go for a second weapon. as you upgrade weapons in the game, you go from white, to green, to blue, to pink, to 2nd pink, to red. these paths are limited to a certain weapon, so one weapon upgrades into another and upgrades into another. normally, you have to have the previous weapon to upgrade into the next; however, at any point in the white-blue territory, you can do a buyout where you pay a solid premium of extra materials to be able to jump in and skip the previous weapons. this is a great feature for someone who isnt liking the playstyle of a particular weapon and wants to swap off into another path.however, once you enter the pink territory, you must specialize. once you go down a weapon route, you are locked into it, and cannot freely move between them between upgrades. this means that if you wish to get a different weapon, you have to go all the way back to the related blue, grind for that, and then grind the rest of that path. it puts an immense amount of stress to pick the right gun and feed into the meta for the player and, because the balancing in the game isnt the best, some weapons like the AMB-17 severely underperform compared to other weapons of similar rarity. imagine completing the immense hundreds-hour grind to get the AMB-17 only to find it is massively underperforming and specialized for dueling close quarters only, and now having no choice but to completely restart a huge chunk of the grind with no mercy.this leads me into my next gripe: if you at any point what a different weapon or wish to have a backup weapon, there is no softening of the grind and you must do the grind completely over again for that weapon even if its in an earlier tier. i believe there should be a system where once you achieve a weapon of a particular rarity, all other weapons in that rarity drop in price. that would mean getting another weapon like a shotgun AND a sniper rifle wouldnt double your grind and instead only increase it by a bit. the grind is fun and fine the first time; nobody wants to do it again and again just to try different weapons and strategies.i believe this game would greatly benefit from it moving away from the free-to-play model, or at the very least, moving away from the extreme unfairness towards the player in regards to the grind. it crushes the game and any freedom the player wants to have. i will not be recommending this game until something is addressed in relation to repetition of the already huge grind this game has. this is coming from a player that doesn't mind a long grind as the later parts in the game have, i just believe its unfair to have to restart it and go through so much of the game again just to have a different weapon of the same tier.that's my piece and main gripes. of course, i have more, notably the lack of solid balancing across the board but i won't speak on that to keep this as brief as i can. i really enjoy this game and its approach, and it crushes me to see what is in my opinion such fatal and obvious blunders in game development. i hope this post finds the developers well and they genuinely address this, i would love to see some kind of system like this implemented to reduce multiple repeats of grinding.(p.s. add transmog wtf every mmo in existence has it PLEASE)

writing this review at 80 hours. One character in each main faction. So to start of this review is negative, thats for the general populace, this isn't going to be hardly any fun for the typical gamer, or those uninitiated to the stalker franchise, because anomolies will make you uninstall.PROS:- incredibly addictive gameplay loop. The loop is perfect for a shooter MMO.- Stalker universe, although fan made.- extraction shooter elements in an open world game = awesome dopamine highs.- gun play, and modification is pretty good considering the studio's size.- progression is fairly well designed and balanced. in PVP enemies that should still be hanging around the early game zone aren't a challenge if you're used to that grittier PVP style of extraction shooters.(ammo types, grenades, healing methods, etc)CONS:- Enemy AI is the worst I've ever seen in my entire life. I made a game on the free steam maker app when I was 14 that had 10 fold better AI. They literally Just run at you and shoot, they do miss but not enough to make it noticeable. Mutant mobs are the same way, but melee makes it more manageable and you can kite the enemies.- extraction shooter type gameplay loop in an MMO. Yeah getting back to base with a brimming bag of goodies feels great but it doesn't happen nearly often enough to support or justify your time. I often spend HOURS farming matts maybe dying once or twice to something that's genuinely my error, then just having nato troops spawn on me or spot me and waste me across the map.(early-mid game issue) Progression is EXTREMELY SLOW because of this and it just makes you feel like the several hours you just invested got you absolutely nothing in game.- Devs don't give a ♥♥♥♥. Seriously they perma banned a known cheater/streamer then just let them make an ult and said "well they aren't cheating anymore" even though they were. Same applies to campers, they have 0 intentions of fixing this issue and would appearantly rather the game just die.- Devs also do very predatory monetary things cloaked in the "transparent purchase" ideology. Skins for guns/armor cost a few bucks a piece and can only be applied once to a gun, I've been told trading that gun or armor in for the next upgrade gives the paint back but haven't even bothered to test it.- Game is literally pay to win, a premium membership gives you more loot from any events that spawn in the world, and in a game that the entire progression system is based on crafting gear and buying consumables, well thats not hard to spot.- AI balance is also atrocious, I could forgive the damage numbers etc if the AI had, well AI, but considering they are literal aimbots its just not a fair practice.- map design also does not support this AI issue as you can't even hide in cover. what little cover exists the enemies will just run up on you not giving you time to even reload, let alone heal. Outside of that your only options for hard cover are trees typically which often aren't even big enough to cover you completely and arm shots from nato soldiers will lay you out even with appropriate armor types. so. yeah.- No sort of fast travel, would accept this if the game at least had respawn options, but it doesn't. you're forced to respawn in a fixed location(last visited safe zone, excluding a few certain quest locations) which are few and far between, IE no safe zone to respawn at in the dump so if youre a stalker that died 500 meters into the dump, prepare to run 1500 meters to get back and pray you don't get camped, sqaud pvp'd, or wasted by OP AI on the way back or you're doing it again. in a single player experience this would be fine, but its a freakin MMO. thats not acceptable IMO.- Finally, No way, absolutely no way to avoid PVP. It's always a possibility. There are a couple of zones where its unlikely, but Bandits or stalkers can still make their way to these zones, there are even quests that encourage it. This is just absolutely unacceptable. I love the PVP loop of games like this but again, ITS AN MMO. its not tarkov, its not staliker, its not the cycle. It's an MMO. Players have posed many viable and several awesome ideas to curb this issue such as dedicated PVP only zones, with a toggle in the other zones, temporary cease fires that can be voted on that would toggle off PVP, more instances to drastically reduce the chances of enemies running into eachother etc. devs don't care. I can respect they are making the game they want to make, but imo its stupid to take that philosophy into an MMO. Thats a game that lives or dies by its community, not the devs whims, they should have made a pvp exclusive or single player experience if thats what they wanted to do. again they just honestly do not give a ♥♥♥♥ about the community. - almost forgot, but the servers suck ass. On NA I tend to play with more South Americans than anything else, outside of latency being a problem, again, mmo. This creates a huge language barrier that makes trying to team up and play as part of a community much more difficult.TL;DR for a free to play game its fun as hell, but after awhile the massive list of cons vs pros just really bogs the game down. The devs don't care about the community much and don't care about cheaters or campers in the sleightest. You'll have more play sessions that end up being a waste of several hours than fun productive play sessions. Personally Im only giving this game another month or so and if the devs don't fix the blatant issues, this game will get trashcanned.

As soon as anomalies or enemy AI is changed this review becomes immediately positiveGame is good has solid progression and actually gets some solid variety by the end of the game. This is all ruined by anomalies like vortexes and blackholes and infinite ammo npcs sniping you. The game does not punish you hard resource wise since you can normally buy your bag back from the auction or grab your stuff after the fact. But this is a huge time sink and vortexes/blackholes can be incredibly obvious or totally invisible depending on time of day or night-vision. I appreciate the developers very obvious love of STALKER however spamming random semi invisible traps which kill you instantly often stacked side by side in later areas is not fun. This is always the straw that breaks the camels back for introducing new players or keeping people who have played playing a while meaning it drives away veterans and new players. The conflict comes in where the devs eventually either have to make dying less punishing to compensate for how much running there is in the game by design or redo much of the systems in place to create less running or drive away the people they need to make their game successful. All of these alternatives suck and all to keep random deaths around that really arent fair no matter how much you cope.Solutions-Use insta death anomalies only in incredibly small tight areas and make them more pronounced-Make blackholes larger and more pronounced but also make them a gameplay element where you can hover bullets/grenades around them to ricochet to other players/npcs. Make vortexes do 40-60% of HP and hold the player in place for 2.5 seconds since having no mobility and half your health gone is already punishing enough in most situations.NPCs with annoying AI and infinite ammo I imagine will be fixed with future updates it just sucks in early areas like the swamp where you have negative cover and are normally outgunned.Please fix these so I dont have to abandon this game as soon as another battle royal style MMO-Lite gets introduced.

At 40 hours into the game, I must admit I am impressed. I have played plenty of MMOs, MMO shooters, and MMO RPGs - this one is definitely among my favorite. This is why:I'm a STALKER fan first and foremost. Played all 3 games, numerous mods, identify as Clear Sky. This, while not one for one, is faithfully inspired by the series in ways fans will recognize right away. There is, however, enough new and different content to make veterans curious.The writing is surprisingly clever, funny at times, and leaves you to fill in some blanks. Not all quests are kill and fetch quests - some involve murder mysteries, prophetic dreams, selling snake oil, and riding the line between order and chaos. The gunplay is good. Hits register like they should, kills feel satisfying, and reloads (typically) are well animated. Item variety is diverse, and there are many mechanics at play, introduced bit by bit to not overwhelm. Combat is frequent and the presence of PvP gives you a feeling of anxiety like in DayZ or Tarkov. You treasure what you loot because you can lose it, and feel satisfied when you return to base with it. I like it! The difficulty does appear to jump dramatically as you get to new zones, but armor progression makes this curve smoother. Just remember this IS an MMO: progress will be much slower by default.80 hour edit: Lots of running. Atmosphere remains tense. Lots of PvP encounters, you learn safeish routes with time. Lots of content from the russian servers haven't been brought over yet. Game handles well, even on older hardware, occasional crashes though. Main story quest rewards are unusually generous. Still feels good.110 Hours: Beat the main storyline. Some of the boss fights were not well thought out. The pacing on the missions, basically puzzle after puzzle, is exhausting. The reward is an endgame armor though, so you get to wear the achievement. Definitely not a game for everyone, but if you love Stalker, and don't mind PVP involved in it, you'll do fine here.

This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. Stalcraft is a game that combines the best of two worlds: the post-apocalyptic setting of S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and the sandbox gameplay of Minecraft. The game is a free-to-play MMOFPS with survival horror elements, set in the open world of the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone. The game offers a variety of activities and modes, such as exploring, hunting, looting, crafting, questing, and fighting against other players and mutants.The game’s graphics are surprisingly good, considering that it started as a Minecraft mod. The game has its own engine, which allows for realistic lighting, shadows, and weather effects. The game’s environments are rich and diverse, with many locations to discover and secrets to uncover. The game’s sound design is also immersive, with ambient noises, radio chatter, and gunshots creating a tense atmosphere.The game’s combat system is fast and fluid, with a wide range of weapons and gadgets to choose from. The game’s signature feature is the blade mode, which lets you cut through anything with your knife, similar to Metal Gear Rising. The game’s difficulty is challenging, but fair, rewarding skill and strategy. The game also has a progression system, where you can upgrade your weapons, skills, and equipment with the currency and materials you earn in the game.The game’s story is intriguing and well-written, with a main storyline that introduces you to the Zone and its mysteries, and many side quests that flesh out the world and its characters. The game’s voice acting and cutscenes are high-quality, and the game’s soundtrack is fitting, featuring a mix of rock, metal, and electronic music that matches the game’s mood and action.Stalcraft is a game that deserves more attention and praise than it gets. It is a game that delivers on its promise of being a fun and exhilarating MMOFPS that lets you explore and survive in the Zone. It is a game that respects its source material, but also creates its own identity and personality. It is a game that is worth playing for any fan of FPS, survival, or sandbox games, or just good games in general.

Please keep in mind I haven't played this in about a year and a half. I have no idea if they've changed it for the better or worse lately.This being said, while I was incredibly skeptical of the game at first, after I researched it a bit, I decided to give it a fair shake. I don't regret it. I played a bandit along with some friends, and managed to complete what story content there was, and then some, nearly getting to the point where I was going to have to choose a sub-faction to progress any further.Firstly, the elephant in the room:There is PVP in the game, obviously, but if you're risk-averse like I am, you can mostly avoid that until you're almost finished with the story. It's not until the pickle grind at Factory where you're truly forced into conflict with the rival faction. Take this with an especially large grain of salt, however, as if you're patient, careful, and lucky, you can still get the trading materials you need (the aforementioned pickles) to upgrade your gear simply by sneaking around in enemy territory. In all honesty I got more of a thrill from doing that than any amount of monotonous blasting done at the usual territory intersection points. I'd generally fly by the seat of my pants with my ill-gotten gains all the way back through 2 enemy regions just to loop back to friendly areas, and barely make it back to Factory before the next blowout. And that was fun for me.Edit: The pickle grind has been rendered pretty stress-free. Previously, zombies dropped anomalous coal that you had to grind in addition to pickles. Now they just drop pickles, which makes hoping and praying you don't die in factory absolutely moot.If it doesn't appeal to you, though, rest assured that even up that point there's plenty to do in other areas. If you don't care about getting past Factory, there's quite a bit to explore, and even more if you want to roll another character for the rival faction. For a STALKER game, the team has put quite a lot of love into the activity of anomaly diving. The anomaly fields present in the game are diverse, interesting, and even more deadly in some cases than the OG stalker games. They truly evoke the wonder of treasure hunting in an alien environment well, something that is another staple of the original games. While you might not get "good" artifacts in every dive, you can at the very least usually get something worth selling, and the satisfaction of navigating a clever little maze.All in all, despite the unusual presentation of a STALKER game with minecraft-clone graphics, this is a game that at least follows suit decently with the spirit of the originals.

I played this for nearly 3 hours (as you can see by the 2.7 hours on record)I really like the games idea, i always wanted to play S.T.A.L.K.E.R Co-op-esque game, this was the thing that got close to it. However, within my only 3 hours of playing, i already realized that perhaps the game is not exactly for me.Sure its not for me, why it cant be for others? I will simply put it as: PVP Aspect of the game.I really wish Steam added a neutral review option (Like many others want) because this would be the only situation where i would put it as that. I recommend but also not recommend for reasons.A pretty misleading thing in the description of the game is... Well, the game being PVP focused. The thing is, it really isnt? There are way more PVE related stuff rather than PVP. This aint Rust, ARK: Survival Evolved, etc. Hell, you realize this within like, an hour or two of playing this game. Sure, i only have 3 hours on this game, but i have another friend that plays this more than me, and agrees with me, this game has more PVE than PVP.Speaking of PVP, do not even try to complain about it, specially on the Steam forums. Because theres... About 90% chance you will get a response of "git gud" or "Skill issue", while yes, if you get killed in a 1v1 situation where both of you were aware of each other, yes thats fair. Whats not fair is getting sniped, camped or even when you get unlucky just because you get absolutely sprayed by a person that you didnt see in a place you just looked at. I experienced the 3rd one, but even simply looking at reviews shows you that many people complain being griefed/camped (Specially at choke points and such). This shows that the PVP aspect of the game affects the community, specially the ones that are louder.You may be wondering: "If its PVP focused, you must get a big payday of it right?" Well... Wrong. Most of the time, you get nothing. Sure you can get sometimes an artifact IF YOU ARE LUCKY, or get the more grindier items like Swamp Rocks (Even though those are easy to get lol), but thats the end of it. You dont get their weapons, their armor, nada, hell there are stuff that are even bound-locked, which decreases of getting items possibility, which dont get me wrong is a good system, it just further more stomps the idea of it being PVP focused.Its funny, because you are better off leaving players alone. Why? They get loot, you get loot, you dont spend bullets or even medicals, its a win-win.If you kill, you are losing bullets (That you may not get back unless you pay or have a bag of ammo), you can lose medicals, or even get it backfired and you get killed, but if you dont, what do you get from them? Oh look, items that would be worth around 25 money, and its all loots from enemies that you can simply kill if you go around the place and find Dog packs and Fleshies nest...You see the issue?Not to mention, theres a faction split down the road in the story, and to my understanding, even if you are in the "Bandit" faction, and you take (For example) Covenant split faction, the Mercenaries, despite them being part of Bandits, can kill you all of sudden, just because split faction. Though this is only what i heard apparently this could be very false l o l.Another issue for me is Anomalies, but thats a different thing honestly, just so you know, they are pretty meh.Should you play the game? I will say this:If you want to play this for the PVP, go ahead, but unless you get lucky or you get around it, have fun getting killed by others and also most of the time getting little to not value back from killing players.If you want to play this for the PVE, dont even try. There were few times we got jumped by enemies that were semi-geared up, but only survived because my friend was prepared gear wise. Not to mention, theres little to not PVP protection. You get a 15 second protection when leaving a mission-related hideouts and stuff. You get PVP protection in the base, but that doesnt stop from people camping the main outposts or be nearby.Another thing i have to complain about is the fact that, in the tutorial it makes it look like you can get weapons easily. Why? You loot an enemies corpse and what do you find? A weapon. Thats like that for every (To my knowledge every) enemy in the tutorial. But then in the open world, you kill AI Enemy (Be it Bandit or Stalker) and they drop... Pretty much nothing. I think Stalcraft is basically the perfect game, but you'll either love it or hate it. It's an MMOFPS with dedicated servers and large instanced areas, but those areas are divided into channels, so you'll only have a handful of other players in your area at any time, keeping the world feeling lonely but not dead. It's actually quite polished and bug free despite looking like it might be jank at a glance. It does a great job at capturing the atmosphere and gameplay of Stalker. While it sometimes has the tension of a game like Escape from Tarkov, it's not as punishing, nor is the fear of death as constant - you eventually learn where you're safe and where to stay alert. Getting to that point will mean dying a lot, but dying is just an inconvenience rather than a major setback. The game has pretty cool story missions that have RPG-esque decision making, platforming puzzles (which are sometimes infuriating but feel great when you beat them), boss battles (which are also infuriating, but, in a good way, trust me), and other interesting twists.If you're intimidated by PvP, these are important things to note:1. You choose a faction (Stalkers or Bandits), and therefore about half the playerbase is friendly and cannot hurt you.2. The map is divided in a way where it's unlikely you run into hostile players most of the time. Sometimes you need to venture into enemy territory, but it's only sometimes.3. There are "bound items" you keep on death. This includes all weapons/armor as well as some consumables. "unbound" items drop in a bag. If you die, you can run back and get your bag. Other players can loot it, so sometimes you get your stuff back, sometimes not. You don't drop money if you die. There are safe zones where you can deposit between expeditions, so you only ever risk what you got on a current outing, plus some very cheap supplies.4. Completing events in the open world gives upgrade materials which are used for getting better weapons/armor. When you die, these upgrade materials get bundled into an item called a "lost bag", and only you can open that "lost bag". Other players can sell it back to you or discard it. This means everyone has to farm their own upgrade materials, and if someone kills you in PvP, they can basically put a price on the progression you made since you last deposited at a safe zone. Sometimes players will just send your back bag to you. This system basically means PvP is something players do for their own survival rather than as a means to progress, which keeps the amount of toxic murdering fairly low, and it means dying with some loot isn't always as painful.5. The time to kill is very low, and even players with bad weapons can headshot endgame players a couple times and kill them. Usually whoever gets the drop on another player will win in PvP. Go into Stalcraft knowing you'll get randomly destroyed sometimes.6. Allegedly there are hackers but the devs seem to care and take action about it. I haven't had a distinct experience where I felt like someone was definitely hacking in my first 150 or so hours.Some info on the PvE1. Group play is never required. Having a friend can be convenient but it's also more rewarding to complete events in the open world solo, so being a lone wolf isn't necessarily worse than grouping up.2. Currently there isn't anything resembling dungeons or raids, but I think they might be added sometime soon.3. There isn't a huge variety of enemies or game mechanics but the enemies that are there are interesting enough that I don't mind. In a lot of RPG-ish shooter games, the enemies feel like bullet sponges, but in this game they're relatively easy to kill but have a different mix of health pools, movement patterns, and lethality that mean you're best off using different weapons, evasive maneuvers, or use of cover when fighting any of them. Mutant dogs? They're faster than me, so a pistol works best since I can reload it quickly and scare off most of the pack by firing more often than with a rifle. Bloodsuckers? They're a bit slower and tankier, so kite them and use a shotgun. Enemy soldiers? They're too accurate to run up on, so long range assault rifle, get a kill and reload behind cover. Little rats that nibble at my ankles? Knife will do, no reason to make extra noise.4. The gameplay loop once the story has been completed is basically just completing open world events for upgrade materials, banking them, and upgrading your weapons and armor. Once you have all the best-in-slot weapons/armor you want, there isn't much else to do at the moment, but I anticipate this will change or at least take longer to do in the near future. It will take quite a long time just to do that. If you're not a grinder, you might find this boring/repetitive.Notes on monetization1. There's a premium subscription which gives around 15% more rewards from open world events. This is "pay to progress faster" rather than "pay to win" because you eventually will get the best gear and be at a level playing field with anyone else who got to that point. Despite that taking kind of a long time (maybe 150-200 hours of non-afk gameplay), it doesn't take so long that this feels necessary to get there, it would still be 130-175 hours or thereabouts. You also get some extra storage space, but the storage you're given as a free-to-play is so extremely generous that I haven't even remotely considered this to be any added value at all. The premium subscription also allows you to complete a few extra daily missions but this is a pretty minor increase to the rate at which you'll progress.2. You can buy these upgrade materials outright for a real-money currency, but the cost of them seems unjustifiable relative to just playing the game. You can also buy these materials using in-game money from other players but it's pretty expensive to do that too.3. Other than that, real-money can only be used for buying skins/weapon camos from loot boxes. You can buy the skins/camos opened from these loot crates from other players using in-game money.4. I don't feel the monetization is predatory or egregious - I kind of want to spend money on the game considering how much fun I've had, but because the skins/camos come from loot boxes, I don't feel inclined to gamble, and using money for upgrade materials just seems like I'd be cutting my normal gameplay shorter.Overall, the game is really well designed and I feel it's successful in being the kind of game it wants to be, a grindy, slightly tense, very atmospheric MMOFPS. I'm not a big fan of the minecraft art style but I've learned to look past it. My only complaint is the lack of aspirational content that would require the very best gear, but to my knowledge this is coming soon, and I'm not maxed out or anything, so, I'm not too worried about it.

Ultimately I can't recommend this one, by the time I finished the campaign and reached the real grind for materials to gear up I began feeling sour about the progression model, especially after the jank and BS contained in the campaign. The primary problem with this game has to be the sheer amount of time you have to spend running to get to a farming spot after you die. 10+ minutes just on autopilot following the same path you always did to get to Yanov, and and the end of it you get the privilege of grinding for hours to get arbitrary materials for your next gun. Even if I got all my resources back every time I died, it probably would have taken me 10 hours to get the Protecta, as a good 1 HR long run got me less than a tenth of what was needed, and that's not even a max tier weapon, it's just the ticket to play in Limansk to be able to kill the chimera you need to kill to get out.Unfortunately, something like half of resource runs are going to end with a death, where you loss all of the stuff you just grinded an  hour for, and if you're lucky you get to do a painful 10 minute corpse run to get your stuff back. Now that may not need to be a problem, but the vast majority of deaths feel like total BS:1. Accidentally running into a black hole. You just need to know the location of these guys because half of the time they are literally invisible. Meaning if you don't know there are blackholes in an area, there can be literally nothing to alert you to the danger.2. Dying to a jank spawn of animals. For some reason 2-3 nodes of mutants will occasionally all congregate together and decide to insta kill you, given that you only have so many shells in your shotgun, and you can't outrun the mutants, beyond a certain number attacking at once there's really nothing you can do to avoid death.3. Dying to NPCs, who can sometimes do nothing and sometimes kill you inside 2 seconds even with an armour plate (and god help you if your plate breaks)Even though I had exhilarating moments of just barely making it out alive, or fighting 4 players and winning, it ultimately was not worth the frustration of the grind, especially when this most fun part of the game rewards you with basically nothing except a few bullets and a bag of their resources to throw away (as most players seemed to do) or mail back to the player if you're nice.

"Stalcraft" is an exceptional game that seamlessly blends the sandbox creativity of Minecraft with the intense survival elements of the Stalker series, creating a unique and thrilling FPS experience. From the moment you step into its immersive world, you're greeted with a vast, procedurally generated landscape filled with mysteries to uncover and challenges to overcome.One of the standout features of Stalcraft is its dynamic day-night cycle, which not only adds to the realism but also significantly impacts gameplay. During the day, players can focus on gathering resources, constructing bases, and exploring the environment. However, as night falls, the game transforms into a tense survival experience reminiscent of Stalker, with dangerous creatures prowling in the darkness, forcing players to rely on their wits and strategic planning to survive.The crafting system in Stalcraft is robust and intuitive, allowing players to trade artifacts obtained from nature with NPCs to obtain a wide range of weapons, tools, and structures. Whether you're building a fortified outpost to defend against hostile creatures or crafting powerful weapons to take on challenging enemies, the game gives you the freedom to play according to your preferred style.Combat in Stalcraft is fast-paced and satisfying, with a variety of weapons at your disposal, obtained through trading rather than traditional crafting. From makeshift firearms to high-tech gadgets salvaged from abandoned facilities, each weapon has its unique characteristics, adding depth to the gameplay experience.The AI of both enemies and allies is well-designed, providing a challenging but fair experience that keeps you on your toes without feeling overwhelming.In addition to its engaging gameplay mechanics, Stalcraft boasts stunning visuals that bring its post-apocalyptic world to life. Wasn't expecting to like this as much as I did. Ignore the craft part of the title, it's every bit a Stalker game as the Stalker games themselves, just in a blockier form. If you played and loved those games, you'll feel right at home here.--60+ hour edit: So I've got more time into the game now, and the cracks have really shown themselves. There's an unfortunately thin line between this game just being frustrating to play and it actually not being fun anymore. Main story quests that feature awful parkour sections with little to no checkpoints and awful controls that were clearly not meant for that kind of movement, near-unwinnable boss fights that almost require you to break the AI's pathing (Minstrel was honestly the breaking point for me), normal enemies that can spot you and melt you with pinpoint accuracy through trees, convoluted fetch quests that just feel like busy work deliberately made to send you over and over again into enemy territory for one thing just to run back.The PVP-- is a mixed bag at times. Sometimes fights actually do feel pretty fair and when they do, it's genuinely fun running out just to look for a fight, especially around the bar. However, 80% of enemy player encounters throughout the rest of the game are made up of campers sitting around at the entrances/exits to specific areas looking for easy kills. It doesn't matter whether you're bandit or stalker, both sides are going to have players looking to grief and because of the way instances are handled where you can't swap between them manually, you might be forced to just log out and come back outside of peak hours to lower your chance of running into a rat.I still feel that the game is very much a Stalker experience. They've nailed the atmosphere that we've have come to expect from the genre, but I can't recommend this game outside of that bubble anymore because it's gotten to the point where the frustration outweighs the fun. Maybe one day I'll come back to it and give it another go and see how I feel, but there are other games that I could be spending time with that won't be spent not having fun.
