This game captures the feeling of the Stalker series perfectly. the Atmosphere, the genuine feeling of unease that your in this Radioactive and Paranormal alternate universe where thinking tactically and intelligently is the smarter of the virtues. A game where recklessness and poor planning will see your character torn to shreds in anomalies, Killed by the other faction, or dying to the Emission storm, or Dying to the mutated Fauna or other hazards in this world.Like Escape from Tarkov this game has a Soft death punishment aspect to it. where you loose your loot and equipment but keep the core essentials, (guns armour, Ammo pouches, backpacks and other bound/quest items) So planning weapon and resource usage is important otherwise you will give a bandit/stalker a fat payday when you die.The multiplayer experience is almost top notch. A game of stealth and wits as you take risks and live dangerously. where good gun-play and smart positioning can win you fights or see you sent back to your spawn base after losing everything that isn't bound to you.A few points of Critique for the Devs, Since I have played the Russian version.-Keep it fair and balanced: the international community will not tolerate favouritism between factions. Equal opportunities between factions. Always.-No Pay to Win mechanics: The international Community frowns Heavily on this and this is a fast track to killing your game community fast. Real fast. Monetisation should always revolve around perhaps giving player boosts or Cosmetics but not to the point where it gives them a unfair advantage in PVP. So no superior armours (like the red armoured people had in the Russian version.)-Lose the loot boxes: Loot boxes are very dangerous and flimsy territory that in the end may hurt your monetisation model. They are seen as glorified gambling and many people in your community will avoid them (especially at the expensive level they are at now, for a single cosmetic feature 5$ USD for a single skin or charm is perhaps a little much) That being said perhaps offer loot boxes for early release but a month later release the content to a store that you can outright purchase the cosmetic feature. Or scrap the feature and just have a cosmetic store. -The premium subscription already shows tremendous potential, bonus loot and bonus to merchants is a nice boon to have And it does not change the dynamic much when it comes to the PVP aspects so its already in favourable territory. Perhaps sweeten the deal by letting the premiums gain access to new gear or features one to four weeks early if you really want to fatten the allure of the premium support model. But remember, Keep it fair, Preems should not have a unfair advantage over  a free persons experience. Keep the core pvp of the game balanced and you will do well.-Better Animations: My only hard Critique so far in this game is the lacklustre animations when your observing another player, While this would have been fine as a MC mod this needs to be addressed as a standalone game. Animations can telegraph a great deal of things in a PVP situation, whether a player is Aiming down sights or isn't and it can do wonders to improve the experience overall, if your animations looked something on the Calibre of perhaps Battle-Bit Remastered then your game will be simply beautiful.Otherwise, Welcome to the International Community EXBO, What you have here holds Tremendous promise and has a very long life ahead of it. Do right by your community and you will go far. So far you have my support.

Most of the positive reviews have 2-15 hrs in this game. Im going to shed some light on what its like past the swamp (first area) and the cordon (second area). This is a game that you only progress with PVE and is designed to set you back using PVP. There are very very little reasons to engage in PVP other than getting lose ammo and probably some small change through valuables you collect doing objectives. That being said players of opposing factions find themselves camping quest objectives to set back progress, camping chokepoints that lead to other areas, and by the games design, the bandit faction has a much easier time farming resources based solely on map planning. PVE:What you will find yourself doing more than anything is public events. These include killing roaming mutants, killing roaming bandits, protecting roaming mutants from roaming AI, and not getting blown up by electric bolts. Most all of the events are one of these things but mainly can be summed up to kill group of thing in this location for 99% of the game. Despite how boring this sounds, this is the most fun thing in the entire game. There is not one other thing that is close to as enjoyable as these events and they are decent. I rate the events 53% good.  Problem, events grant rewards based on participation. If you participate one single kill then you get not much if you do all of it you get lots. Anyone can join you and anyone can steal the majority of the damage. Despite this game having squads you are actually encouraged to play alone. Use resources from events to navigate through a weapon tree that will have you walking across the map to get a worse version of the gun you want so you can get a slightly better version of that. Rinse and repeat 5 or 6 times and you got the gun you wanted in the first place. This game has no fast travel and getting killed on the way resets you to last base you were at. You will be walking to the same place over and over at some points. PVPOverlooking the fact that there is no report feature for in game hacking which not only exists but you will meet at some point. The PVP has roughly a 2% impact on your progression from killing enemies, at the same time PVP hinders your experience about 70% of the time. While you dont get crafting materials from killing other players you still lose yours. Setting back potentially hours of grinding for the lose ammo in your pocket. I dont think i have seen PVP that is this unrewarding while being such a high setback on death. Many players will do it just for the thrill of making your life miserable by camping entrances to safe zones others do it out of fear they will do the same to you. Finally at the higher areas you will need to do events not only in enemy territory but dead in front of their spawn. You kill 1 and 2 more pop right out. Making many of the later crafting recipes near impossible to do without spending insane amounts of money in the auction house. And that is the entire game explained. TLDR: The game has its fun moments but due to how they have PVP implemented into the game you will constantly be set back hours of work for little reward. Even looking past that the PVE is as complicated as go here kill thing standing here. I think this game has massive potential to be great but you cant do PVP and PVE poorly, you have to do at least one right. That is pretty much the entire game summed up.

Short and Sweet: The game itself isnt really bad and has a great basic design... but the lack of variations on the events and the resource grind gets bad fast. Since the Dev's actually commented and they are active I figure I'll expand on my review. The game it self is nothing more than an online "Stalker" game with "Minecraft" graphics and a simple but well planned design, where most games these days are trying to do "a little something for everyone" and falling short. STALCRAFT is on par as a Stalker or Metro environment  (maybe even a little too much with the environmental threats... *cough black holes cough*) It has some simple story driven quests that are interesting most of the time even if its just a simple fetch quest... The main issue comes from how you progress in the game as you advance and how player and PVP death works.When playing the game aside from the main quests you are meant to explore, participate in events, and of course PVP between the factions which is nothing new... To start from the "top" and work my way down the basic advancement is done via leveling up reputation in zones and grinding up resources to upgrade or make better weapons and armor or acquire needed "tools". You get these items by either finding them or completing events / killing creatures or completing side missions. While in the game there are three types of "stuff" you carry your "never drop" "Drop and only you can loot" and "Drop but anyone can loot"...So basically while playing the game you will be out questing and gathering resources to upgrade / make gear by going from event to event gathering stuff... but the issue is that all the events are mainly one type which effects the resource reward so you end up with a disparaging bottle neck ratio of resources. Usually where PVP would help balance this out when you are killed all your resources are placed into a bag that only YOU can open but the other player can still take off with that bag and just vendor it. So basically as you spend time in the zone gathering things your "risk" goes up but the "reward" is always on the "low end" due to the drop restrictions. Like taking a side mission that unexpectedly teleports you to an instanced area that your character was not ready for and there is no "exit" while on one of your "quest loops" through the zone. Or you run across a black hole.. Or a person who is out to PVP despite there being little no reward... Or you just happen to go exploring in the wrong spot and rack up so much rad/tox so fast you just turn into a ghoul almost instantly.All in all its not a "bad" game, its just the risk vs reward isnt balanced and the mechanics that are meant to "prolong gameplay" are stretched out too far that they detract FROM the gameplay. Its "All or nothing in the zone" in the sense you go all out on effort or come back with nothing lol

TL;DR Game is fun, community is incredibly toxic, EXBO aren't prioritising help for newer players.Let me start off by saying this game is fun.That being said as the game currently stands I cannot recommend anyone to play this game.There are a few systems that are fundamentally flawed that gets more and more noticeable the further you get into the game.The biggest issue for newer players is 'Matchmaking'.The matchmaking system is a hidden system in the game that you cannot view, your gear score is irrelevant.Whenever you leave the safe zone the game takes a 'screenshot' of your gear. You will be match made to what the game believes is your highest level gear you have ever worn.If you get a Purple or a Red quality item from a loot box or the Season pass and go to take it for a spin, you will suddenly be fighting people with Purple/Red gear. Even if you go back to your earlier gear you will still be facing people that heavily out gear you.Sealclubbing/GatekeepingEventually you will reach the Bar. Regardless of which side you are on, Stalker or Bandit. There will be other factions camping your locations just for the sake of PvPing or ruining your day. They usually have zero reason for being there, sometimes they will steal your resource bag and sell it back to you via the Auction House OR drop it somewhere. Sometimes they will drop it somewhere easy to find, sometimes they will drop it in a impossible location. If they die, they can be back within minutes while you can lose all of your farm. They also usually will outclass you in equipment and artifacts.This both gets better and worse in the North.The North:You've finally made it to the end game. Both Bandits and Stalkers both get split into 2 Subfactions each. The game is now a four faction game instead of two.Each subfaction has their own 'Safe Zone' (Note other factions can walk to the safe zone) with access to the very basics. The resources you can gain from these safe zones are much lower than the conflict zones, but generally speaking it's a much more pleasant time farming in your Safe or the Conflict zone next to you compared to the Bar areas. It's a lot faster to run back if you die as well.That being said, the camping and gate keeping gets a lot worse, expect to see the same names pop up over and over again at the entrances and exists to zones in the North. At this point they don't even try to hide it. Some people even have alts in other factions so they can scout the areas safely and worse, trade your dropped loot over to a alt that is friendly to you so you can't get it back. (Which according to EXBO is a perfectly legitimate strategy)Clans:So you have either saved up 10,000,000 and decided to create a clan or you are applying to join one.It's worth noting that established top clans typically control most of the market for high quality artifacts and equipment and have high KD and gear requirements. But my recommendation is to try to get into a top clan rather than creating one.First off congratulations, you have made it to the very endgame content.If you decided to make your own clan, in order to promote anyone to any sort of administrative position you will need to level up your clan. Else your clan has three ranks, Recruit, Trooper and Leader.How do you level up your clan?You need to recruit 30 members. You need to perform 10 (very easy) special deliveries (Capped at 3 a day)You need to win 5 subdivision battle stages.The problem is with the subdivision battles. They are a mess.Clan Subdivision Battles:Every day at the same time, a Clan Subdivision battle can occur. Either a Brawl, a Tournament or a fight over one of four locations on the Map at Forge-11. If for whatever reason you cannot make that specific time of day, tough luck, you can't participate.Clan Subdivision battles are the only way to obtain Crimson Casings.If you are a new clan, you will struggle to win any of these unless you can get all your members online and geared up in +15 Master gear and have a decent artifact build.As a Brawl is a 4 way fight, where alliances is allowed. Typically speaking the top clans will try to 'buy' the lower clans out so they can get a free or easy win. You will either need to get lucky and hope you get matched against three other even clans or just try again another day.A Tournament is a 1v1 fight between two clans, that only happen on specific days of the week. The easiesst way to level up your clan to level 2 is to win at Tournaments as it's less chaotic. But then again you have to get lucky one of the 10 clans that signed up is at your level and you get paired with them. (Not many people actually sign up to Tournaments)Basically subdivision battles come down to how active your clan is and how much money you can invest in your clan mates.RMT: (Real money trading)Did I mention this game can be considered completely pay to win?On the surface, there isn't too much to see. You can buy a Season Pass and Premium, both offer slight advantages but both can be easily obtained using in game currency if you wanted. It's not the worst thing to farm and if you sell the non bound items from the season pass you can expect to make your money back.You can buy Season Passes/Premimum to sell on the Auction house for in game money. You can technically buy Barter resources from the Auction House however usually it isn't worth it.It's worth noting that there are 'crates' in this game that can drop equipment such as weapons/armour/scanners/backpacks.Most of the items you get from crates are tradable and sellable on the Auction House.That being said, there are several websites outside of the game where people will trade real money for in game items/currency. (Like most games) As far as I can tell nothing is done about this.People will try to buy the items for cheap by advertising in discord or scanning through the auction house and then resell those items at huge markups on RMT sites. RMT is against TOS but nothing is done about the sites doing it and I have not heard of people being banned for it.Lack of Guides/Information about fundamental systems:While there are lots of quest guides on youtube, various features such as how to hunt Artifacts, how the clan system works, Hideout guides amongst other features have their information gatekept by the community.New people coming into the scene won't be able to easily find this information. The main forum for this game is Discord and it's terrible to search through. You can find 5 people asking the same question but no one offering an answer.

Okay so, let me get into it a bit...On the surface you may see this game and think its just a minecraft/roblox rip off with some stalker elements. You may even download it cause its free, run around for 10 minutes and not really realise wtf is going on, I did this a few months back and deleted the game soon after. That was before I'd even played Stalker gamma.After playing gamma I was browsing steam and saw this pop up again, after spending hundreds of hours in the zone I was like screw it, I'll give it a go again but this time, I'll ask a couple buddies to try it with me.That was 3 days ago and as you can see from my hours, it has stuck this time around.So getting into the game, yes the graphics take some getting used to BUT what you will find after persisting past the first zone (Great Swamps for you Stalker players out there) is a deep, engaging MMO, set in the same universe as Stalker but with its own thing going on. You start by picking between Loners or Bandits and your bases are either side of the swamp to eachother, as the beginning quests progress and you push further out and start grinding resources you will come across the other faction which results in open world PvP. The PvEvP element is where the game shines imho, while you do lose stuff upon death its not a full on extraction type shooter game where you lose everything. You will lose some meds, some ammo and some mats you farmed. yes it can be frustrating running back when you keep dying to players or anomalies or PvE but again, its engaging and somehow doesn't feel too tedious (♥♥♥♥ black holes tho, they can suck a nut)Overall, its not perfect. Some things feel like cheap 1 shot things like blackholes and some bosses but the PvP is mostly balanced once you learn whats going on and how to get better gear. It has some elements of skip mechanics (if you have done the grinding for the area you are in) but no direct p2w. The gameplay is akin to a DayZ or Tarkov more than Stalker but it still feels like Stalker, just... Blockier xDMe and my friends are just reaching mid game after 40 hours with some funny moments already. I'd have to give it a 8/10 definitely worth playing especially if you like stalker, Tarkov or DayZ

So this lurker has some words about this game.. here, have a seat..A quick run down is Stalcraft has a couple core themes/mechanics you've seen from other games such as stalker and escape from tarkov obviously, but also mwz/dmz and oddly enough eve online and made something interesting. If you're like me and you've been looking for a spooky open world pvpve experience based on modern gunplay then this is a strong contender for being a favorite. give it a shot its free. at the very least itll occupy you for an hour or two.Now as for what it is and how good it does that.. Stalcraft is just an mmo take on a big team deathmatch game. You pick a faction at character creation (stalker/bandit) and head out from their respective bases to do decently written quests and other tasks in fairly large maps along side other players which makes up the core pvpve experience of the game. Theres 3 regional servers to play on: NA, EU, and SEA i think it was? and the overall world map, which is pretty big, is then broken down into about 7 or so mid-sized sub maps that connect to each other at specific points much like eve onlines gate mechanics.So the basic gameplay loop so far from what i've seen is a lot like eve online i'd say. Once you leave your factions base you have 20 sec of invulnerability to dash into the bushes in case anyone is around, go do what you gotta do like mwz/dmz while watching for enemy players, then get your loot back to base or you'll lose it... sorta.. unfortunately a major flaw in the game presents itself at this point imo.This is where you'd think tarkov mechanics would kick in for the chefs kiss.. But no.. ALL GEAR IN THE GAME IS BOUND TO THE PLAYER AND DOES NOT DROP ON DEATHI guess this part will mean something different to different people, good or bad, but its a major aspect to the game either way. Basically your equipment: Main gun, sidearm, melee, armor suit, backpack, and many inventory items are bound to the player and are kept after dying. For me this is really disappointing because theres not much risk when exploring i feel and also very little reward for winning in pvp when all you'll loot from someone is ammo, meds, and crafting stuff. I guess things would be too difficult otherwise with as often as you die maybe? Its not a deal breaker for me but for some maybe.. My hope is one day hardcore versions of the servers are setup with permanent loss of loot enabled. Thatd be fun but i like a challenge in my games it seems.As for the pvp i really like it. There isnt anything too special about it. The gunplay is good enough (audio is a little grating) but i dont think theres enough guns or customization ability. It seems like they're trying to mimic tarkovs setup but it doesnt work well enough sadly. And it should be said clearly that the main thing about this game is PVP. You'll see a lot of reviews blasting about how unfair or mean something is.. I mean that stuff is a given in a game like this. While it is voxelish looking like minecraft, there is no mining or real crafting so dont go walking in a straight line right out your base. Besides other players theres all sorts of things thatll kill you. Make sure you dont take too much out with you on your runs. Keep all the droppable stuff in your bases inventory and work you're way up. I really wish the crafting and economy get worked on. That whole side of the game just feels underdeveloped.. But yeah, looting shinys off people is a lot of fun but just know though that most shinys are protected in this game. Otherwise i'm having a lot of fun!Im still new at this and havent really seen how end game really plays so i'll update the review once i get there which im sure i will. Theres enough meat to the the game to keep me occupied.

You can choose from two factions. Loners & Bandits. (I'd argue that Bandits have an easier time navigating the map.) These Factions eventually evolve into sub-factions.  ->  or  , and  ->  or . There's PvP  except for safe zones. The community can be pretty awful in the faction chats but most of my interactions with with teammates in my own faction have been positive. While its possible to play this solo, you'll have an easier time throughout the Zone squadding up. Most of my playtime has been solo so far, but once you start getting to the opposing factions area to farm some mats, you'll have an easier time with at least another person.Its almost full loot PvP. If you die, you won't lose your weapon/armor and anything with a padlock icon on it. If you die full of barter mats (which you need to upgrade & craft gear), there's a chance for other players to find your bag and either auction your bag or mail it back to you. They can't open your "lost backpack" full of mats, only their own lost backpack.You'll eventually get to the point where you need to farm cables. Do the main story quest long enough to get a free metal detector. The ones you can craft are pretty garbage and a waste of space. You can recharge them at the generators in bases.Any Daily Quest you do that requires you to turn in an item to the "supplier", its just the guy you buy ammo/consumables from. Just select the "I'm here about the ad" option. Speaking of quests... READ. Your choices have consequences. If you fail a quest, that's it, there's no re-do. People that blow through dialogue just might end up spending all their money on vodka for a drunk. :P Some options offer different/bonus rewards as well.If you're a fan of the STALKER series, and don't mind the PvP aspect. In this game, though, you're constantly at risk of being killed by other players, and when that happens, you lose your items (though not your gear, thankfully).After spending hours farming for materials, it's disheartening to be killed while trying to return to safety. It's not just a one-time thing either; it keeps happening. If you dislike PvP, I’d strongly recommend skipping this game, as the constant threat of player killing undermines the fun.Even though I enjoy the PvE content, I found myself stuck in a loop of losing progress after hours of gameplay, simply because I kept losing my items to other players. Those items are crucial for upgrading your gear, so every time I died, it felt like a setback. If the developers ever add a PvE-only server, I’d consider coming back, but if that never happens, there are other games that offer a more enjoyable experience without the constant PvP stress.

The War of 1838: Causes, Events, and ImpactIntroduction:The War of 1838, also known as the Rebellion of 1837-1838, was a significant conflict that took place in Upper and Lower Canada, which are present-day Ontario and Quebec in Canada. This war was a culmination of years of political and social unrest, fueled by grievances of the French-speaking population against the British colonial rule. In this essay, we will delve into the causes, events, and impact of the War of 1838, shedding light on the factors that led to this conflict and its profound consequences for Canadian history.I. Causes of the War of 1838:Political and Economic Factors:a. Lack of Representative Government: The British colonial administration in Canada had limited representation, which led to frustrations among the French-speaking population, as they felt marginalized and excluded from political decision-making.b. Economic Struggles: The economy of both Upper and Lower Canada faced challenges, including high taxes and trade restrictions imposed by the British government. This economic hardship added to the discontent among the people.Ethnic and Cultural Tensions:a. French-English Divide: The majority of the population in Lower Canada was French-speaking, while Upper Canada was predominantly English-speaking. This linguistic and cultural divide created tensions between the two communities, with the French Canadians feeling that their language and traditions were being suppressed.b. Preservation of French-Canadian Identity: French Canadians sought to preserve their cultural heritage and protect their language rights, further exacerbating the tensions with the English-speaking population.Influence of American Republicanism:a. Inspiration from the American Revolution: The success of the American Revolution and the establishment of a republic influenced some Canadian reformers, who desired similar political liberties and self-governance.b. Fear of American Expansionism: The British authorities and loyalists feared that the discontent in Canada could lead to American intervention or an invasion, posing a threat to British control in the region.II. Events of the War of 1838:The Rebellions of 1837:a. Lower Canada Rebellion: In November 1837, the Lower Canada Rebellion erupted with armed uprisings against the British administration. Led by Louis-Joseph Papineau, the rebels aimed to establish a more democratic and representative government.b. Upper Canada Rebellion: In December 1837, the Upper Canada Rebellion broke out under the leadership of William Lyon Mackenzie. The rebels in Upper Canada sought to address similar grievances, including demands for responsible government and an end to corrupt practices.British Response and the Military Campaigns:a. Suppression of the Rebellions: The British authorities swiftly moved to suppress the rebellions. Troops were sent to Canada, and the colonial militias were mobilized to restore order and quell the uprisings.b. Battle of Saint-Eustache: In December 1837, a significant battle took place in Saint-Eustache, Lower Canada, between the rebels and British forces. The rebels were defeated, leading to the collapse of the rebellion in Lower Canada.c. Battle of Montgomery's Tavern: In December 1837, the Battle of Montgomery's Tavern occurred near Toronto, Upper Canada. The rebel forces were again defeated, resulting in the failure of the Upper Canada Rebellion.Aftermath and Trials:a. Suppression of Dissent: Following the rebellions, the British cracked down on dissent and implemented stricter measures to control the Canadian population.b. To start the review, I like the game, very fun. I've played as stalker for ~25 hrs as of writing this. I'm also going to be writing this in part for the dev and for anybody that feels like reading. I haven't played an MMORPG before so I won't be comparing this to other games. I want to write some things I think the game does well and some things it doesn't do well on. Also there is a TLDR at the bottom.To start with the bad, as you progress in the game the demand for resources go up. This is because you need to buy more expensive equipment and more of it such as gun attachments. I normally wouldn't have an issue with this since IRL nicer things are more expensive, but a person with quite a few hours in the game complained about the game being PTW(pay to win). You should also expect your profits to go up as you get better equipment but the supply and demand don't seem to match according to some more experienced players. The developer responded to a player complaining about the game being PTW and I will respond to that here since comments were turned off on the other post:>Format for dev resonseFormat for my critique.>Let us note that the equipment from the in-game store acts as an alternative equipment, it does not provide any advantages .That is a lie. If in a game I hit (esc) and click (store), style cases are the first thing to appear and just mentioning the trade coin reward, it is 36.0821% in total chance, is a currency to buy resources. (although you can get this resource through the season pass, you can also just buy levels for that). You can also buy end game equipment in other tabs but I am not going to purchase or mention it because what do I know. -_( ._. )_->Those purchases are considered as skipping ("skip") a certain amount of time that you or other Zone Researchers could spend on extracting resources for a similar suit or weapon in a Barter.This is just what PTW is. You also can't say 'These purchases don't provide any advantage,' and 'You can just skip to the end of the game with money.' Those are conflicting sentences(give or take some exaggeration).(del bc char lim)>The parts of the weapon you mentioned, for example, the Gauss Riffle currently can be obtained from the Exchanger for the Act Tickets that are earned through Battle Pass levels and its tasks and challenges. They are rather easy to complete and won't require an "obligatory" card swipe to claim all act tickets.The original poster was complaining about an op weapon being a PTW weapon. What the dev says is kind of true. The season pass was very easy to complete for the first 20 levels, and then the difficulty spiked. From what I can tell the easiest method to grind the battle pass is to kill other players, which tilts in favor of the PTW players. I do like the combat system though but that's in the positive feedback section. (del bc char lim)In defense of the developer for making the game PTW. There has to be some sort of transaction for the developer to profit off of, at least if anyone wants this game to be in active development. I won't be shaking a finger at the developer for trying to profit off the game, I'm just disappointed in the developer for degrading their game with such transactions. The transaction thing wouldn't be a problem if A MAJOR COMPONENT OF THE GAME IS PVP AND FACTIONS. Please be aware of this in future development. The game has a decently deep rooted structure in micro-transactions so if your playing/going to play the game, don't expect this to change(at least for a good long while). It's the developers right to make or break their game and people should be aware of this, the developer should also be aware of their community. Another negative aspect of the game would be high level players can enter the newbie zones and genocide everybody. This has led to new players rage quiting and being discouraged from playing. The high level players are discouraged by doing this from the newbie loot being bad and having all the quests complete down at the newbie areas. Although you may be forgetting the powerful incentive, the season pass wants you to kill players. Even if this isn't the case, me and many other players have experienced getting absolutely steamrolled at the newbie base by player(s) guarding a quest area. I can think of some ways to fix this issue (example: encouraging group movements), but it's not really certain if any of them will fix anything so I won't push for any.A generic problem with the game is enemy npc's will just see you through any foilage or walls with no bullet collision. As human beings, we are deeply set in the idea of 'fair'. Even the word fair can have major impacts on a associates behavior in a negotiation. This is seen as unfair and unfun when under heavy fire by enemy's with heat vision nasa satilite 400x zoom eyeballs. This ruins the prone mechanic(PvE) because you can't see with foilage in your face and when an entire base of enemies are running at you because it is their god given mission to kill you with their unending suppressive fire.Also, from what I've experienced, the game can be a nightmare to play when the servers are full. This happened when I was stuck at The Bar and I only had newbie equipment with no modifications. Also difficult when I was still in The Swamps.---- What I like about the gameI love the combat. The adrenaline rush you get from combat is intense. I especially love the fact that you can kill anyone in a couple seconds with good headshots (given there is no insane difference in weapons and armor). The fact that you can die so quickly makes you on edge and makes combat very fast paced.Ammunition is fairly inexpensive but still something to account for. I feel that the exchange of ammunition is very balanced given it's your ultimate lifeline in the game.The map detail is phenomenal and I think the map is very well built. Although sadly I cannot experience the game in it's glory because I cannot afford a good computer. In fact, the computer I'm using was won at a raffle from my high school and they got it from sams club for 100$. My good laptop blew up from a hiccup in the laptop, thanks Lenovo, and I was denied repair.( my sob story) Although I don't feel any connection to any characters in the game and the story isn't very cohesive, the story and side quests were very fun to do.The secrets in the game are an amazing addition. I found The PP-2000 in the newbie area and it's done me faithful ever since. I found it 8 hours into the game. Although sadly I have not been able to progress my weapon tree since, even though I put 18 more hours into the game. It is possible that the developer balanced the game against players unless they find these secrets, and that's why progression seems slow. A thing the developer should note if they made a mistake in balancing.--- The end of my review, and then some personal remarks.At the time I love this game. From where I'm at it looks like I'm going to have to dump my time into the game to see any of the progression I was once seeing. I may need to head up to The Bar to see some progression but I'm just finishing up The Garages. To the developer, I think you did an amazing job on the game and I can see a lot of effort and time being put into the map. I'm sad to say I may have to remove myself from the game since I lack the financial power(I'm not going to make progress with money). I'll buy the season pass when I can to support the game since I believe the game has given me a good time and it's worth that much.To wanna be players: I think the game is worth playing a bit, at least to The Garages. Edit: The network issues still randomly show up some days but its been clear for enough time to progress into the game and actually review its content.TL;DR: The only reason to play this is if you want to play something vaguely resembling a Stalker game with your friends. There are much better alternatives for any other aspect of stalcraft, like better battle royales, better competitive shooters, better mmos, better number crunching games, etc. And if you just wanted to play more stalker? Anomaly/Gamma mods are a thing and Stalker 2 is coming out soon.Probably the best thing i can say about this is that it has a decent movement system allowing you to climb all sorts of things, something i didnt expect from a game like this. It does also manage to catch at least a fraction of the atmosphere of the stalker series. Otherwise the sound design is just functional, nothing impressive there, the graphics are fine, the maps themselves are fine.And then there's all the bad stuff.Most of the early game grind is nullified by some coupons, its all fairly smooth until you get to veteran ranks, then its all a massive atrocious grind, the only saving grace being the main quest line gear and (if you're really lucky) some gear from lootboxes. And yes it has lootboxes and all the premium bs you can imagine, along with mechanics that serve no purpose other than artificially increasing the grind, such as the max durability decrease on item upgrades.Weapon stats are a bit of a random mess, with some weapons of the same rank being clearly superior choices, which immediately cuts down on build variety in any sort of pvp scenario. On top of that, mutants have awfully bloated hitpoints, which is only done for the sake of introducing a "bonus damage vs mutants" stat on snipers and shotguns, even less variety for mutant hunting.The world map encounters get more boring and uninspired and way too time consuming as it goes on. Jumping around in a circle or just shooting some orbs for a few minutes, wow, such fun, now do that like 50 times over for a single unimpressive gear upgrade (along with all the other events of course). Also new encounters can just spawn on top of you and then you're suddenly surrounded by 5 assault rifle armed npcs.There is no real pvp balance in the early game areas, players can show up with such high rank gear and and meds  that you cant do any real damage to them. The only thing preventing this from happening more often is the fact that they dont have any real reason or benefits to do this other than just shooting up the newbies for the sake of it.Squad mechanics in this mmo are rather barebones. All main story and side quests are single player, so no playing that with others. And then you finally reach the late game subfactions and are unable to join whichever you want. Depending on your character starting faction you only have 2 options out of 4, okay, but then if one of those subfactions has too many players in it it will just be locked so you only get ONE option. So either wait however long it takes, or join the other and grind some more to pay to switch later when available. This must be the laziest way of balancing this. What's even worse is that once one player joins a subfactions you can say goodbye to the whole squad thing, since you cant form a squad even if they're not a hostile faction to you. If you can't all join due to the inane player limit on subfactions then good luck, cant play with your friends anymore, no more squad.And as far as the solo content goes, nearly all the missions are just fetch or kill x npcs quests, with some insignificant choices here and there. Technically, if you follow some chains of completely unrelated side quests and choose all the right options in dialogues (which you have absolutely no way of knowing in advance unless you looked it up) you can get some decent gear to help with early game progression.The very few more interesting main quests have some fun ideas and unique areas but are let down by the boring repetitive and just too long boss fights.The enemy ai is absolute trash, all they can do (both human npcs and mutants) is running at you in a straight line and attacking. Their detection range seems to be very inconsistent as well. Occasionally the dogs will run away across half the map when damaged, which is an annoyance more than anything else.Old review:Pretty much unplayable due to random 10-20s lag spikes and random disconnects. From what i could gather from other reports and my testing so far it might have something to do with their anti cheat system massively overreacting to even the slightest bit of network instability after some recent update. I can't even say its a problem with the connection on my end, literally no other multiplayer game ive ever played has had such severe network issues.

From my first few hours playing this weird minecraft-wannabe STALKER-wannabe shooter, I can say I'm kind of impressed.I started out my playthrough as a Stalker. While I suppose it's not really that big of a deal progression wise which faction you pick, some of the reviews do have a point on the game.While the gear you get out of the start kind of sucks ass, it can easily be upgraded and you can get armor plates for dirt cheap. Not the plates that some players like to camp in my area with, but good enough for what you need. The coat you get at the start of the game has 6x less overall protection than the 'suit with armor' and it's not incredibly hard to farm the animals and bandits/NATO required to get the gear. I believe a lot of the problems people face with this game is expanding out too fast with their old smg and hoping to make it somewhere. While it does, you can be swarmed by the opposing faction and they can take your ♥♥♥♥. When people say "Full-loot PVP" that is not true. Cash, Guns, armor, gear, modifications, and a ton of the starter medkits, grenades, and 9mm ammunition POUCHES (And they give you a TON of 9mm ammo) all have a flag that outright prevents it from being dropped on death. Personal inventory is probably one of the best yet, and while you can only access it inside the main safe zones, it provides you with an absolute ♥♥♥♥ ton of space to put all your precious valuables that are flagged to drop on death. The main stuff being: medkits, bandages, grenades, UNBOXED ammo, any drops that mutant animals and NPCS give, and in my case, "Green algae" and "Swamp stones" which you use to upgrade your gear. Yes, even the pouched ammo you get from the goods trader is not available to be dropped on death. So no, I wouldn't consider it a "Full Loot PVP" at least at the start of the game.And even with the starter piece of ♥♥♥♥ smg they give you, I was still decking poor bandit saps that decided it was a good idea to pop up along the way. I did get myself decked quite a few times too, but that's part of the fun.I would suggest whatever you need to gather to build better weapons, armor, backpacks, gear, etc... you gather strategically and attempt to avoid the enemy faction that likes to pop up along the route. Get a nice supply of barter supplies from killing nests first and then try to venture out and find bandits/NATO that'll give you the other barter supply.As long as you're not carrying dicktons of unboxed ammo around, it's not the end of the world to die in this game. The camping issue is kind of sort of a problem though. But it's more basically team deathmatch rather than a horrifying free for all like I've seen in other games trying to accomplish the same thing.In short, STALCRAFT does the stalker genre of games quite decently, though the pvp kind of dulls things down just a little bit. I'd bring some friends or find someone to adventure with on your faction, or you're probably in for a rough ride.

The game was alright initially. its probably a 4/10. Pros:1. Faction NPCs that actually patrol, fight one another, and fight mutants2. Enemy mutants and any NPCs can get caught in anomalies and actually die by them (seriously, why is this so rare among stalker MMORPGs). 3. Loot pack system on death - when you die, players can only grab basic consumables from your body. Weapons and gear doesnt drop. Rare materials drop in these lost packs. Only the player from whom they dropped from can open them and grab the resources. Meaning bandits and such have to try to ransom it back to you. 4. Decent travel times. A big issue I have with games like Stay Out and Will to Live is you end up spending huge swaths of time just running. Like 30mins or more just..running between locations. Stalcraft maps aren't as big so it doesn't take you 30 minutes to run between locations. More like 10-15. 5. Story is pretty good for this games situation (minecraft modded engine). Story has choices (though I dont' think they impact the world around you). Decent voice acting. Surprisingly good. Middle Ground:1. Minecraft graphics Cons:1. PvP - There's a ton of PvP. Its basically a PvP game, dare I say more battle royal feeling than MMORPG. Like an MMO-Battle Royale. There's some maps that are far enough away from enemy bases that they don't bother going there. However, that's a minority of the maps. Most of the other maps every 5 minutes you're fighting players. The opposing factions KoS no matter what (cause why not, there's no reason not too). You've got people hiding in trees. People just waiting around to kill you. You'll have people sit there camping quest locations and travel points for hours with snipers and assault rifles. And for no reason either. Its not that profitable. They're PvPing for the sake of PvP, no profit or anything. Which at that point I ask, why do I not just go play a PvP game? There's nothing worse than playing for 2 hours and 90% of any progression you were even able to make is as a result of your premium daily log in rewards. I've played a lot of MMORPG games with this none stop PvP design. The core design philosophy when doing these kind of games is that it NEEDs to be more beneficial and profitable to be out farming than PvPing. You want players to PvP while farming items. You do NOT want roaming gank squads and gank players resetting everyone's progression for that play session for kicks. Which is what is happening. There's not an easy solution to this as the minecraft engine I'm sure is putting limitations on them. And maybe I just need to put this game down for a month or two why the hype players get bored and leave. Or maybe maps need smaller populations. Who knows. But your progression starts to move at a snails pace because you're spending 90% of your time fighting players. Like I just made it to the last tier of armor for green armor, after 23 hours of playing. That's not because its hard. Its because I spent so much time running for 10-15 minutes, only to die to a player. Losing my progression and travel time. Rinse and repeat. Probably would've taken me another 10+ hours to do if I hadn't subscribed to their premium service for extra rewards/items. 2. Enemy AI - The enemy NPCs with guns and AI are like terminators. Insane accuracy, fast damage. They kill you fast. So the idea, especially while solo, is you take shots at them. Duck behind cover and use a medkit and heal. Rinse and repeat. There's not really a strategy behind it. Just medpack spam because those guys can shoot a pixel on your foot from a mile away. like 40% of my deaths are to players, 40% to anomalies (fair, I don't mind this), and 20% to terminator NPCs. They take a lot of medpacks and paying attention to how far away NPC bases are3. No immersion - because you're constantly fighting players and watching the tree lines for some prone sniper camping the area, you can't really get immersed. You've got this constant sense of "GOTTA GO FAST" to avoid losing all your progression for the day or all your run time.  No sense of immersing yourself in the world or exploration. 4. F2P cash shop - Premium is almost required if you don't want to tear you hair out while grinding. And they had p2w items at launch. If this game is like other MMORPG stalker games, I can easily see it coming back. Stay Out also had the same issue and they removed it before steam launch because of western audience outcry. But added them back in after all the western players quit. Wouldn't be surprised if we eventually see gear in the shop again (or pay money to bypass grind). 5. Faction inbalance - For the Copper Cable/Alum cable phase of progression (which is where I am currently stopped at), bandits have a much larger advantage. Their spawn point is very close to the two major maps for farming. Stalkers do have an alum cable farm map close to them, but not copper. As a result, bandits progression at this stage is much much easier and faster. As their travel time is cut in half and the chances of them getting ambushed are significantly lower. From what I understand talking to other players on the RU side, the RU servers (they've been open for years), the Merc side is heavily stacked. With a majority of players playing on Bandits and the Merc sub faction. I can easily see this release going down the same path. So yeah in short, this is more of a PvP MMO-Battle Royale game rather than a MMORPG STALKER game. You will spend a vast majority of your time pvping or dying to pvp.

As much as I like the game, there are some issues that just makes it feel like a huge waste of time. I would definitely not recommend this game to anyone having a full time job, unless you like dealing with tons of frustration in the limited time they have while achieving minimum to nothing. EXBO's attitude against cheaters is frustrating, there is no real punishment for cheating. Cheaters can just make a new character/account and keep on cheating. One of them in particular continues pumping out content and has a toxic attitude towards the community, pretty much laughing in our face and stating this has only brought them more exposure.The game feels like a running simulator, the amount of time you have to run from A to B is just silly. For example as a Stalker running from Cordon to the BAR can easily take 15minutes or more if you don't know the route there, and by the time you get there, you get killed 200m before entering the BAR safe zone... multiple times. I ended up dying 4-5 times on my way there, multiply this by 15minutes per run, you end up with 1h-1h15m of just running and achieving nothing in the process. A fast travel system which you can unlock and then use by paying roubles or something similar would help.The BAR area is pure cancer. You have to expect dying a couple of times either to campers or cheaters before you can make it to the exit, and if you actually manage to do so the exits have a high chance of being camped by players wearing end game gear, which take so little damage that it becomes frustrating when you only wear story mission gear.Early Bandit/Stalker bases in the Swamp/Cordon are heavily imbalanced. Bandits have a much easier time travelling from the Swamp to Cordon, and then from Cordon to Agroprom/Dump. Their base is literally closer to the exits by miles. I've made a Bandit alt just because it's easier to get around those areas.Matchmaking is a joke. There should be different brackets depending on KDA and gear score. Players should not be put in the same matchmaking where end game geared players are, just because they managed to get 1 story purple item.The lost backpack system needs a rework. Losing all your stuff over and over again to the above mentioned issues ( campers/cheaters) is just frustrating, You should at least be able to keep some % of it's contents and if you kill someone and receive their lost backpack, make a reward system for putting it up on the AH or a karma system for sending it back to the player, instead of just vendoring it to the fence.Overall I like the game and the whole MMO PVPVE aspect behind it.I will mostilely continue playing it, but these issues will sooner or later make players, that don't have 16h a day to invest in the game, frustrated enough that they will eventually leave..I believe some quality of life improvements are needed in order to help a larger player  base enjoy the game.PS: Note on the game's reviews,  there are quite many "positive reviews" from players playing the game for 1-2 hours and with only 1-2 products on steam. A bit dodgy if you ask me.

I love this game. Have you read ever read Roadside Picnic or played one of the STALKER games before? Do you wanna know what it's really like to live in the hellhole we call "the zone"? Well then, you've come to the right place because this game nails it!From the atmosphere, to the low player count, to the rugged armor, to the enemy designs, Stalcraft is a living, breathing rendition of the zone in all its glory (and in all its cruelty).Stalcraft also has a unique death mechanic wherein you lose all your resources but you keep your valuables, which incentivizes bandits to attack stalkers and vice versa without making the game too frustrating!It also has a bunch of different ways for you to gather resources and make money, though different tasks yield different rewards, and you will oftentimes need to do a great many different things in order to get anything done, especially late-game.Also, if you like hazard suits, this game has plenty of them, and while there are sub-factions, you don't need to join them, so if you're like me and want to just RP as a scientist, feel free to do so!...I should warn you all however, I don't know if this was ever fixed or not, but when you make a character, you can NEVER reuse their name, EVEN IF YOU DELETED THEM. So, make sure you like your name before you take it. (And try not to worry about it afterwards, I know I worried about it for a while, but in the end, it is just a name)Also, if you use camo or paint in this game, for either weapons or armor, remember that the only way to get back that paint is by upgrading the armor. Using the paint scraper just deletes the paint forever and replacing with another paint also deletes the previous paint forever.Also there's an HEV suit skin for one suit of armor in the game, but it doesn't look very good. Still, I consider that a plus.Also the game has a ton of customization for weapons (and a little for armor too)!

While I had my fair share of fun, I can't really reccomend it.The devs are absolutely oblivious to what makes a boss fight fun and challenging, and, as a result the majority of bosses are just bullet sponges. typically faster than you and they can kill you in 2/3 hits.Making the stats of an enemy incredibly high doesn't make it more fun or difficult, it just creates a wall.If you don't believe me check out "Stalcraft x cheese boss" and see how many videos are out there just explaining how to cheese unfair bossfights, in order to go on with the story. The parkour sessions (which feel like leftovers of this game's roots as a Minecraft mod) are also quite annoying to deal with, and absolutely unfun.The monetization is rather predatory, since you can buy lootcrates (which have an incredibly low probability to drop what you're looking for), a "Premium subscription" (about 8 euros a month), and a battle pass (15 euros every 3 months + grinding 1/2 hundred hours to complete it each time).Of course there are paid skins as well, but as skins they don't really influence the game.The only positive side of the monetization system is that you can buy both the premium and the battle pass with ingame currency, but, of course, you'll need a quite high amount of it, which means a lot of farming.The positives are that the game, especially until the Bar (and at Bar's low levels) is incredibly fun, so if you'd like to try out a STALKER like experience but online, while focusing only on main and side quests with a friend or two is fine, but once you're done with it (it could probably take you around 100 hours) you'll be stuck in the endgame loop.You might be wondering, how's the endgame loop?Well, grinding, grinding, grinding and more grinding.Killing the same 7 type of enemies (not joking, literally 7 but reskinned for the endgame) Ghouls, armed NPCs, mutant dogs, mutant pigs, mutant rats, mutant boars and the skitters.Delivering the same backpacks to more or less the same locations, figthing for the control of the same 6 outposts everyday, doing the daily missions that repeat themselves, for hundred of hundred of hours.The endgame loop of is just doing more of what you've already done for the past 150+ hours till you'll have crafted the gear/found the artifacts that you want and finally quit.With the passing of time the devs have been reducing the amount of resources that you obtain through the grind, which means that it'll take you even longer to obtain your next upgraded weapon/armor, but I'd guess that the devs are afraid that once players reach the endgame and understand that there's absolutely nothing new to do, they'll just leave and the game's retention rate will just drop.Last but not least, this game is developed and published by a Russsian software house, so, while I am no one to judge other people choices when it comes to their wallets, just remember that if you spend money on Stalcraft you're actively supporting the Russian economy.Overall I'll keep playing it as a time killer, but if you're looking for a great MMORPG to sink your time in, I'd suggest to look somewhere else.

The game has some pretty weird issues I've noticed recently, that can really keep me from just recommending the game.Sure, the game is meant to be hard on the player and very unforgiving, but the hard issue is making it, "fair." A game can be unforgiving but still be entirely fair to the user. Tarkov, before its cheaters issue, was a very unforgiving game, but can still be very fair to its user. Stalcraft is unforgiving, but also has issues with fairness, and overall functionality & balance. Let me explain:NPC's definitely need work. NPC's, in extreme fog in the dark, can pinpoint your location at anywhere from 50-80 meters it seems. I'm not talking NATO soldiers, I'm talking your average stalker encampment. These guys have some insane vision capabilities that never changes in the weather, which is unforgiving, but also unfair to users. You're reducing the players vision, but not the enemy's.Guns also need some work. You'll find plenty of times where the gun just... *doesn't reload.* Like, at all. You'll see the animation, and you'll reliably think, "This is done, I'm ready for the next firefight." Only to shoot 11 bullets instead of your typical 30 to finish them off because the gun never actually reloaded, despite what the animation showed you.Another glaring issue lies with shotguns, which apparently do NOT deal damage if you don't load them all the way. I found this out the hard way using the Shorty 590 (Super shorty. Secondary, 3 round shotgun.) If you reload the gun, and decide to pull the trigger halfway through loading, it will NOT deal its full damage. This might not sound too bad, but when you EXPECT a gun to work for you, and you begin to get that game sense of how much you think any one weapon you've become accustomed to will deal, and all of a sudden it doesn't, you feel extremely cheated out of a victory.Another definite rework is in the knives. The knife has a TINY hitbox. It's virtually impossible to reliably use one without basically touching whatever you're looking at. Despite it having a slicing or stabbing animation, it has the same sized hitbox. The real hitbox requires you to be literally be cursor-on-target. Even being slightly off means missing the target. This is extremely annoying when dealing with just about any mutant. Rats have a tiny hitbox, meaning you have to let them hit you so you can get them to stay still long enough just to hit them. Same thing with dogs, and even boars.Quite a few of the quests are extremely frustrating as well. I've heard everyone complain about how annoying the courier quest is. Beating couriers up for info. It seems to be entirely RNG. You have to somehow find a courier first, and then hope they give you the info. I spent 40 minutes on the quest because despite no one else being in the area recently, not a single courier spawned. Others I know spent hours trying to do it.Finally, the, "Quest areas" for lack of a better word, where you must venture in it alone and do a quest's are really finicky. Sometimes, the exit won't load (and to the dev, yes I am up to date in my drivers,) meaning any and all loot you found is basically gone, because you can't pick up loot in there, and if you /s you lose your loot. Respawning does not solve the issue either. Sometimes enemies just straight up don't do anything, sometimes they are aggressive before you've even fully loaded in.The game has potential, but right now it needs a lot of work. It's unforgiving, but it's a slippery uphill battle to even play the game.

The potential for Stalcraft is enormous, but unfortunately, the game feels like a walking simulator at times. The quests are boring and lackluster, often requiring you to run back and forth without doing much else. Even the combat encounters can be underwhelming, with enemies that can be taken down with just a single hit.One frustrating aspect of the game is the Emission (Reset/Wipe) that occurs every 3-4 hours, which you have to keep track of on your own since the game doesn't notify you. This can be especially annoying if you're not close to an underground area where you can stay safe.Another issue is the lack of fast travel options in the game. You need to walk across the entire zone to get to another, which can result in losing a lot of time if you die along the way. Furthermore, if you die in a different zone, you will not respawn at the base of that zone, but instead in the latest zone you were in, forcing you to walk back through the same zone again. This can become tedious and frustrating quickly.The game also has zone-locked items, meaning you cannot buy certain items unless you are in the correct zone. For example, if you want a low-level item from a gun vendor, you will need to travel back to the previous zone to purchase it, even if you have the required resources and money. This can be incredibly frustrating and time-consuming.Lastly, the lack of character customization in an MMO is a letdown. While it may not be the most important aspect of the game, it can still make the experience feel more personal and engaging.Overall, while Stalcraft has the potential to be a great game, it falls short in many areas, resulting in a lackluster and often frustrating experience.

Good concept, but nearly unplayable due to game designers' oversightAfter 150 hours of playtime, I can confidently say: the gameplay drastically changes depending on the time of day. This is the core issue with the developers' current approach.Night-time (2 AM - 6 AM): Near Perfect- The game becomes almost ideal- You occasionally encounter both friendly players and opponents- Always on alert, but can play peacefully most of the time, with rare real enemy encountersDaytime: Unplayable Chaos- PvP is useless and annoying: you don't get items from players you kill, but you lose yours. People mostly kill each other to avoid being killed, while some with late-game gear kill for fun or to help friends. It's more complex than that, but losing stuff isn't even the main problem...- 90% of the gameplay becomes RUNNING, RUNNING, RUNNING the same routes over and over to your death point. This makes it unplayable for most people. As someone with limited play time after work, I sometimes didn't gather anything - just stuck in a death-running loop until bedtime. You can't change server. If there's a guy with master weapon camping you - you can only try to kill him after you ran 5 km after your death. But most likely there'll be another guy - and then another guys. Even if there will be no enemies - allies share your farm so you farm crap anyway.- Leaving your base almost guarantees death by players with late-game weapons or parties- Even if you survive, all spots are already farmed/being farmed, so you gain basically nothing, and you'll lose that shortly. Allies share farm, so there's not much point in sticking together.The current state feels like Counter-Strike during peak hours, with everyone crammed onto a couple of servers. Players constantly die, run back and forth, and die again (except those with premium gear or late-game equipment).You can barely play properly, aside from rushing main quests that transport you to individual, invulnerable locations. It's essentially a single-player experience.Is it playable? YES, but only LATE AT NIGHT OR by rushing the main quest and ignoring everything else. The game looks good, and the STALKER vibe is awesome, but you probably won't notice that if you're dying every time you leave the base.The game does feature a great single-player (or co-op) experience, but all my friends dropped out after a while due to these issues. I'm not sure if the developers plan to change anything, though limiting the number of people on a server doesn't seem that hard.Overall: Good concept, great atmosphere, but current implementation makes it frustrating for most players during peak hours.

Now lets get to how the controls work: you can only press one key at a time, unless it is directional. Now read that statement again. Do you understand how bad this is? This means you can not move and attack at the same time. You actually have to stop, then hit attack, wait for your attack action to complete, and then you can move.No really, read that above paragraph once more....because this will cause so many deaths it is infuriating. If you are still moving when you hit the attack button, you will hear the sword swinging, but you won't be attacking. You can't dash right after attacking. You can't dash and then instantly attack. Well, If you actually stop moving, and then hit the attack key...just like while moving you will hear the attack sound but won't be attacking. So you have to wait before you can attack. Or I am guessing it is waiting since you have to wait a second after hitting attack to actually see your sword come out.Yep, you know what I am going to say...go back and re-read that last sentence again, because the controls are so utterly bad that even after hitting an attack there is a delay before anything happens. That makes combat difficult in an action game...but it isn't just attack. Wait until you find out you can jump off walls, and how awkward it feels where you can just keep jumping against the same wall to get to areas you might not want to get to."Insert re-read that last sentence here" because I stopped playing after passing the Minotaur like guy with the big ax, got the potion, and then jumped to the top of the area against the right wall, to get above the level. I then ran to the right where I shouldn't be, fell of the edge of the map and was stuck.This reminds me of the days in my computer programming class where I was in such a hurry to make something, that I didn't even test it. This game is plagued with numerous bugs.First of all, when you hold the arrow keys or [w], [a], [s], [d] the game disables the attack button, which may seem reasonable as it forces players to be more responsive. However, the running animation continues to play, and you can still hear the sword swinging sound, leaving you uncertain if you're dealing damage with each swing. Fun fact, you don't inflict any damage in this state, so it's important not to hold the movement keys while attacking.Another poorly implemented aspect is the dashing mechanic, which is riddled with glitches. I encountered two core problems with i.Firstly, if your hitbox dashes into an enemy or wall, you become stuck. This becomes especially frustrating in the first level, where the linear path includes a tower section. Often, you dash into a wall and get trapped, leaving you vulnerable to enemy attacks. The second issue arises when you're unable to dash after recently attacking enemies. While this function is intended to prevent spamming, the sprite performs the dash animation, plays the sound, but remains in the idle position, essentially allowing you to stand in one spot and dash without actually moving, which is very much game-breaking.One last major issue with the game was the requirement to defeat every enemy before facing the boss. It became tedious to eliminate each enemy, and attempting to reach the "exit" area before doing so will result in falling into a void, forcing players to restart. This was exacerbated by certain levels that prevented backtracking due to impassable terrain, such as thicker upper terrain blocking the ability to use the infinite wall jump.To the developers:To address the first problem, prioritize either the sound effects or animations by implementing a condition check that ensures running consistently takes precedence over attacking, or vice versa.To resolve the second problem, incorporate a condition check that examines the position the sprite dashes into, using a raycast.To tackle the third problem, clearly communicate to players at the beginning of the game that they must eliminate all enemies. Additionally, consider adding a door to the boss area that remains closed until all enemies are defeated, preventing accidental falls into the void. You could also introduce ladders or ropes in tall areas, allowing players to ascend or descend easily by holding the corresponding key (e.g., [w] or [upper arrow]), facilitating traversal and backtracking throughout the map.tl;drIn the game's current state, I just could not recommend it, even for hardcore hack and slash players, it is just a buggy mess.Edit 1:I've completed the game within an hour, mainly due to how buggy the final level is, I dashed into the same staircase numerous times, and it forced me to restart the level. The game is repetitive and lame, only experience it for the Steam achievements, if you really want it.

There's a lot of potential here, but I'm not convinced that the game knows whether it's an adult AVN or a quest-based RPG. The graphics are really good, the gameplay pretty simple and intuitive in the main part.However, for an adult game there aren't a great many scenes, no replay/gallery, limited control of each (2-3 viewpoints for each of a few poses) and a single save-slot, which precludes any form of replay other than end-to-end. Being a Unity app, the scenes are drawn real-time, as opposed to being pre-rendered video, which makes for a better experience, but again the game doesn't make the most of the potential - there is for example no control over clothing, customisation of the main protagonist &c.For an RPG, it loses any sort of tension by virtue of there not being a "bad outcome" - the quest play is (afaik) completely linear. Surprisingly decent adventure game that could’ve easily worked without the naughty bits. The game is essentially a fetch quest game with aspects of the walking sim genre. However, as opposed to a lifeless world that you explore at a sluggish speed, here you get to run around a fairly large village and huge forest area where populace hasn't mysteriously disappeared or perished from unnatural reasons.People appear more like objects, despite having life-like characteristics. You can't communicate or interact with them unless it’s a quest. The majority of them simply stand around, with guards standing next to entrances and villagers standing in front of tables or in the middle of a crowd. You play Bernadette, a local beggar who also happens to have a killer body. Since there’s a big debt hanging over her head, she has no choice but to use what she has.While the absence of voice actors in independent games is completely acceptable, the complete lack of sound effects creates an odd ambiance. The only thing you hear throughout the entire game is a generic medieval music. The script is fine, but there’s nothing here that will blow your mind.The main objectives of the game is to follow waypoints and finish quests. Multiple quests opening at once and at least two choices during conversations imply different conclusions and an open world, however that isn't the case. To advance the plot, all quests must be finished, and choices are merely different bits of text leading to the same conclusion.Playing a beggar gives you access to people's homes and the ability to steal items from barrels and other storage areas around the village. You won't be caught because nobody is watching what happens. Every stolen item is instantly turned into money that is used to buy something within the quest. But there's a huge bug: if you steal stuff from several containers in a row, only the last one will count. There are some bonus activities like purchasing furniture and collecting statues, but there is no actual incentive to do so. And don't help random people by giving them money. This will just make the game longer because you'll be forced to waste time by stealing. Two inactive "Books" and "Achievements" tabs in the game suggest stuff that hasn’t been implemented yet. Perhaps in future updates. It’s a shame exploration is not rewarded because there’s a bunch of interesting stuff to see in the game. Also, you're free to walk around even after you beat the game.The sex scenes make this title stand out from the crown, although you could remove them and still have a decent game. In any case, you don't get to see them very often. There might be a scene after a quest or you can sell your body to someone around the village, but it’s not what the game is all about.The graphics are passable, but not quite as good as they appear in the game's pictures. However, at least the game works properly. This is not one of those games whose bad coding drags even the most powerful hardware to its knees, despite the odd hiccups. If this is all custom work, it’s very impressive.

perfectly describes what this VN is all about. Considering that, this isnt just a romance or slice of life type of story, but also a fantasy story that has some mystery elements as you try to unravel what is actually going on and who the mysterious woman is that keeps appearing and what she wants.Since I always enjoy a nice fantasy story, I quite like this game and I especially enjoy the idea of showing DnDs events as if you were actually living through them. In those scenarios there is also a lot of crazy stuff happening and it is also the part that offers you the most action. The real life portions on the other end are far more normal and show you nice interactions between a group of close friends and the beautiful relationship of the mc and his girlfriend. Depending on your choices you can even get closer to the other female members of your friend group for that extra spicyness. The entire relationship concept stays very wholesome though and there isnt any cheating behind anyones backs for example.The art in this VN is honestly on a pretty high level. The backgrounds and character models all look good and the game also has quite a lot of animations that are all running on a nice framerate. So if you like yourself some animated adult scenes then yes they are in this. The animations are also used for other scenes though which I really enjoy since it makes the experience more dynamic. There is also already quite a decent amount of content which makes the asking price very fair imo.The game also offers you quite a bunch of choices, which a lot of them though dont make much of a difference, but the most important things are considered in them, for example that you can decide not to get closer to any of the other girls if that is what you want.

Okay, so, my overall rating on this piece is 9/10. Which, let me just say, I did not expect I was going to give.
