I enjoyed the splice of life moments (Like, honestly, the only one I skimmed was the basketball game played with Oscar and I can't recall the other name other than it starts with a K), I enjoyed the D&D moment (which I surprisingly in depth and very enjoyable to play through. I REALLY enjoy the characters. All of the characters. You have 5 core characters, (You, your GF, the two guys friends, and the two female friends) with two secondary characters (as i see them). The only secondary character I wanted to see more of was Baily (I know I spelled that wrong), your GFs Younger sister. Then we get what I assume is the antagonist (starts with an A, names are not my strong suite) and to be honest, I REALLY like how innocent she plays off to be. Kinda. The only part of her that is a dead giveaway to her possible evil antics are the horns on her head. Which, if the devs are interested in any ideas on, I would remove and just lightly alter some of her mannerisms/dialogue because with a couple minor, minor adjustments, you would swear that her imprisonment was unjustified and she was an innocent soul that could just give you a means to sway the thoughts of others. Overall, this game took me the 18 hours I played (give or take an hour for some expected pauses) and I got through the existing 5 chapters. That would be my only other criticism with this piece is that its out as a completed game but only 5 chapters long. Now, with VNs, I get it. I am working towards making my own VN in RenPy and it is a time demanding task. What will determien if I bump this rating up or down 1 is going to be how they release chapters going forward. I believe the game is posted free (or it was $15USD) and based on that, if they come out as DLCs, my only hope is they come out in groups of chapters, not one chapter at a time. Depends on how development is going really. 18 hours over 5 chapters is almost 4 hours of content per chapter. That is a fairly healthy ratio considering the happy medium per chapter is 3 hours. Also, also, may I just mention that the animation in this is really nice. Its the first VN I have played with animations as smooth as this. Yea, sure, Being a ♥♥♥ or College Kings 1 (or 2) has animated scenes, but they are usually very simple with little going on other than a repeat of motion. Usually with no more than two variances to the motion taking place. It works, but its not as fun as how creative this piece has been. Get it before the price goes up peeps! Its worth adding to your collection!Oh... side note, I only have 1 concern with this game and that is re-playability. So, a comparison to the other titles I have played is that a lot of what happens is not by choice, it is simply going on. You get some options, but keep this in mind. Your GF IS your GF. Like I wanted to honestly run a game dating the younger sister of the GF (idk why, that character just appeals to me more) but at the moment, its not optional. And considering the direction of the game, I don't see there being a possibility to break up with your current gf to date someone else. (Skylor was another character I was interested in as a partner). With that in mind, a lot of these interactions you are having with other women are not through the entanglments of an earned relationship with them directly, but an open sexual relationship between friends that appears to be developing over time. Its not bad, do not get me wrong. It is just limiting. You also won't be going solo with the other girls either. This isn't like College Kings where you can cheat on everyone you date all at once for the sake of sex. What this game lacks for in choice makes up for in Story and Narative and I am 100% hear for it so devs, if you see this, I have no problems with this, but it was on my mind while playing. It might be a bit much to suggest but if the option appeals, having different versions of the game that you can run with minor changes to adjust who you are dating at the start may be worth it? Idk. Depends. But that concludes my thoughts. I have enjoyed this regardless.

Between Two Worlds transcends the line between a good story and a adult visual novel.  If you removed all the sex there is still a solid choice based VN lurking about.  The models are fairly reflective of real people, there are no cover girl fashion models, balloon chested future back surgery candidates, beefcake edition men, or Buick sized members.  Now should you support a game currently in development?  As a current patron of the game, I say YES.  The creator(s) are responsive and from that contact I would say are committed to the project. (spoiler free review – up to the end of Chapter 5)A group of friends have normal day to day lives and are running a role-playing Campaign (like DnD). Supernatural events start surrounding the main character that seem to be somehow connected to their running campaign.The story follows a group of friends while focusing on a male main character. All characters are well fleshed out and interact realistically with each other as friends would.They have a game night once a week where they play role-playing games (like DnD).One day, after encountering a strange book the MC starts experiencing supernatural events that seem so be somehow related to their most recent campaign.The story follows three main threads: the daily lives of the friend group, the supernatural plots of strange happenings surrounding the MC and the relationship between the MC and his girlfriend Hannah (also part of the group).The story, at the time of writing, is unfinished and contains 5 chapters.The relationship between the MC and his girlfriend Hannah is a solid and realistic BF-GF relationship. They see each other when they can, and they have fun when they have the time and the place. It is all realistic and, overall, quite wholesome. There is a good amount of care put into their sex scenes and the writing really bring across how much they love and care for each other.In the context of the role-playing campaign the MC’s character is a womanizer and the DM actively places potential sexual encounters (in the context of the fantasy). There is an additional optional scene where the MC’s character the character of another of the group’s members can also have fun ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°).A final optional possibility is a three-way relationship, agreed between the main couple, to include one of their female friends. The conversations leading up to this possibility and the scene itself have been very thoughtfully written and everything is done with purposeful tact and respect for the feelings of everyone involved in such situations. It’s actually one of the greatest plus marks for this title as these sorts of sexual encounters are usually just glossed over and everyone just accepts it, but the devs of “Between Two Worlds” have gone out of their way to make a very grown-up and realistic depiction of this type of relationships.The UI is pretty standard Ren’Py but it is well customized and scales pretty well.The models are very well made. Overall, everything is done with a lot of attention to detail, however the renders are not done with a lot of resolution. Unless you want to look at them in 2k or 4k you won’t notice it though, as the overall art direction is good and so the models are quite clean. The environments are slightly less polished, but not by much. There are quite a variety of settings, so it is understandable that some corners were cut here. The main scenarios, however, are quite well made (main MC’s apartment, countryside cabin and Oscar’s Apartment) There are animated scenes (repeating and non-repeating) used through the game, mostly in the sex scenes and in dialogue scenes when the MC explains something, and the other character is “reacting”. They are all well-made with no unnatural physics behaviours or model tearing (that I saw).Highly recommended VN. It provides one of the most realistic and grown-up depictions of adult friendships and stable relationships in the context of adult video games.The idea of having a in-universe role-playing game opens the possibility for more “freaky” situations (sexual and otherwise) without undermining the more grounded approach to the characters and overall story.The supernatural aspect, although present, is never overwhelming and there might even be a non-mystical explanation for it (as of Chapter 5’s ending it is still an open topic).Even though the story is still unfinished I highly recommend this VN.

The Good:1. The renders are high quality, and there are plenty of them for the few sex scenes in the game. (I'll get back to that later.)2. Well written. There are genuine moments of comedy, emotional moments, and a couple of romantic moments. Being able to realistically weave these things together sometimes back to back is challenging for many writers, so good job. Also, the TTRPG segments were depicted very realistically, other than the actual roleplay of sex in a group setting. Most tables don't go for that, but this is a sex game, and if it weren't in the sessions, the game would be lacking even more sex scenes than it already is. 3. Unlike most AVNs, Between Two World's chapters seem to be allowed to go as long as they need to reach a satisfying story ending, and not just a predetermined time limit of around an hour, but that can be a double-edged sword, especially considering my next point. The Not So Good:1. I've said a few times already, but it still needs to be repeated; there is a severe lack of sex scenes in this porn game. I think we are barely at 1 per chapter, and with how long each chapter can be, that's just not enough. Also, the sex that was there was bland. Half the game takes place in a world where magic exists. I am sure there are ways magic can be used to spice things up. The dev even tries it with one scene during a play session, but that's been it so far. 2. There needed to be more actual gameplay. Between Two World's story centers around a group of friends' weekly TTRPG sessions. There has not been a more opportune setting to insert character options or hidden dice rolls to determine the success of an action for choices or possible combat actions. There were initiate possibilities, and they chose to stick to just a linear story progression. 3. The story as it is now, is very linear. There are some choices, but only a few that matter. My most meaningful choice so far was to throw a traditional-style birthday party or go on a weekend retreat to celibate this person's birthday instead. There are some minor choices as well, mainly in the TTRPG sessions. But as far as I can tell, these just flavor how most encounters are resolved. Using  Magic Missile or Lighting Storm doesn't mean one spell will succeed and the other option will fail. They just have different animations.  4. Assets are reused from other AVNs.  I've been corrected. The character model is not the same as Jill's. Funny that they were able to identify what character I was talking about without me saying their name though, so that shows just how similar they look.It's like they cast Keira Knightley, and I said it's Natalie Portman. what's the difference really? Other "real world" locations are also reused. The characters also just keep going to the same places over and over. Realistic to how people actually are, but boring for a story. Final Thoughts:Between Two Worlds is frustrating for me. I want to like it and say go play it, it's good, but I can't. I found myself bored a lot and skipping much of the fantasy world stuff until the current last chapter (six as of the time of writing). I became more invested in the fantasy once it was no longer attached to the table. It's because I knew I had no impact on the game session stuff, even less so than the rest of the time I was playing Between Two Worlds, so I didn't care. There was additional separation because it was the MC's character I was forced to watch being played by a character I already had little control of. Additionally, the lack of meaningful choices really doesn't compel me to revisit this story to see what I missed, which I don't think you can even miss any sex scene I think. The dev tells you there are no wrong choices at the start, and you won't miss anything,  so why even have the options to begin with? I get I'm in the minority in this community. Most AVN players just want to sleep with all the girls and not miss any content on a single play-through. Still, this review is from my point of view, so you get to be subject to what I think a good AVN should have.

There is magic, there is sex and, it turns out, there is a very real struggle for power. But wait! What is this magic that would bleed over into the real world and blur the lines of where the game ends and reality begins? And will you, as MC, make decisions that work to have Good triumph over Evil or will you fall prey to the lust for power and go to the Dark Side?The story is wonderfully written and the renders are quite good, with lovely attention to detail and beautifully smooth animations. While this  a story-first AVN, there's certainly enough A in the VN to be ... satisfying. (If you're looking for a primarily fappity-oriented harem game, this probably isn't the AVN for you. If you like good stories, though, it's worth the price of admission!) Each character is very likeable and the story is wholesome in a feel-good sense that makes coming back to play through for new achievements or just browsing the witty dialog very much worthwhile. For an added bonus, the developer, Droosk, is very much present in the Steam discussions and Discord channels. At the time of writing, BTW should probably be 11-12 chapters in total planned with 6 currently released. Based on what has been presented thus far, it's fair to say that Droosk seems to be planning on significant character development and growth opportunities in the chapters to come.After something like 35-ish hours invested, I'm giving it a solid 10/10: Would Ride Again. Pros: -Play D&D, experiencing the story within the story.-Well designed character art.-Interesting story line.Cons:-To few choice points.-Many of the choice points seem minimal / tonal.-Some areas of the story seem to go on forever whether you wanted or not.This is a visual novel with rather ironically light role playing elements where you  play a young man interacting with mostly college age women, d&d (or technically pathfinder, but similar difference), and supernatural elements. I really liked the story in a story aspect, and ever since "Life is Strange: Before the Storm" had its d&d scenes, I've loooved randomly running into side d&d story content inside of games like this. It adds a lot to the story with the occasional problem of sometimes being more interesting than the actual base story-but what can you do? In any event, the story in a story aspect is further extended by the supernatural occult element, where not only will the adult slice of life story jump back and forth between d&d and the base story, but also between the aforementioned and the supernatural elements. As mentioned, most adult elements are well rendered with gorgeous and realistic character art, though there does seem to be, at least in some of the mid-early chapters, a bit of a push towards younger characters both in the d&d game and the actual base story (i.e. tiny gnomes, fairies, and then two kid sister style characters as romantic interests) which is a bit much unless you're into that sort of thing. The other problem is that there are not enough choice points in my opinion; sometimes you will go through many, many pages and mouse clicks before reaching some, so that huge swaths of the novel seem like a kinetic visual novel opposed to the CYOA we are here for. As the protagonist is not customisable and gets a touch annoying at times, this can make for a long experience at times; though the interesting three point story complete with good quality adult content makes up for it. So, overall, I'd rate it as recommended for those that are looking for an adult fantasy/contemporary slice of life mashup.

The game has a linear plot, but this is not necessarily a bad thing. In this case, I think it's a positive thing, because the title is about what it's about, which is the story of Arcadie's second born.The writing style is just right, I didn't have any problems reading and understanding it, which is something to be thankful for. The pace of the story in general is good and steady, and most importantly, it has no humdrum or unnecessary moments that could affect the pace. I think all the characters are particularly well done. They are not walking stereotypes, and they are not perfect either. The fact that the different characters have their positive and negative points, and the fact that they are imperfect and make mistakes, I think that's what makes them human, and helps a lot in the immersion of the story. Another point to take into account is how customisable the MC is through the options presented to us. Not only in terms of actions that affect the story, but also in terms of the MC's personality and reactions to events. The author has been very detailed in that sense, and it's something that has really entertained me.I think she also does something that a lot of authors don't dare to do, or don't want to do, and that is to allow for character development. You can start with a naive, good-natured character, but the choices allow you to lose your head over the course of the story, and change radically. Apart from that, the MC can be heartless if he wants to be. The issue of the romantic relationships you can have with other characters, I think that's also done quite masterfully. Because it's not just an add-on for getting into bed and doing hand-holding, but it can also affect how certain aspects of the story go, depending on those relationships. To the point, that you can have romances with the characters, as a way to manipulate them for your plans. Overall I think it is an interactive game that is well worth buying and playing. Because of how customisable the MC is, it has significant replayability, so it can offer hours of gameplay.

That's all you need to know if you don't like spoilers, but if you don't care, or if you already know how the story goes, then here are a bunch of my nit picks.You never feel powerful. You have a vile of the most powerful magic blood in existence, the thing that is meant to make you a myth, a legend, something people will be talking for eons about, and it does nothing. I am aware it gives you more mana, but other than that, it does nothing. There is no supercharged move you can pull off because of it, there is no feat of magic that looks like something a greek god would pull off, nonono, that would be too much to write apparently. Like, yea, she was blood-lusted, but if you were supper cautious or overly prepared, the game should've rewarded you, perhaps not with your sister surviving unscathed, but with her still alive. I would've totally loved playing as the second fiddle to a furious empress who can't fight anymore, and would've saved the game from the third nit-pick I have.Deus ex machina, a term that everyone knows. I’ve long anticipated the release of Arcadie: Second-Born, having eagerly tracked its progress since the first uploaded demo. I enjoyed reading through the novel then, and I’ve enjoyed the finished product all the more.Arcadie: Second-Born is a superlative work of interactive fiction. Not only is the novel well-written and emotive, the author has moreover done a magnificent job of employing the conventions of the genre to their fullest and most effective use. The narrative expectations constructed prior to and during the novel are convincingly sold to the reader and then abruptly subverted in a way that does not feel contrived. The interpersonal relationships into which the player character can enter—romantic, familial, and platonic; friendly and adversarial—are (depending on the relation) authentically tense, sweet, and solemn. The skills in which the player character may specialize all feel meaningful, as their selection bears not only where skill checks are present, but also enables the selection of certain choices and reveals unique bits of dialogue. In other words, the skills act to shape the personality of the player character themselves. The different ways in which the story can conclude feel appropriately distinct, based on the different, contrary emotions to which they’ve given rise when I played through them.Above all, I appreciate that the author has written a story that is memorable and has created a setting that is emotionally and intellectually captivating. Having played through the novel on multiple occasions, I’m not only satisfied but am also possessed by a burning curiosity about the history and geopolitics of Arcadie and its surrounding states, in addition to the fates and philosophies of many of the novel’s characters.To anyone who’s a fan of fantasy settings involving the use of the pen and the sword, in which you can interact with a host of different characters, many of whom have realistic and sometimes fascinatingly profound motivations and philosophies, and in which your choices feel meaningful—I would recommend Arcadie: Second-Born.

Arcadie is an engaging and immersive interactive novel. The story is fine even if it treads rather familiar ground but its character development and interaction where this work truly shines. The plot is standard fantasy fare dealing with assassination/betrayal and the subsequent conflict within a kingdom. Very much to the novel's advantage the protagonist starts off as a royal spare bypassing the stereotypical chosen one cliche and giving the player ample opportunities to define their character in an organic way.Arcadie does a creditable job of weaving the plot together. In truth though the political and military machinations take a back seat to characterization. I can think of few games (if any) that have created such compelling supporting characters. The romance(s) are well paced and feel earned and rewarding (even if the two romance options are unequal in terms of depth and level of engagement). Indeed the dialogue and character development are engaging enough that I have replayed the game/novel multiple times much like rereading a favorite book. There are occasional grammatical/compositional errors or awkward word choices that I suspect are down to the work having been written in another language before being translated into English. However, the mistakes were rare enough to not detract from my enjoyment of Arcadie: Second Born.All in all, I highly recommend this work.

Gameplay: 8/10Visuals: NA/10Audio: NA/10Replayability: 8/10In a world where PC gaming no longer stands on the edge of the frontier in terms of innovative technology and ground-breaking graphics, games such as Arcadie, Second Born that take a more basic and dated approach to storytelling serve as a great reminder that the content and passion of a product is worth more than impressive graphics and immersion. The story was extremely interesting, and willing to cross lines that can only be crossed in games where developers don't worry about pleasing audiences or creating that feel-good happy ending. While it is a simple text-based novel, the Choose-Your-Own-Adventure aspect is so present that it differs from classic reading by letting you explore many options to forge your own path, while still having good and consistent world-building to have you along.Visuals are neutral for me, as while I did not expect animations or cutscenes of some sort, character portraits or complimentary artwork could have been used to flesh out some of the more defined characters, although I understand that highlights specifics may have broken the immersion for people who may imagine the characters in a different way. On another note, I do wish you could change the text color, as I was playing at a very late night and the contrast between the text and background was blinding, but that is a rather trivial complaint that was easily remedied.The complete lack of audio is an interesting choice. While I think some people might hate this and choose to not play due to the dead silence that persists throughout, I put on the Witcher 3 complete soundtrack which in my opinion enhanced my immersion and the atmosphere. I find that this game leaves a lot of aspects out and I'm starting to believe that that was on purpose, in order to allow another layer of depth to the choose your own adventure aspect.As for replayability, my first play through took just over three hours to finish. You are allowed to go back pages and change decisions, as well as save and load to your heart's content. If you know you are not going to want to go through everything again, I think the save/load method should allow you to get through most of the content you were hoping to see without committing another three hours to the game. As in terms of actual story differences, I cannot say how much each playthrough differs, but when I clicked on the community page, I had another ending quite different than mine spoiled to me by some idiot who put spoilers in a post title. I won't say exactly what the post was, but I'm happy as it looked like they were dealing with a rather unfortunate outcome.Another thing I would like to touch on in terms of replayability is romance. It is what drew me into playing this game, and I did not even end up doing anything romantically related at all, because I was too busy saving the kingdom. Romance is completely optional and customizable, and the creator makes it clear that romancing a character is not a linear path as what most games are (eg: pick this dialogue in this scene to start the romance) but rather is a split path that allows multiple opportunities to make your move, meaning that if something seems out of character to you or you feel that more imposing matters are at hand, you can move past that point without being locked out of said romance. To make a short story even shorter, Arcadie Second Born is well worth the full price and feels like what new-generation storytelling should be, where we can bend the narrator's choice to our will in order to create stronger attachments or simply create different perspectives. If you like/liked to read, and perhaps feel like enjoying some medieval fantasy on your down time, you will like this game.

I'm usually a pretty big fan of CYOA books, and even more than that I'm a huge fan of political intrigue, medieval fantasy and games about governing but despite my best efforts Arcadie just isn't a very good CYOA book. The big issues here are the actual impact you have on the story, the quality of the writing, horrible characterization and pacing as well as a complete disconnect between the events of the book and what makes sense for the world.To start your choices in the game don't exactly have much real impact, yes you'll see an extra scene or two, get a different line here and there or change the ending, but the game consistently feels like you're on rails from the beginning, in fact the entire first act until the battle really feels like you're just a bystander to events. Sure its intended to be that way and you get more freedom later on but that doesn't mean its fun, you end up just witnessing events and only really giving your opinion on those events rather than changing them and creating an interesting divergent path. This is one of the biggest problems in the game. There's a huge emphasis on a wide variety of responses and while it helps you differentiate who you're playing as, the real impact of these choices only serves to change the context you view events in rather than actually changing the events themselves. This tends to make the story feel very hollow since you constantly are asked for an opinion or some input but again it only makes you feel like a bystander to the events rather than a catalyst for them. I played for about 6 hours and I really only saw a couple events occur that actually felt like I caused them but these were extremely few and far between. The quality of the writing left a lot to be desired, unnecessary details are thrown at you and scene changes are done so swiftly that you barely get any sense of the scenes you find yourself reading. Descriptions either become so simple as to leave you unimmersed or so detailed as to bore you since the writing isn't particularly evocative or immersive except for the romance and smut which is actually quite good.The pacing is easily the biggest flaw with the writing though, I've played many CYOA books and even the subpar ones can coast by on a simple premise even if the pacing isn't great. The problem with Arcadie is that its aiming to do so much without anywhere near the amount of competency needed to actually write a good political thriller or epic fantasy so it just falls on its face. In Arcadie things just sort of happen in the game, again with very little player discretion. One minute you're in a council meeting then suddenly there's a ball, then you're at a fort preparing for a battle and then right back at a council meeting. This all happens with virtually no buildup or time to digest anything, it feels like the player is just being flung from scene to scene without any care taken to immerse the player or let the text breathe. This jarring feeling characterizes a lot of the book and its one of the bigger reasons why the game feels so linear especially when the events that occur seem like they should be under your purview. In the end the pacing just feels like the author had too many ideas and no idea how to gracefully transition between them while giving the player agency over that content.Another thing I really didn't like was the characterization, most of the main cast were very one note and largely fell into some basic archetypes with very little nuance. They aren't entirely cookie cutter but upon meeting the character you get their entire vibe virtually immediately, this left so little mystery about the main romantic interests and really flattened them as characters and if not for the well written smut then the romantic interests would be entirely uninteresting. The supporting cast, if you'd even say the game has any is also quite bare bones. A haughty noble, a righteous revolutionary, its all really too simple and boring and if the game were merely some fantasy epic or whatever it'd be more excusable but in a game clearly trying to evoke the ideas of political intrigue it just makes everything so unbelievable and lifeless. Complexity and nuance was really lacking from almost every character in the book. The lack of nuance was worst with your sibling, who from the very beginning was made out to be a complete warmonger without any real redeeming qualities. In isolation this would be fine but every character is like this, feeling entirely one note and as a result, forgettable.Finally the book has a weird amount of immersion breaking stuff in it. For starters there's the leader of the nobles' private council, a character who just seems so out of place. When you first meet him he mocks your dead sibling, challenges your right to rule and positions himself against you no matter what you do. It feels like a complete parody of a noble. The kingdom of Arcadie is a very militant and authoritarian institution, yet this schmuck openly questions you like it wasn't horribly dangerous. Furthermore, apparently this council he leads is both unknown to the masses yet actually responsible for appointing you the monarch? Yet earlier, Cyril tells you that no matter what they'll support you since you're the monarch? Very odd. I know the character is meant to show you the vibes of the nobility, that they just want to undermine you for their own power but like, it comes off so outrageously out of place that it knocks the legs out of any political intrigue you might've expected. Then there's the Aether chandeliers and stuff you find everywhere but yet apparently only the royal family have ever been able to actually use Aether, so what are your family just enchanting a bunch of chandeliers? Are these really old ones? Or is there some other way these are made? It just feels so odd introducing this unique magical force that is rare and apparently your sibling is the only one who can reasonably utilize it within centuries, yet these light sources are everywhere. There's plenty more out of place things like your character being so extremely ill-equipped to run a country because of 2 whole children your parents never thought to prepare you alongside your sibling, or a conversation with a foreign monarch going from heated difficult negotiations to him rolling over without the slightest push back just because you said some tough words. The game just feels like someone wanted to write a cool story about being a monarch with political intrigue and choice and skills and whatnot but had such little understanding of how all this would actually work, everything just feels so one note and lacking almost any complexity at all.Anyway, I spoke plenty now. Finishing off, the UI is pretty good though I would've like a sepia theme like what Choice Of Games has. I also really appreciate the ability to save and load which I think is kinda necessary in games like this so its a very welcome addition. Beyond that I can't say much praise for the game, though again the romance and smut scenes are a definite highlight.

is a completely texted-based choose-your-own-adventure (CYOA) novel by  In , you play as, yep, you guessed it, the second-born child of the D'Arcadie line: the Royal Family. Your elder sister, Ariana, has The Gift: the ability to control and use aether. Your bloodline is well known for it, but it's become very rare. The fact that your sister is the first aether user in over three hundred years, shines a great light on her. She is the future Queen too. These two things combined make Ariana special to your parents and while she's showered in praise, you are always in her shadow. Despite this, you were still given the best education possible and are allowed more freedom than your sibling. Your kingdom, Arcadie, is at war on almost all sides of the border. Your lands hold a great deal of fertile land and others want it. To some people, the King and Queen are seen as warmongers, forcing their loyal subjects to fight for their own selfish desires, instead of actively trying to compromise and make peace. However, one of the commanders of your armies does manage to broker a peace treaty and this is where the novel will start. You can guess that things don't go as smoothly as planned. The plot was spaced out nicely: more often than not, flowed at an acceptable pace. Things move realistically for a mission that has a time limit to it. There isn't much I can say without it spoiling the story, but prepare yourself for twists, turns and an emotional journey. As for the characters, you can choose your characters' gender and that of the romance options (RO), catering them to your preferences. You are also offered a few basic cosmetic customisation options for the MC: hair/skin/eye colour etc. These are used for some flavour text throughout the novel. You can choose your forename but for story purposes, your surname will always be D'Arcadie. What you can expect:My one grievance with the ROs is their age. It's not something I'm often bothered by but story-wise, they feel a bit young to both be commanders of your armies. I'd have expected persons of an older age/more experience to hold those positions. I assume the decision to make them young was to be able to keep their age close to the MC, who is in her early 20s. That's sort of the average for novels like these I believe.I found the world to be crafted in a way that added interest to the story of a thriving country that is forced to fight for its land: the reasons made sense. All of the characters were fully fleshed out with their own backgrounds, motivations, desires and reasons for doing what they do. I felt as if a lot of care and attention went into making this CYOA novel: it really showed in the amount of pleasure I received from reading it.Most of the CYOA games I've played in the past were from the more well-known interactive fiction provider Choice of Games/Host of Games:  have already beaten their platform, in my eyes, with the quality of life options they have implemented into their own software. A save and load system, and although it only has a few direct saves, it also gives you the possibility to make saves directly to your pc, outside of the game, that you can name yourself. They also provide a back button, a simple thing but it adds so much more freedom. As with any text, it isn't easy to decipher the meaning behind the words sometimes, and choosing an option you perceive to have a certain tone, only for it to actually have a different one, can make it feel very out of character for you. Just being able to pick through the choices and see which you prefer, or sating your curiosity, offered a lot more enjoyment to my reading.  Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed my first playthrough of  and was very glad about what I received for my money's worth. I'm not often a fan of war-related stories but the well-designed world and characters very much pulled me in and ensured that I stayed too. I would more than recommend this to anyone who enjoys interactive fiction, thinks the story sounds interesting, or perhaps fancies playing through their very first choose-your-own-adventure title.

Arcadie: Second-Born is a captivating text-based interactive fiction game available on Steam and Google Play. While it might not dazzle you with graphics or sound, its rich narrative and character depth make it worth exploring.The gameplay mechanics are familiar for fans of the genre, resembling other interactive fiction titles. While nothing stands out as groundbreaking, the experience remains polished and engaging throughout. The game draws you in with its narrative and character interactions rather than flashy visuals.The story is a heart, featuring multi-dimensional characters and unexpected twists. As you navigate the world, the relationships you build feel genuine and realistic for most of the journey. However, the ending left me feeling unsatisfied, almost like a cliffhanger that didn’t tie up loose ends.- Complete and polished experience- Fresh take on fantasy interactive fiction- Engaging characters and relationships- Anticlimactic ending with no real closure-Decisions felt inconsequential, leading to a frustrating narrative disconnectI thoroughly enjoyed my six hours with Arcadie: Second-Born, but the lack of closure in the ending was disappointing. It’s a game I’m glad to have purchased for the experience, even if the finale felt rushed and anticlimactic.While the journey through Arcadie: Second-Born is well-crafted and enjoyable, the conclusion left much to be desired. If you’re a fan of interactive fiction, it’s worth a play, but be prepared for an ending that may not meet your expectations.

This is a pretty brutal story, but one I quite enjoyed and happen to think is worth the price of admission and time invested. I don't feel the need to hold my big conclusion for the end, that's the takeaway, but I'll expand on that.The story is complete, but leaves room for more, rather than being a nugget of a story that demands a sequel to provide any sense of resolution.The characters are distinct and well written, interesting, endearing, whether as villains, friends, family, lovers, or whatever part they play in events. That extends to your own character, who can be competent and play an important role in events while giving you, the player, room to develop them as a person in the way that you desire.The story makes it clear that your character has lived in the shadow of the elder heir, but at no point did I feel that their place in the story was fully eclipsed by it or that they were lacking in agency. Events unfold along a particular path, sure, but only inasmuch as you cannot control the world around you, you are always afforded agency with how you react to events as they unfold, and the choices you make feel meaningful, and have an impact on the other characters swept up in events, both in the moment and in the long term.There were definite moments where the progression of your skills felt like they had an impact and were recognized within the world, but it never felt like a grind, and the opportunity cost of focusing was rewarding without becoming paralyzing.The pacing of the story was also good throughout, giving you chances to breathe and develop relationships and an understanding of the world between pitting you into frenetic, perilous circumstances that reach satisfying climaxes which build as they go. Giving you time to process what happens without dwelling so long that you lose interest. The prose is engaging and always pushing you forward, being concise where needed and expansive where justified, varying between those in a way that is satisfying as a reader while also always providing you the opportunity to engage with it on your own terms through your choices.The romances are satisfying, at least the ones I pursued, there seemed to be other options that might appeal to other people that I wasn't interested in, and I see that as a good thing.I am very happy with this and look forward to more, whether they decide to continue with this world and character or if they try their hand at other stories. As I said before, this is very satisfying as a standalone but leaves fertile ground for a continuation, which is a very difficult line to walk that many fail at.

A very fun and interesting concept that has been executed very well, but lacking some key features which I think would really help this game flourish to explode in popularity.The mechanic that only 1 person in the team can have a view on the outside world and what's actually happening amongst the other teams is great. This does however make communication so incredibly important, more so than most other games because you *need* someone to be explaining what happens and what's going on. I think this is the biggest demotivator for public games, which are important for a consistent playerbase to boost a game's popularity. People without trusting friends will simply feel frustrated playing this game, because everything down to the entire scoring and reward system (hitting enemy tanks and destroying them) has to be communicated, the only thing available to everyone is your own tank's health.Having some sort of indication when enemies are hit would be a huge step in the right direction, at the very least some sort of message like "enemy tank was hit for 100 damage!" that all players would see. Maybe you could even have a couple of peepholes which let players see a tiny radius around the tank for immediate surroundings information.But, the biggest thing this game needs I think is some sort of replay system, give players the satisfaction of rewatching the match from the outside world so they can relive the moments they didn't see. Especially because I've had matches where the round ended and nobody knew how it ended since no one happened to be looking through the periscope at the time.Destructible terrain. I know, this is difficult to implement, but was always one of the best features of other 2D tank games and especially with some of the boxed in maps would allow for some super fun and interesting matches.Party up lobbying. I think the most successful gamemode for this game would be the ability to party up a team with your friends and join an online game with lots of other tanks, communicating locally just with your friends in your tank but part of a much larger battle. This type of game requires a large number of people to get a decent match going, not everyone has that many friends.

I don't normally complain about game pricing--I'd happily pay $50 for an amazing 5-hour experience vs. paying $20 for a 100-hour slog. But I have to complain about CyberTD. This is an extremely feature-starved game priced at $20--basically a game-jam game with a thin coat of paint and very little imagination. Just so you are clear before you buy:- There is only one "tower" and you can barely control where you place it- The tower has fixed weapons that do not change throughout the round, which can last 20-30 minutes- There are no gameplay features on any of the maps--just a single random enemy path- The ONLY control you have as a player is to select your deck and weapons at the beginning of the run and select 1 upgrade card every time you level up (most of these are just +10% stat boosts, with very few having any mechanical effect)- There are no card selection mechanics like rerolling/banishing/freezing etc.- The writing and voice acting is there to add faux production value but contributes little- Interface is clunky, un-intuitive, and pretty bad even for a mobile title- Very few enemy types with at most 5 or 6 total mechanics that have almost no effect on gameplay- After a few hours, you realize cards that increase damage by X% are multiplicative (i.e. compound on each other) and enemy health also seems to scale multiplicatively. In practice, this means you'll pick the +damage card 90% of the time and you auto-win, up until the cap where you get out-scaled by enemies and need to grind more levels for better cards. Rinse and repeat.Overall: Just play Heretic's Fork instead. It is ALSO a TD deck-builder with one tower, but is priced at $10 and has interesting decisions to make (and a killer metal soundtrack)

Clockwork Origins has got some decent experience making deep and complex TD games with a twist and if you played any of the Elemental Wars games and enjoyed them then this will feel familiar yet refreshingly different.This mixes up deck building with TD to create something that feels really unique brings a completely fresh take on the genre to the table. You have a single tower and can level up various stats after each round by picking a random card from your deck. After you fail a round the game collects all your points to level you up. At each level you unlock new progressions such as more cards, more weapons or perks. You go back to your hub. Modify your tower. Build your deck. Then get back out and try to get further. At first you can barely get through three rounds but steadily that progression improves as you unlock more stuff.The game becomes this balance between building the perfect deck to try and increase the chances of being able to pick a powerful card during the game as well as building out the perfect tower to take advantage of those cards.It's a slow burn at first as the game introduces you gently to it's mechanics by after an hour of play when you have levelled up and gathered enough cards you suddenly find yourself progressing much further and things can become fairly frantic.It also runs flawlessly on the deck right out of the gate. I disabled the touch pad because it goes ballistic but aside from that its the perfect game for handheld play. Each round can be fairly quick (at first but as you get better they get longer) and after every round when you have unlocked a new card or toy you get that urge to get right back into the action and play another round.You then get weekly challenges and modifiers to add even more variety. If you are a fan of TD games or deck builders then this is absolutely worth a look especially if you have a Steam Deck (there is a Nintendo Switch version as well). I've found myself repeatedly picking up the deck for a quick round and then suddenly its five rounds later and i'm still goingAlso the developers the have clearly put in a lot of work to refining and polishing the game-play and balance as well as making sure both mouse and keyboard as well as controller support is cleanly implemented as was the case with Elemental War 2

I never really review early access games if I can help it because people too often review an EA game based on what it can be and not what it is. As it is, this game is 100% worth the $13 price-tag in the current state it's in. That being said, it has some huge ideals for future patches that if it actually pulls through on its promises, this game might be the single best shopkeeper sim out there. It's well balanced. Hard enough to make a profit that it takes many hours of rewarding gameplay to get to the next step of your shop. The addition of collecting/opening singles is ingenious. If I get bored of the stocking/restocking element, I am ripping packs to get my card collecting/chase fix. The UI is really great. I haven't played a shopkeeping game with as good of a UI as this one. Restocking shelves is satisfying and you really get a lot of variety of things to sell. The things I've been thinking they should add are mostly on the roadmap, which is awesome. I downloaded the other Tetramon games to check them out on GooglePlay but honestly, none of them really compare to this one. Whoever made this not only understands TCGs in general, but also understands what a good shopkeeping style game requires. The fact that smelly customers who hold you hostage well after closing is a hilarious touch and it really shows that the creator is an avid TCG player. lol. If you like shopkeeping games, this game is honestly the best one I've played so far in a long, long time.

Rating: 3.5/5 StarsTCG Card Shop Simulator is a fun and unique game with a lot of potential. The concept of running your own trading card game shop is fresh, and it's incredibly satisfying to stock, manage, and sell cards. However, despite the enjoyable gameplay, there are a few areas that need improvement for it to truly shine.One major issue is that there's not enough incentive for players to unlock and display all the available products in their shop. Once you’ve stocked everything, the game starts feeling repetitive and somewhat pointless. A reward system or additional goals for completionists would really enhance the experience.Another improvement could be in the in-game review app. Right now, it feels disconnected from your shop’s actual success. It would be much more engaging if it linked directly to your sales performance, XP, or progress—giving players a tangible sense of growth and achievement.Lastly, the frequency of customers requesting individual cards becomes annoying over time. This mechanic disrupts the flow of the game and could be tweaked or balanced to make it less of a chore.Overall, TCG Card Shop Simulator is a solid 3.5-star game with the potential to easily hit 5 stars if these areas are addressed. It’s enjoyable but could be much more rewarding with a few key adjustments.

Early Access score: 7..6/10Overall Game Right Now score: 3.5/10At time of review, Trading Card Game Card Shop Simulator—yes, probably should've dropped that extra 'Card' in the title—has an entertainment bell-curve to it. Coupled with time-tested game mechanics guaranteed to fire a small shot of dopamine at the right time, it's entirely possible people continue playing the game without noticing that they are no longer having fun. However, the ever-improving game play, roadmap, frequent updates, and general theme—coupled with the game providing scratches for the itches it creates—are more than enough to keep many people playing on and excited about the game's immediate future.And of course, there's moments where you feel like Bernard Black, scowling at customers, judging them, loathing your little card shop somehow being the busiest place in town.The game begins by learning that you can Jump and Sprint. I don't know why, but have assumed it's for getting the character unstuck if you ever somehow manage to find yourself caught in a bundle of items. You name your store—mine's —and then start on about your day as the new dealer in town, pedalling nerd crack to the fiends. Very soon, you have been introduced to the game's main mechanics and the familiar 'day-in; day-out' cycle of shop simulators begins.The general gist of it is you buy stock, place stock, price stock, open store, handle transactions, close store, and repeat. However, if that was it, this game wouldn't be so well-reviewed. There are three other  mechanics.The quality of the NPC models and animations often set off a type body language; yes, they know they have a problem; yes, they are ashamed of it and avoid eye-contact when handing over money; yes, when they dump two dozen packets of cards on your counter, they can hear your inner monologue saying, "You ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nerd."But you are not immune to the same affliction. The game allows you to dip into your own product and rip open card packets, and build your own collection. No one sees it, you can't use it to play, there's no reason to notice any details on the cards, but they do hold market values so they can be sold individually in the shop, with more worthless cards being bundled into "starter packs" and sold that way too.Some reviewers have said this is their favourite part of the game, though it's personally dull for me. The mechanic isn't dissimilar to loot boxes or slot machines which, for some people, can be addicting. Nice artwork, bright colours, reward sounds, timing for tension, etc. But at the end of the day, you're just holding down LMB while the process plays out and concludes, presenting you immediately with another packet, "Just one more?"It's worth noting that the developers have said they are working on the card game being playable, which would drastically improve the point of this mechanic. Perhaps also if people could display or trade cards—I don't know how hard that would be—this would be a big improvement too.There's something humorous about walking up to a stranger, spraying them with deodoriser, watching them recoil in disgust, but their addiction means they know  know they'll still be buying your crack afterwards.Smelly customers have negative effects on others in the store. Dealing with them is a small mechanic that breaks up the monotonous flow of regular shop routine while appealing to those that are striving for maximum profit each day.Beyond having machines placed around the store that automatically blast these customers as they walk by, there is not much else to this part of the game, nor anything similar to it.It's not as elaborate as it sounds, but exists and is done in two ways. The first is simply having tables in the store for people to play which passively generates income and XP while customers play. The second is adjusting the different games you host (only one type at a time) which can influence the market next day, somehow. For the most part, the second mechanic doesn't really influence the 'big picture', so can be easily forgotten or ignored.Other game types are also specific to the values of different card types, but unless you're sitting on a very high value card or planning to sell only cards of a certain type next day, there's not much reason to use these. The proportion of profit from individual card sales to everything else isn't all too influential either.Notably, the roadmap mentions the feature of organising tournaments, so this could be expanded nicely in the future. are...primitive. A shop owner can only wonder how the type of person that wants a job at a card game shop can somehow be so slow at figuring out the right amount of change to give back to a customer. Even a 'Normal' grade employee still seems to understand they're being paid for their time in the store, not the amount of work they actually do, and of course disappears in the middle of a task the second it hits 9:00 PM. However, they are still useful as the shop expands, in the same way that introducing a 10% bullet time would be., it's not the prettiest and I wonder where the 2.9 GB is going. The models and animation are...peculiar, while the lighting and textures are minimal at best. I think this really impacts any sort of immersion someone might feel about "running their own store" because your brain is always aware that it's a basic budget game. The lack of customisation around the store impacts this too as you are, after all, set up in the same blank template everyone else is with little else in the way of models, which I can only assume are bought assets. there's not much going on here and you will quickly drop the volume on the single loop of music so that you can just listen to your own. and no way to increase it. However, the roadmap lists increased difficulty at a later date. in general is indeed quite exciting and will be the saving grace should it happen. There is certainly no shortage of potential felt when playing.I wouldn't recommend the game in the current state and current price but it's likely I would in the near future as it improves through Early Access. The rate of updates from the developers implies this is very likely. I still give the Early Access score to be quite high, but the price tag, although low, is the main drawback. It's just not worth it, yet.Fortunately, players can buy and try the game and experience most of it within the Steam refund window if they feel like they've been duped.

In a world full of all sorts of weird and niche simulator games, TCG Card Shop Simulator is one of the few that genuinely appeals to me. It combines a satisfying loop of stocking shelves, running the cash register, organizing your shelves and floor space, expanding your shop, and progressively unlocking new products to sell and new types of shelves and cases to display product on with the addiction of cracking open countless card packs to either build up a collection or to sell off any valuable pulls to your customers. This game feeds off my past addiction to Magic: the Gathering and brings back fond memories of the many hours I spent at a newly opened FLGS to support the owner.There is already a substantial amount of content in Early Access (v0.49 as of this review) and more is being added fairly frequently, and I am excited for the future of this game as there is a lot planned for it including adding a playable version of the Pokemon-inspired TCG and adding other different types of TCGs into the game. Personally, I'm hoping for an M:tG type TCG to be added though I'm sure that is a monumental amount of work to pull off.Even as it is now, I highly recommend TCG Card Shop Simulator as it is well worth it's current price with its addicting gameplay loop and dozens of hours of potential play time to unlock everything currently available, and it will only continue to get bigger and better over time.

I'm just going to get straight to the point. This game is very addicting and it has more elements to it than just owning a card shop such as giving change back, ect. Note that some of my cons are planned for future updates but I'm just listing them anyways. There may be alot of cons but the game is still a 8.5-9/10 for me and none of them are too harsh.Here are my pros and cons to simplify this review:Pros-+Great variety of content for early access+Can open packs and booster boxes to get cards that you collect or sell+Ability to pull very rare and valuable cards, making it rewarding+AI Npcs can play the actual card game in your shop via tables+Game provides you with a few challenges and obstacles such as managing money, paying rent, and keeping smelly customers clean while they enter the shop to avoid others from leaving+The game has some compatibility with mods which extends it further(Play the base game first before you try other mods)+Ability to hire workers that vary in skills+A fair amount of upgrades that extend the space of your shop+A decent amount of furniture to buy for a EA game+Review app that allows you to see how your shop is doing+Ability to go outside of the shop(would be cool if it was expanded a bit and maybe had some NPC card dealers that could sell you rare cards at random on a street corner. Maybe also a way to add banners and advertisement for the shop)+Great variety of tetramon for a EA game-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Cons--Not enough variety of furniture to purchase. Some are worse like the vintage card table takes up a bit more space and looks worse than the standard card display table-Opening card packs can take a long time and become tedious. There should be an option to open them even faster than what the game offers.(Currently a mod does this so I recommend using that if you want to speed things up)-Card pull rates for some rare cards can be really low and rng. I think the values should increase slightly to make things interesting-Workers stand around when nothing to do. I feel like there should be a cleaning option for the shop or something for them to do so they don't just sit around.-No ability for customers to play board games together-Exp gain is very slow mid to late game that it becomes boring. Exp gain needs an increase and also more ways to gain exp other than just ringing customers up and opening card packs.-No wallpapers or other decorations to make your shop look unique-No card grading to increase value-Not enough task to do other than a few at the start of the game-Shop space could be improved a bit more, feels a bit small still-Collision space on alot of furniture takes up way too much space and no ability to overlap the spaces such as placing trash cans close or other small shelfs-Lack of interesting dialogue from customers and workers. Would be interesting to see customers responses or thoughts such as rude customers, happy, ect.-No way to play the card game itself with other customers-[Optional] Online with at least one other person to manage a shop together or just someone to visit that you can trade cards with.-Ability to trade cards with customersGreat game overall but with more updates it can become one of the best simulators out there. A official mobile release would be great as well to play on the go. I highly recommend this game and keep in mind that it can get addicting real fast!

Positives:A game that has heart and soul. What I mean is that there is clear passion that has been put into this game. It feels like a game that the developers themselves likely would play which in my eyes is the best kind of experience. The asking price is more than worth it. Best enjoyed as a casual experience to relax and live out the fantasy of owning a card shop. It is interesting having a certain degree of control over the card economy and having full agency of customizing your shop. I feel the game is at its best from level 1-40 where the progression is at its most refined. With this in mind the player will spend most of the game opening card packs and checking out customers until they get employees. Negatives: Without a doubt the most tedious and time consuming games for completion. Going for all of the achievements was one of the most long and drawn out grind fests that I have ever experienced in a video game. After about level 45 is when the game play slows down to a slog and it is within the players best interest to min max their shop to at least speed up the grind. I can admire that the game has "realistic" card rarities but it is almost absurd how long it takes to get enough cards for the various achievements. I highly recommend downloading a mod that lets the player hold a 1000 cards and skip the opening animation. Without it, it would take literally hundreds of hours just to get the achievements. Ignoring achievement grinding, it becomes clear to the player that the customers are very much basic AI. Customer reviews don't affect the experience and are ultimately pointless info for the player. Furthermore customers have a set number of moves when entering your shop. There is a chance they will go in looking for a specific item and if they don't find it, they will walk out immediately. It is actually detrimental to your profit by having a card table out with no cards on it as many customers will walk out after seeing there are no cards on it. Other customers purchase random items regardless of cost. It then is beneficial for the player to only sell a handful of expensive items to save the headache of having to restock so many useless items. The game has so much potential but I hope to see the customers and shop mechanics to be refined more in the future. It is in early access and it excellent for what it is. I hope to see some of these things improved in the future.

TCG Card Shop Simulator brings a unique twist to the simulator genre by putting players in the role of a trading card game (TCG) shop owner. At first, the concept is intriguing – managing stock, catering to niche customer requests, and even organizing card tournaments. The game captures the excitement of card collecting with realistic mechanics around pricing and rare finds, providing a solid foundation for fans of TCGs and management simulators alike.However, despite its charm, the gameplay can quickly feel repetitive. There’s a lack of depth in customer interactions and limited options for store customization, which might leave players longing for more dynamic features. The graphics, while functional, feel somewhat basic, and the soundtrack is serviceable but could use more variety to maintain immersion. Overall, "TCG Card Shop Simulator" is a pleasant experience for TCG enthusiasts but could benefit from more robust gameplay elements to keep players engaged in the long run.
